The **10,000 metres** or the **10,000-metre run** is a common [long-distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running") track running event. The event is part of the [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_(sport) "Athletics (sport)") programme at the [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") and the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships"), and is common at championship-level events. The race consists of 25 laps around an Olympic-sized 400 m track. It is less commonly held at track and field meetings due to its duration. The 10,000-metre track race is usually distinguished from its [road running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") counterpart, the [10K run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10K_run "10K run"), by referring to the distance in metres rather than kilometres.

The 10,000 metres is the longest standard track event, approximately equivalent to 6 miles 376 yards or 32,808 feet 5 inches.

[![Image 88](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9d/Taisto_M%C3%A4ki_sets_10%2C000_m_world_record.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taisto_M%C3%A4ki_sets_10,000_m_world_record.jpeg)

[Taisto Mäki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taisto_M%C3%A4ki "Taisto Mäki") from [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland") breaks the 30-minute barrier in [Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki "Helsinki") on 17 September 1939.

Added to the Olympic programme in 1912, athletes from Finland, nicknamed the "[Flying Finns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_Finn "Flying Finn")", dominated the event until the late 1940s. In the 1960s, African runners began to come to the fore.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_m#cite_note-1) In 1988, the women's competition debuted in the Olympic Games.

Official records are kept for outdoor 10,000-metre track events. The world record for men is held by [Joshua Cheptegei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Cheptegei "Joshua Cheptegei") of [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") in 26:11.00, set in [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia "Valencia"), Spain on 7 October 2020. For women, the world record is held by [Beatrice Chebet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet "Beatrice Chebet") of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), in 28:54.14, set in Eugene, Oregon, on 25 May 2024.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_m#cite_note-2)

The 10,000 metres demands exceptional levels of aerobic endurance, and elite athletes typically train in excess of 160 km (100 miles) a week.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_m#cite_note-3)

## 6 miles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=10,000_metres&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: 6 miles")]

10,000 metres is the slightly longer metric derivative of the 6-mile (9,656.1-metre) run, an event common in countries when they were using the [imperial measurement system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_units "Imperial units"). 6 miles was used in the [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_Commonwealth_Games "Athletics at the Commonwealth Games") until 1966 and was a [championship in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Outdoor_Track_and_Field_Championships "USA Outdoor Track and Field Championships") in non-Olympic years from 1953 to 1973. It is 24 laps around a 1⁄4-mile (402 m; 440 yd; 1,320 ft) track.

**Nairobi** ( [_ny-ROH-bee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")) (_Jiji kuu la Nairobi_, in [Swahili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_language "Swahili language")), is the [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city "Capital city") and largest city of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), located in the south-central part of the country. As of 2026, it has a population of 5.6 million and a metropolitan population of 15.95 million,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-Africapolis2025-5) making it the [8th most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Africa_by_population "List of cities in Africa by population") in [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") and the 4th most populous metropolitan area. The city goes beyond its borders and has expanded into neighbouring counties, making it the 4th largest metropolitan area in Africa.

Nicknamed the "Green City under the Sun", Nairobi is uniquely notable for being the only capital city in the world that hosts a [national park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_National_Park "Nairobi National Park") within its boundaries. Its name originates from the [Maasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_language "Maasai language") phrase _Enkare Nyirobi_, meaning "place of cool waters".

As the national capital, Nairobi is home to the [Kenyan Parliament Buildings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_Buildings_(Kenya) "Parliament Buildings (Kenya)"), the [State House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_House,_Nairobi "State House, Nairobi") and the [Supreme Court Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Kenya "Supreme Court of Kenya"). It is the major financial and economic hub of [East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa "East Africa"), hosting thousands of Kenyan businesses and international companies and organisations, including the [United Nations Environment Programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Environment_Programme "United Nations Environment Programme") (UN Environment) and the [United Nations Office at Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Office_at_Nairobi "United Nations Office at Nairobi") (UNON). The [Nairobi Securities Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_Securities_Exchange "Nairobi Securities Exchange") (NSE) is one of the largest [stock exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_exchange "Stock exchange") in Africa and the second-oldest exchange on the continent. It is Africa's fourth-largest stock exchange by trading volume, capable of processing 10 million trades a day. Nairobi is considered a [global city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_city "Global city") and was ranked as a "Beta World City" by the [Globalisation and World Cities Research Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization_and_World_Cities_Research_Network "Globalization and World Cities Research Network") as of 2024.

Nairobi was founded in 1898 by colonial authorities in [British East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_Africa "British East Africa"), as a rail depot on the [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#Railroad "Uganda")–[Kenya Railway.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rail_transport_in_Kenya "Rail transport in Kenya") The authorities favoured it as an ideal resting place due to its [high elevation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montane_ecosystems "Montane ecosystems"), [temperate climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperate_climate "Temperate climate"), and adequate water supply.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-Greenway2-9) The town quickly grew to replace [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa") as the capital of Kenya in 1907.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-10)

After independence in 1963, Nairobi became the capital of the [Republic of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-11) During Kenya's early period, the city became a centre for the [coffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee "Coffee"), [tea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tea "Tea") and [sisal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisal "Sisal") industries.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-13) Successive post-independence governments have built and turned Nairobi into a modern metropolitan city with a diverse population and a growing economy.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-14)

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Nairobi_18_99.jpg/250px-Nairobi_18_99.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nairobi_18_99.jpg)

Nairobi in 1899

The site of Nairobi was originally a swamp land occupied by a [pastoralist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism "Pastoralism") people, the [Maasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people "Maasai people"), the long-distance trader community, [Akamba People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamba_people "Kamba people"), as well as the [agriculturalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculturalist "Agriculturalist")[Kikuyu people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people "Kikuyu people").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-ReferenceB-15) The name Nairobi comes from the [Maasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_language "Maasai language") expression meaning 'cool waters'. referring to the cold water stream which flowed through the area.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-16) With the arrival of the [Uganda Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Railway "Uganda Railway"), the site was identified by [Sir George Whitehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Whitehouse "George Whitehouse") for a store depot, shunting ground and camping ground for the [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indians_in_Kenya "Indians in Kenya") labourers working on the railway.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-Anne-Marie_Deisser_2016,_p.76-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-18)

Whitehouse, chief engineer of the railway, favoured the site as an ideal resting place due to its high elevation, temperate climate, adequate water supply and being situated before the steep ascent of the [Limuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limuru "Limuru")[escarpments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escarpments "Escarpments").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-Anne-Marie_Deisser_2016,_p.76-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-19) His choice was criticised by officials within the [Protectorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_Protectorate "East Africa Protectorate") government who felt the site was too flat, poorly drained and relatively infertile.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-ReferenceB-15)

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/The_entrance_to_the_Nairobi_Railway_Station_in_1899.jpg/250px-The_entrance_to_the_Nairobi_Railway_Station_in_1899.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_entrance_to_the_Nairobi_Railway_Station_in_1899.jpg)

The entrance to Nairobi railway station in 1899

In the pre-colonial era, the people of modern Kenya mostly lived in villages amongst their tribes and cultural groups, where they had rulers within their communities rather than one singular government or leader.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-20)

In 1898, Arthur Church was commissioned to design the first town layout for the railway depot. It constituted two streets – [Victoria Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mboya_Street "Tom Mboya Street") and [Station Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moi_Avenue_(Nairobi) "Moi Avenue (Nairobi)"), ten avenues, staff quarters and an Indian commercial area.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-Anne-Marie_Deisser_2016,_p.76-17) The railway arrived at Nairobi on 30 May 1899, and soon Nairobi replaced Machakos as the headquarters of the provincial administration for the Ukamba province.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-22)

On the arrival of the railway, Whitehouse remarked that "Nairobi itself will in the course of the next two years become a large and flourishing place and already there are many applications for sites for hotels, shops and houses."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-Anne-Marie_Deisser_2016,_p.76-17) The town's early years were however beset with problems of [malaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaria "Malaria") leading to at least one attempt to have the town moved.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-23) In the early 1900s, Bazaar Street, now Biashara Street, was completely rebuilt after an outbreak of [plague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubonic_plague "Bubonic plague") and the burning of the original town.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-24)

Between 1902 and 1910, the town's population rose from 5,000 to 16,000 and grew around [administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_administration "Public administration") and tourism, initially in the form of [big game hunting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_game_hunting "Big game hunting").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-Sana_Aiyar_2015,_p.42-25) In 1907, Nairobi replaced [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa") as the capital of the East Africa Protectorate.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-26) In 1919, Nairobi was declared to be a municipality.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-28)

In 1921, Nairobi had 24,000 residents, of which circa 12,000 were native Africans.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-ReferenceA-29) The next decade saw growth in native African communities in Nairobi, and they began to constitute a majority for the first time.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-ReferenceA-29) This growth caused planning issues, described by Thorntorn White and his planning team as the "Nairobi Problem".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-30) In February 1926, colonial officer Eric Dutton passed through Nairobi on his way to [Mount Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya "Mount Kenya"), and said of the city:

> Maybe one day Nairobi will be laid out with tarred roads, with avenues of flowering trees, flanked by noble buildings; with open spaces and stately squares; a cathedral worthy of faith and country; museums and art; theatres and public offices. And it is fair to say that the Government and the Municipality have already bravely tackled the problem and that a town-plan ambitious enough to turn Nairobi into a thing of beauty has been slowly worked out, and much has already been done. But until that plan has borne fruit, Nairobi must remain what she was then, a slatternly creature, unfit to queen it over so lovely a country.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-Dutton-31)

After [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), continuous expansion of the city angered both the indigenous [Maasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people "Maasai people") and [Kikuyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people "Kikuyu people").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-32) This led to the [Mau Mau Uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_Uprising "Mau Mau Uprising") in the 1950s, and the [Lancaster House Conferences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancaster_House_Conferences_(Kenya) "Lancaster House Conferences (Kenya)"), which initiated a transition to Kenyan independence in 1963.

In the spring of 1950, the East African Trades Union Congress (EAUTC) led a [nine-day general strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_Nairobi_general_strike "1950 Nairobi general strike") in the city.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-cotu-kenya-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-libcom-34)

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/COLLECTIE_TROPENMUSEUM_Zicht_op_Nairobi_met_op_de_voorgrond_het_stadspark_met_tribune_TMnr_20014416.jpg/250px-COLLECTIE_TROPENMUSEUM_Zicht_op_Nairobi_met_op_de_voorgrond_het_stadspark_met_tribune_TMnr_20014416.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:COLLECTIE_TROPENMUSEUM_Zicht_op_Nairobi_met_op_de_voorgrond_het_stadspark_met_tribune_TMnr_20014416.jpg)

Nairobi in 1973

Nairobi remained Kenya's capital after independence, and its continued rapid growth put pressure on the city's infrastructure, with power cuts and [water shortages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_scarcity "Water scarcity") becoming a common occurrence.

In September 1973, the [Kenyatta International Conference Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyatta_International_Conference_Centre "Kenyatta International Conference Centre") (KICC) was opened to the public. The 28-story building at the time was designed by the Norwegian architect Karl Henrik Nøstvik and Kenyan David Mutiso. It is the only building within the city with a helipad that is open to the public. Of the buildings built in the Seventies, the KICC was the most eco-friendly and most environmentally conscious structure. Its main frame was constructed with locally available materials like gravel, sand, cement and wood, and it had wide open spaces which allowed for natural aeration and lighting. Cuboids made up the plenary hall, the tower consisted of a cylinder composed of several cuboids, and the amphitheatre and helipad both resembled cones. The tower was built around a concrete core, and it had no walls but glass windows, which allowed for maximum natural lighting. It had the largest halls in eastern and central Africa.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-35)

In 1972, the [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank") approved funds for further expansion of the then Nairobi Airport (now [Jomo Kenyatta International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta_International_Airport "Jomo Kenyatta International Airport")), including a new international and domestic passenger terminal building, the airport's first dedicated cargo and freight terminal, new taxiways, associated aprons, internal roads, car parks, police and fire stations, a State Pavilion, airfield and roadway lighting, fire hydrant system, water, electrical, telecommunications and sewage systems, a dual carriageway passenger access road, security, drainage and the building of the main access road to the airport (Airport South Road). The cost of the project was more than US$29 million, US$111.8 million in 2013 dollars.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-nairobiairport-36) On 14 March 1978, construction of the terminal building was completed on the other side of the airport's single runway and opened by President [Jomo Kenyatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta "Jomo Kenyatta") less than five months before his death. The airport was renamed Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in memory of its first president.

The United States Embassy, then located in downtown Nairobi, was bombed in August 1998 by [Al-Qaeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda "Al-Qaeda") and the [Egyptian Islamic Jihad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_Islamic_Jihad "Egyptian Islamic Jihad"), as one of a series of [US embassy bombings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_United_States_embassy_bombings "1998 United States embassy bombings"). It is now the site of a memorial park.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-37)

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Nairobi_Skyline_from_BBC_Studios.jpg/250px-Nairobi_Skyline_from_BBC_Studios.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nairobi_Skyline_from_BBC_Studios.jpg)

Nairobi showing Fedha Towers, ICEA Building, the Nairobi Safari Club and Anniversary Towers

In November 2012, President [Mwai Kibaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mwai_Kibaki "Mwai Kibaki") opened the KES 31 billion Thika Superhighway. This mega-project in Kenya started in 2009 and ended in 2011. It involved expanding the four-lane carriageway to eight lanes, building underpasses, providing interchanges at roundabouts, erecting flyovers and building underpasses to ease congestion. The 50.4-kilometre road was built in three phases: Uhuru Highway to Muthaiga Roundabout; Muthaiga Roundabout to [Kenyatta University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyatta_University "Kenyatta University") and; Kenyatta University to [Thika Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thika_Town_Constituency "Thika Town Constituency").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-38)

In May 2017, President [Uhuru Kenyatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uhuru_Kenyatta "Uhuru Kenyatta") inaugurated the Standard Gauge Railway, which connects Nairobi to Mombasa.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-39) It was primarily built by a Chinese firm with about 90% of total funding from China and about 10% from the Kenyan government. A second phase is also being built, which will link [Naivasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naivasha "Naivasha") to the existing route and also the [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") border.

In August 2020, Nairobi County Assembly Speaker [Beatrice Elachi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Elachi "Beatrice Elachi") resigned.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-1R-40) In December 2020, recently elected[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-41) Nairobi County Assembly Speaker Benson Mutura was sworn in as acting Nairobi Governor four days after the previous Nairobi Governor [Mike Sonko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Sonko "Mike Sonko") was impeached and removed from office.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-nodeputy-42) At the time of Mutura's swearing in as acting Governor, which he will hold for at least 60 days, Nairobi did not have a Deputy Governor as well.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-nodeputy-42) Nairobi has seen several major infrastructure projects in the 2020s. The Nairobi Expressway, completed in 2022, was developed to reduce traffic congestion along Mombasa Road.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-43) In 2021, the Green Park Bus Terminal, part of efforts to improve public transport, began operations.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-44) In line with the Kenyan government's Affordable Housing Program, various housing developments are underway to accommodate the city's growing population.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-45)

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Nairobi%2C_Kenya.JPG/250px-Nairobi%2C_Kenya.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nairobi,_Kenya.JPG)

A satellite view of Nairobi, 2004

Nairobi is situated at [1°09′S 36°39′E / 1.150°S 36.650°E](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Nairobi&params=1_09_S_36_39_E_&title=Nairobi%2C+Kenya) and [1°27′S 37°06′E / 1.450°S 37.100°E](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Nairobi&params=1_27_S_37_06_E_&title=Nairobi%2C+Kenya) and occupies 696 square kilometres (270 sq mi).

Nairobi is situated between the cities of Kampala and Mombasa. As Nairobi is adjacent to the eastern edge of the [Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Rift_Valley "Kenya Rift Valley"), minor earthquakes and tremors occasionally occur. The [Ngong Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngong_Hills "Ngong Hills"), located to the west of the city, are the most prominent geographical feature of the Nairobi area. [Mount Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya "Mount Kenya") is situated north of Nairobi, and [Mount Kilimanjaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kilimanjaro "Mount Kilimanjaro") is towards the south-east.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-46)

The [Nairobi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_River "Nairobi River") and its [tributaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tributary "Tributary") traverse through the Nairobi County and join the larger River Athi on the eastern edge of the county.

[Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") laureate [Wangari Maathai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wangari_Maathai "Wangari Maathai") fought fiercely to save the indigenous [Karura Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karura_Forest "Karura Forest") in northern Nairobi, which was under threat of being replaced by housing and other infrastructure.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-47)

Nairobi's western suburbs stretch all the way from the Kenyatta National Hospital in the south to the UN headquarters at Gigiri suburb in the north, a distance of about 20 kilometres (12 mi). The city is centred on the City Square, which is located in the Central Business District. The [Kenyan Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_of_Kenya "National Assembly of Kenya") buildings, the [Holy Family Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_Basilica_of_the_Holy_Family,_Nairobi "Cathedral Basilica of the Holy Family, Nairobi"), Nairobi City Hall, Nairobi Law Courts, and the [Kenyatta Convention Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyatta_International_Convention_Centre "Kenyatta International Convention Centre") all surround the square.

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Rain_clouds_forming_Nairobi.jpg/250px-Rain_clouds_forming_Nairobi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rain_clouds_forming_Nairobi.jpg)

Rain clouds over estates, December 2019

Under the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"), Nairobi has a [subtropical highland climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") (Cwb). At 1,795 metres (5,889 ft) above sea level, evenings may be cool, especially in the June/July season, when the temperature can drop to 9°C (48°F). The sunniest and warmest part of the year is from December to March, when temperatures average in the high-twenties [Celsius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celsius "Celsius") during the day. The mean maximum temperature for this period is 28°C (82°F).[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-48)

There are rainy seasons, but rainfall can be moderate. The cloudiest part of the year is just after the first rainy season, when, until September, conditions are usually overcast with drizzle. As Nairobi is situated close to the equator, the differences between the seasons are minimal. The seasons are referred to as the [wet season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_season "Wet season") and [dry season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_season "Dry season"). The timing of sunrise and sunset varies little throughout the year for the same reason.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-49)

### Nairobi metropolitan region

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nairobi&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Nairobi metropolitan region")]

Nairobi is found within the Greater Nairobi Metropolitan region, which consists of parts of 5 out of 47 counties in Kenya, which generate about 40% of the entire nation's GDP as per 2022 data by the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-55)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-56) Nairobi County on its own contributes to 27.5% of the country's GDP according to the same report while [Kiambu county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiambu_County "Kiambu County") comes second with 5.9%.

### Districts and neighbourhoods

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nairobi&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Districts and neighbourhoods")]

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Nairobi_South.jpg/250px-Nairobi_South.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nairobi_South.jpg)

Nairobi southern suburbs,2003

Nairobi is divided into a series of constituencies, with each being represented by members of Parliament in the National Assembly. The initial constituencies before the 2010 constitution which led to the county electoral boundaries being redrawn were: Makadara, Kamukunji, Starehe, [Langata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langata "Langata"), Dagoretti, [Westlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlands,_Nairobi "Westlands, Nairobi"), Kasarani, and [Embakasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embakasi "Embakasi").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-57) The new electoral boundaries after this were revised to Embakasi North, Embakasi South, Embakasi Central, Embakasi East, Embakasi West, Makadara, Kamukunji, Starehe, Mathare, Westlands, Dagoretti North, Dagoretti South, Langata, Kibra, Ruaraka, Roysambu and Kasarani.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-58)

The main administrative divisions of Nairobi are Central, Dagoretti, [Embakasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embakasi "Embakasi"), Kasarani, [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera"), Makadara, Pumwani, and [Westlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlands,_Nairobi "Westlands, Nairobi"). Most of the upmarket suburbs are situated to the west and north-central of Nairobi, where most European settlers resided during the colonial times AKA 'Ubabini'.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-59) These include [Karen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen,_Kenya "Karen, Kenya"), [Langata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langata "Langata"), [Lavington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavington,_Nairobi "Lavington, Nairobi"), [Gigiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigiri "Gigiri"), [Muthaiga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muthaiga "Muthaiga"), Brookside, Spring Valley, Loresho, [Kilimani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimani "Kilimani"), Kileleshwa, Hurlingham, [Runda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runda "Runda"), [Kitisuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitisuru "Kitisuru"), Nyari, Kyuna, [Lower Kabete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Kabete "Lower Kabete"), Westlands, and Highridge, although Kangemi, Kawangware, and [Dagoretti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagoretti "Dagoretti") are lower income areas close to these affluent suburbs. The city's colonial past is commemorated by many English place-names.

Most lower-middle and upper-middle income neighbourhoods are located in the north-central areas, such as Highridge, Parklands, Ngara, Pangani, and areas to the southwest and southeast of the metropolitan area near the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. The most notable ones include Avenue Park, Fedha, Pipeline, Donholm, Greenfields, Nyayo, Taasia, Baraka, Nairobi West, Madaraka, Siwaka, South B, South C, Mugoya, Riverbank, Hazina, Buru Buru, Uhuru, Harambee Civil Servants', Akiba, Kimathi, Pioneer, and Koma Rock to the centre-east and Kasarani to the northeast area, among others.

The low and lower-income estates are located mainly in far eastern Nairobi. These include, Umoja, Kariokor, [Dandora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dandora "Dandora"), [Kariobangi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kariobangi "Kariobangi"), [Kayole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kayole "Kayole"),Njiru, Chokaa, [Ruai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruai "Ruai"), [Kamulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamulu "Kamulu"), [Embakasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embakasi "Embakasi"), and [Huruma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huruma "Huruma"). Kitengela suburb, though located further southeast, Ongata Rongai and Kiserian further southwest, and Ngong/Embulbul suburbs, also known as 'Diaspora' to the far west are considered part of the Greater Nairobi Metropolitan area. More than 90% of Nairobi residents work within the Nairobi Metropolitan area, in the formal and informal sectors. Many [Somali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somali_people "Somali people") immigrants have also settled in [Eastleigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastleigh,_Nairobi "Eastleigh, Nairobi"), nicknamed "Little [Mogadishu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mogadishu "Mogadishu")".[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-60) A complete list of Nairobi postal codes by area and constituency is available online.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-61)

The [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera") slum in Nairobi is claimed by the Kenyan government to have a population of 185,777.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-62) However, non-governmental sources generally estimate the slum to have a population of 500,000 to 1,000,000, depending on what areas are defined as comprising Kibera.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-63)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-64)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-65)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-66)

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Central_park_.jpg/250px-Central_park_.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Central_park_.jpg)

Central Park

Nairobi has many parks and open spaces throughout the city. Much of the city has dense tree-cover and plenty of green spaces.

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/A_lone_giraffe_in_Nairobi_National_Park.jpg/250px-A_lone_giraffe_in_Nairobi_National_Park.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_lone_giraffe_in_Nairobi_National_Park.jpg)

A giraffe at [Nairobi National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_National_Park "Nairobi National Park"), with Nairobi's skyline in background

The most famous park in Nairobi is [Uhuru Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uhuru_Park "Uhuru Park"). The park borders the central business district and the neighbourhood Upper Hill. Uhuru (_Freedom_ in [Swahili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_language "Swahili language")) Park is a centre for outdoor speeches, services, and rallies. The park was to be built over by former President [Daniel arap Moi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_arap_Moi "Daniel arap Moi"), who wanted the 62-storey headquarters of his party, the [Kenya African National Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_African_National_Union "Kenya African National Union"), situated in the park.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-67) However, the park was saved following a campaign by [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") winner [Wangari Maathai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wangar%C4%A9_Maathai "Wangarĩ Maathai").

Central Park is adjacent to Uhuru Park, and includes a memorial for [Jomo Kenyatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta "Jomo Kenyatta"), the first president of Kenya, and the Moi Monument, built in 1988 to commemorate the second president's first decade in power.

Both Uhuru Park and Central Park were renovated by the-then Nairobi Metropolitan Services (NMS) together with the [Kenya Defence Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Defence_Forces "Kenya Defence Forces").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-68) The process started in September 2023 and incorporates several key elements, including a cascading water feature, upgraded sanitation facilities, a skateboarding zone, and pedestrian-friendly paths.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-69)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-70) It also highlights statues of native wildlife, carefully groomed lawns, thriving trees, improved footpaths, and expanded green zones.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-71) A botanical section has been established as well, showcasing a diverse collection of flowers and plant species to reflect Kenya's abundant floral heritage.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-74)

[Jeevanjee Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeevanjee_Gardens "Jeevanjee Gardens") is located within the Central Business District and is easily accessible via foot, private vehicles and public transport.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-75) Among Nairobi's most historic and oldest public green spaces, the park was created in the early 20th century by Asian industrialist [A.M. Jeevanjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alibhai_Mulla_Jeevanjee "Alibhai Mulla Jeevanjee").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-76)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-77)

The John Michuki Memorial Park is situated along the [Nairobi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_River "Nairobi River"), stretching from Globe Cinema Roundabout to Museum Bridge. It was previously known as the Mazingira Park, and was reopened in August 2020 by President [Uhuru Kenyatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uhuru_Kenyatta "Uhuru Kenyatta") after renovation by the [Kenya Forest Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Forest_Service "Kenya Forest Service"), Kenya Forestry Research Institute (KEFRI), and [National Environment Management Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Environment_Management_Authority_of_Kenya "National Environment Management Authority of Kenya") (NEMA).[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-78)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-79) The park is named in tribute to the late former Cabinet Minister [John Michuki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Michuki "John Michuki"), who was instrumental in the restoration of the Nairobi River and its surroundings during his time as Minister for Environment.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-80)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-81)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-82)

[Nairobi Arboretum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_Arboretum "Nairobi Arboretum"), founded in 1907 by E. Batiscombe as a trial site for forestry tree species, is a 30-hectare botanical reserve that hosts more than 350 types of trees and functions as both a leisure destination and a research hub.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-83) It is located near the [State House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_House,_Nairobi "State House, Nairobi").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-84)

[Karura Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karura_Forest "Karura Forest"), the city-based nature reserve, features nature trails, picnic spots, caves and waterfalls. It is an excellent destination for birdwatching as the area is home to over 200 documented bird species. While strolling along the trails, visitors may also catch glimpses of monkeys and bushbucks.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-85)

Nairobi City Park, is located between Forest Road and Limuru Road. As one of Nairobi's oldest and most expansive urban green spaces, spanning over 60 hectares, City Park holds considerable ecological value. It preserves one of the last remaining patches of indigenous forest that once blanketed the region. The park is home to a rich array of biodiversity, including [Sykes' monkeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sykes'_monkey "Sykes' monkey"), various bird species, and a wide assortment of native plant life.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-86) City Park also carries historical weight, because it hosts cemeteries for veterans of World War I and II and is the final resting place of notable figures such as freedom fighter [Pio Gama Pinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pio_Gama_Pinto "Pio Gama Pinto") and former Vice President [Joseph Murumbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Murumbi "Joseph Murumbi"), whose memorial garden is located within the park grounds.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-87)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-88)

Oloolua Nature Trail is situated in [Oloolua Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oloolua_Forest "Oloolua Forest") in the [Karen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen,_Kenya "Karen, Kenya") area of Nairobi. It is under the management of Kenya Institute of Primate Research (KIPRE) and provides opportunities for nature walks, bird watching, and enjoying the natural environment.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-89) Key attractions include a 37-meter deep natural cave that was historically used by Mau Mau fighters, a beautiful waterfall draining into the [Mbagathi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mbagathi_River "Mbagathi River"), a bamboo resting point, and a papyrus swamp.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-90)

[Ngong Road Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngong_Forest "Ngong Forest") Sanctuary contains winding walking and jogging paths that pass through tall trees inhabited by various bird species, with occasional sightings of [Sykes monkeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sykes'_monkey "Sykes' monkey"). The area also includes a picnic site and a playground for children. Additionally, Ngong Road Forest has cycling trails that run beneath the indigenous tree canopy.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-91)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-92)

Langata Botanical Gardens is a private recreational garden located along Langata South Road. The area comprises numerous native trees, expansive well-maintained lawns, and a lagoon inhabited by a diverse range of fish species.

Other private botanical gardens include Maarifa Park Botanical Garden, located in Kitisuru[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-93) and the Five Senses Botanical Gardens by Enaki, located in Nyari, Nairobi.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-94)

Nairobi Botanical Gardens is located within the [National Museum of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museums_of_Kenya "National Museums of Kenya"). The Nairobi Botanical Gardens are organized into themed sections, each highlighting a particular conservation topic. For example, the Children's Garden focuses on botany and habitat, providing a space where visitors can learn about indigenous and exotic plants while enjoying open lawns and an outdoor amphitheatre. Other sections include the Grass Gardens, which showcase important food and beverage plants, the Herbal Garden dedicated to medicinal and food plants, the Succulent Gardens illustrating plant adaptations to arid environments, the Quarry Garden transformed from a former quarry, and the Memorial Garden commemorating World War II with symbolic plants and a water feature.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-95)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-96)

The [August 7th Memorial Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_7th_Memorial_Park,_Kenya "August 7th Memorial Park, Kenya") is located at the site of the [1998 US Embassy bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_United_States_embassy_bombings "1998 United States embassy bombings") and features a green space that offers tranquility.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-97)

### Threats to public spaces

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nairobi&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Threats to public spaces")]

The colonial 1948 Master Plan for Nairobi still acts as the governing mechanism when it comes to making decisions related to urban planning. The Master Plan at the time, which was designed for 250,000 people, allocated 28% of Nairobi's land to public space, but because of rapid population growth, much of the vitality of public spaces within the city are increasingly threatened.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-:0-98) City Park, the only natural park in Nairobi, for example, was originally 60 ha (150 acres), but has since lost approximately 20 ha (50 acres) of land to private development through squatting and illegal alienation which began in the 1980s.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-:0-98)

Greater Nairobi Metropolitan Region, consisting of [Nairobi City County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_City_County "Nairobi City County") (red), [Kajiado County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kajiado_County "Kajiado County") (orange), [Machakos County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machakos_County "Machakos County") (green), and [Kiambu County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiambu_County "Kiambu County") (blue)

The City of Nairobi has the status of a full [administrative county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counties_of_Kenya "Counties of Kenya").

Initially, Nairobi was one of the eight provinces in Kenya before 2013. The Nairobi province differed in several ways from other Kenyan regions. Nairobi Province was not divided into "districts" until 2007, when three districts were created. In 2010, along with the new constitution, Nairobi was renamed a county and consolidated into a [city-county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_and_towns_in_Kenya_by_population "List of cities and towns in Kenya by population"). The county is entirely urban. It had only one local council, [Nairobi City Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_City_Council "Nairobi City Council"), which was replaced by [Nairobi City County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_City_County "Nairobi City County") after the new constitution was effected in March 2013.

Nairobi County has 17 constituencies. Constituency name may differ from division name, such that Starehe Constituency is equal to Central Division, Lang'ata Constituency to Kibera division, and Kamukunji Constituency to Pumwani Division in terms of boundaries.

Nairobi is divided into 17 [constituencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divisions_of_Kenya "Divisions of Kenya") and 85 [wards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locations_of_Kenya "Locations of Kenya"),[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-test-99) mostly named after residential estates. Kibera Division, for example, includes [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera"), Kenya's largest slum, and the affluent estates of [Karen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen,_Kenya "Karen, Kenya") and [Langata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langata "Langata").

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Nairobi_economic_capital_of_africa.jpg/250px-Nairobi_economic_capital_of_africa.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nairobi_economic_capital_of_africa.jpg)

Nairobi is a major financial capital of Africa, and one of the most modern cities in Africa.

Nairobi is home to the [Nairobi Securities Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_Securities_Exchange "Nairobi Securities Exchange") (NSE), one of Africa's largest [stock exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_exchange "Stock exchange"). The NSE was officially recognised as an overseas stock exchange by the [London Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Stock_Exchange "London Stock Exchange") in 1953. The exchange is Africa's fourth largest in terms of trading volumes, and fifth largest in terms of Market Capitalization as a percentage of GDP.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-101)

Nairobi is the regional headquarters of several international companies and organisations. In 2007, [General Electric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric "General Electric"), [Young & Rubicam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_&_Rubicam "Young & Rubicam"), [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google"), [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Coca-Cola_Company "The Coca-Cola Company"), [IBM Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM"), and [Cisco Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco_Systems "Cisco Systems") relocated their African headquarters to the city.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-102)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-103) The [United Nations Office at Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Office_at_Nairobi "United Nations Office at Nairobi") hosts [UN Environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Environment_Programme "United Nations Environment Programme") and [UN-Habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Human_Settlements_Programme "United Nations Human Settlements Programme") headquarters.

Several of Africa's largest companies are headquartered in Nairobi. [Safaricom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safaricom "Safaricom"), the largest company in Kenya by assets and profitability is headquartered in Nairobi, KenGen, which is the largest African stock outside [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-104) is based in the city. [Kenya Airways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Airways "Kenya Airways"), Africa's fourth largest airline, uses Nairobi's [Jomo Kenyatta International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jomo_Kenyatta_International_Airport "Jomo Kenyatta International Airport") as a hub.

Nairobi has not been left behind by the FinTech phenomenon that has taken over worldwide. It has produced a couple of tech firms like Craft Silicon,[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-105) Kangai Technologies,[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-106) Jambo Pay[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-107) and Hostraha Limited.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-108) which have been in the forefront of technology,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-109) innovation and cloud based computing services. Their products are widely used and have considerable market share presence within Kenya and outside its borders.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-110)

Goods manufactured in Nairobi include clothing, textiles, building materials, [processed foods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Processed_food "Processed food"), beverages, and cigarettes.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-111)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-112) Several foreign companies have factories based in and around the city. These include [Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodyear_Tire_and_Rubber_Company "Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company"), [General Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Motors "General Motors"), [Toyota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota "Toyota"), and [The Coca-Cola Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Coca-Cola_Company "The Coca-Cola Company").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Nairobi has a large [tourist industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourist_industry "Tourist industry"), being both a tourist destination and a transport hub.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-113)

### Central Business District (CBD)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nairobi&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Central Business District (CBD)")]

Nairobi has grown around its [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district"), usually referred to colloquially as "the CBD". This takes a pentagonal shape, around the Uhuru Highway, Haile Selassie Avenue, Moi Avenue, and University Way. It features many of Nairobi's important buildings, including the City Hall and Parliament Building. The city square is also located within the perimeter.

Most of the skyscrapers in this region are the headquarters of businesses and corporations, such as I&M and the [Kenyatta International Conference Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyatta_International_Conference_Centre "Kenyatta International Conference Centre"). The [United States Embassy bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_United_States_embassy_bombings "1998 United States embassy bombings") took place in this district, prompting the building of a new embassy building in the suburbs.

In 2011, the city was considered to have about 4 million residents. A large beautification project took place in the Central Business District, as the city prepared to host the 2006 Afri-Cities summit. Iconic buildings such as the [Kenyatta International Conference Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyatta_International_Conference_Centre "Kenyatta International Conference Centre") had their exteriors cleaned and repainted.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-114)

Nairobi downtown area or central business district is bordered to the southwest by [Uhuru Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uhuru_Park "Uhuru Park") and Central Park. The [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa") to [Kampala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala "Kampala") railway runs to the southeast of the district.

Prism Tower in Upper Hill

Two areas outside the Central Business District that are seeing growth in companies and office space are [Upper Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Hill,_Nairobi "Upper Hill, Nairobi"), which is located, approximately 4 km (2.5 mi) from the Central Business District and [Westlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlands,_Nairobi "Westlands, Nairobi"), about the same distance from the city centre.

Companies that have moved from the Central Business District to Upper Hill include [Citibank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citibank "Citibank"), and in 2007 [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Coca-Cola_Company "The Coca-Cola Company") began construction of their [East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa "East Africa") and Central African headquarters in Upper Hill,[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-115) cementing the district as the preferred location for office space in Nairobi. The largest office development in this area is [UAP Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UAP_Tower "UAP Tower"), completed in 2015 and opened for business in July 2016.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-116) It is a 33-storey tower 163 meters high. The World Bank and [International Finance Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Finance_Corporation "International Finance Corporation"), part of the World Bank Group, are also located in Upper Hill at the Delta Center, Menegai Road. Earlier on, they were located in the Hill Park Building and CBA Building respectively, both in Upper Hill, and prior to that in View Park towers in the Central Business District.

To accommodate the large demand for floor space in Nairobi, various commercial projects are being constructed. New business parks are being built in the city, including the flagship [Nairobi Business Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_Business_Park "Nairobi Business Park").

### Construction boom and real estate development projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nairobi&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Construction boom and real estate development projects")]

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/A_view_of_Nairobi_from_the_Kenyatta_International_Conference_Centre.jpg/250px-A_view_of_Nairobi_from_the_Kenyatta_International_Conference_Centre.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_view_of_Nairobi_from_the_Kenyatta_International_Conference_Centre.jpg)

A view of Nairobi from the [Kenyatta International Conference Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyatta_International_Conference_Centre "Kenyatta International Conference Centre")

Nairobi is undergoing a construction boom. Major real estate projects and skyscrapers are coming up in the city. Among them are the pinnacle twin towers which will tower at 314 m, [Britam Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britam_Tower "Britam Tower") (200 m), Avic International Africa headquarters (176 m), Prism tower (140 m), Pan Africa insurance towers, Pallazzo offices, and many other projects. Shopping malls are also being constructed like the recently completed Garden city Mall, Centum's [Two rivers Mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two_Rivers_Mall "Two Rivers Mall"), The Hub in Karen, Karen waterfront, Thika Greens, and the recently reconstructed Westgate Mall.

High-class residential apartments for living are coming up like Le Mac towers, a residential tower in Westlands Nairobi with 23 floors. Avic International is also putting up a total of four residential apartments on Waiyaki way: a 28-level tower, two 24-level towers, and a 25-level tower. Hotel towers are also being erected in the city.

Avic International is putting up a 30-level hotel tower of 141 m in the Westlands. The hotel tower will be operated by Marriot group. Jabavu limited is constructing a 35 floor hotel tower in Upper Hill which will be high over 140 metres in the city skyline. Arcon Group Africa has also announced plans to erect a skyscraper in Upper hill which will have 66 floors and tower over 290 metres, further cementing Upper hill as the preferred metropolis for multinational corporations launching their operations in the Kenyan capital.

As of 2024, Nairobi has an estimated population of 4.8 million, up from 4.3 million in 2019, making it the largest city in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). The city spans approximately 696 km², with a population density of about 6,900 inhabitants per km². Nairobi's demographics are characterized by a youthful and rapidly growing population, reflecting ongoing urbanization and migration trends.

Nairobi has experienced one of the highest growth rates of any city in Africa. Since its foundation in 1899, Nairobi has grown to become the second-largest city in the African Great Lakes, despite being one of the youngest cities in the region. The growth rate of Nairobi was estimated in 2023 to be 2.09% a year.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-119) It is estimated that Nairobi's population will reach 5 million people in 2025.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-120)

Given this high population growth, owing itself both to urban migration and high birth rates, the economy has yet to catch up. Unemployment is estimated at 5.5% within the city,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-121) mainly in the high-density, low-income areas of the city which can make them seem even denser than the higher-income neighbourhoods.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-122)

**Religion in Nairobi** is diverse but predominantly Christian. Approximately 88.85% of Nairobi's population identifies as [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"), with [Protestants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism") accounting for 31.34%, [Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") for 24.01%, and [Evangelicals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelicalism "Evangelicalism") for 20.70%. Other Christian groups include African Instituted Churches (7.08%), Other Christian denominations (5.19%), and a small [Orthodox Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodoxy "Eastern Orthodoxy") community (0.53%). [Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam "Islam") is the second-largest religion in the county, practiced by approximately 7.53% of residents. Nairobi also has the largest [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism") population in Kenya, with 38,141 adherents, accounting for approximately 63% of the national Hindu population. Smaller proportions of the population adhere to [traditional African religions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_African_religions "Traditional African religions") (0.16%), other religions (1.07%), or report [no religion or atheism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irreligion "Irreligion") (1.26%), with the remainder classified as don't know or not stated.

In the 2019 Census, Christianity was the most widely practiced religion in Nairobi, accounting for 89% of the population, of which the majority belong to Protestant and Evangelical churches. In 2019, Muslims were 7.6% of the population.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-125)

Nairobi is diverse in African cultures. As a cosmopolitan African city, it hosts all the diverse tribes that make up Kenya, and hosts a large immigrant population from other African countries.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-126)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-127)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-128)

Nairobi has two informal nicknames. The first is "The Green City in the Sun", which is derived from the city's foliage and warm climate.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-129) The second is the "Safari Capital of the World", which is used due to Nairobi's prominence as a hub for safari tourism.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-130)

In 2026, Nairobi made it to the final for the "World Capital of Kindness" competition, beaten only by San Donato Milanese, Italy (first place).

_[Kwani?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwani%3F "Kwani?")_ is Kenya's first literary journal and was established by writers living in Nairobi. Nairobi's publishing houses have also produced the works of some of Kenya's authors, including [Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C5%A9g%C4%A9_wa_Thiong'o "Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o") and [Meja Mwangi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meja_Mwangi "Meja Mwangi") who were part of post-colonial writing.

Many film makers also practice their craft out of Nairobi. Film-making is still young in the country, but people like producer Njeri Karago and director Judy Kibinge are paving the way for others.

Perhaps the most famous book and film set in Nairobi is _[Out of Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Out\_of\_Africa "Out of Africa")_. The book was written by [Karen Blixen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Blixen "Karen Blixen"), whose pseudonym was Isak Dinesen, and it is her account of living in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Karen Blixen lived in the Nairobi area from 1917 to 1931. The neighbourhood in which she lived, [Karen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen,_Kenya "Karen, Kenya"), is named after her.

In 1985, _[Out of Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Out\_of\_Africa\_(film) "Out of Africa (film)")_ was made into a film, directed by [Sydney Pollack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Pollack "Sydney Pollack"). The film won 28 awards, including seven [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). The popularity of the film prompted the opening of Nairobi's [Karen Blixen Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Blixen_Museum,_Kenya "Karen Blixen Museum, Kenya").

Nairobi is the setting of many of the novels of [Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C5%A9g%C4%A9_wa_Thiong'o "Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o"), Kenya's foremost writer.

Nairobi has been the set of several other [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States") and [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Film_Industry "British Film Industry") films. The most recent of these was _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_ (2005), a large part of which was filmed in the city. The story revolves around a British diplomat in Nairobi whose wife is murdered in northern Kenya. Much of the filming was in the [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera") slum.

Among the latest Kenyan actors in Hollywood who identify with Nairobi is [Lupita Nyong'o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupita_Nyong'o "Lupita Nyong'o"). Lupita received an Oscar award for [best supporting actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") in her role as Patsy in the film _[12 Years a Slave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12\_Years\_a\_Slave "12 Years a Slave")_ during the _[86th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/86th\_Academy\_Awards "86th Academy Awards")_ at the Dolby theatre in Los Angeles. Lupita is the daughter of Kenyan politician Peter Anyang' Nyong'o.

Most new Hollywood films are nowadays screened at Nairobi's cinemas. Up until the early 1990s, there were only a few film theatres and the repertoire was limited. There are also two [drive-in cinemas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drive-in_theater "Drive-in theater") in Nairobi.

In 2015 and 2016, Nairobi was the focus point for the American television series _[Sense8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")_ which shot its first and second seasons partly in the city. The TV series has high reviews in [The Internet Movie Database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Internet_Movie_Database "The Internet Movie Database") (IMDb).

In 2015 Nairobi was featured in the British thriller film _[Eye in the Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye\_in\_the\_Sky\_(2015\_film) "Eye in the Sky (2015 film)")_, which is a story about a lieutenant general and a colonel who faced political opposition after ordering a drone missile strike to take out a group of suicide bombers in Nairobi.

In 2017, the name "Nairobi" was taken as a code-name by a female main character in the famous Spanish TV series _[Money Heist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money\_Heist "Money Heist")_.

In Nairobi, there are a range of restaurants. Besides being home to _[nyama choma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyama\_choma "Nyama choma")_ which is a local term used to refer to roasted meat, there are American fast food restaurants such as [KFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KFC "KFC"), [Subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subway_(restaurant) "Subway (restaurant)"), [Domino's Pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domino's "Domino's"), [Pizza Hut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza_Hut "Pizza Hut"), [Hardee's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardee's "Hardee's") and [Burger King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burger_King "Burger King"), and the longer established South African chains, [Galito's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galito's "Galito's"), [Steers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steers_(restaurant) "Steers (restaurant)"), PizzaMojo, and [Spur Steak Ranches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spur_Steak_Ranches "Spur Steak Ranches").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-131)

Coffee houses, doubling up as restaurants and mostly frequented by the upper middle classes, such as Artcaffe [Nairobi Java House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_House "Java House") and Dormans, have become increasingly popular in recent days. Traditional food joints such as the popular K'osewe's in the city centre and Amaica, which specialize in African delicacies, are widespread.

The Kenchic franchise which specialized in old-school chicken and chips meals was popular, particularly among the lower classes and students, with restaurants all over the city and its suburbs. However, as of February 2016, Kenchic stopped operating its eatery business. Upscale restaurants often specialize in specific cuisines such as Italian, Lebanese, Ethiopian, and French, but are more likely to be found in five star hotels and the wealthier suburbs in the West and South of the city.

Nairobi has an annual restaurant week (NRW) at the beginning of the year, January–February. Nairobi's restaurants offer dining packages at reduced prices.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-132) NRW is managed by Eatout Kenya which is an online platform that lists and reviews restaurants in Nairobi, and provides a platform for Kenyan foodies to congregate and share.

Nairobi is the centre of Kenya's music scene. [Benga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benga_music "Benga music") is a Kenyan genre which was developed in Nairobi. The style is a fusion of [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") and [Luo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_(Kenya_and_Tanzania) "Luo (Kenya and Tanzania)") music forms. Mugithi is another popular genre in Kenya, with its origins in the central parts of the country. A majority of music videos of leading local musicians are also filmed in the city.

In the 1970s, Nairobi became the prominent centre for [music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music "Music") in the [African Great Lakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Great_Lakes "African Great Lakes"). During this period, Nairobi was established as a hub of [soukous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soukous "Soukous") music. This genre was originally developed in [Kinshasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinshasa "Kinshasa") and [Brazzaville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazzaville "Brazzaville"). After the political climate in the region [deteriorated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congo_Crisis "Congo Crisis"), many Congolese artists relocated to Nairobi. Artists such as [Orchestra Super Mazembe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Mazembe "Super Mazembe") moved from [Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo") to Nairobi and found great success.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-133)[Virgin records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_records "Virgin records") became aware of the popularity of the genre and signed recording contracts with several soukous artists.

More recently, Nairobi has become the centre of the [Kenyan hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_hip-hop "Kenyan hip-hop") scene. The genre has become very popular amongst local youth, and domestic musicians have become some of the most popular in the region.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-134) Successful artists based in Nairobi include [Jua Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jua_Cali "Jua Cali"), [Nonini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonini "Nonini"), [Camp Mulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Mulla "Camp Mulla"), [Juliani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juliani "Juliani"), [Eric Wainaina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Wainaina_(musician) "Eric Wainaina (musician)"), and [Nameless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Mathenge "David Mathenge"). Popular record labels include [Ogopa DJs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogopa_DJs "Ogopa DJs") and [Calif Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calif_Records "Calif Records").

Nairobi, including the coastal towns of Mombasa and Diani, have recently become the centre of [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") in Kenya, producing DJs as well as producers like [DJ Fita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Fita "DJ Fita").

Many nightclubs in and around the city have witnessed a growth in the population that exclusively listen to Electronic Dance Music, especially amongst the younger generations.[_[neutrality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Neutral\_point\_of\_view "Wikipedia:Neutral point of view")is [disputed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Nairobi# "Talk:Nairobi")_] Gospel music is also popular in Nairobi just as in the rest of Kenya, with gospel artists having a great impact in the mostly Christian city.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Musical group [Sauti Sol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauti_Sol "Sauti Sol") performed for U.S. President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") when he was in the city for the 2015 [Global Entrepreneurship Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Entrepreneurship_Summit "Global Entrepreneurship Summit").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-135)

Nairobi is the African Great Lakes region's sporting centre. Notable annual events staged in Nairobi include [Safari Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safari_Rally "Safari Rally"), [Safari Sevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safari_Sevens "Safari Sevens")[rugby union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union "Rugby union") tournament, and [Nairobi Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_Marathon "Nairobi Marathon").

The premier sports facility in Nairobi and generally in Kenya is the [Moi International Sports Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moi_International_Sports_Centre "Moi International Sports Centre") in the suburb of Kasarani. The complex was completed in 1987, and was used to host the 1987 [All Africa Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Africa_Games "All Africa Games"). The complex comprises a 60,000 seater stadium, the second largest in the African Great Lakes (after Tanzania's new national stadium), a 5,000 seater gymnasium, and a 2,000 seater aquatics centre.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-136) In 2029, the venue will host the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2029_World_Athletics_Championships "2029 World Athletics Championships"). It will be the first World Athletics Championships to be ever held in Africa.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-137)

The [Nyayo National Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyayo_National_Stadium "Nyayo National Stadium") is Nairobi's second largest stadium renowned for hosting global rugby event under the "Safaricom Sevens". Completed in 1983, the stadium has a capacity of 30,000.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-138) This stadium is primarily used for [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"). The facility is located close to the Central Business District, which makes it a convenient location for political gatherings.

[Nairobi City Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_City_Stadium "Nairobi City Stadium") is Nairobi's first stadium, and used for club football.

[Nairobi Gymkhana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_Gymkhana_Club "Nairobi Gymkhana Club") is the home of the [Kenyan cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_cricket_team "Kenyan cricket team"), and was a venue for the [2003 Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Cricket_World_Cup "2003 Cricket World Cup").

Ulinzi Sports Complex was officially opened by President Uhuru Kenyatta in 2022 after its construction that started in 2020.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-139) It has a capacity of 7,500, an 8-lane Athletics track, training grounds and an indoor arena.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-140)

Dandora Stadium, a 4,000 capacity stadium opened in 2024, hosts some of the top flight national league football tournaments. The stadium has seats in the VIP section and regular stands.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-141)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-142)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-143)

[Talanta Sports Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talanta_Sports_Stadium "Talanta Sports Stadium"), with a capacity of 60,000, is currently under construction with an estimated completion date of February 2026.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-144)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-145)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-146)

[Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") is the most popular sport in the city by viewership and participation. This is highlighted by the number of football clubs in the city, including [Kenyan Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Premier_League "Kenyan Premier League") sides [Gor Mahia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gor_Mahia_F.C. "Gor Mahia F.C."), [A.F.C. Leopards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.F.C._Leopards "A.F.C. Leopards") Sports Club, [Tusker F. C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tusker_F.C. "Tusker F.C.") and [Mathare United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathare_United_F.C. "Mathare United F.C.").

Kenya, together with Tanzania and Uganda will be cohosting the 2025 [CHAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Nations_Championship "African Nations Championship") competition.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-147)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-148) Also, the three countries will jointly host the 2027 [AFCON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa_Cup_of_Nations "Africa Cup of Nations") football competition.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-149)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-150)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-151)

There are several [golf courses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_course "Golf course") within a 20 km radius of Nairobi.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-152) The oldest 18-hole golf course in the city is the Royal Nairobi Golf Club. It was established in 1906 by the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland"), just seven years after the city was founded. Other notable golf clubs include the Windsor Golf Hotel and Country Club, Karen Country Club, VetLab Sports Club, Golf Park Golf Club, Kenya Railways Golf Club, Sigona Golf Club and Muthaiga Golf Club.

The [Kenya Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Open "Kenya Open") golf tournament, which is part of the [European Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Tour "European Tour"), takes place in Nairobi.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-153)

The [Ngong Racecourse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngong_Racecourse "Ngong Racecourse") in Nairobi is the centre of [horse racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughbred_racing "Thoroughbred racing") in Kenya.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-154)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-155)

The Kenya Open Polo tournament and other polo games are often hosted at the Nairobi Polo Club.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi#cite_note-156)

The Horse Association of Kenya offices are located in Nairobi, at Racecourse.

Rugby is a popular sport in Nairobi with 8 of the 12 top flight clubs based here.

[The Rugby Football Union of East Africa (RFUEA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_Football_Union_of_East_Africa "Rugby Football Union of East Africa") is hosted in Nairobi.

Basketball is a popular sport played in the city's primary, Secondary and college leagues. Many of the city's urban youth are basketball fans and watch the American [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association").

Nairobi often hosts a number of marathons including:

*   Nairobi City Marathon
*   Standard Chartered Nairobi Marathon
