Relations with Somalia have historically been tense, although there has been some military co-ordination against Islamist insurgents. Kenya has good relations with the United Kingdom.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-upenn-149) Kenya is one of the most [pro-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-American "Pro-American") nations in Africa, and the wider world.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-pewglobal_20060622-150)

With [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") trial dates scheduled in 2013 for both President Kenyatta and Deputy President [William Ruto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Ruto "William Ruto") related to the 2007 election aftermath, US president [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"), who is half-Kenyan, chose not to visit the country during his [mid-2013 African trip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_visits_to_Sub-Saharan_Africa#Table_of_visits "United States presidential visits to Sub-Saharan Africa").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201401211851-151) Later in the summer, Kenyatta visited China at the invitation of President [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") after a stop in Russia and not having visited the United States as president.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-wp01-152) In July 2015, Obama visited Kenya, the first American president to visit the country while in office.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-nation_2808378-153)

The [British Army Training Unit Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army_Training_Unit_Kenya "British Army Training Unit Kenya") (BATUK) is used for the training of [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") infantry battalions in the arid and rugged terrain of the [Great Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley "Great Rift Valley").[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201908061130-154)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-155)

### Armed forces

[![Image 30: Emblem of the Kenya Defence Forces](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Emblem_of_the_Kenya_Defence_Forces.svg/250px-Emblem_of_the_Kenya_Defence_Forces.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Emblem_of_the_Kenya_Defence_Forces.svg)

Emblem of the Kenya Defence Forces

The Kenya Defence Forces are the armed forces of Kenya. The [Kenya Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Army "Kenya Army"), [Kenya Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Navy "Kenya Navy"), and [Kenya Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Air_Force "Kenya Air Force") compose the National Defence Forces. The current Kenya Defence Forces were established, and its composition laid out, in Article 241 of the 2010 [Constitution of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kenya "Constitution of Kenya"); the KDF is governed by the Kenya Defence Forces Act of 2012.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-156) The [President of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Kenya "President of Kenya") is the [commander-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-chief "Commander-in-chief") of all the armed forces.

The armed forces are regularly deployed in peacekeeping missions around the world. Further, in the aftermath of the national elections of December 2007 and the violence that subsequently engulfed the country, a commission of inquiry, the [Waki Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waki_Commission "Waki Commission"), commended its readiness and adjudged it to "have performed its duty well."[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-157) Nevertheless, there have been serious allegations of human rights violations, most recently while conducting counter-insurgency operations in the [Mt Elgon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mt_Elgon "Mt Elgon") area[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-158) and also in the district of [Mandera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandera "Mandera") central.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_486206-159)

Kenya's armed forces, like many government institutions in the country, have been tainted by [corruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corruption_in_Kenya "Corruption in Kenya") allegations. Because the operations of the armed forces have been traditionally cloaked by the ubiquitous blanket of "state security", the corruption has been hidden from public view, and thus less subject to public scrutiny and notoriety. This has changed recently. In what are by Kenyan standards unprecedented revelations, in 2010, credible claims of corruption were made with regard to recruitment[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-160) and procurement of armoured personnel carriers.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-161) Further, the wisdom and prudence of certain decisions of procurement have been publicly questioned.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-162)

### Administrative divisions

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Kenya%2C_administrative_divisions_-_en_-_colored.svg/250px-Kenya%2C_administrative_divisions_-_en_-_colored.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenya,_administrative_divisions_-_en_-_colored.svg)

Kenya's 47 counties

Kenya is divided into [47 semi-autonomous counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counties_of_Kenya "Counties of Kenya") that are headed by governors. These 47 counties form the first-order divisions of Kenya.

The smallest administrative units in Kenya are called [locations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locations_of_Kenya "Locations of Kenya"). Locations often coincide with electoral wards. Locations are usually named after their central villages/towns. Many larger towns consist of several locations. Each location has a chief, appointed by the state.

Constituencies are an electoral subdivision, with each county comprising a whole number of constituencies. An interim boundaries commission was formed in 2010 to review the constituencies and in its report, it recommended the creation of an additional 80 constituencies. Previous to the 2013 elections, there were 210 [constituencies in Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituencies_of_Kenya "Constituencies of Kenya").[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_200801130520-163)

### Human rights

[Homosexual acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuality "Homosexuality") are illegal in Kenya and typically punishable by up to 14 years in prison.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-164) According to a 2020 survey by the [Pew Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center "Pew Research Center"), 83% of Kenyans believe that homosexuality should not be accepted by society.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-pewresearch.org-165) While addressing a joint press conference together with President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") in 2015, President Kenyatta declined to assure Kenya's commitment to gay rights, saying that "the issue of gay rights is really a non-issue... But there are some things that we must admit we don't share. Our culture, our societies don't accept."[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-cnn_20170725-166)

In November 2008, [WikiLeaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WikiLeaks "WikiLeaks") brought wide international attention to _The Cry of Blood_ report, which documents the extrajudicial killing of gangsters by the Kenyan police. In the report, the [Kenya National Commission on Human Rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_National_Commission_on_Human_Rights "Kenya National Commission on Human Rights") (KNCHR) reported these in their key finding "e)", stating that the [forced disappearances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forced_disappearance "Forced disappearance") and [extrajudicial killings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extrajudicial_killing "Extrajudicial killing") appeared to be official policy sanctioned by the political leadership and the police.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-ediec_20080925-167)[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-capitalfm_20170401-168)

## Economy

Kenya's [macroeconomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macroeconomics "Macroeconomics") outlook has steadily posted robust growth over the past few decades mostly from road, rail, [air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-cost_carrier "Low-cost carrier") and [water transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_transport "Water transport") infrastructure projects as well as massive investments in [Information and Communication Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_and_communications_technology "Information and communications technology"). The Kenyan economy is the largest in East Africa. After independence, Kenya promoted rapid economic growth through public investment, encouraged smallholder agricultural production and provided incentives for private industrial investment. Kenya is East Africa's regional transportation and financial hub. Kenya's financial sector is vibrant, well developed and diversified boasting the highest financial inclusion in the region and globally.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-169)

Foreign investments in Kenya remain relatively weak considering the size of its economy and its level of development. As of 2022, Kenya's total FDI stock stood at US$10.4 billion, accounting for a mere 9.5% of the country's GDP.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-170)

Kenya has a [Human Development Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index "Human Development Index") (HDI) of 0.628 (medium), ranked 143 out of 193 in the world as of 2023. As of 2022, 25.4% of Kenyans lived on less than $2.15 a day.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-mpi2024-171) Based on the most recent data from 2022, 25.4% of the population is affected by [multidimensional poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multidimensional_Poverty_Index "Multidimensional Poverty Index") and an additional 26.4% vulnerable to it.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-mpi2023-172)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-mpi2024-171) In 2017, Kenya ranked 92nd in the World Bank [ease of doing business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ease_of_doing_business_index "Ease of doing business index") rising from 113th in 2016 (of 190 countries).[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-173) The important agricultural sector employs around 30% of the workforce.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-174) Kenya is usually classified as a [frontier market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontier_market "Frontier market") or occasionally an [emerging market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerging_market "Emerging market"), and is one of the [Developing countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_country "Developing country").

The economy has seen much expansion, seen by strong performance in tourism, higher education and [telecommunications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecommunications_in_Kenya "Telecommunications in Kenya") and decent post-drought results in agriculture, especially the vital tea sector.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-lcweb2.loc.gov-175) Kenya's economy grew by more than 7% in 2007, and its foreign debt was greatly reduced.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-lcweb2.loc.gov-175) This changed immediately after the disputed presidential election of December 2007, following the chaos which engulfed the country.

Telecommunications and financial activity over the last decade now comprise 62% of GDP. 22% of GDP still comes from the unreliable agricultural sector which employs 75% of the labour force (a characteristic of under-developed economies that have not attained [food security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_security "Food security")). A small portion of the population relies on food aid.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-:1-176) Industry and manufacturing is the smallest sector, accounting for 16% of GDP. The services, industry and manufacturing sectors only employ 25% of the labour force but contribute 75% of GDP.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-lcweb2.loc.gov-175) Kenya also exports textiles worth over $400 million under [AGOA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AGOA "AGOA").

Privatisation of state corporations like the defunct Kenya Post and Telecommunications Company, which resulted in East Africa's most profitable company—[Safaricom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safaricom "Safaricom"), has led to their revival because of massive private investment.

As of May 2011, economic prospects were positive with 4–5% GDP growth expected, largely because of expansions in tourism, telecommunications, transport, construction, and a recovery in agriculture. The [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank") estimated growth of 4.3% in 2012.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-WorldBanki-177)

In March 1996 the presidents of Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda re-established the [East African Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_African_Community "East African Community") (EAC). The EAC's objectives include harmonising tariffs and customs regimes, free movement of people and improving regional infrastructures. In March 2004, the three East African countries signed a [Customs Union Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customs_union "Customs union").

Kenya has a more developed financial services sector than its neighbours. The [Nairobi Securities Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi_Securities_Exchange "Nairobi Securities Exchange") (NSE) is ranked 4th in Africa in terms of market capitalisation. The Kenyan banking system is supervised by the [Central Bank of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Kenya "Central Bank of Kenya") (CBK). As of late July 2004, the system consisted of 43 commercial banks (down from 48 in 2001) and several [non-bank financial institutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-bank_financial_institution "Non-bank financial institution") including mortgage companies, four savings and loan associations and several core foreign-exchange bureaus.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-lcweb2.loc.gov-175)

The inaugural Kenya Innovation Week (KIW) was started in 2021, from 6 to 10 December 2021, at the Kenya School of Government in Lower Kabete, Nairobi.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-178)

Tourism contributes around 6% to Kenya's economy.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-179)[Tourism in Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_Kenya "Tourism in Kenya") is the third-largest source of foreign exchange revenue, behind diaspora remittances and agriculture.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-theeastafrican_4093616-180) The Kenya Tourism Board is responsible for maintaining information pertaining to tourism in Kenya.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-181)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-182) The main tourist attractions are photo safaris through the [60 national parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_national_parks_of_Kenya "List of national parks of Kenya") and game reserves. Game reserves include [Maasai Mara Game Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_Mara_Game_Reserve "Maasai Mara Game Reserve"), [Samburu National Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samburu_National_Reserve "Samburu National Reserve"), [Solio Game Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solio_Game_Reserve "Solio Game Reserve"), [Shaba National Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaba_National_Reserve "Shaba National Reserve"), [Buffalo Springs National Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Springs_National_Reserve "Buffalo Springs National Reserve") among others. Other attractions include the [wildebeest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildebeest "Wildebeest") migration at the [Masaai Mara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masaai_Mara "Masaai Mara"); historical mosques, and colonial-era forts at [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa"), [Malindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malindi "Malindi"), and [Lamu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamu "Lamu"); renowned scenery such as the white-capped [Mount Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya "Mount Kenya") and the [Great Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya "Great Rift Valley, Kenya"); tea plantations at [Kericho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kericho "Kericho"); coffee plantations at [Thika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thika "Thika"); a splendid view of [Mount Kilimanjaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kilimanjaro "Mount Kilimanjaro") across the border into Tanzania; and the beaches along the [Swahili Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_Coast "Swahili Coast"), in the Indian Ocean. Tourists, the largest number being from Germany and the United Kingdom, are attracted mainly to the coastal beaches and the [game reserves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_reserve "Game reserve"), notably, the expansive [East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsavo_East_National_Park "Tsavo East National Park") and [Tsavo West National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsavo_West_National_Park "Tsavo West National Park"), 20,808 square kilometres (8,034 sq mi) to the southeast.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Agriculture

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Kenya-Tealand-Near-Kericho-2012.JPG/250px-Kenya-Tealand-Near-Kericho-2012.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenya-Tealand-Near-Kericho-2012.JPG)

Tea farm near [Kericho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kericho "Kericho"), [Kericho County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kericho_County "Kericho County")

Agriculture is the second-largest contributor to Kenya's gross domestic product (GDP) after the service sector. In 2005, agriculture, including [forestry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forestry "Forestry") and fishing, accounted for 24% of GDP, as well as for 18% of wage employment and 50% of revenue from exports. The principal [cash crops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cash_crop "Cash crop") are tea, horticultural produce, and coffee. Horticultural produce and tea are the main growth sectors and the two most valuable of all of Kenya's exports. The production of major food staples such as [corn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize "Maize") is subject to sharp weather-related fluctuations. Production downturns periodically necessitate food aid—for example in 2004, due to one of Kenya's intermittent [droughts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Droughts "Droughts").[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-wfp_20050426-183)

A consortium led by the [International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Crops_Research_Institute_for_the_Semi-Arid_Tropics "International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics") ([ICRISAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICRISAT "ICRISAT")) has had some success in helping farmers grow new [pigeon pea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigeon_pea "Pigeon pea") varieties instead of maize, in particularly dry areas. Pigeon peas are very drought-resistant, so can be grown in areas with less than 650 millimetres (26 in) annual rainfall. Successive projects encouraged the commercialisation of legumes by stimulating the growth of local seed production and agro-dealer networks for distribution and marketing. This work, which included linking producers to wholesalers, helped to increase local producer prices by 20–25% in Nairobi and Mombasa. The commercialisation of the pigeon pea is now enabling some farmers to buy assets ranging from mobile phones to productive land and livestock, and is opening pathways for them to move out of poverty.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201407181936-184)

Tea, coffee, sisal, pyrethrum, corn, and wheat are grown in the fertile highlands, one of the most successful agricultural production regions in Africa.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-:0-127) Livestock predominates in the semi-arid savanna to the north and east. [Coconuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coconuts "Coconuts"), [pineapples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pineapples "Pineapples"), [cashew nuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cashew_nuts "Cashew nuts"), cotton, [sugarcane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugarcane "Sugarcane"), [sisal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisal "Sisal"), and corn are grown in the lower-lying areas. Kenya has not attained the level of investment and efficiency in agriculture that can guarantee food security, and coupled with resulting poverty (53% of the population lives below the poverty line), a significant portion of the population regularly starves and is heavily dependent on food aid.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-:1-176) Poor roads, an inadequate railway network, under-used water transport, and expensive air transport have isolated mostly [arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arid "Arid") and [semi-arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid "Semi-arid") areas, and farmers in other regions often leave food to rot in the fields because they cannot access markets. This was last seen in August and September 2011, prompting the [Kenyans for Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyans_for_Kenya "Kenyans for Kenya") initiative by the [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cross "Red Cross").[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201201260031-185)

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e4/Kapsowar1.JPG/250px-Kapsowar1.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kapsowar1.JPG)

Agricultural countryside in Kenya

Kenya's [irrigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irrigation "Irrigation") sector is categorised into three organizational types: [smallholder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallholding "Smallholding") schemes, centrally-managed public schemes, and private/commercial irrigation schemes.

The smallholder schemes are owned, developed, and managed by individuals or groups of farmers operating as water users or self-help groups. Irrigation is carried out on individual or on group farms averaging 0.1–0.4 ha. There are about 3,000 smallholder irrigation schemes covering a total area of 47,000 ha. The country has seven large, centrally managed irrigation schemes, namely Mwea, [Bura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bura_irrigation_and_Settlement_Project_(Kenya) "Bura irrigation and Settlement Project (Kenya)"), [Hola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hola,_Kenya "Hola, Kenya"), [Perkera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perkerra_River "Perkerra River"), West Kano, Bunyala, and [Ahero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahero "Ahero"), covering a total area of 18,200 ha and averaging 2,600 ha per scheme. These schemes are managed by the National Irrigation Board and account for 18% of irrigated land area in Kenya. Large-scale private commercial farms cover 45,000 hectares, accounting for 40% of irrigated land. They use high technology and produce high-value crops for the export market, especially flowers and vegetables.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-186)

Kenya is the world's 3rd largest exporter of [cut flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cut_flowers "Cut flowers").[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-kenya-flower-industry-187) Roughly half of Kenya's 127 flower farms are concentrated around [Lake Naivasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Naivasha "Lake Naivasha"), 90 kilometres northwest of Nairobi.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-kenya-flower-industry-187) To speed their export, Nairobi airport has a terminal dedicated to the transport of flowers and vegetables.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-kenya-flower-industry-187)

### Industry and manufacturing

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Orrling_of_Nairobi.jpg/330px-Orrling_of_Nairobi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Orrling_of_Nairobi.jpg)

The [Kenya Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Commercial_Bank "Kenya Commercial Bank") office at KENCOM House (right) in Nairobi

Although Kenya is a low middle-income country, manufacturing accounts for 14% of the GDP, with industrial activity concentrated around the three largest urban centres of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"), [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa"), and [Kisumu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu "Kisumu"), and is dominated by food-processing industries such as grain milling, beer production, sugarcane crushing, and the fabrication of consumer goods, e.g., vehicles from kits.

Kenya also has a cement production industry.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-constructionkenya_20150905-188) Kenya has an [oil refinery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_refinery "Oil refinery") that processes imported crude petroleum into petroleum products, mainly for the domestic market. In addition, a substantial and expanding [informal sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Informal_sector "Informal sector") commonly referred to as _jua kali_ engages in small-scale manufacturing of household goods, auto parts, and farm implements.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-ilo_075529-189)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-190)

Kenya's inclusion among the beneficiaries of the US Government's African Growth and Opportunity Act ([AGOA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AGOA "AGOA")) has given a boost to manufacturing in recent years. Since AGOA took effect in 2000, Kenya's clothing sales to the United States increased from US$44 million to US$270 million (2006).[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-191) Other initiatives to strengthen manufacturing have been the new government's favourable tax measures, including the removal of duty on capital equipment and other raw materials.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-state_138092-192)

In 2023, Kenya is in the process of constructing five industrial parks that will operate tax-free, with an anticipated completion date set for 2030. There are intentions to develop an additional 20 industrial parks in the future.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-economist_20240102-193)

### Transport

Two trans-African automobile routes pass through Kenya: the [Cairo-Cape Town Highway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairo-Cape_Town_Highway "Cairo-Cape Town Highway") and the [Lagos-Mombasa Highway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos-Mombasa_Highway "Lagos-Mombasa Highway"), so the country has an extensive road network of paved and unpaved roads. Kenya's railway system links the nation's ports and major cities, connecting it with neighbouring Uganda. There are 15 airports which have paved runways.

### Energy

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Worker_in_Olkaria_Kenya.jpg/250px-Worker_in_Olkaria_Kenya.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Worker_in_Olkaria_Kenya.jpg)

Workers at [Olkaria Geothermal Power Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olkaria_II_Geothermal_Power_Station "Olkaria II Geothermal Power Station")

The largest share of Kenya's electricity supply comes from geothermal energy,[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201808111333-194) followed by hydroelectric stations at dams along the upper [Tana River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tana_River_(Kenya) "Tana River (Kenya)"), as well as the Turkwel Gorge Dam in the west. A petroleum-fired plant on the coast, [geothermal facilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geothermal_power_in_Kenya "Geothermal power in Kenya") at [Olkaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olkaria "Olkaria") (near Nairobi), and electricity imported from Uganda make up the rest of the supply. A [2,000 MW powerline from Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodo%E2%80%93Moyale%E2%80%93Suswa_High_Voltage_Power_Line "Sodo–Moyale–Suswa High Voltage Power Line") was completed in 2022.

Kenya's installed capacity increased from 1,142 [megawatts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megawatts "Megawatts") between 2001 and 2003 to 2,341 in 2016.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-195) The state-owned [Kenya Electricity Generating Company (KenGen)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Electricity_Generating_Company "Kenya Electricity Generating Company"), established in 1997 under the name of Kenya Power Company, handles the generation of electricity, [Kenya Electricity Transmission Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Electricity_Transmission_Company "Kenya Electricity Transmission Company") handles long distance distribution of electricity, while [Kenya Power and Lighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Power_and_Lighting "Kenya Power and Lighting") handles the electricity transmission and distribution system in the country. Shortfalls of electricity occur periodically, when drought reduces water flow. To become energy sufficient, Kenya has installed [wind power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_power_in_Kenya "Wind power in Kenya") and [solar power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_power_in_Kenya "Solar power in Kenya") (over 300 MW each), and aims to build a nuclear power plant by 2027.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-theeastafrican_4215876-196)[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201311151406-197)

Kenya has proven deposits of oil in [Turkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkana_County "Turkana County"). [Tullow Oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tullow_Oil "Tullow Oil") estimates the country's oil reserves to be around one billion barrels.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201407250355-198) Exploration is still continuing to determine whether there are more reserves. Kenya currently imports all crude petroleum requirements. Since 2013 the government resorted to importing processed white petroleum. [Kenya Pipeline Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Pipeline_Company "Kenya Pipeline Company") is the state-owned parastatal mandated with the storage and transportation of white petroleum. The company was recently privatised by the government with the government owning a minor stake. Kenya has no strategic reserves and relies solely on oil marketers' 21-day oil reserves required under industry regulations. Petroleum accounts for 20%-to-25% of the national import bill.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_220110520-199)

### Chinese investment and trade

Published comments on Kenya's [Capital FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/98.4_Capital_FM "98.4 Capital FM") website by Liu Guangyuan, [China's ambassador to Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Ambassador_to_Kenya "Chinese Ambassador to Kenya"), at the time of President Kenyatta's 2013 trip to Beijing, said, "Chinese investment in Kenya ... reached $474 million, representing Kenya's largest source of foreign direct investment, and ... bilateral trade ... reached $2.84 billion" in 2012. Kenyatta was "[a]ccompanied by 60 Kenyan business people [and hoped to] ... gain support from China for a planned $2.5 billion railway from the southern Kenyan port of Mombasa to neighbouring Uganda, as well as a nearly $1.8 billion dam", according to a statement from the president's office, also at the time of the trip.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-wp01-152)

Base Titanium, a subsidiary of Base resources of Australia, shipped its first major consignment of minerals to China. About 25,000 tonnes of [ilmenite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilmenite "Ilmenite") was flagged off the Kenyan coastal town of Kilifi. The first shipment was expected to earn Kenya about KSh.15–20 billion/= in earnings.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-standardmedia_2000104631-200) In 2014, the Chinese contracted railway project from Nairobi to Mombasa was suspended due to a dispute over compensation for land acquisition.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-railjournal_20141023-201)

### Vision 2030

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Vision2030_logo.svg/250px-Vision2030_logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vision2030_logo.svg)

The official logo of [Vision 2030](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Vision_2030 "Kenya Vision 2030")

In 2007, the Kenyan government unveiled [Vision 2030](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Vision_2030 "Kenya Vision 2030"), an economic development programme it hopes will put the country in the same league as the [Asian Economic Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Asian_Tigers "Four Asian Tigers") by 2030. In 2013, it launched a National Climate Change Action Plan, having acknowledged that omitting climate as a key development issue in Vision 2030 was an oversight failure. The 200-page Action Plan, developed with support from the [Climate & Development Knowledge Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_&_Development_Knowledge_Network "Climate & Development Knowledge Network"), sets out the Government of Kenya's vision for a 'low-carbon climate resilient development pathway'. At the launch in March 2013, the Secretary of the Ministry of Planning, National Development, and Vision 2030 emphasised that climate would be a central issue in the renewed Medium-Term plan that would be launched in the coming months. This would create a direct and robust delivery framework for the Action Plan and ensure climate change is treated as an economy-wide issue.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201305140754-202) Furthermore, Kenya submitted an updated, more ambitious NDC on 24 December 2020, with a commitment to abate greenhouse gases by 32 per cent by 2030 relative to the business-as-usual scenario and in line with its sustainable development agenda and national circumstances.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-203)

### Oil exploration

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/70/Kenya_Aerial_2009-08-27_14-26-44.JPG/250px-Kenya_Aerial_2009-08-27_14-26-44.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenya_Aerial_2009-08-27_14-26-44.JPG)

[Lake Turkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Turkana "Lake Turkana") borders Turkana County.

Kenya has proven oil deposits in [Turkana County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkana_County "Turkana County"). President Mwai Kibaki announced on 26 March 2012 that [Tullow Oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tullow_Oil "Tullow Oil"), an Anglo-Irish [oil exploration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_exploration "Oil exploration") firm, had struck oil, but its commercial viability and subsequent production would take about three years to confirm.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_17513488-204)

Early in 2006, Chinese president [Hu Jintao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Jintao "Hu Jintao") signed an oil exploration contract with Kenya, part of a series of deals designed to keep Africa's natural resources flowing to China's rapidly expanding economy.

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Lions_Family_Portrait_Masai_Mara.jpg/250px-Lions_Family_Portrait_Masai_Mara.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lions_Family_Portrait_Masai_Mara.jpg)

The deal allowed for China's state-controlled offshore oil and gas company, [CNOOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_National_Offshore_Oil_Corporation "China National Offshore Oil Corporation"), to prospect for oil in Kenya, which is just beginning to drill its first exploratory wells on the borders of Sudan and the disputed area of [North Eastern Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Eastern_Province,_Kenya "North Eastern Province, Kenya"), on the border with Somalia and in coastal waters. There are formal estimates of the possible reserves of oil discovered.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-ft_0000779-205)

### Action against pollution

In 2017, Kenya banned single-use plastic bags. According to the national environmental authority, 80% of the public has adhered to this ban. Subsequently, in 2020, the prohibition of single-use plastics was extended to protected areas, including parks and forests.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-:4-206)

A law passed in July 2023 mandates companies to actively reduce the pollution and environmental impact caused by the products they introduce into the Kenyan market, either individually or through collective schemes. Unlike previous practices, businesses are now obligated to participate in waste collection and recycling initiatives, such as the Petco initiative established by the government in 2018.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-:4-206)

### Labour and human capital

Kenya has a labour force of around 24 million and a total labour force participation rate of 74%, the unemployment rate in 2022 was estimated at 5.6%[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-207)

According to the World Bank's 2019 Human Capital Index (HCI), which measured human capital of the next generation, Kenya ranked first in sub-Saharan Africa with an HCI score of 0.52. The index combined several key indicators, which are school enrolment, child survival, quality of learning, healthy growth and adult survival into a single index ranging between 0–1.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-businessdailyafrica_2254280-208)

### Microfinance

More than 20 institutions offer business loans on a large scale, specific agriculture loans, education loans, and loans for other purposes. Additionally, there are:

*   emergency loans, which are more expensive in respect to interest rates, but are quickly available
*   group loans for smaller groups (four to five members) and larger groups (up to 30 members)
*   women's loans, which are also available to groups of women

Out of approximately 40 million Kenyans, about 14 million are unable to receive financial service through formal loan application services, and an additional 12 million have no access to financial service institutions at all. Further, one million Kenyans are reliant on informal groups for receiving financial aid.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-209)

To mitigate this problem, the mobile banking service [M-Pesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-Pesa "M-Pesa") was launched in 2007 by [Vodafone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vodafone "Vodafone") and [Safaricom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safaricom "Safaricom"), in collaboration from the Financial Deepening Challenge Fund competition established by the UK government's Department for International Development. M-Pesa allows users to deposit, withdraw, transfer money, pay for goods and services (Lipa na M-Pesa), access credit and savings, all with a mobile device,[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-210) has provided access to digital transactions to millions of Kenyans in poverty situation.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-211)

## Demographics

[![Image 42](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Kikuyu_woman_traditional_dress.jpg/250px-Kikuyu_woman_traditional_dress.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kikuyu_woman_traditional_dress.jpg)

A [Bantu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_peoples "Bantu peoples")[Kikuyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people "Kikuyu people") woman in traditional attire

The census carried out by the [Kenya National Bureau of Statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_National_Bureau_of_Statistics "Kenya National Bureau of Statistics") in 2019 reported Kenya's population as 47,564,296.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-KNBS2019-7) The country has a young population, with 73% of residents under 30 because of rapid [population growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_growth "Population growth"),[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_200902152039-212)[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-213) from 2.9 million to 40 million inhabitants over the last century.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_9292632-214)

Nairobi is home to [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera"), one of the world's largest slums. The shantytown is believed to house between 170,000[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-nation1-215) and one million people.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-nationalgeographic_100322-216) The UNHCR base in [Dadaab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadaab "Dadaab") in the north houses around 500,000.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-DadaabPop-217)

### Ethnic groups

Kenya has a diverse population that includes many of Africa's major ethnoracial and linguistic groups. Although there is no official list of Kenyan ethnic groups, the number of ethnic categories and sub-categories recorded in the country's census has changed significantly over time, expanding from 42 in 1969 to more than 120 in 2019.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Balaton-Chrimes2020-218) Most residents are [Bantus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_peoples "Bantu peoples") (60%) or [Nilotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples "Nilotic peoples") (30%).[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Asongumarr-219)[Cushitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cushitic_languages "Cushitic languages") groups also form a small ethnic minority, as do Arabs, Indians, and Europeans.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Asongumarr-219)[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Okothndaloh-220)

According to the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS), the largest native ethnic groups in 2019 were the [Kikuyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people "Kikuyu people") (8,148,668), [Luhya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhya_people "Luhya people") (6,823,842), [Kalenjin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people "Kalenjin people") (6,358,113), [Luo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_people "Luo people") (5,066,966), [Kamba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamba_people "Kamba people") (4,663,910), [Somali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalis "Somalis") (2,780,502), [Kisii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisii_people "Kisii people") (2,703,235), [Mijikenda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mijikenda_peoples "Mijikenda peoples") (2,488,691), [Meru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meru_people "Meru people") (1,975,869), [Maasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people "Maasai people") (1,189,522), and [Turkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkana_people "Turkana people") (1,016,174). The [North Eastern Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Eastern_Province,_Kenya "North Eastern Province, Kenya") of Kenya, formerly known as NFD, is predominantly inhabited by ethnic Somalis. Foreign-rooted populations include [Arabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omanis "Omanis"), [Asians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indians_in_Kenya "Indians in Kenya"), and [Europeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_people_in_Kenya "White people in Kenya").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Census2019a-2)

### Languages

Kenya's ethnic groups typically speak their mother tongues within their own communities. The two [official languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_language "Official language"), English and [Swahili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_language "Swahili language"), are used in varying degrees of fluency for communication with other populations. English is widely spoken in commerce, schooling, and government.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Cugrwed-221)[Peri-urban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peri-urbanisation "Peri-urbanisation") and rural dwellers are less multilingual, with many in rural areas speaking only their native languages.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Broassim-222)

[British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English "British English") is primarily used in Kenya. Additionally, a distinct local dialect, [Kenyan English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_English "Kenyan English"), is used by some communities and individuals in the country, and contains features unique to it that were derived from local [Bantu languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_languages "Bantu languages") such as Kiswahili and [Kikuyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gikuyu_language "Gikuyu language").[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Cliike-223) It has been developing since colonisation and also contains certain elements of [American English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_English "American English"). In January 2026, Kenya was ranked 3rd best English-speaking nation in Africa behind South Africa and Zimbabwe and 9th in the world according to English Proficiency Index (2025). [Sheng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheng_slang "Sheng slang") is a Kiswahili-based [cant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cant_(language) "Cant (language)") spoken in some urban areas. Primarily a mixture of Swahili and English, it is an example of linguistic [code-switching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code-switching "Code-switching").[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Nphil-224)

69 languages are spoken in Kenya. Most belong to two broad language families: [Niger-Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger-Congo_languages "Niger-Congo languages") ([Bantu branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_languages "Bantu languages")) and [Nilo-Saharan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilo-Saharan_languages "Nilo-Saharan languages") ([Nilotic branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_languages "Nilotic languages")), spoken by the country's Bantu and Nilotic populations respectively. The Cushitic and Arab ethnic minorities speak languages belonging to the separate [Afroasiatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afroasiatic_languages "Afroasiatic languages") family, with the Indian and European residents speaking languages from the [Indo-European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-European_languages "Indo-European languages") family.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Ethnken-225)
