### Religion

[![Image 43](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Catholic_Church_in_Mombasa.JPG/250px-Catholic_Church_in_Mombasa.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Catholic_Church_in_Mombasa.JPG)

[Holy Ghost Catholic Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Ghost_Cathedral,_Mombasa "Holy Ghost Cathedral, Mombasa") in Mombasa

Most Kenyans are [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians "Christians") (85.5%), with 33.4% [Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant "Protestant"), 20.6% [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_Kenya "Catholic Church in Kenya") and 20.4% [Evangelical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelicalism "Evangelicalism"). The Catholic Church is the largest single Christian church in Kenya, with about 10 million members.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Census2019a-2) The [Presbyterian Church of East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presbyterian_Church_of_East_Africa "Presbyterian Church of East Africa") has 3 million followers in Kenya and surrounding countries.[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201304030240-227) There are smaller conservative [Reformed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformed_tradition "Reformed tradition") churches, the [Africa Evangelical Presbyterian Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa_Evangelical_Presbyterian_Church "Africa Evangelical Presbyterian Church"),[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-228) the [Independent Presbyterian Church in Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Presbyterian_Church_in_Kenya "Independent Presbyterian Church in Kenya"), and the [Reformed Church of East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformed_Church_of_East_Africa "Reformed Church of East Africa"). [Orthodox Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church "Eastern Orthodox Church") has 621,200 adherents.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-oikoumene_20080203-229) Kenya has by far the highest number of [Quakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaker "Quaker") of any country in the world, with around 146,300.[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-230) The only [Jewish synagogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_synagogue "Jewish synagogue") in the country is in Nairobi.

Islam is the [second largest religion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_Kenya "Islam in Kenya"), comprising 11% of the population.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-religious-freedom-3) 60% of Kenyan Muslims live in the [Coastal Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast_Province "Coast Province"), comprising 50% of the total population there, while the upper part of Kenya's [Eastern Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Province_(Kenya) "Eastern Province (Kenya)") is home to 10% of the country's Muslims, where they are the majority religious group.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-state_108374-231)[Indigenous beliefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_traditional_religion "African traditional religion") are practised by 0.7% of the population, although many self-identifying Christians and Muslims [maintain some traditional beliefs and customs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_syncretism "Religious syncretism"). Nonreligious Kenyans are 1.6% of the population.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Census2019a-2)

Some Hindus also live in Kenya. The numbers are estimated to be around 60,287, or 0.13% of the population.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Census2019a-2)

### Health

[![Image 44](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Kapsowarhospital1.jpg/250px-Kapsowarhospital1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kapsowarhospital1.jpg)

Outpatient Department of AIC Kapsowar Hospital[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-232) in [Kapsowar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapsowar "Kapsowar")

Health care is one of the low-priority sectors in Kenya and was allocated 4.8% of the national budget in 2019/2020 or just 4.59% of GDP compared to high-priority sectors such as education which was allocated more than 25%. This is below the 4.98% average in [Sub-Saharan Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-Saharan_Africa "Sub-Saharan Africa") and 9.83% spent globally.

According to the National and County Health Budget Analysis FY 2020/21, the breakdown of county health expenditure was 58% on Policy Planning and Administrative Support Services, 28% on Curative and Rehabilitative Health Services, 8% on Preventive and Promotive Health Services and 7% on Other Programmes.

Health care is largely funded by private individuals and their families or employers through direct payments to [health care providers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_provider "Health care provider"), to the [National Health Insurance Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hospital_Insurance_Fund "National Hospital Insurance Fund") or to medical insurance companies. Additional funding comes from local, international and some government [social safety net](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_safety_net "Social safety net") schemes. Public hospitals are [fee-for-service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fee-for-service "Fee-for-service") establishments that generate large amounts of county and national government revenues making them highly political and corrupt enterprises.[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-233)

Private health facilities are diverse, highly dynamic, and difficult to classify, unlike public health facilities, which are easily grouped in classes that consist of community-based (level I) services, run by [community health workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_health_worker "Community health worker"); dispensaries (level II facilities), run by nurses; health centres (level III facilities), run by [clinical officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_officer "Clinical officer"); sub-county hospitals (level IV facilities), which may be run by a clinical officer or a [medical officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_practitioner "General practitioner"); county hospitals (level V facilities), which may be run by a medical officer or a [medical practitioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consultant_(medicine) "Consultant (medicine)"); and national referral hospitals (level VI facilities), which are run by fully qualified medical practitioners.

[![Image 45](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Table_rco_co_mo_medical_practitioners.png/250px-Table_rco_co_mo_medical_practitioners.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Table_rco_co_mo_medical_practitioners.png)

Table showing different grades of clinical officers, medical officers, and medical practitioners in Kenya's public service

[Nurses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nursing "Nursing") are by far the largest group of [front-line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front-line "Front-line") health care providers in all sectors, followed by clinical officers, medical officers, and medical practitioners. These are absorbed and deployed into government service in accordance with the Scheme of Service for Nursing Personnel (2014), the Revised Scheme of Service for Clinical Personnel (2020) and the Revised Scheme of Service for Medical Officers and Dental Officers (2016).

[Traditional healers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_healer "Traditional healer") ([herbalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbalist "Herbalist"), [witch doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witch_doctor "Witch doctor"), and [faith healers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_healer "Faith healer")) are readily available, trusted, and widely consulted as practitioners of first or last choice by both rural and urban dwellers.

Despite major achievements in the health sector, Kenya still faces many challenges. The estimated [life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_expectancy "Life expectancy") dropped in 2009 to approximately 55 years – five years below the 1990 level.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201906041433-234) The [infant mortality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant_mortality "Infant mortality") rate was high at approximately 44 deaths per 1,000 children in 2012.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_202008022334-235) The WHO estimated in 2011 that only 42% of births were attended by a skilled health professional.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-236)

[Diseases of poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diseases_of_poverty "Diseases of poverty") directly correlate with a country's [economic performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy "Economy") and [wealth distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wealth_distribution "Wealth distribution"): In 2015/16, 35.6% of Kenyans lived below the poverty line.[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-Poverty_Incidence_in_Kenya-237) Preventable diseases like malaria, HIV/AIDS, pneumonia, diarrhoea, and malnutrition are the biggest burden, major child-killers, and responsible for much morbidity; weak policies, corruption, inadequate health workers, weak management, and poor leadership in the public health sector are largely to blame. According to 2009 estimates, [HIV/AIDS prevalence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_HIV/AIDS_adult_prevalence_rate "List of countries by HIV/AIDS adult prevalence rate") is about 6.3% of the adult population.[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201903291237-238) However, the 2011 UNAIDS Report suggests that the HIV epidemic may be improving in Kenya, as HIV prevalence is declining among young people (ages 15–24) and pregnant women.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201306010117-239) Kenya had an estimated 15 million cases of [malaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaria "Malaria") in 2006.[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_202102281114-240)[Tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis") is a major public health problem. The per capita incidence of TB in Kenya more than quadrupled between 1990 and 2015.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-241)

The 2024 Global Hunger Index gave Kenya a 25.0 score, indicating that the severity of hunger is "serious".[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-242)

### Women

The [total fertility rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_fertility_rate "Total fertility rate") in Kenya was estimated to be 4.49 children per woman in 2012.[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-google_284249880000-243) According to a 2008–09 survey by the Kenyan government, the total fertility rate was 4.6% and the contraception usage rate among married women was 46%.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201901020453-244)[Maternal mortality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maternal_mortality "Maternal mortality") is high, partly because of [female genital mutilation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female_genital_cutting "Female genital cutting"),[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-lcweb2.loc.gov-175) with about 27% of women having undergone it.[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-245) However, this practice is on the decline as the country becomes more modernised, and in 2011 it was banned in Kenya.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-theguardian_20110908_women-246) Women were economically empowered before colonialisation. By colonial land alienation, women lost access and control of land.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-autogenerated1-247) They became more economically dependent on men.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-autogenerated1-247) A colonial order of gender emerged where males dominated females.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-autogenerated1-247) Median age at first marriage increases with increasing education.[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-248) Rape, defilement, and battering are not always seen as serious crimes.[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-auto2-249) Reports of sexual assault are not always taken seriously.[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-auto2-249)

### Youth

Article 260 of the [Kenyan Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Kenyan_constitutional_referendum "2010 Kenyan constitutional referendum") of 2010 defines youth as those between the ages of 18 and 34.[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-250) According to the 2019 Population and Census results, 75 per cent of the 47.6 million population is under the age of 35, making Kenya a country of the [youth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth "Youth").[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-251) Youth unemployment and underemployment in Kenya has become a problem.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-auto3-252) According to the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS), approximately 1.7 million people lost their jobs as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, which eliminated some informal jobs and caused the economy to slow.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-auto3-252) The Kenyan government has made progress in addressing the high youth unemployment by implementing various affirmative action programs and projects which include: the [National Youth Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Youth_Service_(Kenya) "National Youth Service (Kenya)"), The National Youth Enterprise Development Fund,[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-253) The Women Enterprise Fund,[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-254)_Kazi Mtaani, Ajira Digital, Kikao Mtaani_,[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-255)_Uwezo fund_,[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-256) Future Bora[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-257) and _Studio mashinani_[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-258) that [empower youth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth_empowerment "Youth empowerment"), offer job opportunities and to raise one's standard of living.

### Education

[![Image 46](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/Community_work_in_Kenya_DVIDS342488.jpg/250px-Community_work_in_Kenya_DVIDS342488.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Community_work_in_Kenya_DVIDS342488.jpg)

Schoolchildren in a classroom

[![Image 47](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/MSc_student_at_Kenyatta_University.jpg/250px-MSc_student_at_Kenyatta_University.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MSc_student_at_Kenyatta_University.jpg)

An MSc student at [Kenyatta University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyatta_University "Kenyatta University") in Nairobi

Children attend nursery school, or kindergarten in the private sector, until they are five years old. This lasts one to three years (KG1, KG2 and KG3) and is financed privately because there has been no government policy on pre-schooling until recently.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-standardmedia_2000188257-259)

Basic formal education starts at the age of six and lasts 12 years, consisting of eight years in primary school and four in high school or secondary. Primary school is free in public schools and those attending can join a vocational youth/village polytechnic, or make their own arrangements for an apprenticeship program and learn a trade such as tailoring, carpentry, motor vehicle repair, brick-laying and masonry for about two years.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-:2-260)

Those who complete high school can join a [polytechnic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_technology "Institute of technology") or other technical college and study for three years, or proceed directly to university and study for four years. Graduates from the polytechnics and colleges can then join the workforce and later obtain a specialised higher diploma qualification after a further one to two years of training, or join the university—usually in the second or third year of their respective course. The [higher diploma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_diploma "Higher diploma") is accepted by many employers in place of a bachelor's degree and direct or accelerated admission to post-graduate studies is possible in some universities.

[![Image 48](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/Masai_girl_at_school_doing_maths.jpg/250px-Masai_girl_at_school_doing_maths.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Masai_girl_at_school_doing_maths.jpg)

A Maasai girl at school

Public universities in Kenya are highly commercialised institutions and only a small fraction of qualified high school graduates are admitted on limited government-sponsorship into programs of their choice. Most are admitted into the social sciences, which are cheap to run, or as self-sponsored students paying the full cost of their studies. Most qualified students who miss out opt for middle-level diploma programs in public or private universities, colleges, and polytechnics.

In 2018, 18.5 per cent of the Kenyan adult population was illiterate, which was the highest rate of literacy in East Africa.[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-261)[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-262) There are very wide regional disparities: for example, Nairobi had the highest level of literacy at 87.1 per cent, compared to North Eastern Province, the lowest, at 8.0 per cent. Preschool, which targets children from age three to five, is an integral component of the education system and is a key requirement for admission to Standard One (First Grade). At the end of primary education, pupils sit the [Kenya Certificate of Primary Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Certificate_of_Primary_Education "Kenya Certificate of Primary Education") (KCPE), which determines those who proceed to secondary school or vocational training. The result of this examination is needed for placement at secondary school.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-:2-260)

Primary school is for students aged 6/7-13/14 years. For those who proceed to the secondary level, there is a national examination at the end of Form Four– the [Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Certificate_of_Secondary_Education "Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education") (KCSE), which determines those proceeding to the universities, other professional training, or employment. Students sit [examinations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Examinations "Examinations") in eight subjects of their choosing. However, English, Kiswahili, and mathematics are compulsory subjects.

The Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS), formerly the Joint Admissions Board (JAB), is responsible for selecting students joining the public universities. Other than the public schools, there are many private schools, mainly in urban areas. Similarly, there are a number of international schools catering to various overseas educational systems.

Kenya was ranked 102nd in the [Global Innovation Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index "Global Innovation Index") in 2025.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-263)[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-264)

## Culture

[![Image 49](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Kenyan_dancers.jpg/250px-Kenyan_dancers.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenyan_dancers.jpg)

Kenyan boys and girls performing a traditional dance

[![Image 50](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Nation_media_house.jpg/250px-Nation_media_house.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nation_media_house.jpg)

Nation Media House, which hosts the [Nation Media Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_Media_Group "Nation Media Group")

The [culture of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Kenya "Culture of Kenya") comprises multiple traditions from 42 (+) tribes.[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-tandfonline_1863642-265) Kenya has no single prominent culture. It instead consists of the various cultures of the country's different communities.

Notable populations include the [Swahili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_people "Swahili people") on the coast, several other [Bantu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_peoples "Bantu peoples") communities in the central and western regions, and Nilotic communities in the northwest. The [Maasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people "Maasai people") culture is well known to tourism, despite constituting a relatively small part of Kenya's population. They are renowned for their elaborate upper-body adornment and jewellery.

Kenya has an extensive music, television, comedy and theatre scene.

### Literature

[![Image 51](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Ng%C5%A9g%C4%A9_wa_Thiong%27o_%28signing_autographs_in_London%29.jpg/250px-Ng%C5%A9g%C4%A9_wa_Thiong%27o_%28signing_autographs_in_London%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ng%C5%A9g%C4%A9_wa_Thiong'o_(signing_autographs_in_London).jpg)

Kenyan author Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o

[Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ng%C5%A9g%C4%A9_wa_Thiong'o "Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o") is one of Kenya's best-known writers. His novel _[Weep Not, Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weep\_Not,\_Child "Weep Not, Child")_ depicts life in Kenya during the British occupation. The story details the effects of the Mau Mau on the lives of Kenyans. Its combination of themes—[colonialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonialism "Colonialism"), education, and love—helped make it one of the best-known African novels.

[M.G. Vassanji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.G._Vassanji "M.G. Vassanji")'s 2003 novel _The In-Between World of Vikram Lall_ won the [Giller Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotiabank_Giller_Prize "Scotiabank Giller Prize") in 2003. It is the fictional memoir of a Kenyan of Indian heritage and his family as they adjust to the changing political climates in colonial and post-colonial Kenya.

Since 2003, the literary journal _[Kwani?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwani%3F "Kwani?")_ has been publishing Kenyan contemporary literature. Kenya has also nurtured emerging versatile authors such as Paul Kipchumba (Kipwendui, Kibiwott) who demonstrate a pan-African outlook.[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-266)

### Music

[![Image 52](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Juacali_1.jpg/250px-Juacali_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Juacali_1.jpg)

Popular Kenyan musician Jua Cali

Kenya has a diverse assortment of popular music forms, in addition to multiple types of [folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") based on the variety of over 40 regional languages.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201111031307-267)

Drums are the most dominant instrument in popular Kenyan music. Drum beats are very complex and include both native rhythms and imported ones, especially the Congolese [cavacha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavacha "Cavacha") rhythm. Popular Kenyan music usually involves the interplay of multiple parts, and more recently, showy guitar solos as well. There are also a number of local hip-hop artists, including [Jua Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jua_Cali "Jua Cali"); Afro-pop bands such as [Sauti Sol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauti_Sol "Sauti Sol"); and musicians who play local genres like Benga, such as [Akothee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akothee "Akothee").

Lyrics are most often in Kiswahili or English. There is also some emerging aspect of [Lingala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingala_language "Lingala language") borrowed from Congolese musicians. Lyrics are also written in local languages. Urban radio generally only plays English music, though there also exist a number of vernacular radio stations.

_Zilizopendwa_ is a genre of local urban music that was recorded in the 1960s, 70s, and 80s by musicians such as [Daudi Kabaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daudi_Kabaka "Daudi Kabaka"), [Fadhili William](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fadhili_William "Fadhili William"), and Sukuma Bin Ongaro, and is particularly enjoyed by older people—having been popularised by the Kenya Broadcasting Corporation's Kiswahili service (formerly called Voice of Kenya or VOK).

The Isukuti is a vigorous dance performed by the [Luhya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhya_people "Luhya people") sub-tribes to the beat of a traditional drum called the Isukuti during many occasions such as the birth of a child, marriage, or funeral. Other traditional dances include the [Ohangla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohangla "Ohangla") among the [Luo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_peoples "Luo peoples"), Nzele among the [Mijikenda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mijikenda_peoples "Mijikenda peoples"), [Mugithi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mugithi "Mugithi") among the [Kikuyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kikuyu_people "Kikuyu people"), and [Taarab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taarab "Taarab") among the [Swahili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili_people "Swahili people").

Kenya has a growing Christian gospel music scene. Prominent local gospel musicians include the [Kenyan Boys Choir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Boys_Choir "Kenyan Boys Choir").

[Benga music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benga_music "Benga music") has been popular since the late 1960s, especially in the area around [Lake Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria "Lake Victoria"). The word _benga_ is occasionally used to refer to any kind of pop music. Bass, guitar, and percussion are the usual instruments.

### Sports

[![Image 53](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/2012_Olympics_-_Womens_5000m_start_4.jpg/250px-2012_Olympics_-_Womens_5000m_start_4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2012_Olympics_-_Womens_5000m_start_4.jpg)

Jepkosgei Kipyego and Jepkemoi Cheruiyot at the 2012 London Olympics

Kenya is active in several sports, among them [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket"), [rallying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rallying "Rallying"), [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), [rugby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union "Rugby union"), [field hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_hockey "Field hockey"), and [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing"). The country is known chiefly for its dominance in [middle-distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle-distance_running "Middle-distance running") and [long-distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running") athletics, having consistently produced Olympic and [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games") champions in various distance events, especially in 800 m, 1,500 m, 3,000 m steeplechase, 5,000 m, 10,000 m, and the marathon. Kenyan athletes (particularly [Kalenjin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people "Kalenjin people")), continue to dominate the world of distance running, although competition from Morocco and Ethiopia has reduced this supremacy. Some of Kenya's best-known athletes include the four-time women's [Boston Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Marathon "Boston Marathon") winner and two-time world champion [Catherine Ndereba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Ndereba "Catherine Ndereba"), 800m world record holder [David Rudisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Rudisha "David Rudisha"), former [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)") world record-holder [Paul Tergat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tergat "Paul Tergat"), and 5000m Olympic gold medalist [John Ngugi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Ngugi "John Ngugi"). Kenya's most decorated athlete is three-time Olympic gold medalist and eleven-time world marathon major champion, [Eliud Kipchoge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge "Eliud Kipchoge").

Kenya won several medals during the Beijing Olympics: six gold, four silver, and four bronze, making it Africa's most successful nation in the 2008 Olympics. New athletes gained attention, such as [Pamela Jelimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Jelimo "Pamela Jelimo"), the women's 800m gold medalist who went on to win the [IAAF Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_Golden_League "IAAF Golden League") jackpot, and [Samuel Wanjiru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Wanjiru "Samuel Wanjiru"), who won the men's marathon. Retired Olympic and Commonwealth Games champion [Kipchoge Keino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipchoge_Keino "Kipchoge Keino") helped usher in Kenya's ongoing distance dynasty in the 1970s and was followed by Commonwealth Champion [Henry Rono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Rono "Henry Rono")'s spectacular string of world record performances. Lately, there has been controversy in Kenyan athletics circles, with the defection of a number of Kenyan athletes to represent other countries, chiefly Bahrain and Qatar.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-IAAF-268) The Kenyan Ministry of Sports has tried to stop the defections, but they have continued anyway, with [Bernard Lagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Lagat "Bernard Lagat") being the latest, choosing to represent the United States.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-IAAF-268) Most of these defections occur because of economic or financial factors.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-bbc_4566821-269) Decisions by the Kenyan government to tax athletes' earnings may also be a motivating factor.[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-reuters_20140122-270) Some elite Kenyan runners who cannot qualify for their country's strong national team find it easier to qualify by running for other countries.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-nation_1957996-271)

[![Image 54](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/David_Rudisha_Daegu_2011.jpg/250px-David_Rudisha_Daegu_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:David_Rudisha_Daegu_2011.jpg)

Kenyan Olympic and world record holder in the 800 metres, [David Rudisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Rudisha "David Rudisha")

Kenya has been a dominant force in women's volleyball within Africa, with both the clubs and the national team winning various continental championships in the past decade.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-kenyapage_20150620-272)[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-chimpreports_20150621-273) The women's team has competed at the Olympics and [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIVB_Volleyball_Women's_World_Championship "FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship"), though without any notable success. Cricket is another popular sport, also ranking as the most successful team sport. [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_cricket_team "Kenyan cricket team") has competed in the [Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_World_Cup "Cricket World Cup") since [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Cricket_World_Cup "1996 Cricket World Cup"). They upset some of the world's best teams and reached the semi-finals of the [2003 tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Cricket_World_Cup "2003 Cricket World Cup"). They won the inaugural World Cricket League Division 1 hosted in Nairobi and participated in the World T20. They also participated in the [ICC Cricket World Cup 2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Cricket_World_Cup_2011 "ICC Cricket World Cup 2011"). Their current captain is [Rakep Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakep_Patel "Rakep Patel").[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-274)

[![Image 55](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Roshan_Ali.jpg/250px-Roshan_Ali.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Roshan_Ali.jpg)

Roshan Ali, former goalkeeper of Kenya field hockey team

Rugby is increasing in popularity, especially with the annual Safari Sevens tournament. The [Kenya Sevens team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_rugby_sevens_team "Kenya national rugby sevens team") ranked 9th in the IRB Sevens World Series for the 2006 season. In 2016, the team beat Fiji at the Singapore Sevens finals, making Kenya the second African nation after South Africa to win a World Series championship.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-supersport_160417-275)[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-bbc_36067269-276)[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-telegraph_20160417-277)[Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_football_team "Kenya national football team") was once also a regional powerhouse in football. However, its dominance has been eroded by wrangles within the now defunct [Kenya Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Football_Federation "Kenya Football Federation"),[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_364022-278) leading to a suspension by [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") which was lifted in March 2007.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In the motor rallying arena, Kenya is home to the world-famous [Safari Rally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safari_Rally "Safari Rally"), commonly acknowledged as one of the toughest rallies in the world.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_025841-279) First held in 1953, it was a part of the [World Rally Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Rally_Championship "World Rally Championship") for many years until its exclusion after the 2002 event owing to financial difficulties. Some of the best rally drivers in the world have taken part in and won the rally, such as [Björn Waldegård](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bj%C3%B6rn_Waldeg%C3%A5rd "Björn Waldegård"), [Hannu Mikkola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannu_Mikkola "Hannu Mikkola"), [Tommi Mäkinen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommi_M%C3%A4kinen "Tommi Mäkinen"), [Shekhar Mehta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Mehta "Shekhar Mehta"), [Carlos Sainz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sainz_Sr. "Carlos Sainz Sr."), and [Colin McRae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_McRae "Colin McRae"). The Safari Rally returned to the world championship in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Safari_Rally "2021 Safari Rally"), after the 2003–2019 events ran as part of the [African Rally Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Rally_Championship "African Rally Championship").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Nairobi has hosted several major continental sports events, including the [FIBA Africa Championship 1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Africa_Championship_1993 "FIBA Africa Championship 1993"), where [Kenya's national basketball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_national_basketball_team "Kenya national basketball team") finished in the top four, its best performance to date.[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201710081749-280)

Kenya also has its own [ice hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey "Ice hockey") team, the Kenya Ice Lions.[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-nhl_316726578-281) The team's home ground is the [Solar Ice Rink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_Ice_Rink "Solar Ice Rink") at the Panari Sky Centre in Nairobi,[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_202205271122-282)[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_202207071426-283) which is the first and largest [ice rink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_rink "Ice rink") in all of Africa.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-mg_20051225-284)

[Kenya men's national field hockey team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_men's_national_field_hockey_team "Kenya men's national field hockey team") was considered one of the good teams in the world during 1960s and 1970s.

Kenya took 6th position in [1964 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics") hockey tournament and 4th in 1971 [Men's FIH Hockey World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_FIH_Hockey_World_Cup "Men's FIH Hockey World Cup").

### Cuisine

[![Image 56](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Ugali_%26_Sukuma_Wiki.jpg/250px-Ugali_%26_Sukuma_Wiki.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ugali_&_Sukuma_Wiki.jpg)

[Ugali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugali "Ugali") and [sukuma wiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukuma_wiki "Sukuma wiki"), staples of Kenyan cuisine

Kenyans generally have three meals in a day—breakfast (_kiamsha kinywa_), lunch (_chakula cha mchana_), and supper (_chakula cha jioni_ or simply _chajio_). In between, they have the 10-o'clock tea (_chai ya saa nne_) and 4 p.m. tea (_chai ya saa kumi_). Breakfast is usually tea or porridge with bread, [chapati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapati "Chapati"), [mahamri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahamri "Mahamri"), boiled sweet potatoes, or [yams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yam_(vegetable) "Yam (vegetable)"). [Githeri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Githeri "Githeri") is a common lunchtime dish in many households, while [Ugali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugali "Ugali") with vegetables, sour milk ([mursik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mursik "Mursik")), meat, fish, or any other stew is generally eaten by much of the population for lunch or supper. Regional variations and dishes also exist.

In western Kenya, among the [Luo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_(Kenya_and_Tanzania) "Luo (Kenya and Tanzania)"), fish is a common dish; among the [Kalenjin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people "Kalenjin people"), who dominate much of the Rift Valley Region, mursik—sour milk—is a common drink.

In cities such as Nairobi, there are fast-food restaurants, including [Steers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steers_(restaurant) "Steers (restaurant)"), [KFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KFC "KFC"),[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-nbcnews_13223149-285) and [Subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subway_(restaurant) "Subway (restaurant)").[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_1691534-286) There are also many fish-and-chips shops.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-287)

[Cheese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheese_in_Kenya "Cheese in Kenya") is becoming more popular in Kenya, with consumption increasing particularly among the middle class.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201711140418-288)[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-archive_201711140409-289)

**Kenya**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-12) officially the **Republic of Kenya**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-13) is a country located in East Africa. With an estimated population of more than 54.2 million as of mid-2026,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-14) it is the [26th-most populous country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population") in the world[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-KNBS2019-7) and the [seventh-most populous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_African_countries_by_population "List of African countries by population") in Africa. Kenya's capital and largest city is [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). The second-largest and oldest city is [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa"), a port city located on [Mombasa Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa_Island "Mombasa Island"). Other major cities within the country include [Kisumu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu "Kisumu"), [Nakuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakuru "Nakuru") and [Eldoret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldoret "Eldoret"). Going clockwise, Kenya is bordered by South Sudan to the northwest, Ethiopia to the north, Somalia to the east, the Indian Ocean to the southeast, Tanzania to the southwest, and [Lake Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria "Lake Victoria") and Uganda to the west. [Its geography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Kenya "Geography of Kenya"), [climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_in_Kenya "Climate change in Kenya") and [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Kenya "Demographics of Kenya") vary. In western Rift Valley counties, the landscape includes cold, snow-capped mountaintops (such as Batian, Nelion, and Point Lenana on [Mount Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya "Mount Kenya")) with surrounding forests, wildlife, and fertile agricultural regions in temperate climates. In other areas there are dry, [arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arid "Arid"), and [semi-arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate") climates, as well as absolute deserts (such as the [Chalbi Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalbi_Desert "Chalbi Desert") and [Nyiri Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyiri_Desert "Nyiri Desert")).

Kenya's earliest inhabitants included some of the first humans to evolve from ancestral members of the genus [Homo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo "Homo"). Ample fossil evidence for this evolutionary history has been found at [Koobi Fora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koobi_Fora "Koobi Fora"). Later, Kenya was inhabited by [hunter-gatherers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter-gatherer "Hunter-gatherer") similar to the present-day [Hadza people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadza_people "Hadza people").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-researchgate_271694891-16) According to archaeological dating of associated artefacts and skeletal material, [Cushitic speakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Cushitic_languages "South Cushitic languages") first settled in the region's lowlands between 3,200 and 1,300 BC, a phase known as the Lowland [Savanna Pastoral Neolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna_Pastoral_Neolithic "Savanna Pastoral Neolithic"). [Nilotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilo-Saharan_languages "Nilo-Saharan languages")-speaking [pastoralists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism "Pastoralism") (ancestral to Kenya's Nilotic speakers) began migrating from present-day South Sudan into Kenya around 500 BC.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-EhretCHS-17)[Bantu people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_languages "Bantu languages") settled at the coast and the interior between 250 BC and 500 AD.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-18) European contact began in 1500 AD with the [Portuguese Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire"), and effective colonisation of Kenya began in the 19th century during the [European exploration of Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_exploration_of_Africa "European exploration of Africa"). Modern-day Kenya emerged from [a protectorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_Protectorate "East Africa Protectorate"), established by the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") in 1895, and the subsequent [Kenya Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony "Kenya Colony"), which began in 1920. Mombasa was the capital of the [British East Africa Protectorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_Africa_Protectorate "British East Africa Protectorate"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-britannica_20250110-19) which included most of what is now Kenya and southwestern Somalia, from 1889 to 1907. Disputes between the UK and the colony led to the [Mau Mau revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_revolution "Mau Mau revolution"), which began in 1952, and the declaration of Kenya's independence in 1963. After independence, Kenya remained a member of the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations").

Kenya is a [presidential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_system "Presidential system")[representative democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representative_democratic "Representative democratic") republic, in which elected officials represent the people and the president is the head of state and government.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-vic_20071213-20) The country is a member of the United Nations,

**Kenya**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-12) officially the **Republic of Kenya**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-13) is a country located in East Africa. With an estimated population of more than 54.2 million as of mid-2026,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-14) it is the [26th-most populous country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population") in the world[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-KNBS2019-7) and the [seventh-most populous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_African_countries_by_population "List of African countries by population") in Africa. Kenya's capital and largest city is [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). The second-largest and oldest city is [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa"), a port city located on [Mombasa Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa_Island "Mombasa Island"). Other major cities within the country include [Kisumu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kisumu "Kisumu"), [Nakuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakuru "Nakuru") and [Eldoret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldoret "Eldoret"). Going clockwise, Kenya is bordered by South Sudan to the northwest, Ethiopia to the north, Somalia to the east, the Indian Ocean to the southeast, Tanzania to the southwest, and [Lake Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria "Lake Victoria") and Uganda to the west. [Its geography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Kenya "Geography of Kenya"), [climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_in_Kenya "Climate change in Kenya") and [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Kenya "Demographics of Kenya") vary. In western Rift Valley counties, the landscape includes cold, snow-capped mountaintops (such as Batian, Nelion, and Point Lenana on [Mount Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya "Mount Kenya")) with surrounding forests, wildlife, and fertile agricultural regions in temperate climates. In other areas there are dry, [arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arid "Arid"), and [semi-arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate") climates, as well as absolute deserts (such as the [Chalbi Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalbi_Desert "Chalbi Desert") and [Nyiri Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyiri_Desert "Nyiri Desert")).

Kenya's earliest inhabitants included some of the first humans to evolve from ancestral members of the genus [Homo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo "Homo"). Ample fossil evidence for this evolutionary history has been found at [Koobi Fora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koobi_Fora "Koobi Fora"). Later, Kenya was inhabited by [hunter-gatherers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter-gatherer "Hunter-gatherer") similar to the present-day [Hadza people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadza_people "Hadza people").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-researchgate_271694891-16) According to archaeological dating of associated artefacts and skeletal material, [Cushitic speakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Cushitic_languages "South Cushitic languages") first settled in the region's lowlands between 3,200 and 1,300 BC, a phase known as the Lowland [Savanna Pastoral Neolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savanna_Pastoral_Neolithic "Savanna Pastoral Neolithic"). [Nilotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilo-Saharan_languages "Nilo-Saharan languages")-speaking [pastoralists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism "Pastoralism") (ancestral to Kenya's Nilotic speakers) began migrating from present-day South Sudan into Kenya around 500 BC.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-EhretCHS-17)[Bantu people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bantu_languages "Bantu languages") settled at the coast and the interior between 250 BC and 500 AD.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-18) European contact began in 1500 AD with the [Portuguese Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Empire "Portuguese Empire"), and effective colonisation of Kenya began in the 19th century during the [European exploration of Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_exploration_of_Africa "European exploration of Africa"). Modern-day Kenya emerged from [a protectorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_Protectorate "East Africa Protectorate"), established by the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") in 1895, and the subsequent [Kenya Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony "Kenya Colony"), which began in 1920. Mombasa was the capital of the [British East Africa Protectorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_Africa_Protectorate "British East Africa Protectorate"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-britannica_20250110-19) which included most of what is now Kenya and southwestern Somalia, from 1889 to 1907. Disputes between the UK and the colony led to the [Mau Mau revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Mau_revolution "Mau Mau revolution"), which began in 1952, and the declaration of Kenya's independence in 1963. After independence, Kenya remained a member of the [Commonwealth of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Nations "Commonwealth of Nations").

Kenya is a [presidential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_system "Presidential system")[representative democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representative_democratic "Representative democratic") republic, in which elected officials represent the people and the president is the head of state and government.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya#cite_note-vic_20071213-20) The country is a member of the United Nations,
