### Law

Germany has a [civil law system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system) "Civil law (legal system)") based on [Roman law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_law "Roman law") with some references to [Germanic law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_law "Germanic law").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-149) The _[Bundesverfassungsgericht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal\_Constitutional\_Court\_of\_Germany "Federal Constitutional Court of Germany")_ (Federal Constitutional Court) is the German Supreme Court responsible for constitutional matters, with power of [judicial review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judicial_review "Judicial review").[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-150) Germany's specialised supreme court system includes the [Federal Court of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Court_of_Justice "Federal Court of Justice") for civil and criminal cases, along with the [Federal Labour Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Labour_Court "Federal Labour Court"), [Federal Social Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Social_Court "Federal Social Court"), [Federal Fiscal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Fiscal_Court "Federal Fiscal Court"), and [Federal Administrative Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Administrative_Court_(Germany) "Federal Administrative Court (Germany)") for other matters.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-151)

Criminal and private laws are codified on the national level in the _[Strafgesetzbuch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strafgesetzbuch "Strafgesetzbuch")_ and the _[Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%BCrgerliches\_Gesetzbuch "Bürgerliches Gesetzbuch")_ respectively. The German penal system seeks the [rehabilitation of the criminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rehabilitation_(penology) "Rehabilitation (penology)") and the protection of the public.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-152) With the exceptions of petty crimes, tried by a single professional judge, and of serious political crimes, all charges are adjudicated by mixed tribunals where [lay judges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lay_judge "Lay judge") (_[Schöffen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sch%C3%B6ffe "Schöffe")_) and professional judges preside together.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-153)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-154)

In 2016, Germany's murder rate stood at a low of 1.18 murders per 100,000.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-155) In 2018, the overall [crime rate in the country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_in_Germany "Crime in Germany") fell to its lowest since 1992,[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-156) while in 2024, it was reported that violent crime reached a 15-year high, with overall crime rising as well.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-157)

[Same-sex marriage in Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_Germany "Same-sex marriage in Germany") has been legal since 2017, and [LGBT rights in the country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Germany "LGBT rights in Germany") are generally protected.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-158)

### Foreign relations

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Group_photo_of_the_G7_members_at_the_Scholss_Elmau_summit_%282%29.jpg/250px-Group_photo_of_the_G7_members_at_the_Scholss_Elmau_summit_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Group_photo_of_the_G7_members_at_the_Scholss_Elmau_summit_(2).jpg)

Germany hosted the [2022 G7 summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_G7_summit "2022 G7 summit") at [Schloss Elmau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schloss_Elmau "Schloss Elmau") in [Bavaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bavaria "Bavaria").

Germany has a network of [227 diplomatic missions abroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_in_Germany "List of diplomatic missions in Germany")[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-159) and maintains relations with more than 190 countries.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-160) Germany is a member of the [Council of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Europe "Council of Europe"), [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO"), the [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development "Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development"), the [G7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G7 "G7"), the [G20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G20 "G20"), the [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank") and the [IMF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund"). Germany has played an influential role in the European Union since its inception[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-161) and has maintained [a strong alliance with France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco-German_cooperation "Franco-German cooperation")[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-162) and all neighbouring countries since 1990. Germany promotes the creation of a [more unified European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_integration "European integration") political, economic and security apparatus.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-163) Because of its [economic power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_power "Economic power") and political influence, Germany is widely considered to be a [great power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_power "Great power").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-Milena_Steriob-164)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-PaulWirtz2004-165)

The governments of [Germany and the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany%E2%80%93United_States_relations "Germany–United States relations") are close political allies.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-166) Cultural ties and economic interests have crafted a bond between the two countries resulting in [Atlanticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanticism "Atlanticism").[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-167)

Germany's development policy functions as a distinct sector within its foreign policy framework. It is formulated by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development and carried out by the implementing organisations. The German government sees development policy as a joint responsibility of the international community.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-168) Germany was the world's [second-biggest aid donor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_development_aid_sovereign_state_donors "List of development aid sovereign state donors") in 2019 after the United States.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-169)

### Military

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Leopard_2_A5_der_Bundeswehr.jpg/250px-Leopard_2_A5_der_Bundeswehr.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Leopard_2_A5_der_Bundeswehr.jpg)

[Leopard 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopard_2 "Leopard 2") battle tanks of the German Army

Germany's military, the _Bundeswehr_ (Federal Defence), is organised into the _[Heer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_Army "German Army")_ (Army and special forces [KSK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kommando_Spezialkr%C3%A4fte "Kommando Spezialkräfte")), _[Marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_Navy "German Navy")_ (Navy), _[Luftwaffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German\_Air\_Force "German Air Force")_ (Air Force) and _[Cyber- und Informationsraum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyber\_and\_Information\_Domain\_Service "Cyber and Information Domain Service")_ (Cyber and Information Domain Service) branches.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-170) In absolute terms, German military spending in 2025 was the [fourth-highest in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_military_expenditures "List of countries by military expenditures").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-171) In response to the 2022 [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_War "Russo-Ukrainian War"), Chancellor Olaf Scholz announced that German military expenditure would be increased past the NATO target of 2%, along with a one-time 2022 infusion of 100 billion euros, representing almost double the 53 billion euro military budget for 2021.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-172)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-173) In 2023, military spending according to NATO criteria amounted to $73.1 billion, or 1.64% of the country's GDP, well below the NATO target of 2%. In 2026, Germany reported an estimated spending of $147.002 billion to NATO, exceeding said target at 2.69% of GDP.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-:0-174)

As of May 2024, the _Bundeswehr_ has a strength of 180,215 active soldiers and 80,761 civilians.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-175) Reservists are available to the armed forces and participate in defence exercises and deployments abroad.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-bwzukunft-176) Until 2011, [military service was compulsory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_Germany "Conscription in Germany") for men at age 18, but this has been officially suspended and replaced with a voluntary service.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-177)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-178) Since 2001 women may serve in all functions of service without restriction.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-179) According to the [Stockholm International Peace Research Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_International_Peace_Research_Institute "Stockholm International Peace Research Institute"), Germany was the [fourth-largest exporter of major arms in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_arms_exports "List of countries by arms exports") between 2021 and 2025.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-180)

In peacetime, the _Bundeswehr_ is commanded by the [Minister of Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Defence_(Germany) "Minister of Defence (Germany)"). In a [state of defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_defence "State of defence"), the Chancellor would become commander-in-chief of the _Bundeswehr_.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-181) The role of the _Bundeswehr_ is described in the [Constitution of Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Germany "Constitution of Germany") as defensive only. But after a ruling of the Federal Constitutional Court in 1994, the term "defence" has been defined not only to include protection of the borders of Germany, but also crisis reaction and conflict prevention, or more broadly as guarding the [security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security "Security") of Germany anywhere in the world. As of 2026, the German military has about 3,000 troops stationed in foreign countries including 1,800 in [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania "Lithuania") and nearby countries, about 300 in [Kosovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo "Kosovo"), 300 in [Iraq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq "Iraq") and [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan "Jordan"), and 200 in [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon "Lebanon").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-182)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-183)

## Economy

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/Frankfurt_am_Main%2C_Central_business_district_%282024%29.jpg/250px-Frankfurt_am_Main%2C_Central_business_district_%282024%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Frankfurt_am_Main,_Central_business_district_(2024).jpg)

[Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt "Frankfurt"), a leading business and financial centre in Europe and the seat of the [European Central Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Central_Bank "European Central Bank")

Germany has a [social market economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_market_economy "Social market economy") with a highly skilled [labour force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_force "Labour force"), a low level of [corruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corruption_in_Germany "Corruption in Germany"),[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-184) and a high level of [innovation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Innovation "Innovation").[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-185) It is the [largest economy in Europe by nominal GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_in_Europe_by_GDP_(nominal) "List of sovereign states in Europe by GDP (nominal)"), as well as the world's [third-largest by nominal GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal) "List of countries by GDP (nominal)")[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-186) and [sixth-largest by PPP-adjusted GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(PPP) "List of countries by GDP (PPP)").[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-187) Its PPP-adjusted GDP per capita amounted to 115% of the EU average in 2024.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-188) The [country's service sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_sector_in_Germany "Service sector in Germany") contributes approximately 72% of the total GDP, the industrial sector 27%—with Germany having the [largest manufacturing output in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_manufacturing_output "List of countries by manufacturing output")—and [its agricultural sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_in_Germany "Agriculture in Germany") 1%, as of 2023.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-CIA-118)[The unemployment rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_German_states_by_unemployment_rate "List of German states by unemployment rate") published by [Eurostat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostat "Eurostat") amounts to 3.2% as of January 2020, which is the [fourth-lowest in the EU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_Union_member_states_by_unemployment_rate "List of European Union member states by unemployment rate").[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-Eurostat-189)

Germany is part of the [European single market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_single_market "European single market") which represents more than 450 million consumers.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-190) In 2017, the country accounted for 28% of the [eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone "Eurozone") economy according to the [International Monetary Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund").[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-imf.org-191) Germany introduced the common EU currency, the [euro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro"), in 2002.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-euroc-192) Its monetary policy is set by the [European Central Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Central_Bank "European Central Bank"),[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-193) which is based in [Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt "Frankfurt"), the country's largest financial centre.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-frankfurt-194) Germany is the world's [third-largest exporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_exports "List of countries by exports") and [third-largest importer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_imports "List of countries by imports"),[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-CIA-118) and it has the [second-largest trade surplus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_net_goods_exports "List of countries by net goods exports") after China. [Its largest trading partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_largest_trading_partners_of_Germany "List of the largest trading partners of Germany") in 2025 were China, the United States and the Netherlands.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-195)[Germany's main exports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_exports_of_Germany "List of exports of Germany") are vehicles, machinery, and chemical goods.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-Destatis2-196)

The [German automotive industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_automotive_industry "German automotive industry") is among the most competitive and innovative in the world.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-197) It was the [sixth-largest by production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_motor_vehicle_production "List of countries by motor vehicle production") and largest by export value in 2023.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-198) Germany is home to [Volkswagen Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen_Group "Volkswagen Group"), the world's [second-largest automotive manufacturer by vehicle production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_automotive_manufacturers_by_production "List of automotive manufacturers by production").[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-199)

Of the world's 500 largest stock market-listed companies by revenue in 2024, the [_Fortune_ Global 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_Global_500 "Fortune Global 500"), 29 were based in Germany.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-200) The [DAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DAX "DAX"), Germany's stock market index operated by the [Frankfurt Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_Stock_Exchange "Frankfurt Stock Exchange"), includes 30 major Germany-based companies.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-201) Prominent [German companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_companies "German companies") include [Mercedes-Benz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz "Mercedes-Benz"), [BMW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW "BMW"), [Volkswagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volkswagen "Volkswagen"), [Audi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audi "Audi"), [Porsche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porsche "Porsche"), [Siemens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siemens "Siemens"), [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas"), [SAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAP "SAP"), [Bosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Bosch_GmbH "Robert Bosch GmbH") and [BASF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BASF "BASF"). [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") is a [hub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Startup_ecosystem "Startup ecosystem") for [startup companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Startup_company "Startup company") and has become the leading location for venture capital-funded firms in Europe.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-202) Germany is recognised for its large portion of specialised [small and medium enterprises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_and_medium_enterprises "Small and medium enterprises") known as the _[Mittelstand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mittelstand "Mittelstand")_;[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-203) these companies represent around 48% of the global market leaders in their segments, labelled [hidden champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidden_champions "Hidden champions").[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-204)

[Research and development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_and_development "Research and development") efforts form an integral part of the German economy,[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-205) with the country [ranking fourth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_by_research_and_development_spending "List of sovereign states by research and development spending") in research and development expenditure since 2005.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-206) In 2018, Germany [ranked fourth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_number_of_scientific_and_technical_journal_articles "List of countries by number of scientific and technical journal articles") globally in terms of number of science and engineering research papers published[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-207) and third in the quality-adjusted [Nature Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature_Index "Nature Index") in 2023.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-208) Well-known research institutions in Germany include the [Max Planck Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Planck_Society "Max Planck Society"), the [Helmholtz Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmholtz_Association_of_German_Research_Centres "Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres"), the [Fraunhofer Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraunhofer_Society "Fraunhofer Society"), and the [Leibniz Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leibniz_Association "Leibniz Association").[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-209) Germany is the largest contributor to the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency").[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-210) The country was ranked 11th in the [Global Innovation Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index "Global Innovation Index") in 2025.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-211)

### Infrastructure

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/ICE_3_Oberhaider-Wald-Tunnel.jpg/250px-ICE_3_Oberhaider-Wald-Tunnel.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ICE_3_Oberhaider-Wald-Tunnel.jpg)

High-speed trains like this [ICE 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICE_3 "ICE 3") connect the [whole of Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-speed_rail_in_Germany "High-speed rail in Germany").

With its central position in Europe, Germany is a transport hub for the continent.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-212) Its road network is among the [densest in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_road_network_density "List of countries by road network density").[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-213) The motorway (_[Autobahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobahn "Autobahn")_) is widely known for having no general federally mandated [speed limit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed_limits_in_Germany "Speed limits in Germany") for some classes of vehicles.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-wa_16-09-2013-214) The [Intercity Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercity_Express "Intercity Express") or _ICE_ train network serves major German cities as well as destinations in neighbouring countries with speeds up to 300 km/h (190 mph).[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-215) The largest [German airports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_airports_in_Germany "List of airports in Germany") are [Frankfurt Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_Airport "Frankfurt Airport"), [Munich Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_Airport "Munich Airport") and [Berlin Brandenburg Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Brandenburg_Airport "Berlin Brandenburg Airport").[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-216) The [Port of Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Hamburg "Port of Hamburg") is the [third-busiest port in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_busiest_ports_in_Europe "List of busiest ports in Europe") and one of the twenty [largest container ports in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world's_busiest_container_ports "List of world's busiest container ports").[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-217)

In 2019, Germany was the world's [seventh-largest consumer of energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_energy_consumption "List of countries by energy consumption").[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-218) All [German nuclear power plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_power_plants_in_Germany "Nuclear power plants in Germany") were phased out in 2023.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-219) Germany meets its power demands using 40% [renewable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewable_energy "Renewable energy") (2018),[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-220) and has been called an "early leader" in [solar panels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_panel "Solar panel") and [offshore wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_wind_power "Offshore wind power").[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-International_Energy_Agency-2021-221) The [German energy transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_transition_in_Germany "Energy transition in Germany") (_Energiewende_) is the recognised move to a sustainable economy by means of energy efficiency and renewable energy,[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-222)[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-International_Energy_Agency-2021-221) with the country being called "the world's first major renewable energy economy".[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-223) Germany has reduced its [primary energy consumption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_energy_consumption "Primary energy consumption") by 11% between 1990 and 2015[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-224) and set itself goals of reducing it by 30% until 2030 and 50% by 2050.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-225)

The country is committed to the [Paris Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Agreement "Paris Agreement") and several other treaties promoting biodiversity,[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-226) low emission standards,[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-227) and [water management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_management "Water management").[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-228) As of 2017, Germany's household recycling rate is among the [highest in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recycling_rates_by_country "Recycling rates by country"), at around 65%.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-229) In 2023, Germany was the 14th highest emitting nation of [greenhouse gases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas "Greenhouse gas").[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-230)

### Tourism

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Brandenburger_Tor_abends.jpg/250px-Brandenburger_Tor_abends.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brandenburger_Tor_abends.jpg)

The [Brandenburg Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg_Gate "Brandenburg Gate") in Berlin

Domestic and international travel and tourism directly contributed over €105.3 billion to German GDP in 2015.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-:1-231) Including indirect and induced impacts, the industry supported nearly 4.2 million jobs in 2015.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-:1-231) As of 2024, Germany is the [seventh-most-visited country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Tourism_rankings "World Tourism rankings").[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-232) Its most popular landmarks include [Cologne Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Cathedral "Cologne Cathedral"), the [Brandenburg Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg_Gate "Brandenburg Gate"), the [Reichstag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reichstag_building "Reichstag building"), the [Dresden Frauenkirche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dresden_Frauenkirche "Dresden Frauenkirche"), [Neuschwanstein Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuschwanstein_Castle "Neuschwanstein Castle"), [Heidelberg Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg_Castle "Heidelberg Castle"), the [Wartburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wartburg "Wartburg"), and [Sanssouci Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanssouci_Palace "Sanssouci Palace").[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-233)[Europa-Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa-Park "Europa-Park") near [Freiburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freiburg_im_Breisgau "Freiburg im Breisgau") is Europe's second-most popular theme park resort.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-234)

## Demographics

With a population of 84.7 million according to the 2023 German census,[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-235) Germany is the most populous [member state of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union "Member state of the European Union"), the [second-most populous country in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_population "List of European countries by population")[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-turkey-237) after [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia"),[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-CIA-118) and the [nineteenth-most populous country in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population "List of countries and dependencies by population"). Its [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") stands at 236 inhabitants per square kilometre (610 inhabitants/mi 2). The [fertility rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_fertility_rate "Total fertility rate") of 1.36 children born per woman (2024 estimates) is below the replacement rate of 2.1, but slightly above the EU average of 1.34.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-238) Since the 1970s, Germany's [death rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_rate "Death rate") has exceeded its [birth rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_rate "Birth rate"). However, the country is witnessing increased birth and migration rates since the early 2010s. Germany has the [fourth oldest population in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_median_age "List of countries by median age"), with an average age of 47.8 years.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-CIA-118)

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Hubschrauberflug_Hamburg.jpg/250px-Hubschrauberflug_Hamburg.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hubschrauberflug_Hamburg.jpg)

[Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg "Hamburg") is Germany's [second-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Germany_by_population "List of cities in Germany by population"), with [its seaport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Hamburg "Port of Hamburg") being the country's largest by volume.

Four sizeable groups of people are referred to as national minorities because their ancestors have lived in their respective regions for centuries:[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-BMI_2010-239) There is a [Danish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danes "Danes") minority in the northernmost state of [Schleswig-Holstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schleswig-Holstein "Schleswig-Holstein");[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-BMI_2010-239) the [Sorbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorbs "Sorbs"), a [Slavic population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavic_people "Slavic people"), are in the [Lusatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lusatia "Lusatia") region of [Saxony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_State_of_Saxony "Free State of Saxony") and [Brandenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg "Brandenburg"); the [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_people "Romani people") and [Sinti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinti "Sinti") live throughout the country; and the [Frisians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frisians "Frisians") are concentrated in Schleswig-Holstein's western coast and in the north-western part of [Lower Saxony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Saxony "Lower Saxony").[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-BMI_2010-239)

Germany is [a major destination for immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_Germany "Immigration to Germany"), ranking second in the world after the United States.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-240) In 2015, following the [2015 refugee crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_European_migrant_crisis "2015 European migrant crisis"), the Population Division of the [United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Department_of_Economic_and_Social_Affairs "United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs") listed Germany as host to the [second-highest number of international migrants worldwide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_and_dependent_territories_by_immigrant_population "List of sovereign states and dependent territories by immigrant population"), about 5% or 12 million of all 244 million migrants.[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-241) Refugee crises have resulted in substantial population increases;[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-242) for example, the major influx of Ukrainian immigrants following the [2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine"), whereby over 1.06 million refugees from Ukraine were recorded in Germany as of April 2023.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-243) In 2019, Germany ranked seventh among EU countries in terms of the percentage of migrants in the country's population, at 13.1%.[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-244) In 2022, there were 23.8 million people—28.7 percent of the total population—who had a [migration background](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migration_background "Migration background").[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-245)

Germany has [over 2,000 cities and towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_and_towns_in_Germany "List of cities and towns in Germany"), and 11 officially recognised [metropolitan regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_regions_in_Germany "Metropolitan regions in Germany"). The [country's most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Germany_by_population "List of cities in Germany by population") is [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), and its largest urban area is the [Ruhr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruhr "Ruhr").[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-Demographia-246)
