### Languages

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Bilinguale_Stra%C3%9Fenbeschilderung_Cottbus_b.jpg/250px-Bilinguale_Stra%C3%9Fenbeschilderung_Cottbus_b.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bilinguale_Stra%C3%9Fenbeschilderung_Cottbus_b.jpg)

A bilingual street sign in both [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language") and [Lower Sorbian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Sorbian_language "Lower Sorbian language") in [Cottbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cottbus "Cottbus") (_Chóśebuz_), [Brandenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg "Brandenburg")

German is the official and predominantly spoken language in Germany.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-Eurobarometer_Languages-248) It is one of 24 official and working [languages of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_the_European_Union "Languages of the European Union"), and one of the three procedural languages of the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission"), alongside English and French.[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-249) German is the most widely spoken first language in the European Union, with around 100 million native speakers.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-250)

Recognised native minority languages in Germany are [Danish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danish_language "Danish language"), [Low German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_German "Low German"), [Low Rhenish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Rhenish "Low Rhenish"), [Sorbian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorbian_languages "Sorbian languages"), [Romani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_language "Romani language"), [North Frisian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Frisian_language "North Frisian language") and [Saterland Frisian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saterland_Frisian_language "Saterland Frisian language"); they are officially protected by the [European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Charter_for_Regional_or_Minority_Languages "European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages"). The most used immigrant languages are [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_language "Turkish language"), [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic "Arabic"), [Kurdish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdish_language "Kurdish language"), [Polish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_language "Polish language"), [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"), [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language"), [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"), [Serbo-Croatian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbo-Croatian "Serbo-Croatian"), [Bulgarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgarian_language "Bulgarian language") and other [Balkan languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balkan_languages "Balkan languages"), as well as [Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language "Russian language"). Germans are typically multilingual: 74% of German citizens claim to be able to communicate in at least one foreign language and 35% in at least two.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-EU-Lang-251)

### Religion

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/K%C3%B6lner_Dom%2C_K%C3%B6ln-Altstadt-Nord_-_Luftaufnahme-0276_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-K%C3%B6lner_Dom%2C_K%C3%B6ln-Altstadt-Nord_-_Luftaufnahme-0276_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:K%C3%B6lner_Dom,_K%C3%B6ln-Altstadt-Nord_-_Luftaufnahme-0276_(cropped).jpg)

[Cologne Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Cathedral "Cologne Cathedral"), a UNESCO [World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site")

According to the 2022 census, [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_in_Germany "Christianity in Germany") is the largest religion in Germany at 49.7% of the population; 23.1% identified as [Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism") and 25.1% as [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church").[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-252)

A study, based primarily on church membership rolls, estimated that in 2025 48.1% of the population are not members of any religious organisation or [denomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_denomination "Religious denomination") and 46.3% are Christians.[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-FOWID2025A-253)[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-FOWID2025B-254)[Irreligion in Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irreligion_in_Germany "Irreligion in Germany") is strongest in major metropolitan areas and throughout the former [East Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Germany "East Germany").[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-255)[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-georgetown1-256)

[Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam "Islam") is the second-largest religion in the country.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-Zensus_2011-257) In the 2011 census, 1.9% of respondents (1.52 million people) gave their religion as Islam, but this figure is deemed unreliable because a disproportionate number of adherents of this faith (and other religions, such as Judaism) are likely to have made use of their right not to answer the question.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-258) In 2019, there were an estimated 5.3–5.6 million Muslims with a [migrant background](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migrant_background "Migrant background")[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-260) (6.4–6.7% of the population), in addition to an unknown number of Muslims without a migrant background.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-BAMF2020-259) Most of the Muslims are [Sunnis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni_Islam "Sunni Islam") and [Alevis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alevism "Alevism") from Turkey, but there are a small number of [Shi'ites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islam "Shia Islam"), [Ahmadiyyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmadiyya "Ahmadiyya") and other denominations. Other religions each comprise less than one percent of Germany's population.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-Zensus_2011-257)

In 2011, formal members of the [Jewish community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Germany "History of the Jews in Germany") represented no more than 0.2% of the total German population, and 60% of them resided in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin").[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-261) An estimated 80 to 90 percent of these Jews in Germany are Russian-speaking immigrants from the [former Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-Soviet_states "Post-Soviet states") who came to Germany from the 1980s onwards.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-262)[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-263)

### Education

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Heidelberg_Universit%C3%A4tsbibliothek_2003_b.jpg/250px-Heidelberg_Universit%C3%A4tsbibliothek_2003_b.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Heidelberg_Universit%C3%A4tsbibliothek_2003_b.jpg)

[Heidelberg University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg_University "Heidelberg University"), Germany's oldest institution of higher learning and generally considered one of its most renowned

Responsibility for educational supervision in Germany is primarily organised within the individual [states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_of_Germany "States of Germany"). Optional [kindergarten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kindergarten "Kindergarten") education is provided for all children between three and six years old, after which [school attendance is compulsory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schulpflicht "Schulpflicht") for at least nine years depending on the state. Primary education usually lasts for four to six years.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-ED-264) Secondary schooling is divided into tracks based on whether students pursue [academic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College-preparatory_school "College-preparatory school") or [vocational education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocational_education "Vocational education").[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-265) A system of apprenticeship called _[Duale Ausbildung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual\_education\_system "Dual education system")_ leads to a skilled qualification which is almost comparable to an academic degree. It allows students in vocational training to learn in a company as well as in a state-run trade school.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-ED-264) This model is well regarded and reproduced all around the world.[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-266)

Most of the [German universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_universities_in_Germany "List of universities in Germany") are public institutions, and students traditionally study without fee payment.[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-267) The general requirement for attending university is the _[Abitur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abitur "Abitur")_. According to an OECD report from 2014, Germany is the world's third leading destination for international study.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-268) The established universities in Germany include some of the [oldest in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_oldest_universities_in_continuous_operation "List of oldest universities in continuous operation"), with [Heidelberg University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg_University "Heidelberg University") (established in 1386), [Leipzig University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leipzig_University "Leipzig University") (established in 1409) and the [University of Rostock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Rostock "University of Rostock") (established in 1419) being the [oldest in the country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_oldest_German_universities "List of oldest German universities").[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-269) The [Humboldt University of Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humboldt_University_of_Berlin "Humboldt University of Berlin"), founded in 1810 by the liberal educational reformer [Wilhelm von Humboldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_von_Humboldt "Wilhelm von Humboldt"), became the academic [model for many Western universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humboldtian_model_of_higher_education "Humboldtian model of higher education").[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-270)[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-271)

### Health

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Heiligen-Geist-Hospital_%28L%C3%BCbeck%29.jpg/250px-Heiligen-Geist-Hospital_%28L%C3%BCbeck%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Heiligen-Geist-Hospital_(L%C3%BCbeck).jpg)

The [Hospital of the Holy Spirit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hospital_of_the_Holy_Spirit "Hospital of the Holy Spirit") in [Lübeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L%C3%BCbeck "Lübeck"), established in 1286, is a precursor to modern hospitals.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-272)

Germany's system of hospitals, called _Krankenhäuser_, dates from medieval times, and the country has the world's oldest [universal health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_health_care "Universal health care") system, dating from [Bismarck's social legislation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_von_Bismarck#Social_legislation "Otto von Bismarck") of the 1880s.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-273) Since the 1880s, reforms and provisions have ensured a balanced [health care system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care_system "Health care system"). The population is covered by a health insurance plan provided by statute, with criteria allowing some groups to opt for a private health insurance contract. According to the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") (WHO), Germany's health care system was 77% government-funded and 23% privately funded in 2013.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-health-274) In 2024, Germany spent 12.27% of its GDP on health care.[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-275)

Germany [ranked 21st](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy "List of countries by life expectancy") in the world in 2019 in life expectancy with 78.7 years for men and 84.8 years for women according to the WHO, and it had a very low [infant mortality rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant_mortality_rate "Infant mortality rate") of 4 deaths per 1,000 [live births](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_birth_(human) "Live birth (human)"). In 2019, the principal cause of death was cardiovascular disease, at 37%.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-276)[Obesity in Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obesity_in_Germany "Obesity in Germany") has been increasingly cited as a major health issue: a 2014 study showed that 52 percent of the adult German population was overweight or obese.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-277)

Germany has an extensive psychiatric care system, with rising demand for mental health services; roughly 27.8% of adults experience a mental disorder annually.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-278)[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-279) While the system offers comprehensive, insurance-covered care, it faces a shortage of psychotherapists and [a pandemic-driven surge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_health_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic") in anxiety and depression.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-280) In 2023, 37.7% of adults rated their mental health as excellent or very good.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-281) Germany had the third-highest rate of chronic depression among EU countries in 2019.[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-282)

## Culture

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Striezelmarkt_2009_00950.jpg/250px-Striezelmarkt_2009_00950.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Striezelmarkt_2009_00950.jpg)

The [Striezelmarkt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Striezelmarkt "Striezelmarkt"), a [Christmas market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_market "Christmas market") in [Dresden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dresden "Dresden")

Culture in German states has been shaped by major intellectual and popular currents in Europe, both religious and [secular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secularism "Secularism"), and [German scientists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_German_scientists_by_century "List of German scientists by century"), writers and philosophers have played a significant role in the development of Western thought.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-283) Global opinion polls from the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") revealed that Germany is recognised for having the most positive influence in the world in 2013[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-284) and 2014.[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-285)

Germany is well known for such folk festivals as the [Oktoberfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oktoberfest "Oktoberfest")[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-286) and [Christmas customs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weihnachten "Weihnachten"), which include [Advent wreaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advent_wreath "Advent wreath"), [Christmas pageants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nativity_play "Nativity play"), [Christmas trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_tree "Christmas tree"), [Stollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stollen "Stollen") cakes, and other practices.[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-287)As of 2025, [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") inscribed [55 properties in Germany on the World Heritage List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Sites_in_Germany "World Heritage Sites in Germany").[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-288) There are a number of [public holidays in Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_holidays_in_Germany "Public holidays in Germany") determined by each state; 3 October has been a [national day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_day "National day") of Germany since 1990, celebrated as the _Tag der Deutschen Einheit_ ([German Unity Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Unity_Day "German Unity Day")).[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-289)

### Art, design and architecture

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/Caspar_David_Friedrich_-_Wanderer_above_the_Sea_of_Fog.jpeg/250px-Caspar_David_Friedrich_-_Wanderer_above_the_Sea_of_Fog.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Caspar_David_Friedrich_-_Wanderer_above_the_Sea_of_Fog.jpeg)

[German painters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_painters "German painters") have influenced [Western art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_of_Europe "Art of Europe"). [Albrecht Dürer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albrecht_D%C3%BCrer "Albrecht Dürer"), [Hans Holbein the Younger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Holbein_the_Younger "Hans Holbein the Younger"), [Matthias Grünewald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthias_Gr%C3%BCnewald "Matthias Grünewald") and [Lucas Cranach the Elder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Cranach_the_Elder "Lucas Cranach the Elder") were important German artists of the [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance "Renaissance"), [Johann Baptist Zimmermann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Baptist_Zimmermann "Johann Baptist Zimmermann") of the [Baroque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque "Baroque"), [Caspar David Friedrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caspar_David_Friedrich "Caspar David Friedrich") and [Carl Spitzweg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Spitzweg "Carl Spitzweg") of [Romanticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanticism "Romanticism"), [Max Liebermann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Liebermann "Max Liebermann") of [Impressionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impressionism "Impressionism") and [Max Ernst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Ernst "Max Ernst") of [Surrealism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrealism "Surrealism"). Several German art groups formed in the 20th century; _[Die Brücke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die\_Br%C3%BCcke "Die Brücke")_ (The Bridge) and _[Der Blaue Reiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der\_Blaue\_Reiter "Der Blaue Reiter")_ (The Blue Rider) influenced the development of [expressionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Expressionism "German Expressionism") in Munich and Berlin. The [New Objectivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Objectivity "New Objectivity") arose in response to expressionism during the Weimar Republic. After World War II, broad trends in German art include [neo-expressionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-expressionism "Neo-expressionism") and the [New Leipzig School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Leipzig_School "New Leipzig School").[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-groveart-290)

German designers became early leaders of modern [product design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_design "Product design").[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-291) The [Berlin Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Fashion_Week "Berlin Fashion Week") and the fashion trade fair [Bread & Butter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread_&_Butter_(tradeshow) "Bread & Butter (tradeshow)") are held twice a year.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-292)

Architectural contributions from Germany include the [Carolingian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolingian_architecture "Carolingian architecture") and [Ottonian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottonian_architecture "Ottonian architecture") styles, which were precursors of [Romanesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanesque_architecture "Romanesque architecture"). [Brick Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brick_Gothic "Brick Gothic") is a distinctive medieval style that evolved in Germany. Also in [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_architecture "Renaissance architecture") and [Baroque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque_architecture "Baroque architecture") art, regional and typically German elements evolved (e.g. [Weser Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weser_Renaissance "Weser Renaissance")).[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-groveart-290)[Vernacular architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernacular_architecture "Vernacular architecture") in Germany is often identified by [its timber framing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fachwerkhaus "Fachwerkhaus") (_Fachwerk_) traditions and varies across regions, and among carpentry styles.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-Heinrich_Stiewe_2007-293) When industrialisation spread across Europe, [classicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classicism "Classicism") and a distinctive style of [historicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historicism_(art) "Historicism (art)") developed in Germany, sometimes referred to as _[Gründerzeit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%BCnderzeit "Gründerzeit")_ _style_. [Expressionist architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expressionist_architecture "Expressionist architecture") developed in the 1910s in Germany and influenced [Art Deco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco "Art Deco") and other modern styles. Germany was particularly important in the early [modernist movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture"): it is the home of [Werkbund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutscher_Werkbund "Deutscher Werkbund") initiated by [Hermann Muthesius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Muthesius "Hermann Muthesius") ([New Objectivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Objectivity_(architecture) "New Objectivity (architecture)")), and of the [Bauhaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bauhaus "Bauhaus") movement founded by [Walter Gropius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Gropius "Walter Gropius").[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-groveart-290)[Ludwig Mies van der Rohe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Mies_van_der_Rohe "Ludwig Mies van der Rohe") became one of the world's most renowned architects in the second half of the 20th century; he conceived of the glass façade [skyscraper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyscraper "Skyscraper").[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-294) Renowned contemporary [German architects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_German_architects "List of German architects") and offices include [Pritzker Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritzker_Prize "Pritzker Prize") winners [Gottfried Böhm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gottfried_B%C3%B6hm "Gottfried Böhm") and [Frei Otto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frei_Otto "Frei Otto").[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-295)

### Literature and philosophy

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/Grimm.jpg/250px-Grimm.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Grimm.jpg)

[Brothers Grimm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers_Grimm "Brothers Grimm"), who collected popular German folk tales and published them in [a collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimms'_Fairy_Tales "Grimms' Fairy Tales")

German literature can be traced back to the Middle Ages and the works of writers such as [Walther von der Vogelweide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walther_von_der_Vogelweide "Walther von der Vogelweide") and [Wolfram von Eschenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfram_von_Eschenbach "Wolfram von Eschenbach"). Well-known German authors include [Johann Wolfgang von Goethe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Wolfgang_von_Goethe "Johann Wolfgang von Goethe"), [Friedrich Schiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Schiller "Friedrich Schiller"), [Gotthold Ephraim Lessing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gotthold_Ephraim_Lessing "Gotthold Ephraim Lessing") and [Theodor Fontane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Fontane "Theodor Fontane"). The collections of folk tales published by the [Brothers Grimm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers_Grimm "Brothers Grimm") popularised [German folklore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_folklore "German folklore") on an international level.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-D99ff-296) The Grimms also gathered and codified regional variants of the German language, grounding their work in historical principles; their _[Deutsches Wörterbuch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsches\_W%C3%B6rterbuch "Deutsches Wörterbuch")_, or German Dictionary, sometimes called the Grimm dictionary, was begun in 1838 and the first volumes published in 1854.[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-DWBhistory-297)

Influential authors of the 20th century include [Gerhart Hauptmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhart_Hauptmann "Gerhart Hauptmann"), [Thomas Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Mann "Thomas Mann"), [Hermann Hesse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Hesse "Hermann Hesse"), [Heinrich Böll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinrich_B%C3%B6ll "Heinrich Böll"), and [Günter Grass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%BCnter_Grass "Günter Grass").[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-298) The German book market is the third-largest in the world, after the United States and China.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-299) The [Frankfurt Book Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_Book_Fair "Frankfurt Book Fair") is the most important in the world for international deals and trading, with a tradition spanning over 500 years.[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-300) The [Leipzig Book Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leipzig_Book_Fair "Leipzig Book Fair") also retains a major position in Europe.[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-301)

German philosophy is historically significant: [Gottfried Leibniz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gottfried_Leibniz "Gottfried Leibniz")'s contributions to [rationalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rationalism "Rationalism"); the [enlightenment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment "Age of Enlightenment") philosophy by [Immanuel Kant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immanuel_Kant "Immanuel Kant"); the establishment of classical [German idealism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_idealism "German idealism") by [Johann Gottlieb Fichte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Gottlieb_Fichte "Johann Gottlieb Fichte"), [Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_Wilhelm_Friedrich_Hegel "Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel") and [Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Wilhelm_Joseph_Schelling "Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling"); [Arthur Schopenhauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Schopenhauer "Arthur Schopenhauer")'s composition of metaphysical pessimism; the formulation of [communist theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_theory "Communist theory") by [Karl Marx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Marx "Karl Marx") and [Friedrich Engels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Engels "Friedrich Engels"); [Friedrich Nietzsche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Nietzsche "Friedrich Nietzsche")'s development of [perspectivism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perspectivism "Perspectivism"); [Gottlob Frege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gottlob_Frege "Gottlob Frege")'s contributions to the dawn of [analytic philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytic_philosophy "Analytic philosophy"); [Martin Heidegger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Heidegger "Martin Heidegger")'s works on Being; [Oswald Spengler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswald_Spengler "Oswald Spengler")'s historical philosophy; and the development of the [Frankfurt School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt_School "Frankfurt School") have all been very influential.[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-302)

### Music

[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Joseph_Karl_Stieler%27s_Beethoven_mit_dem_Manuskript_der_Missa_solemnis.jpg/250px-Joseph_Karl_Stieler%27s_Beethoven_mit_dem_Manuskript_der_Missa_solemnis.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joseph_Karl_Stieler's_Beethoven_mit_dem_Manuskript_der_Missa_solemnis.jpg)

[Ludwig van Beethoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven "Ludwig van Beethoven") (1770–1827), one of the most famed composers of [classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music "Classical music"), was born in [Bonn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonn "Bonn").

German [classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music_era "Classical music era") includes works by some of the world's most well-known composers. [Dieterich Buxtehude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dieterich_Buxtehude "Dieterich Buxtehude"), [Johann Sebastian Bach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Sebastian_Bach "Johann Sebastian Bach") and [Georg Friedrich Händel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Frideric_Handel "George Frideric Handel") were influential composers of the [Baroque period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque_music "Baroque music"). [Ludwig van Beethoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven "Ludwig van Beethoven") was a crucial figure in the transition between the Classical and [Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_music "Romantic music") eras. [Carl Maria von Weber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Maria_von_Weber "Carl Maria von Weber"), [Felix Mendelssohn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felix_Mendelssohn "Felix Mendelssohn"), [Robert Schumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Schumann "Robert Schumann") and [Johannes Brahms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Brahms "Johannes Brahms") were significant Romantic composers. [Richard Wagner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Wagner "Richard Wagner") was known for his operas. [Richard Strauss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Strauss "Richard Strauss") was a leading composer of the late Romantic and early [modern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th-century_classical_music "20th-century classical music") eras. [Karlheinz Stockhausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karlheinz_Stockhausen "Karlheinz Stockhausen") and [Wolfgang Rihm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfgang_Rihm "Wolfgang Rihm") are important composers of the 20th and early 21st centuries.[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-303)

In 2013, Germany was the second-largest music market in Europe, and [fourth-largest in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_recorded_music_markets "List of largest recorded music markets").[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-304) German popular music of the 20th and 21st centuries includes the movements of [Neue Deutsche Welle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neue_Deutsche_Welle "Neue Deutsche Welle"), [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"), [Ostrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostrock "Ostrock"), [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music")/[rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_rock "German rock"), [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_punk "German punk"), [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock"), [indie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_rock "Indie rock"), [Volksmusik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volksmusik "Volksmusik") (folk music), [schlager pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlager_music "Schlager music") and [German hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_hip_hop "German hip hop"). German [electronic music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") gained global influence, with [Kraftwerk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraftwerk "Kraftwerk") and [Tangerine Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangerine_Dream "Tangerine Dream") pioneering in this genre.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-305) DJs and artists of the [techno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno "Techno") and [house music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music") scenes of Germany have become well known (e.g. [Paul van Dyk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_van_Dyk "Paul van Dyk"), [Felix Jaehn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felix_Jaehn "Felix Jaehn"), [Paul Kalkbrenner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kalkbrenner "Paul Kalkbrenner"), [Robin Schulz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Schulz "Robin Schulz") and [Scooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scooter_(band) "Scooter (band)")).[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-306)

### Media

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Filmstudio_Babelsberg_Eingang.jpg/250px-Filmstudio_Babelsberg_Eingang.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Filmstudio_Babelsberg_Eingang.jpg)

[Babelsberg Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babelsberg_Studio "Babelsberg Studio") in [Potsdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potsdam "Potsdam"), the first large-scale film studio in the world

The largest internationally operating [media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_media "Mass media") companies in Germany are [Bertelsmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertelsmann "Bertelsmann"), [Axel Springer SE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axel_Springer_AG "Axel Springer AG") and [ProSiebenSat.1 Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ProSiebenSat.1_Media "ProSiebenSat.1 Media"). [Germany's television market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_in_Germany "Television in Germany") is the largest in Europe, with over 38 million TV households as of 2012.[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-307) Around 90% of German households have cable or satellite TV, with a variety of [free-to-view public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_broadcasting#Germany "Public broadcasting") and [commercial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_broadcasting "Commercial broadcasting") channels.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-media-308) There are more than [300 public and private radio stations in Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_radio_stations_in_Germany "List of radio stations in Germany"); Germany's national radio network is the [Deutschlandradio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutschlandradio "Deutschlandradio"), while the public [Deutsche Welle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Welle "Deutsche Welle") is the main radio and television broadcaster in foreign languages.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-media-308) Germany's print media market is the largest in Europe.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-media-308) The [German newspapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_newspapers "German newspapers") with the highest circulation are _[Bild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bild "Bild")_, _[Süddeutsche Zeitung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%BCddeutsche\_Zeitung "Süddeutsche Zeitung")_, _[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurter\_Allgemeine\_Zeitung "Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung")_ and _[Die Welt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die\_Welt "Die Welt")_.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-media-308) The largest [German magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_magazines "German magazines") include _[ADAC Motorwelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADAC\_Motorwelt "ADAC Motorwelt")_ and _[Der Spiegel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Der\_Spiegel "Der Spiegel")_.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-media-308) Germany has [a large video gaming market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_gaming_in_Germany "Video gaming in Germany"), with over 34 million players nationwide.[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-309) The annual [Gamescom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamescom "Gamescom") held in [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne") is the world's largest [gaming convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaming_convention "Gaming convention").[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-310)

German cinema has made major technical and artistic contributions to film. The first works of the [Skladanowsky Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Skladanowsky "Max Skladanowsky") were shown to an audience in 1895. The renowned [Babelsberg Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babelsberg_Studio "Babelsberg Studio") in [Potsdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potsdam "Potsdam") was established in 1912, thus being the first large-scale film studio in the world. Early German cinema was particularly influential with [German expressionists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_expressionist_cinema "German expressionist cinema") such as [Robert Wiene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wiene "Robert Wiene") and [Friedrich Wilhelm Murnau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Wilhelm_Murnau "Friedrich Wilhelm Murnau"). Director [Fritz Lang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fritz_Lang "Fritz Lang")'s _[Metropolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis\_(1927\_film) "Metropolis (1927 film)")_ (1927) is referred to as the first major science-fiction film. After 1945, many of the films of the immediate post-war period can be characterised as _[Trümmerfilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubble\_film "Rubble film")_ (rubble film). East German film was dominated by the state-owned film studio [DEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DEFA_(film_studio) "DEFA (film studio)"), while the dominant genre in West Germany was the _[Heimatfilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heimatfilm "Heimatfilm")_ ("homeland film").[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-311) The [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film") ("Oscar") went to the German production _[The Tin Drum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tin\_Drum\_(film) "The Tin Drum (film)")_ (_Die Blechtrommel_) in 1979, to _[Nowhere in Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nowhere\_in\_Africa "Nowhere in Africa")_ (_Nirgendwo in Afrika_) in 2002, and to _[The Lives of Others](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lives\_of\_Others "The Lives of Others")_ (_Das Leben der Anderen_) in 2007. [Various Germans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_German-speaking_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees "List of German-speaking Academy Award winners and nominees") won an Oscar for their performances in films. The annual [European Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Film_Award "European Film Award") ceremony is held every other year in Berlin, home of the [European Film Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Film_Academy "European Film Academy"). The [Berlin International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_International_Film_Festival "Berlin International Film Festival") known as "Berlinale", awarding the "[Golden Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bear "Golden Bear")" and held annually since 1951, is one of the world's leading [film festivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_festival "Film festival"). The "Lolas" are annually awarded in Berlin, at the [German Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutscher_Filmpreis "Deutscher Filmpreis").[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-312)

### Cuisine

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/BavarianLunch.jpg/250px-BavarianLunch.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BavarianLunch.jpg)

Bavarian [Bratwurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bratwurst "Bratwurst") with mustard, a [pretzel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretzel "Pretzel"), and [German beer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer_in_Germany "Beer in Germany")

[Bread](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_cuisine#Bread "German cuisine") is a significant part of German cuisine, with German bakeries producing about 600 main types of bread and 1,200 types of pastries and [rolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread_roll "Bread roll") (_Brötchen_).[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-313)[German cheeses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_German_cheeses "List of German cheeses") account for about 22% of all cheese produced in Europe.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-314) Germans produce their ubiquitous sausages in almost 1,500 varieties, including [Bratwurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bratwurst "Bratwurst") and [Weißwurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wei%C3%9Fwurst "Weißwurst").[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-315)

The national alcoholic drink is [beer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer_in_Germany "Beer in Germany").[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-316) Germany's beer consumption per capita stood at 110 litres (24 imp gal; 29 US gal) in 2013 and remains among the [highest in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_beer_consumption_per_capita "List of countries by beer consumption per capita").[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-317)[German beer purity regulations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinheitsgebot "Reinheitsgebot") date back to the 16th century.[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-318)[Wine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_wine "German wine") has become popular in many parts of the country, especially near the [German wine regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_German_wine_regions "List of German wine regions").[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-319) In 2019, Germany was the [ninth-largest wine producer in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_wine_production "List of countries by wine production").[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-320)

The 2018 _[Michelin Guide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelin\_Guide "Michelin Guide")_ awarded [eleven restaurants in Germany three stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Michelin_starred_restaurants#Germany "List of Michelin starred restaurants"), giving the country a cumulative total of [300 stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Michelin-starred_restaurants_in_Germany "List of Michelin-starred restaurants in Germany").[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-321)

### Sports

[![Image 42](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/Germany_champions_2014_FIFA_World_Cup.jpg/250px-Germany_champions_2014_FIFA_World_Cup.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Germany_champions_2014_FIFA_World_Cup.jpg)

The [German national football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") after winning the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") for the fourth time in 2014

[Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_in_Germany "Football in Germany") is the most popular sport in Germany. With more than 7 million official members, the [German Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Football_Association "German Football Association") (_Deutscher Fußball-Bund_) is the largest single-sport organisation worldwide,[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-322) and the German top league, the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesliga "Bundesliga"), attracts the second-highest [average attendance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_attendance_figures_at_domestic_professional_sports_leagues "List of attendance figures at domestic professional sports leagues") of all professional sports leagues in the world.[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-323) The [German men's national football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_national_football_team "Germany national football team") won the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") in [1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_FIFA_World_Cup "1954 FIFA World Cup"), [1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup "1974 FIFA World Cup"), [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_FIFA_World_Cup "1990 FIFA World Cup"), and [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"),[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-324) the [UEFA European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") in [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_UEFA_European_Championship "1972 UEFA European Championship"), [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1980 "UEFA Euro 1980") and [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1996 "UEFA Euro 1996"),[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-325) and the [FIFA Confederations Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Confederations_Cup "FIFA Confederations Cup") in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_FIFA_Confederations_Cup "2017 FIFA Confederations Cup").[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-326)

Germany is one of the world's leading [motor sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorsport_in_Germany "Motorsport in Germany") countries, with constructors such as [BMW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW "BMW") and [Mercedes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz "Mercedes-Benz") playing prominent roles in international competition. [Porsche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porsche "Porsche") has won the [24 Hours of Le Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_Hours_of_Le_Mans "24 Hours of Le Mans") race 19 times, and [Audi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audi "Audi") 13 times, as of April 2024.[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-327) The driver [Michael Schumacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Schumacher "Michael Schumacher") has set many motor sport records, having won seven [Formula One World Drivers' Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_World_Drivers'_Champions "List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions").[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-328)[Sebastian Vettel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel") is also among the most successful [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") drivers of all time.[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-329)

[German athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_at_the_Olympics "Germany at the Olympics") historically have been successful contenders in the [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), ranking third in an [all-time Olympic Games medal count](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-time_Olympic_Games_medal_count "All-time Olympic Games medal count") when combining [East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Germany "East Germany") and [West German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_German "West German") medals prior to [German reunification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_reunification "German reunification").[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-330) In 1936, Berlin hosted the [Summer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics "1936 Summer Olympics") and the [Winter Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Winter_Olympics "1936 Winter Olympics") in [Garmisch-Partenkirchen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garmisch-Partenkirchen "Garmisch-Partenkirchen").[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-331)[Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich") hosted the [Summer Games of 1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics").[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-FOOTNOTELarge2007337-332)

**Germany**,[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-13) officially the **Federal Republic of Germany**,[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-15) is a country in [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Europe "Western Europe") and [Central Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Europe "Central Europe"). It lies between the [Baltic Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltic_Sea "Baltic Sea") and the [North Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Sea "North Sea") to the north with the [Alps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alps "Alps") to the south. Its 16 [constituent states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_of_Germany "States of Germany") have a total population of over 83 million, making it the most populous [member state of the European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union "Member state of the European Union") (EU). Germany borders [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") to the north; [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland "Poland") and the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic "Czech Republic") to the east; [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria") and [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland") to the south; and [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"), [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg"), [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), and the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") to the west. The [nation's capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_of_Germany "Capital of Germany") and [most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Germany_by_population "List of cities in Germany by population") is [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") and its main financial centre is [Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt "Frankfurt"); the largest urban area is the [Ruhr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruhr "Ruhr").

Settlement in the territory of modern Germany began in the [Lower Paleolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Paleolithic "Lower Paleolithic"), with various tribes inhabiting it from the [Neolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neolithic "Neolithic") onward, chiefly the [Celts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celts "Celts"), and [Germanic tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_peoples "Germanic peoples") inhabiting the north. [Romans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") named the area [Germania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germania "Germania"). In 962, the [Kingdom of Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Germany "Kingdom of Germany") formed the bulk of the [Holy Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire"). During the 16th century, [northern German regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Germany "Northern Germany") became the centre of the [Protestant Reformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reformation "Reformation"). Following the [Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars") and [the dissolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Holy_Roman_Empire "Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire") of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806, the [German Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Confederation "German Confederation") was formed in 1815.

[Unification of Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unification_of_Germany "Unification of Germany") into the modern [nation-state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_state "Nation state"), [led](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_German_Confederation_Treaty "North German Confederation Treaty") by [Prussia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Prussia "Kingdom of Prussia"), [established](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proclamation_of_the_German_Empire "Proclamation of the German Empire") the [German Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Empire "German Empire") in 1871. After [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") and [a revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Revolution_of_1918%E2%80%931919 "German Revolution of 1918–1919"), the Empire was replaced by the [Weimar Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weimar_Republic "Weimar Republic"). The [Nazi rise to power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler's_rise_to_power "Adolf Hitler's rise to power") in 1933 led to the establishment of [a totalitarian dictatorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany"), [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), and [the Holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust "The Holocaust"). In 1949, [after the war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_of_World_War_II_in_Europe "End of World War II in Europe") and [Allied occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied-occupied_Germany "Allied-occupied Germany"), Germany was organised into [two separate polities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_German_relations "Inner German relations") with limited sovereignty: the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG), or [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany"), and the German Democratic Republic (GDR), or [East Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Germany "East Germany"). The **Protectorate of Uganda** was a [protectorate](link_18) of the [British Empire](link_28) from 1894 to 1962. In 1893 the [Imperial British East Africa Company](link_25) transferred its administration rights of territory consisting mainly of the [Kingdom of Buganda](link_29) to the [British government](link_30).

In 1894 the Uganda Protectorate was established, and the territory was extended beyond the borders of Buganda to an area that roughly corresponds to that of present-day [Uganda](link_13).

The **Protectorate of Uganda** was a [protectorate](link_18) of the [British Empire](link_28) from 1894 to 1962. In 1893 the [Imperial British East Africa Company](link_25) transferred its administration rights of territory consisting mainly of the [Kingdom of Buganda](link_29) to the [British government](link_30).

In 1894 the Uganda Protectorate was established, and the territory was extended beyond the borders of Buganda to an area that roughly corresponds to that of present-day [Uganda](link_13).

In the mid-1880s, the Kingdom of Buganda was divided between four religious factions – Adherents of Uganda's Native Religion, [Catholics](link_31), [Protestants](link_32) and [Muslims](link_33) – each vying for political control.[[2]](https://en.wiki

The [English](link_112) word _Germany_ derives from the [Latin](link_113)_Germania_, which came into use after [Julius Caesar](link_114) adopted it for the peoples east of the [Rhine](link_115).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany#cite_note-16) The [German](link_0) term _Deutschland_, originally _diutisciu land_ ('the German lands'), is derived from _[deutsch](link_116)_ ([cf.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cf [link_117]. "Cf.")_[Dutch](link_118)_), which descended from [Old High German](link_119)_diutisc_ 'of the people' (from _diot_ or _diota_ 'people'), originally used to distinguish the [language of the common people](link_120) from Latin and [its Romance descendants](link_121). This in turn descends from [Proto-Germanic](link_122)*_[þiudiskaz](link_123)_ 'of the people' (see also the Latinised form _[Theodiscus](link_124)_), derived from *_[þeudō](link_125)_, descended from [Proto-Indo-European](link_126)*_

**Martha Karambu Koome** (born 3 June 1960) is a Kenyan advocate who is currently serving as the [chief justice of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_Kenya "Chief Justice of Kenya") and is the first woman to occupy the post.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-3)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Martha_Koome&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Koome was born on 3 June 1960 in Kithiu village, [Meru District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meru_County "Meru County"), Kenya. She attended Our Lady Consolata Mugoiri Girls High School in [Murang'a County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murang'a_County "Murang'a County").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-4) She holds an LL.B. from the [University of Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nairobi "University of Nairobi"), which she received in 1986. Koome enrolled at [Kenya School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_School_of_Law "Kenya School of Law") the following year. She completed her master's degree (LL.M) in public international law at the [University of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_London "University of London") in 2010.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-5)

Koome began her legal career as a legal associate at Mathenge and Muchemi Advocates, and later started a law firm, working as a managing partner until 2003. She was elected as a council member of the [Law Society of Kenya (LSK)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_Society_of_Kenya "Law Society of Kenya") in 1993–1996.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-6)

During her tenure at the [Law Society of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_Society_of_Kenya "Law Society of Kenya"), she took a leading role in constitutional and legal reforms and was part of the constitutional review process as a delegate at the [Bomas of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomas_of_Kenya "Bomas of Kenya") where she partially chaired the thematic area on the Bill of Rights. Koome also served as the inaugural treasurer of the [East Africa Law Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa_Law_Society "East Africa Law Society") between 1994 and 1996. She has also served as chairperson of FIDA, one of the leading human rights organizations in the country.

Koome has distinguished herself as a defender of human and gender rights. She was one of the lawyers who actively participated in the clamor for the repeal of section 2A of the [Constitution of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kenya "Constitution of Kenya") and for the independence of the judiciary. She is an acclaimed expert in [family law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_law "Family law") and she takes a keen interest in the welfare of children. She was a runner-up in the 2020 [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") person of the year.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-7) In 1995 she was appointed by the [African Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union") meeting of heads of states as a commissioner to the African Committee on the Rights and welfare of children. She has also served as the chairperson of the National Council on the Administration of Justice special taskforce on children matters where she helped steer the review of the Children's Act.

Koome was appointed Judge of the [Court of Appeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Appeal_of_Kenya "Court of Appeal of Kenya") in January 2012. Prior to her appointment to the Court of Appeal, she served as a judge of the [High Court of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_(Kenya) "High Court (Kenya)") for over eight years.

In the same year she was appointed as Court of Appeal judge, she was also elected the chairperson of the [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") Magistrates and Judges Association. In 2016 she was among 13 female candidates shortlisted by the Judicial Service Commission for the deputy chief justice position,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-8) which would later be occupied by [Justice Philomena Mwilu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philomena_Mwilu "Philomena Mwilu").

Koome was among 13 candidates who applied for appointment to replace [David Maraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Maraga "David Maraga") when he retired in January 2021.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-9) She was shortlisted for the position, and attended her public interview on 14 April 2021. Koome is a renowned human rights and gender advocate. She participated in the campaign for the repeal of section 2A of the Kenyan constitution which converted Kenya into a multi-party state. This essential repeal introduced term limits on the presidency.

Koome is also a protector of women and children's rights. She was the African Union Commissioner to the African committee on the rights and welfare of children.[](https://nation.africa/kenya/people/martha-koome--3818198)

When the JSC invited memoranda on her suitability for nomination, the president of the [Law Society of Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_Society_of_Kenya "Law Society of Kenya") submitted a complaint[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-lsk-10) accusing her of being an unfair arbiter, by ruling some specific court cases based on [nepotism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism "Nepotism"), favouritism and improper motive by ruling in favour of the executive arm of the Kenyan government for improper motive and sometimes based on ethnicity.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-lsk-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-13) Later, she instructed her lawyers to issue a demand to the LSK president to retract the law society's allegations against her within seven days, threatening to sue him over defamation arising from the complaints he submitted to the JSC.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-14) In May 2021, the president of the LSK, Nelson Havi, told off Koome and demanded she be transparent and accountable for her actions in the mentioned memoranda, by vowing not to apologize for the evidence-backed memoranda.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-15)

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Martha_Koome.jpg/250px-Martha_Koome.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Martha_Koome.jpg)

Martha Koome at the Supreme Court of Kenya

Koome's suitability was also challenged by Khelef Khalifa who questioned the manner in which she took part in a Court of Appeal sitting that reversed a judgment of the High Court that had declared that all returning officers who had been retained by the IEBC to manage the repeat presidential election on 26 October 2017 had been unlawfully appointed.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-17) Once arguments in the case were concluded, the High Court scheduled the judgment for delivery on 25 October 2017, the eve of the repeat presidential election. On the eve of this judgment, the government declared 25 October a public holiday, meaning courts would not be operational and judges would not be in a position to render any judgments. Chief Justice David Maraga issued special authority to the Judicial Review Division of the High Court in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi") to sit during the public holiday so that the judges could dispense with the scheduled judgment. No such authority was given for the Court of Appeal, whose registries remained closed. Once the High Court delivered the judgment holding that the returning officers were in office illegally, the IEBC somehow managed to file an appeal at the Court of Appeal which was closed due to the public holiday, and Koome appeared alongside two other judges of the Court of Appeal to handle the matter. All three judges were not serving in the Court of Appeal in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi") at the time, and the chief justice had not given authority for the court to sit on a public holiday. The three judges had ostensibly been called to sit by the then president of the Court of Appeal, Justice [Paul Kihara Kariuki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Kihara_Kariuki "Paul Kihara Kariuki").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-18) The judges stayed the High Court Judgment, thereby giving the IEBC the green light to run the repeat presidential poll the following day.

When questioned about her role in this case during the interviews, she indicated that she had to comply with the directives of the president of the Court of Appeal who summoned her to sit, and that the sitting was important because it saved the country from a constitutional crisis,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-19) alluding to the apparent lack of a provision in Kenya's laws for the extension of the term of the president where a repeat presidential election is not held within 60 days as demanded by the Constitution.

At the conclusion of the interviews, the JSC announced her nomination for the position, setting her up to be the 1st female, 15th chief justice, and the third chief justice after the [2010 constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kenya "Constitution of Kenya").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-20)

Her name was subsequently transmitted to the president, who sent it to Parliament[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-21) for vetting and approval before her formal appointment. The Justice & Legal Affairs Committee of the National Assembly conducted her vetting hearing on 13 May[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-22) and recommended that the full house should approve her nomination.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-23) The report of the committee was tabled before the full house on 19 May for discussion. The full house voted to approve her nomination on 19 May 2021[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-24) paving the way for her appointment as the chief justice.

Within hours of Parliament's approval vote, President [Uhuru Kenyatta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uhuru_Kenyatta "Uhuru Kenyatta") appointed her on 19 May 2021, as the chief justice of the Republic of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-25) She took her oath of office at State House, [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"), on 21 May 2021.

She assumed office on Monday, 24 May 2021, in an Assumption of Office ceremony at the Supreme Court Building during which Deputy Chief Justice [Philomena Mwilu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philomena_Mwilu "Philomena Mwilu") handed over the instruments of power to the new chief justice.

On Monday 5 February 2024, Hon. Martha Koome presided over the launch and commissioning of the Nairobi Land Justice Working Group which is tasked with Expediting Land Justice through a People Centered Approach.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-28)

Koome is married to Koome Kiragu and has three children.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Koome#cite_note-29)
