### Sports

[![Image 53](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Aerobics.jpg/250px-Aerobics.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aerobics.jpg)

Aerobics

[Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") is the national sport in Uganda. The [Uganda national football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_national_football_team "Uganda national football team"), nicknamed "The Cranes", is controlled by the [Federation of Uganda Football Associations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Uganda_Football_Associations "Federation of Uganda Football Associations"). They have never qualified for the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") finals. Their best finish in the [African Cup of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Cup_of_Nations "African Cup of Nations") was second in [1978](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_African_Cup_of_Nations "1978 African Cup of Nations"). Among clubs, [SC Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SC_Villa "SC Villa") are the most successful, having won the [national league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Premier_League "Uganda Premier League") 17 times and having reached the final of the [African Cup of Champions Clubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAF_Champions_League "CAF Champions League") in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_African_Cup_of_Champions_Clubs "1991 African Cup of Champions Clubs"), a feat also achieved by [Simba SC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simba_SC "Simba SC") in [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_African_Cup_of_Champions_Clubs "1972 African Cup of Champions Clubs"). [KCCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala_Capital_City_Authority_FC "Kampala Capital City Authority FC") are second in national league wins with 13.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

As of 2020, [Uganda at the Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_at_the_Olympics "Uganda at the Olympics") has won a total of two gold, three silver, and two bronze medals, four of which were in [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Boxing at the Summer Olympics") and three in [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_of_athletics "Sport of athletics"). [At the Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_at_the_Commonwealth_Games "Uganda at the Commonwealth Games"), Uganda has collected 13 gold medals and a total 49 medals, all in boxing and athletics.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Uganda national boxing team is called The Bombers.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-261) They have won four medals at the Summer Olympics from 1968 to 1980, as well as two medals the [1974 World Amateur Boxing Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_World_Amateur_Boxing_Championships "1974 World Amateur Boxing Championships"). Notable boxers include [Cornelius Boza-Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornelius_Boza-Edwards "Cornelius Boza-Edwards"), [Justin Juuko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Juuko "Justin Juuko"), [Ayub Kalule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayub_Kalule "Ayub Kalule"), [John Mugabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mugabi "John Mugabi"), [Eridadi Mukwanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eridadi_Mukwanga "Eridadi Mukwanga"), [Joseph Nsubuga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Nsubuga?action=edit&redlink=1 "Joseph Nsubuga (page does not exist)"), [Kassim Ouma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kassim_Ouma "Kassim Ouma"), [Sam Rukundo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Rukundo "Sam Rukundo") and [Leo Rwabwogo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leo_Rwabwogo "Leo Rwabwogo").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In athletics, [John Akii-Bua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Akii-Bua "John Akii-Bua") won the first Olympic gold medal for Uganda. At the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics") in Munich, he won the [400m hurdles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/400_metres_hurdles "400 metres hurdles") race with a world record time of 47.82 seconds.[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-262) 400 metres runner [Davis Kamoga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davis_Kamoga "Davis Kamoga") earned the bronze medal at [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") in Atlanta and the silver medal at the [1997 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1997 World Championships in Athletics"). [Dorcus Inzikuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorcus_Inzikuru "Dorcus Inzikuru") won the 3000 m steeplechase at the [2005 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2005 World Championships in Athletics") and the [2006 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Commonwealth_Games "2006 Commonwealth Games").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[Stephen Kiprotich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Kiprotich "Stephen Kiprotich") has won the marathon at the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") in London and the [2013 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2013 World Championships in Athletics"), and finished second at the 2015 [Tokyo Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Marathon "Tokyo Marathon").[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-263)[Joshua Cheptegei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Cheptegei "Joshua Cheptegei") has won 10 km races at the World Championships, [World Athletics Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "World Athletics Cross Country Championships") and [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games"), and has set world records in 5 km and 15 km. [Halimah Nakaayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halimah_Nakaayi "Halimah Nakaayi") won the 800 meters race at the 2019 World Championships.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket"), Uganda was part of the [East Africa team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_African_cricket_team "East African cricket team") that qualified for the [Cricket World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket_World_Cup "Cricket World Cup") in [1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Cricket_World_Cup "1975 Cricket World Cup"). Recently [Uganda national cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_national_cricket_team "Uganda national cricket team") qualified for [2024 ICC T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup "2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The country has an increasingly successful [national basketball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_national_basketball_team "Uganda national basketball team"). It is nicknamed "The Silverbacks",[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-264) and made its debut at the [2015 FIBA Africa Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIBA_Africa_Championship "2015 FIBA Africa Championship").[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-265)

In July 2011, Kampala, Uganda qualified for the [2011 Little League World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Little_League_World_Series "2011 Little League World Series") in [Williamsport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamsport,_Pennsylvania "Williamsport, Pennsylvania"), Pennsylvania for the first time, beating Saudi Arabian baseball team Dharan LL, although visa complications prevented them from attending the series.[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-266) Little League teams from Uganda qualified for and attended the [2012 Little League World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Little_League_World_Series "2012 Little League World Series").[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-267)

### Cinema

![Image 56](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Ambox_current_red_Asia_Australia.svg/60px-Ambox_current_red_Asia_Australia.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)This section needs to be **updated**. Please help update this article to reflect recent events or newly available information._(January 2020)_

The Ugandan film industry is relatively young. It is developing quickly, but still faces an assortment of challenges. There has been support for the industry as seen in the proliferation of film festivals such as [Amakula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amakula_International_Film_Festival "Amakula International Film Festival"), [Pearl International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_International_Film_Festival "Pearl International Film Festival"), [Maisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maisha_Film_Lab "Maisha Film Lab") African Film Festival and Manya Human Rights Festival. However, filmmakers struggle against the competing markets from other countries on the continent such as those in Nigeria and South Africa in addition to the big budget films from Hollywood.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-cannesvupar.com-268)

The first publicly recognised film that was produced solely by Ugandans was _Feelings Struggle_, which was directed and written by Hajji [Ashraf Ssemwogerere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashraf_Ssemwogerere "Ashraf Ssemwogerere") in 2005.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-269) This marks the year of ascent of film in Uganda, a time when many enthusiasts were proud to classify themselves as cinematographers in varied capacities.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-monitor.co.ug-270)

The local film industry is polarised between two types of filmmakers. The first are filmmakers who use the [Nollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nollywood "Nollywood")[video film era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_film_era "Video film era")'s guerrilla approach to film making, churning out a picture in around two weeks and screening it in makeshift video halls. The second is the filmmaker who has the film aesthetic, but with limited funds has to depend on the competitive scramble for donor cash.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-cannesvupar.com-268)

Though cinema in Uganda is evolving, it still faces major challenges. Along with technical problems such as refining acting and editing skills, there are issues regarding funding and lack of government support and investment. There are no schools in the country dedicated to film, banks do not extend credit to film ventures, and distribution and marketing of movies remains poor.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-cannesvupar.com-268)[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-monitor.co.ug-270)

The Uganda Communications Commission (UCC) prepared regulations starting in 2014 that required Ugandan television to broadcast 70 per cent Ugandan content and of this, 40 per cent to be independent productions. With the emphasis on Ugandan film and the UCC regulations favouring Ugandan productions for mainstream television, Ugandan film may become more prominent and successful in the near future.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-monitor.co.ug-270)

**Uganda**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-13) officially the **Republic of Uganda**,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-14) is a [landlocked country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landlocked_country "Landlocked country") in [East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa "East Africa"). It is bordered to the east by [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), to the north by [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan "South Sudan"), to the west by the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo"), to the south-west by [Rwanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda "Rwanda"), and to the south by [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania"). The southern part includes a substantial portion of [Lake Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria "Lake Victoria"), shared with Kenya and Tanzania. Uganda is in the [African Great Lakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Great_Lakes "African Great Lakes") region, lies within the [Nile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile "Nile") basin, and has a varied [equatorial climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equatorial_climate "Equatorial climate"). As of 2024, it had a population of 45.9 million, of whom 1.8 million live in the capital and largest city, [Kampala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala "Kampala").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-census24-9)

Uganda is named after the [Buganda kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buganda "Buganda"), which encompasses a large portion of the south, including Kampala, and whose language [Luganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luganda "Luganda") is widely spoken; the official language is English, while [Swahili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili "Swahili") is the second official language. The region was populated by people of various ethnicities before Bantu and Nilotic groups arrived around 3,000 years ago. These new inhabitants established influential kingdoms such as the [Empire of Kitara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Kitara "Empire of Kitara"). The arrival of [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs "Arabs") traders in the 1830s and British explorers in the late 19th century marked the beginning of foreign influence. The British established the [Protectorate of Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectorate_of_Uganda "Protectorate of Uganda") in 1894, setting the stage for future political dynamics.

Uganda gained independence in 1962, with [Milton Obote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Obote "Milton Obote") as the first prime minister. The 1966 [Mengo Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mengo_Crisis "Mengo Crisis") marked a significant conflict with the Buganda kingdom, as well as the country's conversion from a [parliamentary system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system") to a [presidential system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_system "Presidential system"). Obote was overthrown in a [military coup in 1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_Ugandan_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1971 Ugandan coup d'état") by [Idi Amin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idi_Amin "Idi Amin"), who subsequently ruled the country under a brutal dictatorship until he was overthrown in 1979 during the [Uganda–Tanzania War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda%E2%80%93Tanzania_War "Uganda–Tanzania War").

Obote returned to power following the controversial [1980 Ugandan general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Ugandan_general_election "1980 Ugandan general election"), prompting a [six-year guerrilla war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugandan_Bush_War "Ugandan Bush War"), ending with the victory of [Yoweri Museveni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoweri_Museveni "Yoweri Museveni")'s [National Resistance Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Resistance_Movement "National Resistance Movement") in 1986. While Museveni's rule resulted in stability and economic growth, political oppression and human rights abuses continued. The abolition of presidential term limits as well as allegations of electoral fraud and repression have raised concerns about Uganda's democratic future. Museveni was elected president in the [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Ugandan_general_election "2011 Ugandan general election"), [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Ugandan_general_election "2016 Ugandan general election"), [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Ugandan_general_election "2021 Ugandan general election"), and [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Ugandan_general_election "2026 Ugandan general election") general elections. Human rights issues, corruption, and regional conflicts, such as involvement in the Congo Wars and the struggle against the [Lord's Resistance Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Resistance_Army "Lord's Resistance Army") (LRA), continue to challenge Uganda. Despite this, it has made progress in education and health, improving literacy and reducing HIV infection, though challenges in maternal health and gender inequality persist.

Geographically, Uganda is diverse, with volcanic hills, mountains, and lakes, including [Lake Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria "Lake Victoria"), the world's second-largest freshwater lake. The country has significant natural resources, including fertile agricultural land and untapped [oil reserves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_reserve "Oil reserve"), contributing to its economic development. The service sector dominates the economy, surpassing agriculture. Uganda's rich [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity "Biodiversity"), with national parks and wildlife reserves, attracts tourism, a vital sector for the economy. **Uganda**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-13) officially the **Republic of Uganda**,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-14) is a [landlocked country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landlocked_country "Landlocked country") in [East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa "East Africa"). It is bordered to the east by [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), to the north by [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan "South Sudan"), to the west by the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo"), to the south-west by [Rwanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda "Rwanda"), and to the south by [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania"). The southern part includes a substantial portion of [Lake Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria "Lake Victoria"), shared with Kenya and Tanzania. Uganda is in the [African Great Lakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Great_Lakes "African Great Lakes") region, lies within the [Nile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile "Nile") basin, and has a varied [equatorial climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equatorial_climate "Equatorial climate"). As of 2024, it had a population of 45.9 million, of whom 1.8 million live in the capital and largest city, [Kampala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala "Kampala").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda#cite_note-census24-9)

Uganda is named after the [Buganda kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buganda "Buganda"), which encompasses a large portion of the south, including Kampala, and whose language [Luganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luganda "Luganda") is widely spoken; the official language is English, while [Swahili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swahili "Swahili") is the second official language. The region was populated by people of various ethnicities before Bantu and Nilotic groups arrived around 3,000 years ago. These new inhabitants established influential kingdoms such as the [Empire of Kitara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Kitara "Empire of Kitara"). The arrival of [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs "Arabs") traders in the 1830s and British explorers in the late 19th century marked the beginning of foreign influence. The British established the [Protectorate of Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectorate_of_Uganda "Protectorate of Uganda") in 1894, setting the stage for future political dynamics.

Uganda gained independence in 1962, with [Milton Obote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Obote "Milton Obote") as the first prime minister. The 1966 [Mengo Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mengo_Crisis "Mengo Crisis") marked a significant conflict with the Buganda kingdom, as well as the country's conversion from a [parliamentary system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system") to a [presidential system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_system "Presidential system"). Obote was overthrown in a [military coup in 1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_Ugandan_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1971 Ugandan coup d'état") by [Idi Amin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idi_Amin "Idi Amin"), who subsequently ruled the country under a brutal dictatorship until he was overthrown in 1979 during the [Uganda–Tanzania War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda%E2%80%93Tanzania_War "Uganda–Tanzania War").

Obote returned to power following the controversial [1980 Ugandan general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Ugandan_general_election "1980 Ugandan general election"), prompting a [six-year guerrilla war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugandan_Bush_War "Ugandan Bush War"), ending with the victory of [Yoweri Museveni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoweri_Museveni "Yoweri Museveni")'s [National Resistance Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Resistance_Movement "National Resistance Movement") in 1986. While Museveni's rule resulted in stability and economic growth, political oppression and human rights abuses continued. The abolition of presidential term limits as well as allegations of electoral fraud and repression have raised concerns about Uganda's democratic future. Museveni was elected president in the [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Ugandan_general_election "2011 Ugandan general election"), [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Ugandan_general_election "2016 Ugandan general election"), [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Ugandan_general_election "2021 Ugandan general election"), and [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Ugandan_general_election "2026 Ugandan general election") general elections. Human rights issues, corruption, and regional conflicts, such as involvement in the Congo Wars and the struggle against the [Lord's Resistance Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Resistance_Army "Lord's Resistance Army") (LRA), continue to challenge Uganda. Despite this, it has made progress in education and health, improving literacy and reducing HIV infection, though challenges in maternal health and gender inequality persist.

Geographically, Uganda is diverse, with volcanic hills, mountains, and lakes, including [Lake Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Victoria "Lake Victoria"), the world's second-largest freshwater lake. The country has significant natural resources, including fertile agricultural land and untapped [oil reserves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_reserve "Oil reserve"), contributing to its economic development. The service sector dominates the economy, surpassing agriculture. Uganda's rich [biodiversity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodiversity "Biodiversity"), with national parks and wildlife reserves, attracts tourism, a vital sector for the economy.
