Sotet

The use of [arts and crafts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arts_and_crafts "Arts and crafts") form part of Kalenjin culture with decorative bead-work being the most highly developed visual art.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-97) The Kalenjin are generally not well known for their handicraft's however, though women do make and locally sell decorated [calabashes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabash "Calabash") made from gourds. These gourd calabashes known as sotet are rubbed with oil and adorned with small colored beads and are essentially the same type of calabashes that are used for storing [mursik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mursik "Mursik").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-98)

### Radio, television, and film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kalenjin_people&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Radio, television, and film")]

Up until the early 21st century, vernacular radio and television stations were essentially banned in Kenya. The liberalization of the media sector in Kenya which began in the 1990s has seen the growth of Kalenjin language content across most modern mediums.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-99) This period has seen the establishment of Kalenjin language media companies such as Kass Media Group, a Kenyan radio and television company, as well as Kalenjin language stations within diverse media groups e.g. Chamgei FM (Royal Media Services) and Kitwek FM ([Kenya Broadcasting Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Broadcasting_Corporation "Kenya Broadcasting Corporation")). There has been a concurrent proliferation of Kalenjin music, television programs and more recently the premier of the first Kalenjin language film, Ngebe Gaa, at the 2019 Eldoret Film Festival.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-100)

Contemporary Kalenjin music has long been influenced by the [Kipsigis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipsigis_people "Kipsigis people") leading to [Kericho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kericho "Kericho")'s perception as a cultural innovation center.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-101) Musical innovation and regional styles, however, abound across all Kalenjin speaking areas.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-102) Popular musicians include Pastor Joel Kimetto (father of Kalenjin Gospel), Mike Rotich, Emmy Kosgei, Maggy Cheruiyot, Josphat Koech Karanja, Lilian Rotich and Barbra Chepkoech.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Jambo_News-103) Msupa S and [Kipsang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipsang "Kipsang") represent an emerging generation of Kalenjin pop musicians.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-104) Notable stars who have passed on include Diana Chemutai Musila ([Chelele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelele "Chelele")), Junior Kotestes and Weldon Cheruiyot (Kenene).[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Jambo_News-103)

A number of writers have documented Kalenjin history and culture, notably B. E. Kipkorir,[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-106) Paul Kipchumba, and [Ciarunji Chesaina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciarunji_Chesaina "Ciarunji Chesaina").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-107)

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Ugali_with_beef_and_sauce.JPG/250px-Ugali_with_beef_and_sauce.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ugali_with_beef_and_sauce.JPG)

Ugali with beef and sauce is a common dish of Kalenjin and [African Great Lakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Great_Lakes "African Great Lakes") cuisine.

[Ugali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugali "Ugali"), known in Kalenjin as kimnyet, served with cooked vegetables such as isageek ([African cabbage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_cabbage "African cabbage")) or sochot ([African nightshade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_nightshade "African nightshade")), and milk form the staples of the Kalenjin diet. Less often ugali, rice or [chapati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapati "Chapati"), is served with roast meat, usually beef or goat, and occasionally chicken. The traditional ugali is made of [millet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millet "Millet") and [sorghum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorghum "Sorghum") and is known as psong'iot. It is considered healthier than ugali made of maize flour (similar to brown bread/white bread) and has seen a resurgence in popularity in tandem with global trends towards healthier eating. The traditional snack moriot (somewhat similar to [corn tortillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corn_tortillas "Corn tortillas")) is obtained from the crust after cooking ugali and is still quite enjoyed.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-108) Similarly, the traditional drink [mursik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mursik "Mursik"), and honey, both considered delicacies (karise/kariseyuek) for a long time remain quite popular.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-109)

Extensive use is made of dairy produce in traditional recipes such as socheek (a vegetable relish made with greens, milk and cream) as well as contemporary meals such as Mcheleng (rice with milk – a creamy smooth dish made as a delicacy for children but usually enjoyed by the entire family) and Bean stew with milk and cream.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-110)

Combination dishes/mixtures while not considered traditionally Kalenjin are encountered in more cosmopolitan areas. The most common of these is _kwankwaniek_, a mixture of maize and beans boiled together ([githeri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Githeri "Githeri")).

Milk or tea may be drunk by adults and children with any meal or snack. Tea (chaiik) averages 40% milk by volume and is usually liberally sweetened. If no milk is available tea may be drunk black with sugar though taking tea without milk is considered genuine hardship.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-111)

In addition to bread, people routinely buy foodstuffs such as sugar, tea leaves, cooking fat, sodas, and other items that they do not produce themselves.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-112)

[Traditional Kalenjin knowledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Kalenjin_society#Traditional_knowledge "Traditional Kalenjin society") was fairly comprehensive in the study and usage of plants for medicinal purposes and a significant trend among some contemporary Kalenjin scientists is the study of this aspect of traditional knowledge.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-113) In more recent times, commercial enterprises have started blending and packaging traditional herbal remedies for the urban Kenyan market. Most noted of these is Harriet's Botanicals which packages Arorwet and Tendwet alternative remedies and distributes them via a number of shops spread across the country.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-115)

One of the more notable Kalenjin scientists is [Prof Richard Mibey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Mibey "Richard Mibey") whose work on the Tami dye helped [revive the textile industry in Eldoret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldoret#Textiles "Eldoret") and western Kenya in general.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-116)

[Nixon Kiplimo Chepseba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon_Chepseba "Nixon Chepseba") (C) of Kenya steps over [Diego Ruiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Ruiz_(runner) "Diego Ruiz (runner)") (L) of Spain and [Carsten Schlangen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carsten_Schlangen "Carsten Schlangen") of Germany after their round 1 men's 1500m heat during the London 2012 Olympics

The Kalenjin have been called by some "the running tribe." Since the mid-1960s, Kenyan men have earned the largest share of major honours in international [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_of_athletics "Sport of athletics") at distances from 800 meters to the marathon; the vast majority of these Kenyan running stars have been Kalenjin.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-theatlantic.com-117) From 1980 on, about 40% of the top honours available to men in international athletics at these distances (Olympic medals, [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Championships_in_Athletics "IAAF World Championships in Athletics") medals, and World Cross Country Championships honours) have been earned by Kalenjin.

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Paul_Tergat_winning_the_2003_Berlin_Marathon.jpg/250px-Paul_Tergat_winning_the_2003_Berlin_Marathon.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paul_Tergat_winning_the_2003_Berlin_Marathon.jpg)

Paul Tergat set a new world record to the marathon at Berlin, 2003.

In 2008, [Pamela Jelimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Jelimo "Pamela Jelimo") became the first Kenyan woman to win a gold medal at the [Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympics "Olympics"); she also became the first Kenyan to win the [Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_Golden_League "IAAF Golden League") jackpot in the same year.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-118) Since then, Kenyan women have become a major presence in international athletics at the distances; most of these women are Kalenjin.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-theatlantic.com-117)[Amby Burfoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amby_Burfoot "Amby Burfoot") of _[Runner's World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runner's\_World "Runner's World")_ stated that the odds of Kenya achieving the success they did at the [1988 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics") were below 1:160 billion. [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") had an even more successful [Olympics in 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Eliud_Kipchoge_and_Vivian_Cheruiyot.png/250px-Eliud_Kipchoge_and_Vivian_Cheruiyot.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eliud_Kipchoge_and_Vivian_Cheruiyot.png)

The Kalenjin people are renowned for their dominance in athletics specifically long-distance running, which has resulted in numerous accolades for Kenya, including Olympic and World Championship medals in both track events and cross country competitions.

A number of theories explaining the unusual athletic prowess among people from the Kalenjin-speaking people have been proposed. These include many explanations that apply equally well to other Kenyans or people living elsewhere who are not disproportionately successful athletes, such as that they run to school every day, that they live at relatively high altitude, and that the prize money from races is large compared to typical yearly earnings. One theory is that the Kalenjin have relatively thin legs and therefore do not have to lift as much leg weight when running long distances.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-119)

## Kalenjin's in diaspora

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kalenjin_people&action=edit&section=47 "Edit section: Kalenjin's in diaspora")]

The [Kalenjin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_culture "Kalenjin culture") diaspora numbers in North America is approx. ~20,000[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-120) residents across the [USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), is primarily organized under Gotabgaa International,[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-121) a national organization founded in 1993 by Prof. John Rugutt and Amb. Peter Rono. Dedicated to inspiring, connecting, and economically empowering its members through education, networking, and cultural awareness, Gotabgaa operates registered chapters in states with significant populations, including Minnesota, Texas (Dallas and Houston), Kansas (Kansas City and Wichita), [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina"), [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma"), [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin"), [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio"), [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa"), and the [Washington D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") area.

[Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia") is the second leading continent for the Kalenjin diaspora, with an estimated population of 15,000+ residents primarily concentrated in **,** Western Australia. Most Kalenjin's in Australia live in the city called [Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth "Perth"), which serves as the community's national headquarters. The community is unified through the Kitwek Association Inc,[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-122) a registered community-based organization dedicated to fostering positive integration, celebrating cultural heritage, and supporting the welfare of Kalenjin migrants across Australia. Through initiatives like "Kitwek Connect" and annual gala events, the association strengthens social bonds and provides essential networking opportunities for its members. Kalenjin people in the diaspora are also located in regions such as [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(state) "Victoria (state)") ([Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne")), [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales "New South Wales") ([Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney")), [Queensland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland "Queensland") ([Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane")), and [South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australia "South Australia") ([Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide")).

The **Kalenjin** are a Southern Nilotic ethnic group native to [East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa "East Africa"), encompassing over 20 [Kalenjin-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_languages "Kalenjin languages") tribes and sub-groups sharing a common cultural and linguistic lineage.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-:6-4) The primary tribes in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), ordered by population, include the [Kipsigis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipsigis_people "Kipsigis people"), [Nandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandi_people "Nandi people"), [Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people"), [Keiyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgeyo_people "Elgeyo people"), [Sabaot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabaot_people "Sabaot people") (including the [Sebei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebei_people "Sebei people") of [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")), [Tugen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugen_people "Tugen people"), [Marakwet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marakwet_people "Marakwet people"), [Arror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arror_people "Arror people"), [Lembus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lembus_people "Lembus people"), [Ogiek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okiek_people "Okiek people"), and others. They represent Kenya's third-largest ethnic group, with a population of 6,358,113 per the 2019 census.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Census2019-5) The collective also includes the [Endorois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endorois "Endorois"), [Sengwer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sengwer_people "Sengwer people"), [Terik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terik_people "Terik people"), Samor, [Endo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marakwet_people "Marakwet people"), and Senger, alongside [Datooga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Datooga_people "Datooga people") clusters of [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-101Tribes-6)

The Kalenjin-speaking peoples are descendants of the [Maliri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maliri_people "Maliri people") of Uganda, a lineage they share with the [Daasanach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daasanach_people "Daasanach people") (Marille) of the [Omo Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omo_Valley "Omo Valley") in [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-MaliriWiki-7) They were influenced culturally and genetically by [Omotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omotic_languages "Omotic languages")-speaking populations, as well as the [Iraqw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqw_people "Iraqw people") and [Maasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people "Maasai people").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-DaasanachBio-8)[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia\_and\_sources\_that\_mirror\_or\_use\_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] Their linguistic seedbed is attributed to the [autochthonous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autochthonous_language "Autochthonous language")[Ogiek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ogiek_people "Ogiek people") (Dorobo) and [Agumba/Umpua/Lumbwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumbwa_people "Lumbwa people") inhabitants of the [Mau Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mau_Forest "Mau Forest") and [Mount Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kenya "Mount Kenya") regions, who represent the aboriginal ties to the area prior to the 17th century.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Witchmen-9)

Geographically and linguistically classified as Highland Nilotes, this group's designation is derived from their ancestral heartland within the high-altitude escarpments of [Kenya's Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_Valley_Province "Rift Valley Province"), though their presence extends across the diverse elevations of the region and beyond. The Kalenjin are globally recognized for their unparalleled success in international [long-distance running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running"), frequently cited as leading examples of [athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athlete "Athlete") dominance in [sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport "Sport") history; the community has produced many of the world's premier runners (e.g., [Eliud Kipchoge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge "Eliud Kipchoge"), [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon"), [Beatrice Chebet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet "Beatrice Chebet").)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-:7-14) They account for a significant majority of the country's elite international athletics medals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-15)

Kalenjin people collectively share a distinct cultural and linguistic heritage.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-16) They have a very strong and direct connection to the [Nile Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_Valley "Nile Valley") and [Ethiopian highlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Highlands "Ethiopian Highlands"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-:2-17) tracing their ancestral migration from these regions.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-19) The [Kalenjin languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_languages "Kalenjin languages") form a specific branch of the Southern Nilotic group within the broader [Nilo-Saharan language family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilo-Saharan_languages "Nilo-Saharan languages").

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Nubian_pyramids_of_Meroe_in_1821.jpg/250px-Nubian_pyramids_of_Meroe_in_1821.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nubian_pyramids_of_Meroe_in_1821.jpg)

The Nubian pyramids of Meroë are a collection of over 200 steep-sided, stone-built tombs in modern-day Sudan, constructed between roughly 300 BCE and 350 CE by the rulers of the Kingdom of Kush. These smaller, UNESCO-listed monuments served as burial places for kings, queens, and officials, reflecting a blend of ancient Egyptian and Nilotic influences.

This history is defined by significant cultural interaction with Southern/Eastern [Cushitic-speaking communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cushitic-speaking_peoples "Cushitic-speaking peoples"), from whom the Kalenjin adopted key social institutions, including the [age-set system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age-set_system "Age-set system") (ipinda), the practice of [circumcision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumcision "Circumcision"), and specific loanwords related to [livestock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livestock "Livestock") and social organization.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-20)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-:2-17) The [Kipsigis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kipsigis_people "Kipsigis people") tribe are believed to have originated further north, with traditional narratives linking them to the [Pharaoh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharaoh "Pharaoh")'s army in [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"). They reportedly grew disillusioned with the Pharaoh's inability to reliably win wars and forged their own path, embracing an independent "us against the world" attitude. The migration south involved significant territorial expansion at the expense of the [Luo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luo_people "Luo people"), [Gusii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gusii_people "Gusii people") (_Kisii_), and [Maasai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maasai_people "Maasai people"). This expansion was driven by a period of Kalenjin military dominance, specifically through the Kipsigis' use of superior weaponry and tactics, utilizing heavy buffalo-hide shields and advanced close-combat techniques to overwhelm local defenses.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-21) These historical shifts defined the current borders, with these tribes now situated as their western and southern neighbors.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-:2-17)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-22) Scholars like Dr. Kipkoeech Arap Sambu have argued that many Kalenjin words have roots in [ancient Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egyptian "Ancient Egyptian") or [Semitic languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semitic_languages "Semitic languages"). For example, the Kalenjin word for land, _Emet_, is compared to the ancient Egyptian Kemet. Some theories suggest the ancestors of the Kalenjin left Egypt at the same time as the [Israelites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israelites "Israelites") but migrated south toward the Rift Valley while the Israelites moved north.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-theeastafrican.co.ke-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Sambu_2007-24)

According to Kalenjin [oral traditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_tradition "Oral tradition"), their ancestors are linked to the [ancient civilizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_civilizations "Ancient civilizations") of the Nile Valley, specifically an origin point known as _[Misiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misri\_legend "Misri legend")_ — often interpreted as ancient Egypt. Potential linguistic similarities, such as the Kalenjin sun deity _Asiis_ being compared to the [Egyptian goddess Isis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isis "Isis"), as evidence of a historical cultural link.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-25) Archaeological and linguistic evidence places the cradle of the Nilotic languages in the Nile Valley, which maintained strong cultural links with the societies of the Nubian Nile Valley further north.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Sirak_7283-26) These connections were reinforced by thousands of years of social and genetic intermixing, as evidenced by significant Nilotic-related ancestry found in ancient [Nubian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nubians "Nubians") populations. This shared heritage is reflected in similar [pastoral traditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism "Pastoralism"), [pottery styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottery "Pottery"), and burial customs across the broader [Nile Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_Basin "Nile Basin"). Following a southward migration that began around 500 BCE,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Sirak_7283-26) they settled predominantly in the Rift Valley region of Kenya, with significant populations also residing in [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda"), [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania") and broader East Africa.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-study.com-27)

Prior to the [2010 Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kenya "Constitution of Kenya"), the [Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_Valley_Province "Rift Valley Province") was Kenya’s largest and most populous province, headquartered in [Nakuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakuru "Nakuru") and spanning over 182,000 square kilometers. The region remains the primary homeland of the Kalenjin people, who represent the area's largest ethnic group across its now-devolved counties.

Native to Eastern Africa, the Kalenjin primarily reside in the Rift Valley region of Kenya, specifically in areas formerly encompassing the [Rift Valley Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_Valley_Province "Rift Valley Province") in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") with substantial populations in the counties of [Kericho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kericho_County "Kericho County"), [Nandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandi_County "Nandi County"), [Bomet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomet_County "Bomet County"), [Baringo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baringo_County "Baringo County"), [Uasin Gishu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uasin_Gishu_County "Uasin Gishu County"), [Elgeyo-Marakwet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgeyo-Marakwet_County "Elgeyo-Marakwet County"), [West Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_County "West Pokot County"), [Trans Nzoia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans-Nzoia_County "Trans-Nzoia County"), [Nakuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakuru "Nakuru"), and [Narok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narok_County "Narok County"). In [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") the Kalenjin-related population primarily reside in the Eastern Region on the slopes of [Mount Elgon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Elgon "Mount Elgon") (Sabiny/Sebei) and the [Karamoja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karamoja "Karamoja") sub-region for (Pokot). They are estimated to be approximately 300,000 to 400,000 Kalenjin people in [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-28) with most belonging to the Sabiny ([Sebei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebei_people "Sebei people")) and [Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people") ethnic groups. In [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania"), they are concentrated in the [Manyara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manyara_Region "Manyara Region") and [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region") regions, as well as areas around Lake Eyasi (represented by the related Datooga groups). This expansion was driven by a period of Kalenjin military dominance, specifically through the Kipsigis' use of superior weaponry and tactics, utilizing heavy buffalo-hide shields and advanced close-combat techniques to overwhelm local defenses.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-21) These historical shifts defined the current borders, with these tribes now situated as their western and southern neighbors.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-:2-17)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-22) Scholars like Dr. Kipkoeech Arap Sambu have argued that many Kalenjin words have roots in [ancient Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egyptian "Ancient Egyptian") or [Semitic languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semitic_languages "Semitic languages"). For example, the Kalenjin word for land, _Emet_, is compared to the ancient Egyptian Kemet. Some theories suggest the ancestors of the Kalenjin left Egypt at the same time as the [Israelites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israelites "Israelites") but migrated south toward the Rift Valley while the Israelites moved north.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-theeastafrican.co.ke-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Sambu_2007-24)

According to Kalenjin [oral traditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_tradition "Oral tradition"), their ancestors are linked to the [ancient civilizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_civilizations "Ancient civilizations") of the Nile Valley, specifically an origin point known as _[Misiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misri\_legend "Misri legend")_ — often interpreted as ancient Egypt. Potential linguistic similarities, such as the Kalenjin sun deity _Asiis_ being compared to the [Egyptian goddess Isis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isis "Isis"), as evidence of a historical cultural link.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-25) Archaeological and linguistic evidence places the cradle of the Nilotic languages in the Nile Valley, which maintained strong cultural links with the societies of the Nubian Nile Valley further north.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Sirak_7283-26) These connections were reinforced by thousands of years of social and genetic intermixing, as evidenced by significant Nilotic-related ancestry found in ancient [Nubian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nubians "Nubians") populations. This shared heritage is reflected in similar [pastoral traditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoralism "Pastoralism"), [pottery styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottery "Pottery"), and burial customs across the broader [Nile Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_Basin "Nile Basin"). Following a southward migration that began around 500 BCE,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-Sirak_7283-26) they settled predominantly in the Rift Valley region of Kenya, with significant populations also residing in [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda"), [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania") and broader East Africa.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-study.com-27)

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Rift_Valley_in_Kenya.svg/250px-Rift_Valley_in_Kenya.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rift_Valley_in_Kenya.svg)

Prior to the [2010 Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kenya "Constitution of Kenya"), the [Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_Valley_Province "Rift Valley Province") was Kenya’s largest and most populous province, headquartered in [Nakuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakuru "Nakuru") and spanning over 182,000 square kilometers. The region remains the primary homeland of the Kalenjin people, who represent the area's largest ethnic group across its now-devolved counties.

Native to Eastern Africa, the Kalenjin primarily reside in the Rift Valley region of Kenya, specifically in areas formerly encompassing the [Rift Valley Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_Valley_Province "Rift Valley Province") in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") with substantial populations in the counties of [Kericho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kericho_County "Kericho County"), [Nandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandi_County "Nandi County"), [Bomet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomet_County "Bomet County"), [Baringo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baringo_County "Baringo County"), [Uasin Gishu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uasin_Gishu_County "Uasin Gishu County"), [Elgeyo-Marakwet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgeyo-Marakwet_County "Elgeyo-Marakwet County"), [West Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_County "West Pokot County"), [Trans Nzoia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans-Nzoia_County "Trans-Nzoia County"), [Nakuru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakuru "Nakuru"), and [Narok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narok_County "Narok County"). In [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") the Kalenjin-related population primarily reside in the Eastern Region on the slopes of [Mount Elgon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Elgon "Mount Elgon") (Sabiny/Sebei) and the [Karamoja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karamoja "Karamoja") sub-region for (Pokot). They are estimated to be approximately 300,000 to 400,000 Kalenjin people in [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalenjin_people#cite_note-28) with most belonging to the Sabiny ([Sebei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebei_people "Sebei people")) and [Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people") ethnic groups. In [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania"), they are concentrated in the [Manyara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manyara_Region "Manyara Region") and [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region") regions, as well as areas around Lake Eyasi (represented by the related Datooga groups). **Brussels**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-fn1-13) officially the **Brussels-Capital Region**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-fn2-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Belgian_Constitution-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-CIRB-creation-16) is a [region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium#Regions "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium") of [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") comprising [19 municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#Municipalities), including the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels"), which is the capital of Belgium.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-article_194-17) The Brussels-Capital Region is located in the central portion of the country. It is a part of both the [French Community of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Community_of_Belgium "French Community of Belgium")[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-d%C3%A9cret-18) and the [Flemish Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Community "Flemish Community"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-19) and is separate from the [Flemish Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Region "Flemish Region") (Flanders), within which it forms an [enclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enclave "Enclave"), and the [Walloon Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walloon_Region "Walloon Region") (Wallonia), located less than 4 km (2.5 mi) south.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-decreet-20)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-21)

Brussels grew from a small rural settlement on the river [Senne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senne_(river) "Senne (river)") to become an important city-region in Europe. Since the end of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), it has been a major centre for [international politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_politics "International politics") and home to numerous international organisations, politicians, [diplomats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomacy "Diplomacy") and [civil servants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_servant "Civil servant").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-BBC_Belgium-22) Brussels is the _[de facto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De\_facto "De facto")_ capital of the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), as it hosts a number of principal [EU institutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EU_institutions "EU institutions"), including its [administrative-legislative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission"), [executive-political](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Council "European Council"), and [legislative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Parliament "European Parliament") branches (though the judicial branch is located in [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg_City "Luxembourg City"), and the European Parliament meets for a minority of the year in [Strasbourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strasbourg "Strasbourg")).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDemey2007-1)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-12010E/PRO/06-23)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-24) Because of this, its name is sometimes used [metonymically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metonymy "Metonymy") to describe the EU and its institutions.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-25)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-26) The secretariat of the [Benelux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benelux "Benelux") and the [headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO_Headquarters "NATO Headquarters") of [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO") are also located in Brussels.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-27)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-28)

Brussels is the most densely populated region in Belgium, and although it has the highest [GDP per capita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP_per_capita "GDP per capita"),[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:4-29) it has the lowest disposable [household income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Household_income "Household income").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-statbel-30) The Brussels Region covers 162 km 2 (63 sq mi) and has a population of over 1.2 million.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:8-31) Its five times larger [metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_metropolitan_area "Brussels metropolitan area") comprises over 2.5 million people, which makes it the [largest in Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_areas_in_Belgium "Metropolitan areas in Belgium").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-BelMun2008-32)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-BelMetr-33)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:5-34) It is also part of a large [diamond-shaped conurbation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Diamond "Flemish Diamond"), extending towards the cities of [Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent "Ghent"), [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp") and [Leuven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leuven "Leuven"), as well as the province of [Walloon Brabant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walloon_Brabant "Walloon Brabant"), in total home to over 5 million people.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVan_MeeterenBoussauwDerudderWitlox2016-35) As Belgium's economic capital and a top financial centre in Western Europe with [Euronext Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euronext_Brussels "Euronext Brussels"), Brussels is classified as an _Alpha-_[global city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_city "Global city").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-36) It is also a national and international hub for rail, road and air traffic,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-37) and is sometimes considered, together with Belgium, as Europe's geographic, economic and cultural crossroads.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-38)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-39)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-40) The [Brussels Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro") is the only [rapid transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_transit "Rapid transit") system in Belgium. In addition, both [its airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airport "Brussels Airport") and [railway stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_railway_stations_in_Belgium "List of railway stations in Belgium") are the busiest in the country.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:2-41)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-42)

Historically Dutch-speaking, Brussels saw a [language shift to French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francization_of_Brussels "Francization of Brussels") from the late 19th century.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-43) Since its creation in 1989, the Brussels-Capital Region has been officially bilingual in French and Dutch,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-44)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-45) although French is the majority language and _[lingua franca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingua\_franca "Lingua franca")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-BruS13EN-46) Brussels is also increasingly becoming multilingual. English is spoken widely and many migrants and [expatriates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expatriate "Expatriate") speak other languages as well.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-BruS13EN-46)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:7-47) The Region is governed by the [Dilliès government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilli%C3%A8s_government "Dilliès government"), a broad bilingual coalition of seven parties.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:10-48)

Brussels is known for its cuisine and gastronomic offer (including its [local waffle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waffle#Brussels "Waffle"), its [chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_chocolate "Belgian chocolate"), its [French fries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_fries "French fries") and its numerous types of [beers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer_in_Belgium "Beer in Belgium")),[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-49) as well as its historical and architectural landmarks; some of them are registered as [UNESCO World Heritage Sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-50) Principal attractions include its historic [Grand-Place/Grote Markt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place") (main square), _[Manneken Pis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manneken\_Pis "Manneken Pis")_, the [Atomium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomium "Atomium"), and cultural institutions such as [La Monnaie/De Munt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Monnaie/De_Munt "La Monnaie/De Munt") and the [Museums of Art and History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Museums_of_Art_and_History "Royal Museums of Art and History"). Due to its long tradition of [Belgian comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_comics "Belgian comics"), Brussels is also hailed as a capital of the [comic strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_strip "Comic strip").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Comic-3)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:1-51)

The most common theory of the origin of the name _Brussels_ is that it derives from the [Old Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Dutch "Old Dutch")_Bruocsella_, _Broekzele_ or _Broeksel_, meaning 'marsh' (_bruoc_ / _broek_) and 'home, settlement' (_sella_ / _zele_ / _sel_) or 'settlement in the marsh'.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-52)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-vgc-53) Saint [Vindicianus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vindicianus "Vindicianus"), the Bishop of [Cambrai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambrai "Cambrai"), made the first recorded reference to the place _Brosella_ in 695,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-54) when it was still a [hamlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamlet_(place) "Hamlet (place)"). The names of all the municipalities in the Brussels-Capital Region are also of Dutch origin, except for [Evere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evere "Evere"), which is possibly [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_languages "Celtic languages") or [Old Frankish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Frankish "Old Frankish").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTETribotDefawe20063-55)

In French, _Bruxelles_ is pronounced [[bʁysɛl]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/6/67/Fr-Bruxelles.ogg/Fr-Bruxelles.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fr-Bruxelles.ogg "File:Fr-Bruxelles.ogg") (the _x_ is pronounced and the final _s_ is silent) and in Dutch, _Brussel_ is pronounced [[ˈbrʏsəl]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/d/d0/Nl-Brussel.ogg/Nl-Brussel.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nl-Brussel.ogg "File:Nl-Brussel.ogg"). Inhabitants of Brussels are known in French as _Bruxellois_ (pronounced [[bʁysɛlwa]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/c1/Fr-bruxellois.ogg/Fr-bruxellois.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fr-bruxellois.ogg "File:Fr-bruxellois.ogg")) and in Dutch as _Brusselaars_ (pronounced [[ˈbrʏsəlaːrs]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")). In the [Brabantian dialect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabantian_dialect "Brabantian dialect") of Brussels (known as [Brusselian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brusselian_dialect "Brusselian dialect"), and also sometimes referred to as [Marollian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marollian_dialect "Marollian dialect")),[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTETreffers-Daller199425-56) they are called _Brusseleers_ or _Brusseleirs_.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-evans-57)

Originally, the written _x_ was pronounced . In the [Belgian French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_French "Belgian French") pronunciation as well as in Dutch, the _k_ eventually disappeared, as reflected in the current [Dutch spelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_spelling "Dutch spelling"), whereas in the more conservative [French form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_orthography "French orthography"), the spelling remained.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-58) The pronunciation in French only dates from the 18th century,[_[contradictory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:All\_self-contradictory\_articles "Category:All self-contradictory articles")_] but this modification did not affect the traditional Brussels usage. In France, the pronunciations [[bʁyksɛl]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/8/8b/Fr-Bruxelles.oga/Fr-Bruxelles.oga.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fr-Bruxelles.oga "File:Fr-Bruxelles.oga") and [[bʁyksɛlwa]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French") (for _bruxellois_) are often heard, but are rather rare in Belgium.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Lerond,_1980_pp._477-59)

The history of Brussels is closely linked to that of [Western Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Europe "Western Europe"). Traces of human settlement go back to the [Stone Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_Age "Stone Age"), with vestiges and place-names related to the civilisation of [megaliths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megalith "Megalith"), [dolmens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolmen "Dolmen") and [standing stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_stones "Standing stones") (Plattesteen near the [Grand-Place/Grote Markt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place") and [Tomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomberg_metro_station "Tomberg metro station") in [Woluwe-Saint-Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woluwe-Saint-Lambert "Woluwe-Saint-Lambert"), for example). During [late antiquity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_antiquity "Late antiquity"), the region was home to [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire "Roman Empire") occupation, as attested by archaeological evidence discovered on the current site of [Tour & Taxis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_&_Taxis "Tour & Taxis"), north-west of the [Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentagon_(Brussels) "Pentagon (Brussels)") (Brussels' city centre).[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-60)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-61) Following the decline of the [Western Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Roman_Empire "Western Roman Empire"), it was incorporated into the [Frankish Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankish_Empire "Frankish Empire").

According to local legend, the origin of the settlement that was to become Brussels lies in Saint [Gaugericus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaugericus "Gaugericus")' construction of a chapel on [an island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-G%C3%A9ry_Island "Saint-Géry Island") in the river [Senne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senne_(river) "Senne (river)") around 580.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEState2004269-62) The official founding of Brussels is usually said to be around 979, when [Charles, Duke of Lower Lorraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles,_Duke_of_Lower_Lorraine "Charles, Duke of Lower Lorraine"), transferred the [relics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relic "Relic") of the [martyr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martyr "Martyr") Saint [Gudula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudula "Gudula") from [Moorsel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moorsel "Moorsel") (located in today's province of [East Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Flanders "East Flanders")) to Saint Gaugericus' chapel. When [Otto II, Holy Roman Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_II,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Otto II, Holy Roman Emperor"), appointed the same Charles to become Duke of [Lower Lotharingia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Lotharingia "Lower Lotharingia") in 977,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTERich%C3%A91983276-63) Charles ordered the construction of the city's first permanent fortification, doing so on that same island.

[Lambert I, Count of Louvain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambert_I,_Count_of_Louvain "Lambert I, Count of Louvain"), gained the County of Brussels around 1000 by marrying Charles' daughter. Because of its location on the banks of the Senne, on an [important trade route](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brabant_Road "Brabant Road") between the [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Flanders "County of Flanders") cities of [Bruges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruges "Bruges") and [Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent "Ghent"), and [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne") in the [Kingdom of Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Germany "Kingdom of Germany"), Brussels became a commercial centre specialised in the textile trade. The town grew quite rapidly and extended towards the upper town (Treurenberg, [Coudenberg/Koudenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coudenberg "Coudenberg"), and [Sablon/Zavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sablon,_Brussels "Sablon, Brussels") areas), where there was a reduced risk of floods. As the town grew to a population of around 30,000, the surrounding marshes were drained to allow for further expansion. In 1183, the Counts of Leuven became [Dukes of Brabant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dukes_of_Brabant "Dukes of Brabant"). Brabant, unlike the county of Flanders, was not fief of the king of France but was incorporated into the [Holy Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire "Holy Roman Empire").

In the early 13th century, the [first walls of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_walls_of_Brussels "First walls of Brussels") were built[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-64) and after this, the city grew significantly. Around this time, work began on what is now the [Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_of_St._Michael_and_St._Gudula "Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula") (1225), replacing an older [Romanesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanesque_architecture "Romanesque architecture") church.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrigode1938185%E2%80%93215-65) To let the city expand, [a second set of walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_walls_of_Brussels "Second walls of Brussels") was erected between 1356 and 1383. Traces of these walls can still be seen; the [Small Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_Ring,_Brussels "Small Ring, Brussels"), a series of boulevards bounding the historical city centre, follows their former course.

View of Brussels, c.1610

In the 14th century, the marriage between heiress [Margaret III, Countess of Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_III,_Countess_of_Flanders "Margaret III, Countess of Flanders"), and [Philip the Bold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_the_Bold "Philip the Bold"), [Duke of Burgundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_of_Burgundy "Duke of Burgundy"), produced a new Duke of Brabant of the [House of Valois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Valois "House of Valois"), namely [Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony,_Duke_of_Brabant "Anthony, Duke of Brabant"), their son.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlockmansPrevenier199930%E2%80%9331-66) In 1477, the Burgundian duke [Charles the Bold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_the_Bold "Charles the Bold") perished in the [Battle of Nancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Nancy "Battle of Nancy").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKirk1868542-67) Through the marriage of his daughter [Mary of Burgundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_of_Burgundy "Mary of Burgundy") (who was born in Brussels) to Holy Roman Emperor [Maximilian I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximilian_I,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor"), the [Low Countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Countries "Low Countries") fell under [Habsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habsburg "Habsburg") sovereignty.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEArmstrong1957228-68) Brabant was integrated into this composite state, and Brussels flourished as the Princely Capital of the prosperous [Burgundian Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burgundian_Netherlands "Burgundian Netherlands"), also known as the [Seventeen Provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen_Provinces "Seventeen Provinces"). After the death of Mary in 1482, her son [Philip the Handsome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_the_Handsome "Philip the Handsome") succeeded as Duke of Burgundy and Brabant.

Philip died in 1506, and he was succeeded by his son [Charles V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor") who then also became [King of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Spain "King of Spain") (crowned in the [Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_of_St._Michael_and_St._Gudula "Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula")) and even Holy Roman Emperor at the death of his grandfather Maximilian I in 1519. Charles was now the ruler of a [Habsburg Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habsburg_Empire "Habsburg Empire") "on which the sun never sets" with Brussels serving as one of his main capitals.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Capital-2)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-69) It was in the [Coudenberg Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coudenberg_Palace "Coudenberg Palace") that Charles V was declared of age in 1515, and it was there in 1555 that he abdicated all of his possessions and passed the [Habsburg Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habsburg_Netherlands "Habsburg Netherlands") to King [Philip II of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_II_of_Spain "Philip II of Spain").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWasseige19954-70) This palace, famous all over Europe, had greatly expanded since it had first become the seat of the Dukes of Brabant, but it was destroyed by fire in 1731.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMardaga1994222-71)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWasseige19956%E2%80%937-72)
