Brussels has a number of public or private-owned [libraries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libraries "Libraries") on its territory.[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-318) Most public libraries in Brussels fall under the competence of the Communities and are usually separated between French-speaking and Dutch-speaking institutions, although some are mixed.[_[verification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

The [Royal Library of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Library_of_Belgium "Royal Library of Belgium") (KBR) is the [national library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_library "National library") of Belgium and one of the most prestigious libraries in the world. It owns several collections of historical importance, like the [Fétis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9tis "Fétis") archives, and is the depository for all books ever published in Belgium or abroad by Belgian authors. It is located on the [Mont des Arts/Kunstberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mont_des_Arts "Mont des Arts") in central Brussels, near the [Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Central_Station "Brussels Central Station").[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-319)

There are several academic libraries and archives in Brussels. The libraries of the [Université libre de Bruxelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_libre_de_Bruxelles "Université libre de Bruxelles") (ULB) and the [Vrije Universiteit Brussel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vrije_Universiteit_Brussel "Vrije Universiteit Brussel") (VUB) constitute the largest ensemble of university libraries in the city. In addition to the Solbosch location, there are branches in [La Plaine/Het Plein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbourhoods_in_Brussels#La_Plaine/Het_Plein "Neighbourhoods in Brussels") and [Erasme/Erasmus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus_metro_station "Erasmus metro station").[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-320)[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-321) Other academic libraries include those of [Saint-Louis University, Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Louis_University,_Brussels "Saint-Louis University, Brussels")[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-322) and the [Catholic University of Louvain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universit%C3%A9_catholique_de_Louvain "Université catholique de Louvain") (UCLouvain).[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-323)

### Science and technology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=48 "Edit section: Science and technology")]

[![Image 133](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Planetarium_Royal_Observatory_Belgium.jpg/250px-Planetarium_Royal_Observatory_Belgium.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Planetarium_Royal_Observatory_Belgium.jpg)

[Planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium_(Belgium) "Planetarium (Belgium)") of the [Royal Observatory of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Observatory_of_Belgium "Royal Observatory of Belgium")

Science and technology in Brussels is well-developed with the presence of several [universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_universities_in_Belgium "List of universities in Belgium") and research institutes. The Brussels-Capital Region is home to several national science and technology institutes including the [National Fund for Scientific Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Fund_for_Scientific_Research "National Fund for Scientific Research") (NFSR), the Institute for the Encouragement of Scientific Research and Innovation of Brussels (ISRIB), the [Royal Academies for Science and the Arts of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Academies_for_Science_and_the_Arts_of_Belgium "Royal Academies for Science and the Arts of Belgium") (RASAB) and the [Belgian Academy Council of Applied Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Academy_Council_of_Applied_Sciences "Belgian Academy Council of Applied Sciences") (BACAS). Several science parks associated with the universities are also spread over the region.

The [Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Belgian_Institute_of_Natural_Sciences "Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences"), located in [Leopold Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_Park "Leopold Park"), houses the world's largest hall completely dedicated to [dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur "Dinosaur"), with its collection of 30 [fossilised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil "Fossil")_[Iguanodon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iguanodon "Iguanodon")_ skeletons.[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-324) In addition, the [Planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium_(Belgium) "Planetarium (Belgium)") of the [Royal Observatory of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Observatory_of_Belgium "Royal Observatory of Belgium") (part of the institutions of the [Belgian Federal Science Policy Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Federal_Science_Policy_Office "Belgian Federal Science Policy Office")), on the [Heysel Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heysel_Plateau "Heysel Plateau") in [Laeken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laeken "Laeken"), is one of the largest in Europe.[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-325)

[![Image 134](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/H%C3%B4pital_Erasme_Haupteingang.jpg/250px-H%C3%B4pital_Erasme_Haupteingang.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:H%C3%B4pital_Erasme_Haupteingang.jpg)

[Erasmus Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasmus_Hospital "Erasmus Hospital") in [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderlecht "Anderlecht")

Brussels is home to a thriving [pharmaceutical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry "Pharmaceutical industry") and [health care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_care "Health care") industry, which includes pioneering [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology "Biotechnology") research. The health sector employs 70,000 employees in 30,000 companies. There are 3,000 life sciences researchers in the city and two large [science parks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_park "Science park"): Da Vinci Research Park and Erasmus Research Park. There are five [university hospitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_hospitals "University hospitals"), a [military hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_hospital "Military hospital") and more than 40 general hospitals and specialist clinics.[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-326)

Due to [its bilingual nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Belgium "Languages of Belgium"), hospitals in the Brussels-Capital Region can be either monolingual French, monolingual Dutch, or bilingual, depending on their nature. University hospitals belong to one of the two [linguistic communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium") and are thus monolingual French or Dutch by law. Other hospitals managed by a public authority must be legally bilingual. Private hospitals are legally not bound to either language, but most cater to both. However, all hospital emergency services in the Capital Region (whether part of a public or private hospital) are required to be bilingual, since patients transported by emergency [ambulance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambulance "Ambulance") cannot choose the hospital they will be brought to.[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-327)

Brussels has an extensive network of both private or public transportation means. Public transportation includes [Brussels buses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_buses "Brussels buses"), [trams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_trams "Brussels trams"), and [metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro") (all three operated by the [Brussels Intercommunal Transport Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Intercommunal_Transport_Company "Brussels Intercommunal Transport Company") (STIB/MIVB)), as well as a set of railway lines (operated by [Infrabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrabel "Infrabel")) and railway stations served by public trains (operated by the [National Railway Company of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Railway_Company_of_Belgium "National Railway Company of Belgium") (SNCB/NMBS)). Air transport is available via one of the city's two airports ([Brussels Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airport "Brussels Airport") and [Brussels South Charleroi Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_South_Charleroi_Airport "Brussels South Charleroi Airport")), and boat transport is available via the [Port of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Brussels "Port of Brussels"). Bicycle-sharing and car-sharing public systems are also available.

The complexity of the Belgian political landscape makes some transportation issues difficult to solve. The Brussels-Capital Region is surrounded by the [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_Region "Flemish Region") and [Walloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia") regions, which means that the airports, as well as many roads serving Brussels (most notably the [Brussels Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Ring "Brussels Ring")), are located in the other two Belgian regions. The city is relatively car-dependent by northern European standards and is considered to be the most congested city in the world according to the [INRIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INRIX "INRIX") traffic survey.[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-auto-328)

[![Image 135](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Brussels_Airlines_A319-112_%28OO-SSG%29_landing_at_Brussels_Airport_%281%29.jpg/250px-Brussels_Airlines_A319-112_%28OO-SSG%29_landing_at_Brussels_Airport_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brussels_Airlines_A319-112_(OO-SSG)_landing_at_Brussels_Airport_(1).jpg)

[Brussels Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airlines "Brussels Airlines")[Airbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus "Airbus") A319 landing at [Brussels Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airport "Brussels Airport") in [Zaventem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaventem "Zaventem")

The Brussels-Capital Region is served by two airports, both located outside of the region's administrative territory. The most notable is [Brussels Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Airport "Brussels Airport"), located in the nearby Flemish municipality of [Zaventem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaventem "Zaventem"), 12 km (10 mi) east of the capital, which can be accessed by motorway (A201), train, taxi and bus. Brussels National Airport has its own railway station. This station is located in the underground (level -1) of the airport terminal building itself. The secondary airport is [Brussels South Charleroi Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_South_Charleroi_Airport "Brussels South Charleroi Airport"), located in [Gosselies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gosselies "Gosselies"), a part of the city of [Charleroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleroi "Charleroi") ([Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia")), some 50 km (30 mi) south-west of Brussels, which can be accessed by motorway (E19 then E420) or a private bus. There is also [Melsbroek Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melsbroek_Air_Base "Melsbroek Air Base"), located in [Steenokkerzeel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steenokkerzeel "Steenokkerzeel"), a military airport that shares its infrastructure with Brussels Airport. The aforementioned airports are also the main airports of Belgium.[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-329)

[![Image 136](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Bassin_de_Biestebroeck_%28DSC_4024%29.jpg/250px-Bassin_de_Biestebroeck_%28DSC_4024%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bassin_de_Biestebroeck_(DSC_4024).jpg)

View along the [Brussels–Charleroi Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%E2%80%93Charleroi_Canal "Brussels–Charleroi Canal") in [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderlecht "Anderlecht")

Since the 16th century, Brussels has had its own harbour, the [Port of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Brussels "Port of Brussels"). It has been enlarged throughout the centuries to become the second Belgian inland port. Historically situated near the [Place Sainte-Catherine/Sint-Katelijneplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_Sainte-Catherine "Place Sainte-Catherine"), it lies today to the north-west of the region, on the [Brussels–Scheldt Maritime Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%E2%80%93Scheldt_Maritime_Canal "Brussels–Scheldt Maritime Canal") (commonly called Willebroek Canal), which connects Brussels to [Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp "Antwerp") via the [Scheldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scheldt "Scheldt"). Ships and large barges up to 4,500 t (9,900,000 lb) can penetrate deep into the country, avoiding break-ups and load transfers between Antwerp and the centre of Brussels, hence reducing the cost for companies using the canal, and thus offering a competitive advantage.

Moreover, the connection of the Willebroek Canal with the [Brussels–Charleroi Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels%E2%80%93Charleroi_Canal "Brussels–Charleroi Canal"), in the very heart of the capital, creates a north–south link, by means of waterways, between the Netherlands, Flanders and the industrial zone of [Hainaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hainaut_(province) "Hainaut (province)") ([Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia")). There, navigation can access the network of French canals, thanks to the important [inclined plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canal_inclined_plane "Canal inclined plane") of [Ronquières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronqui%C3%A8res_inclined_plane "Ronquières inclined plane") and the lifts of [Strépy-Bracquegnies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Str%C3%A9py-Bracquegnies "Strépy-Bracquegnies").

The importance of river traffic in Brussels makes it possible to avoid the road equivalent of 740,000 trucks per year—almost 2,000 per day—which, in addition to easing traffic problems, represents an estimated carbon dioxide saving of 51,545 tonnes (113,637,000 lb) per year.[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-330)

[![Image 137](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Station_Brussel-Zuid_Hoofdgang.jpg/250px-Station_Brussel-Zuid_Hoofdgang.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Station_Brussel-Zuid_Hoofdgang.jpg)

Main hall of [Brussels-South railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-South_railway_station "Brussels-South railway station"), home to the [Eurostar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostar "Eurostar") train service to London

The Brussels-Capital Region has three main train stations: [Brussels-South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-South_railway_station "Brussels-South railway station"), [Brussels-Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Central "Brussels-Central") and [Brussels-North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-North_railway_station "Brussels-North railway station"), which are also the busiest of the country.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-:2-41) Brussels-South is also served by direct high-speed rail links: to London by [Eurostar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostar "Eurostar") trains via the [Channel Tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_Tunnel "Channel Tunnel"); to [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam")[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-331) by Eurostar "Red" (previously [Thalys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thalys "Thalys")) and _[InterCity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InterCity "InterCity")_ connections; to Amsterdam, Paris, and [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne") by Eurostar; and to Cologne and [Frankfurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt "Frankfurt") by the German [ICE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercity_Express "Intercity Express").

The train rails in Brussels go underground, near the centre, through the [North–South connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North%E2%80%93South_connection "North–South connection"), with Brussels Central Station also being largely underground. The tunnel itself is only six tracks wide at its narrowest point, which often causes congestion and delays due to heavy use of the route.

The [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels") has minor railway stations at [Bockstael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bockstael_railway_station "Bockstael railway station"), [Brussels-Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Chapel_railway_station "Brussels-Chapel railway station"), [Brussels-Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Congress_railway_station "Brussels-Congress railway station"), [Brussels-Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-Luxembourg_railway_station "Brussels-Luxembourg railway station"), [Brussels-Schuman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schuman_station "Schuman station"), [Brussels-West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels-West_station "Brussels-West station"), [Haren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haren_railway_station_(Brussels) "Haren railway station (Brussels)"), [Haren-South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haren-South_railway_station "Haren-South railway station") and [Simonis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simonis_metro_station "Simonis metro station"). In the Brussels Region, there are also railways stations at [Berchem-Sainte-Agathe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berchem-Sainte-Agathe_railway_station "Berchem-Sainte-Agathe railway station"), [Boitsfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boitsfort_railway_station "Boitsfort railway station"), [Boondael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boondael_railway_station "Boondael railway station"), [Bordet (Evere)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordet_railway_station "Bordet railway station"), [Etterbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etterbeek_railway_station "Etterbeek railway station"), [Evere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evere_railway_station "Evere railway station"), [Forest-East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest-East_railway_station "Forest-East railway station"), [Forest-South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest-South_railway_station "Forest-South railway station"), [Jette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jette_railway_station "Jette railway station"), [Meiser (Schaerbeek)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiser_railway_station "Meiser railway station"), [Moensberg (Uccle)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moensberg_railway_station "Moensberg railway station"), [Saint-Job (Uccle)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Job_railway_station "Saint-Job railway station"), [Schaarbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schaerbeek_railway_station "Schaerbeek railway station"), [Uccle-Calevoet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uccle-Calevoet_railway_station "Uccle-Calevoet railway station"), [Uccle-Stalle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uccle-Stalle_railway_station "Uccle-Stalle railway station"), Vivier d'Oie-Diesdelle (Uccle), [Merode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merode_station "Merode station") and [Watermael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watermael_railway_station "Watermael railway station").

The [Brussels Intercommunal Transport Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Intercommunal_Transport_Company "Brussels Intercommunal Transport Company") (STIB/MIVB) is the local [public transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_transport "Public transport") operator in Brussels. It covers the 19 municipalities of the Brussels-Capital Region and some surface routes extend to the near suburbs in the other two regions, linking with the [De Lijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Lijn "De Lijn") network in [Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders") and the [TEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TEC_(transport) "TEC (transport)") network in [Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia").

#### Metro, trams and buses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=55 "Edit section: Metro, trams and buses")]

[![Image 138](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Rame_%22Boa%22.jpg/250px-Rame_%22Boa%22.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rame_%22Boa%22.jpg)

[Brussels Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro") carriage at [Erasme/Erasmus metro station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erasme/Erasmus_metro_station "Erasme/Erasmus metro station")

The [Brussels Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro") dates back to 1976,[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-332) but underground lines known as the _[premetro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels\_premetro "Brussels premetro")_ have been serviced by tramways since 1968. It is the only [rapid transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_transit "Rapid transit") system in Belgium ([Antwerp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antwerp_Pre-metro "Antwerp Pre-metro") and [Charleroi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9tro_L%C3%A9ger_de_Charleroi "Métro Léger de Charleroi") both having [light rail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_rail "Light rail") systems). The network consists of four conventional metro lines and three _premetro_ lines. The metro-grade lines are [M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_1 "Brussels Metro line 1"), [M2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_2 "Brussels Metro line 2"), [M5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_5 "Brussels Metro line 5"), and [M6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_6 "Brussels Metro line 6"), with some shared sections, covering a total of 40 km (25 mi).[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-The_network_and_vehicles-333)As of 2017, the Metro network within the region has a total of [69 metro and _premetro_ stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Brussels_Metro_stations "List of Brussels Metro stations"). The Metro is an important [means of transport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_in_Brussels "Transport in Brussels"), connecting with six [railway stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railway_station "Railway station") of the [National Railway Company of Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Railway_Company_of_Belgium "National Railway Company of Belgium") (SNCB/NMBS), and many tram and bus stops operated by STIB/MIVB, as well as with [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders")[De Lijn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Lijn "De Lijn") and [Walloon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia")[TEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TEC_(transport) "TEC (transport)") bus stops.

A comprehensive [bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_buses "Brussels buses") and [tram network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_trams "Brussels trams") covers the region. As of 2017, the Brussels tram system consists of 17 tram lines (three of which – lines [T4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_tram_route_4 "Brussels tram route 4"), [T7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_tram_route_7 "Brussels tram route 7") and T10 – qualify as _premetro_ lines that partly travel over underground sections that were intended to be eventually converted into metro lines).[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-newscientist-334) The total route length is 139 km (86 mi),[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-The_network_and_vehicles-333) making it one of the largest tram networks in Europe. The Brussels bus network is complementary to the rail network. It consists of 50 bus routes and 11 night routes, spanning 445 km (277 mi).[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-The_network_and_vehicles-333)

Since April 2007, STIB/MIVB has also been operating a night bus network called Noctis on Friday and Saturday nights from midnight until 3 a.m.[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-noctisbrus-335) The service consists of 11 routes (N04, N05, N06, N08, N09, N10, N11, N12, N13, N16 and N18).[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-336) The fare on these night buses is the same as during the day. All the lines leave from the [Place de la Bourse/Beursplein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Place_de_la_Bourse,_Brussels "Place de la Bourse, Brussels") in the city centre at 30 minutes intervals and cover all the main streets in the capital, as they radiate outwards to the suburbs.[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-337) Noctis services returned from 2 July 2021 after over a year of disruption due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Belgium "COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium").[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-noctisbrus-335)

#### Other public transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=56 "Edit section: Other public transport")]

[![Image 139](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/VilloStationAlmostFull.jpg/250px-VilloStationAlmostFull.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:VilloStationAlmostFull.jpg)

[Villo!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villo! "Villo!")[shared bicycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shared_bicycle "Shared bicycle") in Brussels

Since 2003, Brussels has had a car-sharing service operated by the [Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bremen "Bremen") company Cambio, in partnership with STIB/MIVB and the local ridesharing company Taxi Stop.[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-338) In 2006, a [public bicycle-sharing programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_bicycle_program "Community bicycle program") was introduced. The scheme was subsequently taken over by [Villo!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villo! "Villo!"). Since 2008, this night-time public transport service has been supplemented by Collecto, a shared taxi system, which operates on weekdays between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m.[[334]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-339) In 2012, the Zen Car electric car-sharing scheme was launched in the university and European areas, though it ceased operating in the city in 2020.[[335]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-340)

[![Image 140](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Wetstraat.jpg/250px-Wetstraat.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wetstraat.jpg)

The [Rue de la Loi/Wetstraat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rue_de_la_Loi "Rue de la Loi") is one of the city's main streets.

In medieval times, Brussels stood at the intersection of routes running north–south (the modern Rue Haute/Hoogstraat) and east–west (Chaussée de Gand/Gentsesteenweg–Rue du Marché aux Herbes/Grasmarkt–Rue de Namur/Naamsestraat). The ancient pattern of streets, radiating from the [Grand-Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand-Place "Grand-Place"), in large part remains, but has been overlaid by boulevards built [over the river Senne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covering_of_the_Senne "Covering of the Senne"), [over the city walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortifications_of_Brussels#Construction_of_the_Small_Ring "Fortifications of Brussels") and over the railway connection between the North and South Stations. In 2012, Brussels had the most congested traffic in Europe and North America, according to US traffic information platform [INRIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INRIX "INRIX").[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-341)

Brussels is the hub of a range of national roads, the main ones being clockwise: the [N1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N1_road_(Belgium) "N1 road (Belgium)") (N to [Breda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breda "Breda")), [N2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N2_road_(Belgium) "N2 road (Belgium)") (E to [Maastricht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maastricht "Maastricht")), [N3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N3_road_(Belgium) "N3 road (Belgium)") (E to [Aachen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aachen "Aachen")), [N4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N4_road_(Belgium) "N4 road (Belgium)") (SE to [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg_City "Luxembourg City")), [N5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N5_road_(Belgium) "N5 road (Belgium)") (S to [Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reims "Reims")), N6 (S to [Maubeuge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maubeuge "Maubeuge")), N7 (SW to [Lille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lille "Lille")), [N8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N8_road_(Belgium) "N8 road (Belgium)") (W to [Koksijde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koksijde "Koksijde")) and N9 (NW to [Ostend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostend "Ostend")).[[337]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-342) Usually named _chaussées_/_steenwegen_, these roads normally run in a straight line, but sometimes lose themselves in a maze of narrow shopping streets. The region is skirted by the [European route E19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E19 "European route E19") (N-S) and the [E40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E40 "European route E40") (E-W), while the [E411](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E411 "E411") leads away to the SE. Brussels has an [orbital motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbital_motorway "Orbital motorway"), numbered R0 (R-zero) and commonly referred to as the [Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Ring "Brussels Ring"). It is pear-shaped, as the southern side was never built as originally conceived, owing to residents' objections.

The city centre, sometimes known as the [Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentagon_(Brussels) "Pentagon (Brussels)"), is surrounded by an inner ring road, the [Small Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_Ring,_Brussels "Small Ring, Brussels") (French: _Petite Ceinture_, Dutch: _Kleine Ring_), a sequence of boulevards formally numbered R20. These were built upon the site of the [second set of city walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_walls_of_Brussels "Second walls of Brussels") following their demolition. The [Metro line 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro_line_2 "Brussels Metro line 2") runs alongside (not actually under) much of these. Since June 2015, a number of [central boulevards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Boulevards_of_Brussels "Central Boulevards of Brussels") inside the Pentagon have become car-free, limiting transit traffic through the old city.[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-343)

On the eastern side of the region, the R21 or [Greater Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_ring_(Brussels) "Greater ring (Brussels)") (French: _Grande Ceinture_, Dutch: _Grote Ring_) is formed by a string of boulevards that curves round from [Laeken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laeken "Laeken") to [Uccle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uccle "Uccle"). Some _premetro_ stations (see [Brussels Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_Metro "Brussels Metro")) were built on that route. A little further out, a stretch numbered R22 leads from Zaventem to [Saint-Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Job_railway_station "Saint-Job railway station").

## Security and emergency services

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=58 "Edit section: Security and emergency services")]

[![Image 141](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/EPP_Summit_March_2012_%2848%29.jpg/250px-EPP_Summit_March_2012_%2848%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EPP_Summit_March_2012_(48).jpg)

Policeman in Brussels

The Brussels local police, supported by the federal police, is responsible for law enforcement in Brussels. The 19 municipalities of the Brussels-Capital Region are divided into six police zones,[[339]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-344) all bilingual (French and Dutch):

*   5339 Brussels Capital Ixelles: the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels") and [Ixelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ixelles "Ixelles")
*   5340 Brussels West: [Berchem-Sainte-Agathe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berchem-Sainte-Agathe "Berchem-Sainte-Agathe"), [Ganshoren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganshoren "Ganshoren"), [Jette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jette "Jette"), [Koekelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koekelberg "Koekelberg") and [Molenbeek-Saint-Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molenbeek-Saint-Jean "Molenbeek-Saint-Jean")
*   5341 South: [Anderlecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anderlecht "Anderlecht"), [Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest,_Belgium "Forest, Belgium") and [Saint-Gilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Gilles,_Belgium "Saint-Gilles, Belgium")
*   5342 Uccle/Watermael-Boitsfort/Auderghem: [Auderghem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auderghem "Auderghem"), [Uccle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uccle "Uccle") and [Watermael-Boitsfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watermael-Boitsfort "Watermael-Boitsfort")
*   5343 Montgomery: [Etterbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etterbeek "Etterbeek"), [Woluwe-Saint-Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woluwe-Saint-Lambert "Woluwe-Saint-Lambert") and [Woluwe-Saint-Pierre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woluwe-Saint-Pierre "Woluwe-Saint-Pierre")
*   5344 Polbruno: [Evere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evere "Evere"), [Saint-Josse-ten-Noode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Josse-ten-Noode "Saint-Josse-ten-Noode") and [Schaerbeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schaerbeek "Schaerbeek")

The Brussels Fire and Emergency Medical Care Service, commonly known by its acronym SIAMU (DBDMH), operates in the 19 municipalities of Brussels.[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-345) It is a class X fire department and the largest [fire service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_service "Fire service") in Belgium in terms of annual operations, equipment, and personnel. It has 9 [fire stations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_station "Fire station"), spread over the entire Brussels-Capital Region, and employs about 1,000 professional [firefighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firefighter "Firefighter"). As well as preventing and fighting fires, SIAMU also provides emergency medical care services in Brussels via its centralised 100 number (and the single 112 emergency number for the 27 countries of the European Union). It is bilingual (French–Dutch).

## Parks and green spaces

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Brussels&action=edit&section=61 "Edit section: Parks and green spaces")]

Brussels is one of the greenest capitals in Europe, with over 8,000 hectares of green spaces.[[341]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-346) Vegetation cover and natural areas are higher in the outskirts, where they have limited the [peri-urbanisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peri-urbanisation "Peri-urbanisation") of the capital, but they decrease sharply towards the centre of Brussels; 10% in the central [Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentagon_(Brussels) "Pentagon (Brussels)"), 30% of the municipalities in the first ring, and 71% of the municipalities in the second ring are occupied by green spaces.

Many parks and gardens, both public and privately owned, are scattered throughout the city. In addition to this, the [Sonian Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonian_Forest "Sonian Forest") is located in its southern part and stretches out over the three [Belgian regions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium#Regions "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium"). As of 2017, it has been inscribed as a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site"), the only Belgian component to the multinational inscription '[Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primeval_Beech_Forests_of_the_Carpathians_and_Other_Regions_of_Europe "Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe")'.[[342]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-347)

This article is about the Brussels-Capital Region. For the municipality within it, which is the de jure national capital, see [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels"). For other places, see [Brussels (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels_(disambiguation) "Brussels (disambiguation)").

"Bruxelles" redirects here. For the Canadian community, see [Bruxelles, Manitoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruxelles,_Manitoba "Bruxelles, Manitoba").

**Brussels**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-fn1-13) officially the **Brussels-Capital Region**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-fn2-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-Belgian_Constitution-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-CIRB-creation-16) is a [region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communities,_regions_and_language_areas_of_Belgium#Regions "Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium") of [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") comprising [19 municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#Municipalities), including the [City of Brussels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Brussels "City of Brussels"), which is the capital of Belgium.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brussels#cite_note-article_194-17) The Brussels-Capital Region is located in the central portion of the country. **Israel**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-29) officially the **State of Israel**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-30) is a country in the [Southern Levant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Levant "Southern Levant") region of [West Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia"). It is [bordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borders_of_Israel "Borders of Israel") by [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon "Lebanon") to the north, [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria") to the northeast, [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan "Jordan") to the east, and [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt") to the southwest. [Israel's western coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_coastal_plain "Israeli coastal plain") lies on the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea"), its southern tip reaches the [Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea"), and to the east is [Earth's lowest point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extremes_on_Earth "Extremes on Earth") near the [Dead Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea "Dead Sea"). [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem") is the government seat and [proclaimed capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_of_Jerusalem "Status of Jerusalem"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-31) while [Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv "Tel Aviv") is Israel's [largest urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gush_Dan "Gush Dan") and economic centre.

The [Land of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_of_Israel "Land of Israel"), also called [Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_(region) "Palestine (region)") or the [Holy Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Land "Holy Land"), was home to the ancient [Canaanites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canaan "Canaan") and later the kingdoms of [Israel and Judah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Israel_and_Judah "Ancient Israel and Judah") and [Hasmonean Judea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmonean_Judea "Hasmonean Judea"). Located near [continental crossroads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levantine_corridor "Levantine corridor"), its [demographics shifted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_Palestine_(region) "Demographic history of Palestine (region)") under various empires. 19th-century Jewish nationalism, alongside [European antisemitism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_antisemitism "European antisemitism"), fuelled the [Zionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionist "Zionist") movement for a [Jewish homeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_homeland "Jewish homeland") in Palestine, then an Ottoman region with an overwhelming Arab majority.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-32) The movement gained [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") support with the 1917 [Balfour Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balfour_Declaration "Balfour Declaration"). After [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), Britain occupied the region and established [Mandatory Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine "Mandatory Palestine"). British rule and [Jewish immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah "Aliyah") in the leadup to the Holocaust intensified [Arab-Jewish tensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercommunal_conflict_in_Mandatory_Palestine "Intercommunal conflict in Mandatory Palestine") with Arab opposition to Zionism driven largely by concerns of displacement and dispossession.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-33)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-34) The 1947 [UN Partition Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine "United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine") proposed separate Arab and Jewish states. The Jewish leadership accepted the plan while the Palestinian Arab leadership rejected it, arguing it violated the principle of [self-determination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-determination "Self-determination") and constituted Western colonial interference.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-35)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:0-36)[Civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947%E2%80%931948_civil_war_in_Mandatory_Palestine "1947–1948 civil war in Mandatory Palestine") followed, and Israel [declared independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence "Israeli Declaration of Independence") on 14 May 1948, shortly before the end of the [mandate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandate_for_Palestine "Mandate for Palestine"). The conflict subsequently escalated with the [intervention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War "1948 Arab–Israeli War") of [Arab states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world "Arab world").

The [1949 armistice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements "1949 Armistice Agreements") left Israel controlling more territory than had been allocated to it under the UN partition plan.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Britannica-37) No independent Palestinian Arab state was established, leaving [Gaza under Egyptian control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Gaza_Strip_by_the_United_Arab_Republic "Occupation of the Gaza Strip by the United Arab Republic") and the [West Bank ruled by Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordanian_annexation_of_the_West_Bank "Jordanian annexation of the West Bank").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Britannica-37)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-38)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFischbach200826%E2%80%9327-39) Most [Palestinian Arabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians")[fled or were expelled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Palestinian_expulsion_and_flight "1948 Palestinian expulsion and flight") during the [Nakba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakba "Nakba"),[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTESlater202081%E2%80%9392,_350-40)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-41)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-42) while Israeli independence prompted [antisemitism in the Arab world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism_in_the_Arab_world "Antisemitism in the Arab world") and [Jewish exodus therefrom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_exodus_from_the_Muslim_world "Jewish exodus from the Muslim world"), mainly to Israel.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:05-43)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:22-44) After the 1967 [Six-Day War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War "Six-Day War"), Israel occupied the West Bank, Gaza and Egyptian [Sinai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_the_Sinai_Peninsula "Israeli occupation of the Sinai Peninsula"), and annexed [East Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_annexation_of_East_Jerusalem "Israeli annexation of East Jerusalem") and the Syrian [Golan Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golan_Heights_Law "Golan Heights Law"). Peace treaties were signed with [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Israel_peace_treaty "Egypt–Israel peace treaty") in 1979 (the Sinai being returned in 1982) and [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Jordan_peace_treaty "Israel–Jordan peace treaty") in 1994. The 1993 [Oslo Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords "Oslo Accords") introduced limited [Palestinian self-rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Authority "Palestinian Authority") in the West Bank and Gaza, while the 2020 [Abraham Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Accords "Abraham Accords")[normalised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_normalization "Arab–Israeli normalization") ties with more Arab states, but the [Israeli–Palestinian conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_conflict "Israeli–Palestinian conflict") persists. Israel's [illegal occupation of the Palestinian territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories "Israeli-occupied territories") has drawn international criticism, with most Middle East experts arguing that Israel's treatment of Palestinians in the West Bank in relation to [Israeli settlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_settlement "Israeli settlement") constitutes a system of [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_apartheid "Israeli apartheid").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-sf-45)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:9-46) After the [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas")-led [October 7 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks "October 7 attacks"), Israel began committing [genocide against Palestinians in Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide "Gaza genocide").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-47) Israel and its allies, including the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), [deny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide_denial "Gaza genocide denial") that Israel's actions constitute genocide.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-48)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-49)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-50)

The [Basic Laws of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_Laws_of_Israel "Basic Laws of Israel") establish the [Knesset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knesset "Knesset") as a [proportionally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proportional_representation "Proportional representation") elected [parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system"). It shapes the [government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Israel "Cabinet of Israel"), led by the [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Israel "Prime Minister of Israel"), and elects the largely ceremonial [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Israel "President of Israel").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-cnn-51) Israel has one of the Middle East's largest economies,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-52)[one of Asia's highest living standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_in_Asia_and_Oceania_by_Human_Development_Index "List of countries in Asia and Oceania by Human Development Index"), and globally ranks [24th in nominal GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal) "List of countries by GDP (nominal)") and [13th in nominal GDP per capita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_GDP_(nominal)_per_capita "List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-IMFWEO.IL-26)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-53) One of the world's most [technologically advanced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_and_technology_in_Israel "Science and technology in Israel") countries,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-54) Israel allocates a larger share of [its economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Israel "Economy of Israel") to research and development [than any other state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_by_research_and_development_spending "List of sovereign states by research and development spending")[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-55)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-56) and is believed to [possess nuclear weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapons_of_Israel "Nuclear weapons of Israel"). The only country with a [revived](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_of_the_Hebrew_language "Revival of the Hebrew language") official language, [Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Hebrew "Modern Hebrew"), the [culture of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Israel "Culture of Israel") combines [Jewish traditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_culture "Jewish culture") with [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_culture "Arab culture") influences.

## Etymology

The names [Land of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_of_Israel "Land of Israel") and Children of Israel have historically been used to refer to the biblical [Kingdom of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Israel_(united_monarchy) "Kingdom of Israel (united monarchy)") and the entire [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews") people respectively. The [name _Israel_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_(name) "Israel (name)") (Hebrew: _Yīsrāʾēl_; [Septuagint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Septuagint "Septuagint")[Ancient Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἰσραήλ, _Israēl_, "[El (God)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_(deity) "El (deity)") persists/rules") refers to the patriarch [Jacob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob "Jacob") who, according to the [Hebrew Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_Bible "Hebrew Bible"), was given the name after he successfully [wrestled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_wrestling_with_the_angel "Jacob wrestling with the angel") with the [Angel of the Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel_of_the_Lord "Angel of the Lord").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-57) The earliest known archaeological artefact to mention the word _Israel_ as a collective is the [Merneptah Stele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merneptah_Stele "Merneptah Stele") of [ancient Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egypt "Ancient Egypt") (dated to the late-13th century BCE).[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-58)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-NollMerneptah-59)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-ThompsonMerneptah-60)[[fn 6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-62)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-63)

Under the [British Mandate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandate_for_Palestine "Mandate for Palestine") (1920–1948), the entire region was known as _Palestine_.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-64)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-65) Upon [establishment in 1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence "Israeli Declaration of Independence"), the country formally adopted the name _State of Israel_ ([Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language"): מְדִינַת יִשְׂרָאֵל, [_\_Medīnat Yisrā'el\__](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/9/93/He-Medinat_Israel.ogg/He-Medinat_Israel.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:He-Medinat_Israel.ogg "File:He-Medinat Israel.ogg")[[mediˈnat jisʁaˈʔel]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hebrew "Help:IPA/Hebrew"); [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): دَوْلَة إِسْرَائِيل, _\_Dawlat Isrāʼīl\__, [[dawlat ʔisraːˈʔiːl]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Arabic "Help:IPA/Arabic")) after other [proposed names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence#Name "Israeli Declaration of Independence") including _[Land of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land\_of\_Israel "Land of Israel")_ (_Eretz Israel_), _Ever_ (from ancestor [Eber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eber "Eber")), _[Zion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zion "Zion")_, and _[Judea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judea "Judea")_, were considered but rejected.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-66)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-67) The name _Israel_ was suggested by [David Ben-Gurion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ben-Gurion "David Ben-Gurion") and passed by a vote of 6–3.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-68)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-69) In the early weeks after establishment, the government chose the term _[Israeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israelis "Israelis")_ to denote a citizen of the state.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-70)

## History

### Prehistory

The [Ubeidiya prehistoric site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubeidiya_prehistoric_site "Ubeidiya prehistoric site") in northern Israel shows the [presence of archaic humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_expansions_of_hominins_out_of_Africa "Early expansions of hominins out of Africa") around 1.5 million years ago.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-71) The second-oldest evidence of [anatomically modern humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomically_modern_human "Anatomically modern human")[outside Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recent_African_origin_of_modern_humans "Recent African origin of modern humans") is a 200,000-year-old fossil from [Misliya Cave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misliya_Cave "Misliya Cave") on Mount Carmel.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-72) The [Natufian culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natufian_culture "Natufian culture") (c. 10,000 BCE) may be linked to the [Proto-Afroasiatic language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proto-Afroasiatic_language "Proto-Afroasiatic language")[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-73)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-74) and is notable for adopting [sedentism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedentism "Sedentism") before the [advent of agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origins_of_agriculture_in_West_Asia "Origins of agriculture in West Asia") and the [Neolithic Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neolithic_Revolution "Neolithic Revolution").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-75)

### Bronze and Iron Ages

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Ruins_atop_Tel_Megiddo_with_circular_altar-like_shrine_and_a_series_of_temples_on_top_of_the_other_dating_from_the_early_bronze-age_through_the_iron-age_periods%2C_Tel_Meggido%2C_Israel_%2819888642855%29.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ruins_atop_Tel_Megiddo_with_circular_altar-like_shrine_and_a_series_of_temples_on_top_of_the_other_dating_from_the_early_bronze-age_through_the_iron-age_periods,_Tel_Meggido,_Israel_(19888642855).jpg)

[Tel Megiddo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Megiddo "Tel Megiddo"), the ruins of a [Canaanite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canaan "Canaan") and later [Israelite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israelites "Israelites") city

Early references to "[Canaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canaan "Canaan")" and "Canaanites" appear in ancient [Near Eastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Near_East "Ancient Near East") and [Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egypt "Ancient Egypt") texts (c. 2000 BCE); these populations were structured as politically independent [city-states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-state "City-state").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-76)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-77) During the [Late Bronze Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Bronze_Age "Late Bronze Age") (1550–1200 BCE), large parts of Canaan formed [vassal states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vassal_state "Vassal state") of the [New Kingdom of Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Kingdom_of_Egypt "New Kingdom of Egypt").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-78) As a result of the [Late Bronze Age collapse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_Bronze_Age_collapse "Late Bronze Age collapse"), Canaan fell into chaos, and Egyptian control over the region collapsed.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-79)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-80) Ancestors of the [Israelites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israelites "Israelites") are thought to have included [ancient Semitic-speaking peoples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Semitic-speaking_peoples "Ancient Semitic-speaking peoples") native to this area.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Miller1986-81):78–79 Modern archaeological accounts suggest that the Israelites and their culture branched out of the Canaanite peoples through [the settlement of the central highlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israelite_highland_settlement "Israelite highland settlement") and the development of a distinct [monolatristic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monolatry "Monolatry")—and later [monotheistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monotheism "Monotheism")—religion centered on [Yahweh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahweh "Yahweh").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-82)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-83) They spoke an archaic form of [Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language"), known as [Biblical Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biblical_Hebrew "Biblical Hebrew").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-84) Around the same time, the [Philistines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philistines "Philistines") settled on the southern [coastal plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_coastal_plain "Israeli coastal plain").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKillebrew2005230-85)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShahin20056-86)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Mesad_Hashavyahu_ostracon.jpg/250px-Mesad_Hashavyahu_ostracon.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mesad_Hashavyahu_ostracon.jpg)

The [Yavne-Yam ostracon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yavne-Yam_ostracon "Yavne-Yam ostracon"), a [Paleo-Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleo-Hebrew_alphabet "Paleo-Hebrew alphabet") inscription documenting administration in [Judah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Judah "Kingdom of Judah")

Most modern scholars agree that the [Exodus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Exodus "The Exodus") narrative in the [Torah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torah "Torah") and [Old Testament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Testament "Old Testament") did not take place as depicted; however, some elements of these traditions do have [historical roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historicity_of_the_Bible "Historicity of the Bible").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-87)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-88) There is debate about the earliest existence of the [Kingdoms of Israel and Judah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_ancient_Israel_and_Judah "History of ancient Israel and Judah") and their extent and power. While it is unclear if there was a [United Kingdom of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Israel_(united_monarchy) "Kingdom of Israel (united monarchy)"),[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-lipschits-89)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Kuhrtp438-90) historians and archaeologists agree that the northern [Kingdom of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Israel_(Samaria) "Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)") existed by ca. 900 BCE[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Finkelstein-91):169–195 and the [Kingdom of Judah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Judah "Kingdom of Judah") by ca. 850 BCE.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Finkelstein,_Israel,_(2020)-92)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Pitcher-93) The Kingdom of Israel was the more prosperous of the two and soon developed into a regional power, with a capital at [Samaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samaria_(ancient_city) "Samaria (ancient city)");[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-94)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:04-95)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-96) during the [Omride dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omrides "Omrides"), it controlled [Samaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samaria "Samaria"), [Galilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galilee "Galilee"), the upper [Jordan Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Valley "Jordan Valley"), the [plain of Sharon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_plain "Sharon plain") and large parts of [Transjordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transjordan_(region) "Transjordan (region)").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:04-95) The Kingdom of Israel [was conquered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samerina "Samerina") around 720 BCE by the [Neo-Assyrian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire "Neo-Assyrian Empire").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Broshi_2001_174-97) The Kingdom of Judah, under [Davidic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davidic_line "Davidic line") rule with its capital in [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem"), later became a [client state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Client_state "Client state") of first the Neo-Assyrian Empire and then the [Neo-Babylonian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Babylonian_Empire "Neo-Babylonian Empire"). It is estimated that [the region's population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_Palestine_(region) "Demographic history of Palestine (region)") was around 400,000 in the [Iron Age II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age_II "Iron Age II").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:42-98) In 587/6 BCE, following a [revolt in Judah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judah's_revolts_against_Babylon "Judah's revolts against Babylon"), King [Nebuchadnezzar II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebuchadnezzar_II "Nebuchadnezzar II")[besieged and destroyed Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Jerusalem_(587_BC) "Siege of Jerusalem (587 BC)") and [Solomon's Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon's_Temple "Solomon's Temple"),[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-99)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-100) dissolved the kingdom and [exiled much of the Judean elite to Babylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babylonian_captivity "Babylonian captivity").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-101)

### Classical antiquity

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Monnaie_-_Prutah%2C_bronze%2C_J%C3%A9rusalem%2C_Jud%C3%A9e%2C_Mattathias_Antigonos_-_btv1b8480202s_%281_of_2%29.jpg/250px-Monnaie_-_Prutah%2C_bronze%2C_J%C3%A9rusalem%2C_Jud%C3%A9e%2C_Mattathias_Antigonos_-_btv1b8480202s_%281_of_2%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Monnaie_-_Prutah,_bronze,_J%C3%A9rusalem,_Jud%C3%A9e,_Mattathias_Antigonos_-_btv1b8480202s_(1_of_2).jpg)

[Hasmonean coin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmonean_coinage "Hasmonean coinage") of [Antigonus II Mattathias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigonus_II_Mattathias "Antigonus II Mattathias"), depicting the [Temple menorah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_menorah "Temple menorah")

After [capturing Babylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Babylon "Fall of Babylon") in 539 BCE, [Cyrus the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrus_the_Great "Cyrus the Great"), founder of the [Achaemenid Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achaemenid_Empire "Achaemenid Empire"), issued [a proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edict_of_Cyrus "Edict of Cyrus") allowing the exiled Judean population to return.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-rennert-102)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-103) The construction of the [Second Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Temple "Second Temple") was completed c.520 BCE.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-rennert-102) The Achaemenids ruled the region as the province of [Yehud Medinata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yehud_Medinata "Yehud Medinata").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Grabbe355-104) In 332 BCE, [Alexander the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great "Alexander the Great") conquered the region as part of his [campaign against the Achaemenid Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wars_of_Alexander_the_Great "Wars of Alexander the Great"). After his death, the area [was controlled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellenistic_Palestine "Hellenistic Palestine") by the [Ptolemaic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ptolemaic_Kingdom "Ptolemaic Kingdom") and [Seleucid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seleucid_Empire "Seleucid Empire") empires as a part of [Coele-Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coele-Syria "Coele-Syria"). Under the Hellenistic kingdoms, ongoing [Hellenisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellenization "Hellenization") generated cultural tensions among the Jewish population that culminated under [Antiochus IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiochus_IV_Epiphanes "Antiochus IV Epiphanes"), whose decrees outlawed Jewish practices and triggered the [Maccabean Revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabean_Revolt "Maccabean Revolt") in 167 BCE. The revolt weakened Seleucid control over Judea; by 142/141 BCE the [Hasmoneans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmonean_dynasty "Hasmonean dynasty") had secured autonomy and soon established an [independent Jewish kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmonean_Judea "Hasmonean Judea") that, in the late 2nd–early 1st century BCE, expanded into neighbouring territories.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-105)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-106)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-107) The [Hasmonean civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmonean_civil_war "Hasmonean civil war") ended with the [Roman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Republic "Roman Republic")[siege of Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Jerusalem_(63_BC) "Siege of Jerusalem (63 BC)") in 63 BCE.

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg/250px-Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Israel-2013-Aerial_21-Masada.jpg)

View of the [Masada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masada "Masada") fortress overlooking the [Dead Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea "Dead Sea"), which is the location of a [1st-century Roman siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Masada "Siege of Masada")

In 37 BCE, [Herod the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herod_the_Great "Herod the Great") was installed as a [dynastic vassal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herodian_dynasty "Herodian dynasty") of [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") following the [Roman–Parthian Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman%E2%80%93Parthian_Wars "Roman–Parthian Wars"). In 6 CE, the area was annexed as the [Roman province of Judaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaea_(Roman_province) "Judaea (Roman province)"); tensions with Roman rule led to a series of [Jewish–Roman wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish%E2%80%93Roman_wars "Jewish–Roman wars"), resulting in widespread destruction. The [First Jewish–Roman War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Jewish%E2%80%93Roman_War "First Jewish–Roman War") (66–73 CE) resulted in the [destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Jerusalem_(70_CE) "Siege of Jerusalem (70 CE)") and a sizable portion of the population being killed or displaced.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:8-108) A second uprising known as the [Bar Kokhba revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_Kokhba_revolt "Bar Kokhba revolt") (132–136 CE) initially allowed the Jews to form an independent state, but the Romans brutally crushed the rebellion, devastating and depopulating Judea's countryside.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:8-108)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-109)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-110)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:02-111)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-112) Jerusalem was rebuilt as a [Roman colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonia_(Roman) "Colonia (Roman)") ([Aelia Capitolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aelia_Capitolina "Aelia Capitolina")), and the province of Judea was renamed [Syria Palaestina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria_Palaestina "Syria Palaestina").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-H.H._Ben-Sasson,_1976,_page_334-113)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Ariel_Lewin_p._33-114) Jews were expelled from the districts surrounding Jerusalem.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:02-111)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-115) Nevertheless, there was a continuous small Jewish presence, and Galilee became its religious center.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-116)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-117)

### Late antiquity and the medieval period

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg/250px-Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar%27am.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ruins_of_the_Ancient_Synagogue_at_Bar'am.jpg)

3rd-century [Kfar Bar'am synagogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kfar_Bar'am_synagogue "Kfar Bar'am synagogue") in the Galilee[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-118)

During the [Byzantine period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_Palestine "Byzantine Palestine"), [Early Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christianity "Early Christianity") displaced [Roman paganism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religion_in_ancient_Rome "Religion in ancient Rome") in the 4th century CE, with [Constantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantine_the_Great "Constantine the Great") embracing and promoting the Christian religion and [Theodosius I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodosius_I "Theodosius I") making it [the state religion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_as_the_Roman_state_religion "Christianity as the Roman state religion"). A series of laws were passed that discriminated against Jews and Judaism, and Jews were persecuted by both the church and the authorities.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:3-119) Many Jews had emigrated to flourishing [diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_diaspora "Jewish diaspora") communities,[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:1-120) while locally there was both Christian immigration and local conversion. By the middle of the 5th century, there was a Christian majority.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-CHJ2-121)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-122) Towards the end of the 5th century, [Samaritan revolts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samaritan_revolts "Samaritan revolts") erupted, continuing until the late 6th century and resulting in a large decrease in the Samaritan population.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-123) After the [Sasanian conquest of Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sasanian_conquest_of_Jerusalem "Sasanian conquest of Jerusalem") and the short-lived [Jewish revolt against Heraclius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_revolt_against_Heraclius "Jewish revolt against Heraclius") in 614 CE, the Byzantine Empire [reconsolidated control of the area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine%E2%80%93Sasanian_War_of_602%E2%80%93628 "Byzantine–Sasanian War of 602–628") in 628.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-124)

In 634–641 CE, the [Rashidun Caliphate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashidun_Caliphate "Rashidun Caliphate")[conquered the Levant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_conquest_of_the_Levant "Muslim conquest of the Levant").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:1-120)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:102-125)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:Ellenblum20102-126) Caliph [Umar ibn al-Khattab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umar_ibn_al-Khattab "Umar ibn al-Khattab") (r.634–644) lifted the Christian ban on Jews entering [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem") and permitted them to worship there.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-127) Over the next six centuries, control of the region transferred between the [Umayyad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umayyad_Caliphate "Umayyad Caliphate"), [Abbasid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbasid_Caliphate "Abbasid Caliphate"), and [Fatimid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatimid_Caliphate "Fatimid Caliphate") caliphates, and subsequently the [Seljuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seljuk_dynasty "Seljuk dynasty") and [Ayyubid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayyubid_dynasty "Ayyubid dynasty") dynasties.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-MosheGil2-128) The population drastically decreased during the following several centuries, dropping from an estimated 1 million during Roman and Byzantine periods to about 300,000 by the early [Ottoman period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire"), and there was steady [Arabisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabization "Arabization") and [Islamisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamization "Islamization").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-auto-129)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:42-98)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:102-125)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:Ellenblum20102-126)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:Broshi1979-130) The end of the 11th century brought the [Crusades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crusades "Crusades"), [papally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope "Pope")-sanctioned incursions of Christian crusaders intent on wresting Jerusalem and the [Holy Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Land "Holy Land") from Muslim control and establishing [crusader states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crusader_states "Crusader states").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-131) The Ayyubids pushed back the crusaders before Muslim rule was fully restored by the [Mamluk sultans of Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamluk_Sultanate_(Cairo) "Mamluk Sultanate (Cairo)") in 1291.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-GudrunKramer-132)

### Modern period and the emergence of Zionism

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils%2C_1870s.jpg/250px-Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils%2C_1870s.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jews_at_Western_Wall_by_Felix_Bonfils,_1870s.jpg)

Jews at the [Western Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Wall "Western Wall") in the 1870s, a holy site in [Judaism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism "Judaism")

In 1516, the Ottoman Empire conquered the region and ruled it as part of [Ottoman Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Syria "Ottoman Syria").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:7-133)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-auto-129) Two violent incidents took place against Jews, the [1517 Safed attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1517_Safed_attacks "1517 Safed attacks") and the [1517 Hebron attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1517_Hebron_attacks "1517 Hebron attacks"), after the Turkish Ottomans ousted the [Mamluks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamluk "Mamluk") during the [Ottoman–Mamluk War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Mamluk_War_(1516%E2%80%931517) "Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517)").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-134)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-JudaicaStudies1999-135) Under the Ottoman Empire, the Levant was fairly cosmopolitan, with religious freedoms for [Christians, Muslims, and Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_of_the_Book "People of the Book").
