In 1561 the [Ottoman sultan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suleiman_the_Magnificent "Suleiman the Magnificent") invited [Sephardic Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephardic_Jews "Sephardic Jews") escaping the [Spanish Inquisition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Inquisition "Spanish Inquisition") to settle in and rebuild the city of [Tiberias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiberias "Tiberias").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-136)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-alfassa2-137)

Under the Ottoman Empire's [millet system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millet_(Ottoman_Empire) "Millet (Ottoman Empire)"), Christians and Jews were considered _[dhimmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhimmi "Dhimmi")_ ("protected") under [Ottoman law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_law "Ottoman law") in exchange for loyalty to the state and payment of the _[jizya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jizya "Jizya")_ tax.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-138)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-139) Non-Muslim Ottoman subjects faced geographic and lifestyle restrictions, though these were not always enforced.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-autogenerated1-140)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-141)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-142) The millet system organised non-Muslims into autonomous communities on the basis of religion.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:4-143)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/THEODOR_HERZL_AT_THE_FIRST_ZIONIST_CONGRESS_IN_BASEL_ON_25.8.1897._%D7%AA%D7%90%D7%95%D7%93%D7%95%D7%A8_%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%A6%D7%9C_%D7%91%D7%A7%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%92%D7%A8%D7%A1_%D7%94%D7%A6%D7%99%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%99_%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%90%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%9F_-_1897.8.25.jpg/250px-THEODOR_HERZL_AT_THE_FIRST_ZIONIST_CONGRESS_IN_BASEL_ON_25.8.1897._%D7%AA%D7%90%D7%95%D7%93%D7%95%D7%A8_%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%A6%D7%9C_%D7%91%D7%A7%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%92%D7%A8%D7%A1_%D7%94%D7%A6%D7%99%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%99_%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%90%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%9F_-_1897.8.25.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:THEODOR_HERZL_AT_THE_FIRST_ZIONIST_CONGRESS_IN_BASEL_ON_25.8.1897._%D7%AA%D7%90%D7%95%D7%93%D7%95%D7%A8_%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%A6%D7%9C_%D7%91%D7%A7%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%92%D7%A8%D7%A1_%D7%94%D7%A6%D7%99%D7%95%D7%A0%D7%99_%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%90%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%9F_-_1897.8.25.jpg)

The [First Zionist Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Zionist_Congress "First Zionist Congress") (1897) in [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basel "Basel"), Switzerland

The [concept of an eventual return to Zion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_to_Zion "Return to Zion") remained a symbol within religious Jewish belief which emphasised that their return should be determined by [Divine Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divine_providence_in_Judaism "Divine providence in Judaism") rather than human action.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAvineri2017-144) The Jewish population of Palestine from the Ottoman rule to the beginning of the Zionist movement, known as the [Old Yishuv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Yishuv "Old Yishuv"), comprised a minority and fluctuated in size. During the 16th century, Jewish communities struck roots in the [Four Holy Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Holy_Cities "Four Holy Cities")—Jerusalem, Tiberias, [Hebron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebron "Hebron"), and [Safed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safed "Safed")—and in 1697, Rabbi Yehuda Hachasid led 1,500 Jews to Jerusalem.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-145) A 1660 [Druze revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Druze_power_struggle_(1658%E2%80%931667)#Lebanon_and_Galilee_campaign "Druze power struggle (1658–1667)") against the Ottomans destroyed [Safed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1660_destruction_of_Safed "1660 destruction of Safed") and [Tiberias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1660_destruction_of_Tiberias "1660 destruction of Tiberias").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:7-133) In the second half of the 18th century, Eastern European Jews who were [opponents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misnagdim "Misnagdim") of [Hasidism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasidic_Judaism "Hasidic Judaism"), known as the [Perushim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perushim "Perushim"), settled in Palestine.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-146)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-147)

In the late 18th century, local Arab Sheikh [Daher al-Umar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daher_al-Umar "Daher al-Umar") created a de facto independent emirate in the Galilee. Ottoman attempts to subdue the sheikh failed. After Daher's death the Ottomans regained control of the area. In 1799, governor [Jazzar Pasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazzar_Pasha "Jazzar Pasha") repelled an [assault on Acre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Acre_(1799) "Siege of Acre (1799)") by [Napoleon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon "Napoleon")'s troops, prompting the French to abandon the Syrian campaign.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-148) In 1834, a [revolt by Palestinian Arab peasants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peasants'_revolt_in_Palestine "Peasants' revolt in Palestine") against Egyptian conscription and taxation policies under [Muhammad Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali_of_Egypt "Muhammad Ali of Egypt") was suppressed; Muhammad Ali's army retreated and Ottoman rule was restored with British support in 1840.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-149) The [Tanzimat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzimat "Tanzimat") reforms were implemented across the Ottoman Empire.

The first wave of modern Jewish migration to [Ottoman-ruled Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Syria "Southern Syria"), known as the [First Aliyah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Aliyah "First Aliyah"), began in 1881, as Jews fled [pogroms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pogrom "Pogrom") in Eastern Europe.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-150) The 1882 [May Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_Laws "May Laws") increased economic discrimination against Jews, and restricted where they could live.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-151)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-152) Antisemitism, pogroms and official policies in tsarist Russia led to the emigration of three million Jews in the years between 1882 and 1914, only 1% of whom went to Palestine. Those who went to Palestine were driven primarily by ideas of self-determination and Jewish identity, rather than as a response to pogroms or economic insecurity.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAvineri2017-144)[Zionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionism "Zionism") emerged during this time as a political movement to reestablish a Jewish homeland in Palestine.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-153) The [revival of the Hebrew language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_of_the_Hebrew_language "Revival of the Hebrew language"), during which [Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language") was adapted for modern use and gradually became the primary language of Jews in Palestine, also began.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-154)

The [Second Aliyah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Aliyah "Second Aliyah") (1904–1914) began after the [Kishinev pogrom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishinev_pogrom "Kishinev pogrom"); some 40,000 Jews settled in Palestine, although nearly half left eventually. Both the first and second waves of migrants were mainly [Orthodox Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthodox_Judaism "Orthodox Judaism").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-155) The Second Aliyah included [Zionist socialist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_Zionism "Labor Zionism") groups who established the _[kibbutz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibbutz "Kibbutz")_ movement based on the idea of establishing a separate Jewish economy based exclusively on Jewish labour.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-156)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTERomano200330-157) Those of the Second Aliyah who became leaders of the [Yishuv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yishuv "Yishuv") in the coming decades believed that the Jewish settler economy should not depend on Arab labour. This would be a dominant source of antagonism with the Arab population, with the new Yishuv's nationalist ideology overpowering its socialist one.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-158) Though the immigrants of the Second Aliyah largely sought to create communal Jewish agricultural settlements, [Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv "Tel Aviv") was established as the first planned Jewish town in 1909. Jewish armed militias emerged during this period, the first being [Bar-Giora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar-Giora_(organization) "Bar-Giora (organization)") in 1907; two years later, the larger [Hashomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashomer "Hashomer") organisation was founded as its replacement.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-159)

### British Mandate for Palestine

[Chaim Weizmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaim_Weizmann "Chaim Weizmann")'s efforts to garner British support for the Zionist movement secured the [Balfour Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balfour_Declaration "Balfour Declaration") of 1917,[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-160) stating Britain's support for the creation of a Jewish "[national home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeland_for_the_Jewish_people "Homeland for the Jewish people")" in Palestine.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-macintyre-161)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-162) Balfour was aware of the developing principle of [self-determination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-determination "Self-determination") and its implications for Palestine. In a letter to a leader of the Zionist movement in the US, he wrote:

> The Powers had committed themselves to the Zionist programme which inevitably excluded numerical self-determination. Palestine presented a unique situation. We are dealing not with the wishes of an existing community but are consciously seeking to reconstitute a new community and definitely building for a numerical majority in the future.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-163)

Weizmann's interpretation of the declaration was that negotiations on the future of the country were to happen between Britain and the Jews, excluding Arabs. [Jewish-Arab relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic%E2%80%93Jewish_relations "Islamic–Jewish relations") in Palestine deteriorated dramatically.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Avi_Shlaim-164)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Allenby_Street.JPG/250px-Allenby_Street.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Allenby_Street.JPG)

Tel Aviv in the 1930s

In 1918, the [Jewish Legion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Legion "Jewish Legion") assisted in the British [conquest of Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_and_Palestine_campaign "Sinai and Palestine campaign").[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-165) In 1920, the territory was divided between Britain and France under the [mandate system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations_mandate "League of Nations mandate"), and the British-administered area (including modern Israel) was named [Mandatory Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine "Mandatory Palestine").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-GudrunKramer-132)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-166)[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-167) Western powers finalized the partition at the [San Remo conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Remo_conference "San Remo conference"), they did so against local opinion. Previously in 1919, the US-led [King–Crane Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King%E2%80%93Crane_Commission "King–Crane Commission"), the only comprehensive social survey of the era, had found overwhelming local opposition to the Zionist project and European mandatory rule.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-168) The Arab opposition to British rule and Jewish immigration led to the [1920 Nebi Musa riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_Nebi_Musa_riots "1920 Nebi Musa riots") and formation of a Jewish militia known as the [Haganah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haganah "Haganah") as an outgrowth of Hashomer, from which the [Irgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irgun "Irgun") and [Lehi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehi_(group) "Lehi (group)") paramilitaries later split.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-169) In 1922, the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations "League of Nations") granted Britain the [Mandate for Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandate_for_Palestine "Mandate for Palestine") under terms which included the Balfour Declaration with its promise to the Jews and with similar provisions regarding the Arab Palestinians.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-170) The [population of the area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_Palestine_(region) "Demographic history of Palestine (region)") was predominantly Arab and Muslim, with Jews accounting for 11%[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-171) and Arab Christians about 10%.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-172)

The [Third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Aliyah "Third Aliyah") (1919–23) and [Fourth Aliyahs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_Aliyah "Fourth Aliyah") (1924–29) brought an additional 100,000 Jews to Palestine. Following the [1929 Palestine riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1929_Palestine_riots "1929 Palestine riots"), the [Hope Simpson Enquiry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Simpson_Enquiry "Hope Simpson Enquiry") documented that land purchases by the Jewish National Fund and other Zionist organizations had led to the eviction of Arab tenant farmers and created an economically disenfranchised class of landless Arabs. Hope Simpson made recommendations including limiting Jewish immigration based on the absorptive capacity of Palestine.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-173)

The [rise of Nazism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler's_rise_to_power "Adolf Hitler's rise to power") and increasing persecution of Jews in 1930s Europe led to the [Fifth Aliyah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Aliyah "Fifth Aliyah"), with an influx of 250,000 Jews. This was a cause of the [Arab revolt of 1936–39](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936%E2%80%931939_Arab_revolt_in_Palestine "1936–1939 Arab revolt in Palestine"), which was suppressed by British security forces and Zionist militias. Several hundred British security personnel and Jews were killed; 5,032 Arabs were killed.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-174)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-175)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-176) 10% of [Palestinian Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_people "Palestinian people") men were killed, wounded, imprisoned, or exiled.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-177)

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/%22Jews_and_Arabs_in_Grim_Struggle_for_Holy_Land%22_article_%281938%29.jpg/250px-%22Jews_and_Arabs_in_Grim_Struggle_for_Holy_Land%22_article_%281938%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%22Jews_and_Arabs_in_Grim_Struggle_for_Holy_Land%22_article_(1938).jpg)

"Jews and Arabs in Grim Struggle for Holy Land", article from 1938

In the 1930s, Britain began considering proposals to partition Palestine. Although some Zionists opposed partition, David Ben-Gurion supported it while regarding it as a temporary arrangement. In summer 1938, he stated that, after the establishment of the state and formation of a large army, they would "abolish partition" and "expand to the whole of Palestine".[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-178)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-179)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-180)

The British introduced restrictions on Jewish immigration to Palestine with the [White Paper of 1939](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Paper_of_1939 "White Paper of 1939"). With countries turning away Jewish refugees fleeing [the Holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust "The Holocaust"), a clandestine movement known as [Aliyah Bet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah_Bet "Aliyah Bet") was organised to bring Jews to Palestine. During World War II, Palestine was [repeatedly bombed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_bombing_of_Mandatory_Palestine_in_World_War_II "Italian bombing of Mandatory Palestine in World War II") by Axis aircraft, causing casualties among Jews and Arabs. About 30,000 Jews from Palestine served in the British military during the war, of whom around 700 were killed.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-181) 12,000 Palestinian Arabs served in the British military.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-182) At the end of the war, 31% of the population of Palestine was Jewish.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-183) The UK faced a [Jewish insurgency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_insurgency_in_Mandatory_Palestine "Jewish insurgency in Mandatory Palestine") over immigration restrictions from 1944, which intensified after the war, and continued conflict with the Arab community over limit levels. The Haganah joined Irgun and Lehi in an armed struggle against British rule.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFraser200427-184) The Haganah attempted to bring tens of thousands of Jewish refugees and [Holocaust survivors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust_survivors "Holocaust survivors") to Palestine by ship. Most ships were intercepted by the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") and the refugees placed in detention camps in [Atlit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlit_detainee_camp "Atlit detainee camp") and [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus_internment_camps "Cyprus internment camps").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Golani2013-185)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-186) The insurgency included bombings and other attacks by Jewish insurgent organisations, including attacks that killed civilians as well as British security personnel and officials.

In July 1946, Irgun [bombed the British administrative headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_David_Hotel_bombing "King David Hotel bombing") for Palestine in the King David Hotel, killing 91.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-187)[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-brtca_irgun-188)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-tclarke81-189)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-bethell-190) The attack was intended to destroy documents that Irgun believed implicated the Jewish Agency in attacks against the British during [Operation Agatha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Agatha "Operation Agatha"), a series of raids, including one on the [Jewish Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Agency_for_Israel "Jewish Agency for Israel").[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-tclarke81-189)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-bethell-190) The Jewish insurgency continued throughout 1946 and 1947 despite concerted efforts by the British military and [Palestine Police Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_Police_Force "Palestine Police Force") to suppress it.

British efforts to mediate with Jewish and Arab representatives were unsuccessful as the Jews were unwilling to accept any solution that did not involve a Jewish state, and suggested a partition of Palestine into Jewish and Arab states. The Arabs were adamant that a Jewish state in any part of Palestine was unacceptable and the only solution was a unified Palestine under Arab rule. In February 1947, the British referred the Palestine issue to the United Nations. On 15 May 1947, the [UN General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Assembly_of_the_United_Nations "General Assembly of the United Nations") resolved that a [Special Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Special_Committee_on_Palestine "United Nations Special Committee on Palestine") be created "to prepare ... a report on the question of Palestine".[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-191) The Report of the Committee[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-192)[proposed a plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine "United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine") to replace the British Mandate with "an independent Arab State, an independent Jewish State, and the City of Jerusalem [...] the last to be under an International Trusteeship System".[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-193)

Meanwhile, the Jewish insurgency peaked in July 1947, with a series of guerrilla raids culminating in [the Sergeants affair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sergeants_affair "The Sergeants affair"), in which the Irgun took two British sergeants hostage as attempted leverage against the planned execution of three Irgun operatives. After the executions were carried out, the Irgun killed the British soldiers, hanged their bodies from trees, and left a booby trap which injured a British soldier. The incident caused outrage in the UK.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Hoffman-194) In September 1947, the British cabinet decided to evacuate Palestine as the Mandate was no longer tenable.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-195)

### 1948 war and establishment of the State of Israel

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/UN_Palestine_Partition_Versions_1947.jpg/250px-UN_Palestine_Partition_Versions_1947.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UN_Palestine_Partition_Versions_1947.jpg)

[1947 partition plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine "United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine") of Palestine between Israel and the [State of Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Palestine "State of Palestine"), as proposed by the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations")

On 29 November 1947, the General Assembly adopted [Resolution 181 (II)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine "United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine"), which recommended partition of Mandatory Palestine into separate Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem being under an international regime.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-181(II)-196) The plan attached to the resolution was that proposed in the report of 3 September, which had allocated the larger share of territory (55%) to The Jewish Agency, the recognised representative of the Jewish community, despite the fact the Jewish population was a third of the population, most of whom were recent immigrants, and owned about 7% of the land. Arabs constituted the majority population and owned about 20% of the land, with the remainder held by the Mandate authorities or foreign landowners. The Jewish leadership accepted the plan but the Arab leadership rejected it.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-197)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Morris2008396-198)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-199)[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-200)

The [Arab League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_League "Arab League") and [Arab Higher Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Higher_Committee "Arab Higher Committee") of Palestine responded that the plan privileged European interests over Palestinians,[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-201) and they would "refuse to be bound" by any resolution to divide the country. They argued the resolution was contrary to [self-determination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-determination "Self-determination") and Arabs constituted the majority of its "lawful inhabitants", who had consistently expressed their desire for their country to "remain united and undivided".[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-202)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:0-36)[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBregman200240%E2%80%9341-203) In December 1947, the Arab Higher Committee proclaimed a strike, and [riots broke out in Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_Jerusalem_riots "1947 Jerusalem riots").[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-204) The situation spiralled into [a civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947%E2%80%931948_civil_war_in_Mandatory_Palestine "1947–1948 civil war in Mandatory Palestine"). Colonial Secretary [Arthur Creech Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Creech_Jones "Arthur Creech Jones") announced that the British Mandate would end in May 1948: the British would evacuate. As Arab militias and gangs attacked Jewish areas, they were faced by the Haganah, and the smaller Irgun and Lehi. In April 1948, the Haganah moved onto the offensive, a phase that included the [Deir Yassin massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deir_Yassin_massacre "Deir Yassin massacre"), in which Irgun and Lehi forces attacked the Arab village of [Deir Yassin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deir_Yassin "Deir Yassin"), killing more than 100 villagers, including women and children.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris200877%E2%80%9378-205)[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-206)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Declaration_of_State_of_Israel_1948.jpg/250px-Declaration_of_State_of_Israel_1948.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Declaration_of_State_of_Israel_1948.jpg)

[David Ben-Gurion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ben-Gurion "David Ben-Gurion") declaring the [establishment of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence "Israeli Declaration of Independence") on 14 May 1948

On 14 May 1948, the day before the expiration of the British Mandate, [David Ben-Gurion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ben-Gurion "David Ben-Gurion"), the head of the Jewish Agency, [declared "the establishment of a Jewish state in Eretz-Israel"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence "Israeli Declaration of Independence").[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-207) The following day, the armies of four Arab countries—Egypt, Syria, Transjordan, and Iraq—entered what had been Mandatory Palestine, launching the [1948 Arab–Israeli War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War "1948 Arab–Israeli War");[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBen-Sasson19851058-208) contingents from [Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutawakkilite_Kingdom_of_Yemen "Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen"), [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco"), [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"), and [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan") joined the war.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris2008205-209)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-210) The purpose of the invasion was to prevent the establishment of the Jewish state.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Morris2008396-198)[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-211)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-212) The Arab League stated the invasion was to restore order and prevent further bloodshed.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-cablegram-213)

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/Raising_the_Ink_Flag_at_Umm_Rashrash_%28Eilat%29_%283x4%29.jpg/250px-Raising_the_Ink_Flag_at_Umm_Rashrash_%28Eilat%29_%283x4%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raising_the_Ink_Flag_at_Umm_Rashrash_(Eilat)_(3x4).jpg)

Raising of the [Ink Flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ink_Flag "Ink Flag") on 10 March 1949, marking the end of the [1948 war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War "1948 Arab–Israeli War")

After a year of fighting, a [ceasefire was declared](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements "1949 Armistice Agreements") and temporary borders established, known as the [Green Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Line_(Israel) "Green Line (Israel)").[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-214)[Jordan annexed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordanian_annexation_of_the_West_Bank "Jordanian annexation of the West Bank") what became known as the [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank"), including [East Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem "East Jerusalem"), and [Egypt occupied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Gaza_Strip_by_the_United_Arab_Republic "Occupation of the Gaza Strip by the United Arab Republic") the [Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip"). 700,000 Palestinians [fled or were expelled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Palestinian_expulsion_and_flight "1948 Palestinian expulsion and flight") by [Zionist militias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionist_political_violence "Zionist political violence") and the [Israeli military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defence_Forces "Israel Defence Forces")—what would become known in Arabic as the _[Nakba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakba "Nakba")_ ('catastrophe').[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-215) The events led to the destruction of most of Palestine's Arab [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Palestine "Culture of Palestine"), [identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_identity "Palestinian identity"), and [national aspirations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_nationalism "Palestinian nationalism"). 156,000 Arabs remained and became [Arab citizens of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_citizens_of_Israel "Arab citizens of Israel").[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:2-216)

By [United Nations General Assembly Resolution 273](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly_Resolution_273 "United Nations General Assembly Resolution 273"), Israel was admitted to the UN in May 1949.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-217) In the early years of the state, the [Labour Zionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_Zionism "Labor Zionism") movement led by Prime Minister Ben-Gurion dominated [Israeli politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Israel "Politics of Israel").[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTELustick198837%E2%80%9339-218)[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-219) Immigration during the late 1940s and early 1950s was aided by the Israeli Immigration Department and the non-government sponsored [Mossad LeAliyah Bet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mossad_LeAliyah_Bet "Mossad LeAliyah Bet") (lit. "Institute for [Immigration B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah_Bet "Aliyah Bet")").[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-220) The latter engaged in clandestine operations in countries, particularly in the Middle East and Eastern Europe, where the lives of Jews were in danger and exit difficult.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-221) Immigration was in accordance with the [One Million Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Million_Plan "One Million Plan"). Some immigrants held Zionist beliefs or came for the promise of a better life, while others escaped persecution or were expelled from their homes.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-222)[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-223)

An [influx of Holocaust survivors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah#Early_statehood_(1948%E2%80%931960) "Aliyah") and [Jews from Arab and Muslim countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_exodus_from_the_Muslim_world "Jewish exodus from the Muslim world") during the first three years increased the number of Jews from 700,000 to 1,400,000. By 1958, the population had risen to two million.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-224) Between 1948-1970, approximately 1,150,000 Jewish refugees relocated to Israel.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-225) Some immigrants arrived as refugees and were housed in camps known as _[ma'abarot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma'abarot "Ma'abarot")_; by 1952, 200,000 people lived in these tent cities.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-226)[Jews of European background](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jews "Ashkenazi Jews") were often treated more favourably than Jews from [Middle Eastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mizrahi_Jews "Mizrahi Jews") and [North African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephardi_Jews "Sephardi Jews") countries—housing units reserved for the latter were often re-designated for the former, so Jews newly arrived from Arab lands generally ended up staying longer in transit camps.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-227)[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTESegev2007155%E2%80%93157-228) Food, clothes and furniture were rationed in this [austerity period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austerity_in_Israel "Austerity in Israel"). The need to solve the crisis led Ben-Gurion to sign a [reparations agreement with West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reparations_Agreement_between_Israel_and_the_Federal_Republic_of_Germany "Reparations Agreement between Israel and the Federal Republic of Germany") that triggered protests by Jews angered that Israel could accept monetary compensation for the Holocaust.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShindler200249%E2%80%9350-229)

There were [further expulsions of Palestinians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949%E2%80%931956_Palestinian_expulsions "1949–1956 Palestinian expulsions") after the establishment of Israel. During the 1950s, Israel was [frequently attacked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_attacks_against_Israeli_civilians_before_1967 "List of attacks against Israeli civilians before 1967") by [Palestinian fedayeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_fedayeen "Palestinian fedayeen"), nearly always against civilians,[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-230) mainly from the Egyptian-occupied Gaza Strip,[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert200558-231) leading to Israeli [reprisal operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reprisal_operations "Reprisal operations"). In 1956, the UK and France aimed to regain control of the [Suez Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez_Canal "Suez Canal"), which Egypt had nationalised. The blockade of the Canal and [Straits of Tiran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straits_of_Tiran "Straits of Tiran") to Israeli shipping, together with fedayeen attacks against Israel's southern population and Arab threatening statements, prompted Israel to attack Egypt.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-232)[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-233)[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-234) Israel joined [a secret alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protocol_of_S%C3%A8vres "Protocol of Sèvres") with the UK and France and overran the [Sinai Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula "Sinai Peninsula") in the [Suez Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez_Crisis "Suez Crisis"), but was pressured to withdraw by the UN in return for guarantees of Israeli shipping rights.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-235)[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-236)[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-237) The war resulted in reduction of Israeli border infiltration.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-238)

[Video 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/34/1961-04-13_Tale_Of_Century_-_Eichmann_Tried_For_War_Crimes.ogv?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

U.S. newsreel on the trial of [Adolf Eichmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Eichmann "Adolf Eichmann")

In the early 1960s, Israel captured Nazi war criminal [Adolf Eichmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Eichmann "Adolf Eichmann") in Argentina and brought him to Israel [for trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eichmann_trial "Eichmann trial").[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBascomb2009219%E2%80%93229-239)[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-240) Eichmann remains the only person executed in Israel by conviction in an Israeli civilian court.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-241) In 1963, Israel was engaged in a diplomatic standoff with the US concerning the Israeli [nuclear programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapons_of_Israel "Nuclear weapons of Israel").[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Haaretz2019-242)[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-243)

Since 1964, Arab countries, concerned over Israeli plans to divert waters of the [Jordan River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_River "Jordan River") into the [coastal plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_coastal_plain "Israeli coastal plain"),[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-244) had tried to divert the headwaters to deprive Israel of water resources, [provoking tensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_over_Water_(Jordan_River) "War over Water (Jordan River)") between Israel on the one hand, and Syria and Lebanon on the other. [Arab nationalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_nationalist "Arab nationalist") led by Egyptian President [Gamal Abdel Nasser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamal_Abdel_Nasser "Gamal Abdel Nasser") refused to recognise Israel and called for its destruction.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-RoutledgeAtlas-245)[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-246)[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-247) By 1966, Israeli-Arab relations had deteriorated to the point of battles between Israeli and Arab forces.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTESegev2007178-248)

In May 1967, Egypt massed its army near the border with Israel, expelled [UN peacekeepers stationed in the Sinai Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Emergency_Force "United Nations Emergency Force"), and blocked Israel's access to the Red Sea.[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-249)[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-250)[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-251) Other Arab states mobilised their forces.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTESegev2007289-252) Israel stated that these actions were a _[casus belli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casus\_belli "Casus belli")_ (a provocation that justified war) and launched a pre-emptive strike ([Operation Focus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Focus "Operation Focus")) against Egypt in June. Jordan, Syria and Iraq attacked Israel.

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Six_Day_War_Territories.svg/250px-Six_Day_War_Territories.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Six_Day_War_Territories.svg)

Territory held by Israel: 
after the war

 The [Sinai Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula "Sinai Peninsula") was returned to Egypt in 1982.

In the ensuing [Six-Day War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War "Six-Day War"), Israel captured and occupied the West Bank from Jordan, the Gaza Strip and Sinai Peninsula from Egypt, and the Golan Heights from Syria.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-253) Israeli forces [expelled ~300,000 Palestinians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naksa "Naksa") from the Gaza Strip and the West Bank. Jerusalem's boundaries were enlarged, incorporating [East Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem "East Jerusalem"). The 1949 Green Line became the administrative boundary between Israel and the [occupied territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories "Israeli-occupied territories").[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShlayRosen2010362%E2%80%93363-254)

Following the 1967 war and the "[Three Nos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khartoum_Resolution "Khartoum Resolution")" resolution of the Arab League, Israel faced attacks from the Egyptians in the Sinai Peninsula during the 1967–70 [War of Attrition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_Attrition "War of Attrition"), and from Palestinian groups targeting Israelis in the occupied territories, globally, and in Israel. Most important among the groups was the [Palestine Liberation Organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_Liberation_Organisation "Palestine Liberation Organisation") (PLO), established in 1964, which initially committed itself to "armed struggle as the only way to liberate the homeland".[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-255) In the late 1960s and early 1970s, [Palestinian groups launched attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_political_violence "Palestinian political violence")[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-256)[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-257) against Israeli and Jewish targets around the world,[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-258) including [a massacre of Israeli athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_massacre "Munich massacre") at the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics") in Munich. Israel responded with an [assassination campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mossad_assassinations_following_the_Munich_massacre "Mossad assassinations following the Munich massacre") against the organisers of the massacre, [a bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Israeli_air_raid_in_Syria_and_Lebanon "1972 Israeli air raid in Syria and Lebanon") and a [raid on the PLO headquarters in Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_Israeli_raid_in_Lebanon "1973 Israeli raid in Lebanon").

On 6 October 1973, the Egyptian and Syrian armies launched [a surprise attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Badr_(1973) "Operation Badr (1973)") against Israeli forces in the Sinai Peninsula and Golan Heights, opening the [Yom Kippur War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War "Yom Kippur War"). The war ended on 25 October with Israel repelling Egyptian and Syrian forces but suffering losses.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-259) An [internal inquiry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agranat_Commission "Agranat Commission") exonerated [the government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_government_of_Israel "Fifteenth government of Israel") of responsibility for failures before and during the war, but public anger forced Prime Minister [Golda Meir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golda_Meir "Golda Meir") to resign.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-260)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] In June 1976, [Air France Flight 139](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_France_Flight_139 "Air France Flight 139") from Israel to France was hijacked by Palestinian guerrillas; Israeli commandos rescued 102 of 106 Israeli hostages.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-261)

The [1977 Knesset elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_Israeli_legislative_election "1977 Israeli legislative election") marked a turning point in Israeli history as [Menachem Begin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menachem_Begin "Menachem Begin")'s [Likud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Likud "Likud") party took control from the [Labor Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Labor_Party "Israeli Labor Party").[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-262) Egyptian President [Anwar El Sadat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anwar_El_Sadat "Anwar El Sadat") made a trip to Israel and spoke before the [Knesset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knesset "Knesset") in what was the first recognition of Israel by an Arab head of state.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBregman2002171%E2%80%93174-263) Sadat and Begin signed the [Camp David Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_David_Accords "Camp David Accords") (1978) and the [Egypt–Israel peace treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Israel_peace_treaty "Egypt–Israel peace treaty") (1979).[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBregman2002186%E2%80%93187-264) In return, Israel withdrew from the Sinai Peninsula and entered negotiations over autonomy for Palestinians in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBregman2002186%E2%80%93187-264)

In March 1978, a PLO raid from Lebanon led to the [Coastal Road massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coastal_Road_massacre "Coastal Road massacre"). Israel responded by launching an [invasion of southern Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_South_Lebanon_conflict "1978 South Lebanon conflict") to destroy PLO bases. Begin's government meanwhile provided incentives for [Israelis to settle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_settlement "Israeli settlement") in the [occupied West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_the_West_Bank "Israeli occupation of the West Bank"), increasing friction with the Palestinians there.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-265)

The 1980 [Jerusalem Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem_Law "Jerusalem Law") was believed by some to reaffirm Israel's 1967 annexation of Jerusalem by government decree and [reignited international controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Security_Council_Resolution_478 "UN Security Council Resolution 478") over the [status of the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_of_Jerusalem "Status of Jerusalem"). No Israeli legislation has defined the territory of Israel, and no act specifically included East Jerusalem therein.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-266) In 1981 Israel [effectively annexed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golan_Heights_Law "Golan Heights Law") the Golan Heights.[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-bbc_golan_profile-267) The international community rejected these moves, with the UN Security Council declaring the Jerusalem Law and Golan Heights Law void.[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-268)[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-269) Waves of [Ethiopian Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_Israel "Beta Israel")[immigrated to Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah_from_Ethiopia "Aliyah from Ethiopia") from the 1980s onwards, while between 1990-94, [immigration from the post-Soviet states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990s_post-Soviet_aliyah "1990s post-Soviet aliyah") increased Israel's population by twelve per cent.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-270)

On 7 June 1981, during the [Iran–Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Iraq_War "Iran–Iraq War"), [Israel's air force destroyed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Opera "Operation Opera") Iraq's sole nuclear reactor, then under construction, to impede Iraq's nuclear weapons programme.[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-271) Following PLO attacks in 1982, Israel [invaded Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Lebanon_War "1982 Lebanon War") to destroy the PLO bases.[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBregman2002199-272) Israel destroyed the military forces of the PLO in Lebanon and defeated the Syrians. An Israeli inquiry (the [Kahan Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kahan_Commission "Kahan Commission")) held Begin and several Israeli generals indirectly responsible for the [Sabra and Shatila massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabra_and_Shatila_massacre "Sabra and Shatila massacre") and held [defence minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(Israel) "Ministry of Defence (Israel)")[Ariel Sharon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariel_Sharon "Ariel Sharon") as bearing "personal responsibility".[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-273) Sharon was forced to resign.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-274)

In 1985, Israel responded to a Palestinian [terrorist attack in Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larnaca_yacht_killings "Larnaca yacht killings") by [bombing PLO's headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Wooden_Leg "Operation Wooden Leg") in Tunisia. Israel withdrew from most of Lebanon in 1986 but continued to [occupy a borderland buffer zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_Southern_Lebanon_(1982%E2%80%932000) "Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon (1982–2000)") in southern Lebanon until 2000, from where Israeli forces [engaged in conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Lebanon_conflict_(1985%E2%80%932000) "South Lebanon conflict (1985–2000)") with [Hezbollah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hezbollah "Hezbollah"). The [First Intifada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Intifada "First Intifada"), a Palestinian uprising against Israeli rule,[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-275) broke out in 1987, with demonstrations and violence in the occupied West Bank and Gaza. Over the following six years, the intifada became more organised and included economic and cultural measures aimed at disrupting the Israeli occupation. Over 1,000 people were killed.[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-276) During the 1991 [Gulf War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War "Gulf War"), the PLO supported [Saddam Hussein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein "Saddam Hussein") and Iraqi missile [attacks against Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_rocket_attacks_on_Israel "Iraqi rocket attacks on Israel"). Despite public outrage, Israel heeded American calls to refrain from retaliating.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-277)[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMowlanaGerbnerSchiller1992111-278)

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Flickr_-_Government_Press_Office_%28GPO%29_-_Foreign_Min._Peres_and_King_Hussein.jpg/250px-Flickr_-_Government_Press_Office_%28GPO%29_-_Foreign_Min._Peres_and_King_Hussein.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flickr_-_Government_Press_Office_(GPO)_-_Foreign_Min._Peres_and_King_Hussein.jpg)

[Shimon Peres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimon_Peres "Shimon Peres") (left) with [Yitzhak Rabin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin "Yitzhak Rabin") (center) and King [Hussein of Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hussein_of_Jordan "Hussein of Jordan") (right), prior to signing the [Israel–Jordan peace treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Jordan_peace_treaty "Israel–Jordan peace treaty") in 1994

In 1992, [Yitzhak Rabin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin "Yitzhak Rabin") became prime minister following [an election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Israeli_legislative_election "1992 Israeli legislative election") in which his party called for compromise with Israel's neighbours.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBregman2002236-279)[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-280) The following year, [Shimon Peres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimon_Peres "Shimon Peres") on behalf of Israel and [Yasser Arafat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasser_Arafat "Yasser Arafat") for the PLO signed the [Oslo Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords "Oslo Accords"), which gave the [Palestinian National Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Authority "Palestinian Authority") (PNA) the right to govern [parts of the West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank_areas_in_the_Oslo_II_Accord "West Bank areas in the Oslo II Accord") and Gaza Strip.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-281) The PLO [recognised Israel's right to exist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Palestine_Liberation_Organization_letters_of_recognition "Israel–Palestine Liberation Organization letters of recognition") and pledged an end to terrorism.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTETessler2009729-282) In 1994, the [Israel–Jordan peace treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Jordan_peace_treaty "Israel–Jordan peace treaty") was signed.[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-283) Arab public support for the Accords was damaged by the continuation of Israeli settlements[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-284) and [checkpoints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_checkpoint "Israeli checkpoint"), and deterioration of economic conditions.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-285) Israeli public support for the Accords waned after [Palestinian suicide attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Palestinian_suicide_attacks "List of Palestinian suicide attacks").[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-286) In November 1995, Rabin [was assassinated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Yitzhak_Rabin "Assassination of Yitzhak Rabin") by a far-right Jew who opposed the Accords.[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-287)

During [Benjamin Netanyahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu "Benjamin Netanyahu")'s premiership at the end of the 1990s, Israel [agreed to withdraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protocol_Concerning_the_Redeployment_in_Hebron "Protocol Concerning the Redeployment in Hebron") from [Hebron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebron "Hebron"),[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBregman2002257-288) though this was never implemented,[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-289) and he signed the [Wye River Memorandum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wye_River_Memorandum "Wye River Memorandum"). The agreement dealt with further redeployments in the West Bank and security issues. The memorandum was criticised by international human rights organisations for its "encouragement" of human rights abuses.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-290)[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-291)[Ehud Barak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehud_Barak "Ehud Barak"), [elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Israeli_general_election "1999 Israeli general election") prime minister in 1999, withdrew forces from southern Lebanon and conducted negotiations with PNA Chairman Arafat and US President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") at the [2000 Camp David Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Camp_David_Summit "2000 Camp David Summit"). Barak offered a plan for the establishment of a [Palestinian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_state "Palestinian state"), including the entirety of the Gaza Strip and 90% of the West Bank with Jerusalem as a shared capital.[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGelvin2005240-292) Each side blamed the other for the failure of the talks.

### 21st century

In late 2000, after a controversial visit by Sharon to the [Temple Mount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_Mount "Temple Mount"), the [Second Intifada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Intifada "Second Intifada") began. The popular uprising faced disproportionate repression from the Israeli state.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-293)[Palestinian suicide bombings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_suicide_attacks "Palestinian suicide attacks") eventually developed into a recurrent feature of the intifada.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-294) Some commentators contend that the intifada was pre-planned by Arafat after the collapse of peace talks.[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-295)[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-296)[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-jewishweek-297)[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-atlantic-298) Sharon became prime minister in a [2001 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Israeli_prime_ministerial_election "2001 Israeli prime ministerial election"); he carried out his plan to [unilaterally withdraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_disengagement_from_the_Gaza_Strip "Israeli disengagement from the Gaza Strip") from the Gaza Strip and spearheaded the construction of the [West Bank barrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank_barrier "West Bank barrier"),[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-299) ending the intifada.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-300) Between 2000 and 2008, 1,063 Israelis, 5,517 Palestinians and 64 foreign citizens were killed.[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-301)

In July 2006, a Hezbollah artillery assault on Israel's northern border communities and a [cross-border abduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Hezbollah_cross-border_raid "2006 Hezbollah cross-border raid") of two Israeli soldiers precipitated the month-long [Second Lebanon War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Lebanon_War "2006 Lebanon War"), including an Israeli invasion of Lebanon.[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-UN1701-302)[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-HRTZ_Harel-303) The war wound down in August 2006 after the passage of [United Nations Security Council Resolution 1701](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_Resolution_1701 "United Nations Security Council Resolution 1701"); Israeli forces mostly withdrew from Lebanon by October 2006 but continued to occupy the Lebanese portion of [Ghajar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghajar "Ghajar") village.[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-304)[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-305) In 2007 the Israeli Air Force [destroyed a nuclear reactor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Outside_the_Box "Operation Outside the Box") in Syria.

In 2008, [a ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Israel%E2%80%93Hamas_ceasefire "2008 Israel–Hamas ceasefire") between [Hamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas "Hamas") and Israel collapsed, resulting in the three-week [Gaza War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_War_(2008%E2%80%932009) "Gaza War (2008–2009)").[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-306)[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-ravid-307) In what Israel described as a response to [over a hundred Palestinian rocket attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Palestinian_rocket_attacks_on_Israel_in_2012 "List of Palestinian rocket attacks on Israel in 2012") on southern Israeli cities,[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-pound-308) Israel began [an operation in the Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Gaza_War "2012 Gaza War") in 2012, lasting eight days.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-309) Israel started another [operation in Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Gaza_War "2014 Gaza War") following an escalation of rocket attacks by Hamas in July 2014.[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-310) In May 2021, another [round of fighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Israel%E2%80%93Palestine_crisis "2021 Israel–Palestine crisis") took place in Gaza and Israel, lasting eleven days.[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-311) By the 2010s, [increasing regional cooperation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_alliance "Arab–Israeli alliance") between Israel and [Arab League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_League "Arab League") countries have been established, culminating in the signing of the [Abraham Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Accords "Abraham Accords"). The Israeli security situation shifted from the traditional [Arab–Israeli conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_conflict "Arab–Israeli conflict") towards the [Iran–Israel proxy conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Israel_proxy_conflict "Iran–Israel proxy conflict") and [direct confrontation with Iran during the Syrian civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Israel_conflict_during_the_Syrian_civil_war "Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war").

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Fires_in_Israel_and_the_Gaza_strip_-_7_October_2023_%2853245908850%29.jpg/250px-Fires_in_Israel_and_the_Gaza_strip_-_7_October_2023_%2853245908850%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fires_in_Israel_and_the_Gaza_strip_-_7_October_2023_(53245908850).jpg)

Satellite view of fires in the [Gaza envelope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_envelope "Gaza envelope") on 7 October 2023

On 7 October 2023, Palestinian militant groups from [Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip"), led by Hamas, launched [a series of coordinated attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks "October 7 attacks") on Israel, leading to the start of the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war").[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-312) On that day, approximately 1,300 Israelis, predominantly civilians, were killed in communities near the Gaza Strip border and [during a music festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re'im_music_festival_massacre "Re'im music festival massacre"). [Over 200 hostages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war_hostage_crisis "Gaza war hostage crisis") were kidnapped and taken to the Gaza Strip.[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Gillett-313)[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-314)[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-natureparty-315) Studies modeling trauma exposure and assessing mental health outcomes estimated that approximately 5.3% of Israelis may develop [PTSD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PTSD "PTSD"),[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-316) with national data showing that probable PTSD nearly doubled from 16.2% to 29.8% and rates of anxiety and depression also rising sharply.[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-317)

After clearing militants from its territory, Israel launched [one of the most destructive bombing campaigns in modern history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_bombing_of_the_Gaza_Strip "Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip")[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-318)[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-319) and [invaded Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_invasion_of_the_Gaza_Strip "Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip") on 27 October with the stated objectives of destroying Hamas and freeing Israel is located in the [Levant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levant "Levant") area of the [Fertile Crescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertile_Crescent "Fertile Crescent"). At the [eastern end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Mediterranean "Eastern Mediterranean") of the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea"), it is bounded by Lebanon to the north, Syria to the north-east, Jordan and the West Bank to the east, and Egypt and the Gaza Strip to the south-west. It lies between latitudes [29°](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/29th_parallel_north "29th parallel north") and [34° N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/34th_parallel_north "34th parallel north"), and longitudes [34°](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/34th_meridian_east "34th meridian east") and [36° E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/36th_meridian_east "36th meridian east").

The sovereign territory of Israel (according to the demarcation lines of the [1949 Armistice Agreements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements "1949 Armistice Agreements") and excluding all territories captured by Israel during the 1967 Six-Day War) is approximately 20,770 square kilometres (8,019 sq mi), of which two per cent is water.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-cia-19) However Israel is so narrow (100 km at its widest, compared to 400 km from north to south) that the [exclusive economic zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclusive_economic_zone "Exclusive economic zone") in the Mediterranean is double the land area of the country.[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-334) The total area under Israeli law, including East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights, is 22,072 square kilometres (8,522 sq mi),[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-335) and the total area under Israeli control, including the military-controlled and partially Palestinian-governed territory of the West Bank, is 27,799 square kilometres (10,733 sq mi).[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-loc-geo-336)

Despite its small size, Israel is home to a variety of geographic features, from the [Negev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negev "Negev") desert in the south to the inland fertile [Jezreel Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jezreel_Valley "Jezreel Valley"), with mountain ranges of the [Galilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galilee "Galilee"), [Carmel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Carmel "Mount Carmel") and towards the [Golan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golan_Heights "Golan Heights") in the north. The [Israeli coastal plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_coastal_plain "Israeli coastal plain") on the shores of the Mediterranean is home to most of the population.[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-337) East of the central highlands lies the [Jordan Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Rift_Valley "Jordan Rift Valley"), a small part of the 6,500-kilometre (4,039 mi)[Great Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley "Great Rift Valley"). The [Jordan River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_River "Jordan River") runs along the Jordan Rift Valley, from [Mount Hermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Hermon "Mount Hermon") through the [Hulah Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulah_Valley "Hulah Valley") and the [Sea of Galilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_of_Galilee "Sea of Galilee") to the [Dead Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea "Dead Sea"), the [lowest point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_points_of_Earth "Extreme points of Earth") on the surface of the Earth.[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-338) Further south is the [Arabah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabah "Arabah"), ending with the [Gulf of Eilat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Aqaba "Gulf of Aqaba"), part of the [Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea"). [Makhtesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makhtesh "Makhtesh"), or "erosion cirques" are unique to the Negev and the [Sinai Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula "Sinai Peninsula"), the largest being the [Makhtesh Ramon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makhtesh_Ramon "Makhtesh Ramon") at 38 km in length.[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-339) Israel has the largest number of plant species per square metre of the countries in the Mediterranean Basin[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-rinat-340) and contains four terrestrial ecoregions: [Eastern Mediterranean conifer–sclerophyllous–broadleaf forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Mediterranean_conifer%E2%80%93sclerophyllous%E2%80%93broadleaf_forests "Eastern Mediterranean conifer–sclerophyllous–broadleaf forests"), [Southern Anatolian montane conifer and deciduous forests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Anatolian_montane_conifer_and_deciduous_forests "Southern Anatolian montane conifer and deciduous forests"), [Arabian Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Desert "Arabian Desert"), and [Mesopotamian shrub desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesopotamian_shrub_desert "Mesopotamian shrub desert").[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-341) Forests accounted for 8.5% of the area in 2016, up from 2% in 1948, as the result of a large-scale forest planting programme by the [Jewish National Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_National_Fund "Jewish National Fund").[[334]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-342)[[335]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-343)

### Tectonics and seismicity

The Jordan Rift Valley is the result of tectonic movements within the [Dead Sea Transform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea_Transform "Dead Sea Transform") (DST) fault system. The DST forms the [transform boundary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transform_fault "Transform fault") between the [African Plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Plate "African Plate") to the west and the [Arabian Plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Plate "Arabian Plate") to the east. The Golan Heights and all of Jordan are part of the Arabian Plate, while the Galilee, West Bank, Coastal Plain, and Negev along with the Sinai Peninsula are on the African Plate. This tectonic disposition leads to a relatively high seismic activity. The entire Jordan Valley segment is thought to have ruptured repeatedly, for instance during the last two major earthquakes along this structure in [749](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/749_Galilee_earthquake "749 Galilee earthquake") and [1033](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1033_Jordan_Valley_earthquake "1033 Jordan Valley earthquake"). The deficit in [slip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fault_(geology)#Slip,_heave,_throw "Fault (geology)") that has built up since 1033 is sufficient to cause an earthquake of M w~7.4.[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Ferry-344)

The most catastrophic known earthquakes occurred in 31 BCE, [363](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/363_Galilee_earthquake "363 Galilee earthquake"), 749, and 1033 CE, that is every ca. 400 years on average.[[337]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-MarcoAFTAU-345) Destructive earthquakes strike about every 80 years, leading to serious loss of life .[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-IllPreped-346) While stringent construction regulations are in place and recently built structures are earthquake resistant, as of 2007 many public buildings as well as 50,000 residential buildings did not meet the new standards and were "expected to collapse" if exposed to a strong earthquake.[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-IllPreped-346)

### Climate

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg/500px-Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Soil_moisture_and_climate_change.svg)

The projections of the [IPCC Sixth Assessment Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPCC_Sixth_Assessment_Report "IPCC Sixth Assessment Report") show clearly the impacts of climate change on Israel even at 2 degrees of warming.

Temperatures vary widely, especially during the winter. Coastal areas, such as those of Tel Aviv and Haifa, have a typical [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate") with cool, rainy winters and long, hot summers. The area of Beersheba and the northern Negev have a [semi-arid climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate") with hot summers, cool winters, and fewer rainy days. The southern Negev and the Arabah areas have a [desert climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_climate "Desert climate") with very hot, dry summers, and mild winters with few days of rain. The highest temperature of 54°C (129°F) was recorded in 1942 in the [Tirat Zvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirat_Zvi "Tirat Zvi") kibbutz.[[339]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-watzman-347)[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-348) Mountainous regions can be windy and cold, and areas at elevation of 750 metres (2,460 ft) or more (same elevation as Jerusalem) usually receive at least one [snowfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snow_in_Israel "Snow in Israel") each year.[[341]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoldreich200385-349) From May to September, rain is rare.[[342]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-350)[[343]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-351)

There are four different [phytogeographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytogeography "Phytogeography") regions, due to its location between the temperate and tropical zones. For this reason, the flora and fauna are extremely diverse. There are 2,867 known [species of plants in Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_endemic_flora_of_Israel "List of endemic flora of Israel"). Of these, at least 253 species are [introduced and non-native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_adventive_wild_plants_in_Israel "List of adventive wild plants in Israel").[[344]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-352) There are 380 [Israeli nature reserves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_parks_and_nature_reserves_of_Israel "National parks and nature reserves of Israel").[[345]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-353)

With scarce water resources, Israel has developed various water-saving technologies, including [drip irrigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drip_irrigation "Drip irrigation").[[346]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-354)[[347]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-355) The considerable sunlight available for [solar energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_energy "Solar energy") makes [Israel the leading nation in solar energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_power_in_Israel "Solar power in Israel") use per capita—practically every house uses solar panels for water heating.[[348]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Solar_energy-356) The [Ministry of Environmental Protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Environmental_Protection_(Israel) "Ministry of Environmental Protection (Israel)") has reported that [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_in_Israel "Climate change in Israel") "will have a decisive impact on all areas of life", particularly for vulnerable populations.[[349]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-MEP_2020-357)
