Israel has the largest Jewish population in the world and is the only country where Jews are the majority.[[606]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-614) As of April 2025, the population was an estimated 10,094,000.[[607]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-615) In 2025, the government recorded 72% of the population as [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Jews "Israeli Jews"), 21% as [Arabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_citizens_of_Israel "Arab citizens of Israel"), and 7% as "Others" (non-Arab Christians and people who have no religion listed).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-population_stat2024-17) Over the last decade, large numbers of migrant workers from Romania, Thailand, China, Africa, and South America have settled in Israel. Exact figures are unknown, as many of them are living in the country illegally,[[608]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-616) but estimates run from 166,000 to 203,000.[[609]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Adriana_Kemp-617) By June 2012, approximately 60,000 [African migrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_immigration_from_Africa_to_Israel "Illegal immigration from Africa to Israel") had entered Israel.[[610]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-618)

About 93% of Israelis live in urban areas.[[611]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-619) 90% of Palestinian Israelis reside in 139 densely populated towns and villages concentrated in the Galilee, [Triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle_(Israel) "Triangle (Israel)") and Negev regions, with the remaining 10% in [mixed cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_cities "Mixed cities") and neighbourhoods.[[612]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-620) The OECD in 2016 estimated the average life expectancy at 82.5 years, the [6th-highest in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy "List of countries by life expectancy").[[613]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-OECD_life_expec-621) Israeli Arab life expectancy lags by 3 to 4 years[[614]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-622)[[615]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-623) and is higher than in most Arab and Muslim countries.[[616]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-624)[[617]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-625) The country has the highest [fertility rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_fertility_rate "Total fertility rate") in the OECD and the only one which is above the replacement figure of 2.1.[[618]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:5-626) Retention of Israel's population since 1948 is about even or greater, when compared to other countries with mass immigration.[[619]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-627) Jewish emigration from Israel (called _[yerida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yerida "Yerida")_), primarily to the United States and Canada, is described by demographers as modest,[[620]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-628) but is often cited by Israeli government ministries as a major threat to Israel's future.[[621]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-629)[[622]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-630)

Approximately 80% of [Israeli Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Jews "Israeli Jews") are [born in Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabra_(person) "Sabra (person)"), 14% are immigrants from Europe and the Americas, and 6% are immigrants from Asia and Africa.[[623]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-631) Jews from Europe and the former Soviet Union and their descendants born in Israel, including Ashkenazi Jews, constitute approximately 44% of Jewish Israelis. Jews from Arab and Muslim countries and their descendants, including both Mizrahi and Sephardi Jews,[[624]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-632) form most of the rest of the Jewish population.[[625]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-633) Jewish intermarriage rates run at over 35% and recent studies suggest that the percentage of Israelis descended from both Sephardi and Ashkenazi Jews increases by 0.5 per cent yearly, with over 25% of schoolchildren now originating from both.[[626]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-634) Around 4% of Israelis (300,000), ethnically defined as "others", are Russian descendants of Jewish origin or family who are not Jewish according to rabbinical law, but were eligible for citizenship under the Law of Return.[[627]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-635)[[628]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Israel_people-636)[[629]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-637)

Israeli settlers beyond the Green Line number over 600,000 (≈10% of the Jewish Israeli population).[[630]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-638)In 2016, [399,300 Israelis lived](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_statistics_for_Israeli_settlements_in_the_West_Bank "Population statistics for Israeli settlements in the West Bank") in West Bank settlements,[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-districts_pop-374) including those that predated the establishment of the State of Israel and which were re-established after the Six-Day War. Additionally there were more than 200,000 Jews living in East Jerusalem[[367]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-jerusalem_pop-375) and 22,000 in the Golan Heights.[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-districts_pop-374) Approximately 7,800 Israelis [lived in settlements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_statistics_for_Israeli_Gaza_Strip_settlements "Population statistics for Israeli Gaza Strip settlements") in the Gaza Strip, known as [Gush Katif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gush_Katif "Gush Katif"), until they were evacuated by the government as part of its 2005 [disengagement plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel's_unilateral_disengagement_plan "Israel's unilateral disengagement plan").[[631]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-639)

Israeli Arabs (including the Arab population of East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights) comprise 21.1% of the population or 1,995,000 people.[[632]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-640) In a 2017 poll, 40% of Arab citizens of Israel identified as "Arab in Israel" or "Arab citizen of Israel", 15% identified as "Palestinian", 8.9% as "Palestinian in Israel" or "Palestinian citizen of Israel", and 8.7% as "Arab"; the same poll found that 60% of Israeli Arabs have a positive view of the state.[[633]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-641)[[634]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-642)

Israel has four major metropolitan areas: [Gush Dan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gush_Dan "Gush Dan") (Tel Aviv metropolitan area; population 3,854,000), [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem_metropolitan_area "Jerusalem metropolitan area") (population 1,253,900), [Haifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haifa_metropolitan_area "Haifa metropolitan area") (924,400), and [Beersheba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beersheba_metropolitan_area "Beersheba metropolitan area") (377,100).[[635]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-643) The largest municipality, in population and area, is Jerusalem with 1,050,153 residents in an area of 125 square kilometres (48 sq mi).[[636]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Israelpopulations-644) Statistics on Jerusalem include the population and area of East Jerusalem, the status of which is in international dispute.[[637]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-645) Tel Aviv and Haifa rank as Israel's next most populous cities, with populations of 494,900 and 297,082, respectively.[[636]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Israelpopulations-644) The (mainly [Haredi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haredi "Haredi")) city of [Bnei Brak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bnei_Brak "Bnei Brak") is the most densely populated city in Israel and one of the [10 most densely populated cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_proper_by_population_density "List of cities proper by population density") in the world.[[638]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-646)

Israel has 16 cities with populations over 100,000. As of 2018 there are 77 localities granted ["municipalities" (or "city") status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_council_(Israel) "City council (Israel)") by the Ministry of the Interior,[[639]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-647)[four of which are in the West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Israeli_settlements_with_city_status_in_the_West_Bank "List of Israeli settlements with city status in the West Bank").[[640]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-648)

### Language

[![Image 49](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_%283777232251%29.jpg/250px-%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_%283777232251%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%D7%A9%D7%9C%D7%98_%D7%A8%D7%97%D7%95%D7%91_%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%93%D7%94_(3777232251).jpg)

[Road sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_signs_in_Israel "Road signs in Israel") in [Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language"), [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language_in_Israel "Arabic language in Israel"), and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language")

The official language is [Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language"). Hebrew is the primary language of the state and is spoken daily by the majority of the population. Prior to 1948, [opposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Yiddish_sentiment "Anti-Yiddish sentiment") to [Yiddish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yiddish "Yiddish"), the historical language of the Ashkenazi Jews, was common among supporters of the Zionist movement, including the Yishuv, who sought to promote [Hebrew's revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_of_the_Hebrew_language "Revival of the Hebrew language") as a unifying national language.[[642]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-650) These sentiments were reflected in the early policies of the Israeli government, which largely banned [Yiddish theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yiddish_theatre "Yiddish theatre") and publications.[[643]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-651) Until 2018, [Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language_in_Israel "Arabic language in Israel") was also an official language;[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-lang1-15) in 2018 it was downgraded to having a "special status in the state".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-lang2-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-lang3-14) Arabic is spoken by the Arab minority and is the main medium of teaching in Arab schools where Hebrew is studied as a subject.[[644]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-arabic_lang-652) Arabic is studied in most Jewish schools and is often used on signage and in transport announcements.[[645]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-653)

Due to mass immigration from the former Soviet Union and [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah_from_Ethiopia "Aliyah from Ethiopia") (some 130,000 [Ethiopian Jews live in Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Jews_in_Israel "Ethiopian Jews in Israel")),[[646]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-The_Ethiopian_Population_In_Israel-654)[[647]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-655)[Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language_in_Israel "Russian language in Israel") and [Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic "Amharic") are widely spoken.[[648]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-656) Over one million Russian-speaking immigrants arrived in Israel between 1990 and 2004.[[649]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-657) French is spoken by around 700,000 Israelis,[[650]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-658) mostly originating [from France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Jews_in_Israel "French Jews in Israel") and North Africa (see [Maghrebi Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maghrebi_Jews "Maghrebi Jews")). English was an official language during the Mandate period;[[651]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-659) it lost this status after the establishment of Israel, but retains a role comparable to that of an official language.[[652]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-660)[[653]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-661) Many Israelis communicate reasonably well in English, as many television programmes are broadcast in English with subtitles and the language is taught in elementary school. The primary medium of teaching in Israeli universities is Hebrew, but some courses are offered in English.[[654]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-662)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

The main language of the [Circassians in Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassians_in_Israel "Circassians in Israel") is [Adyghe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adyghe_language "Adyghe language"), and most of them also know Hebrew and Arabic.

The deaf community in Israel primarily uses [Israeli Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Sign_Language "Israeli Sign Language"). Several [village sign languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Village_sign_language "Village sign language") are used in Israel, most notably the [Al-Sayyid Bedouin Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Sayyid_Bedouin_Sign_Language "Al-Sayyid Bedouin Sign Language") and the [Kafr Qasem Sign Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kafr_Qasem_Sign_Language "Kafr Qasem Sign Language").

### Religion

[![Image 50: A large open area with people bounded by old stone walls. To the left is a mosque with large golden dome.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Westernwall2.jpg/250px-Westernwall2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Westernwall2.jpg)

The [Dome of the Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dome_of_the_Rock "Dome of the Rock") and the [Western Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Wall "Western Wall"), Jerusalem

The estimated religious affiliation as of 2022 was 73.5% Jewish, 18.1% [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims"), 1.9% [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians "Christians"), 1.6% [Druze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Druze "Druze"), and 4.9% other.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-cia-19) The [religious affiliation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_religious_movements "Jewish religious movements") of [Israeli Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Jews "Israeli Jews") varies widely: a 2016 survey by [Pew Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research "Pew Research") indicates that 49% self-identify as [Hiloni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiloni "Hiloni") (secular), 29% as [Masorti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masortim "Masortim") (traditional), 13% as [Dati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dati "Dati") (religious) and 9% as [Haredi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haredi_Judaism "Haredi Judaism") (ultra-Orthodox).[[655]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-663) Haredi Jews are expected to represent over 20% of the Jewish population by 2028.[[656]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-664)[Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_Israel "Islam in Israel") constitute the largest religious minority, making up about 18.1% of the population. About 1.9% of the population is [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_in_Israel "Christianity in Israel"), and 1.6% is [Druze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Druze_in_Israel "Druze in Israel").[[657]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-CIA2022-665) The Christian population comprises primarily [Arab Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Christians "Arab Christians") and [Aramean Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arameans_in_Israel "Arameans in Israel") but also includes post-Soviet immigrants, foreign labourers, [Armenian Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians_in_Israel_and_Palestine "Armenians in Israel and Palestine"), and followers of [Messianic Judaism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messianic_Judaism "Messianic Judaism"), considered by most Christians and Jews to be a form of Christianity.[[658]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-666) Members of many other religious groups, including [Buddhists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism "Buddhism") and [Hindus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism_in_Israel "Hinduism in Israel"), maintain a presence in Israel, albeit in small numbers.[[659]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-667) Out of over one million immigrants from the former Soviet Union, about 300,000 are considered not Jewish by the [Chief Rabbinate of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbinate_of_Israel "Chief Rabbinate of Israel").[[660]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-668)

Israel comprises a major part of the [Holy Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Land "Holy Land"), a region of significant importance to all [Abrahamic religions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abrahamic_religions "Abrahamic religions"). Jerusalem is of [special importance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_significance_of_Jerusalem "Religious significance of Jerusalem") to Jews, Muslims, and Christians, as it is the home of [sites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_places_in_Jerusalem "List of places in Jerusalem") that are pivotal to their religious beliefs, such as the [Old City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_City_(Jerusalem) "Old City (Jerusalem)") that incorporates the [Western Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Wall "Western Wall") and the [Temple Mount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_Mount "Temple Mount") (Al-Aqsa Mosque compound) and the [Church of the Holy Sepulchre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_the_Holy_Sepulchre "Church of the Holy Sepulchre").[[661]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-669) Other locations of religious importance are [Nazareth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazareth "Nazareth") (site of the [Annunciation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annunciation "Annunciation") of [Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_(mother_of_Jesus) "Mary (mother of Jesus)")), [Tiberias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiberias "Tiberias") and [Safed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safed "Safed") (two of the [Four Holy Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Holy_Cities "Four Holy Cities") in Judaism), the [White Mosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mosque,_Ramla "White Mosque, Ramla") in [Ramla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramla "Ramla") (shrine of the prophet [Saleh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salih "Salih")), and the [Church of Saint George and Mosque of Al-Khadr, Lod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Saint_George_and_Mosque_of_Al-Khadr,_Lod "Church of Saint George and Mosque of Al-Khadr, Lod") (tomb of [Saint George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_George "Saint George") or [Al Khidr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Khidr "Al Khidr")). A number of other religious landmarks are located in the [West Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank "West Bank"), including [Joseph's Tomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph's_Tomb "Joseph's Tomb"), the [birthplace of Jesus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_the_Nativity "Church of the Nativity"), [Rachel's Tomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel's_Tomb "Rachel's Tomb"), and the [Cave of the Patriarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cave_of_the_Patriarchs "Cave of the Patriarchs"). The [administrative center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arc_(Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD) "Arc (Baháʼí)") of the [Baháʼí Faith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_Faith "Baháʼí Faith") and the [Shrine of the Báb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_of_the_B%C3%A1b "Shrine of the Báb") are located at the [Baháʼí World Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_World_Centre "Baháʼí World Centre") in [Haifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haifa "Haifa"); the leader of the faith is [buried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_of_Bah%C3%A1'u'll%C3%A1h "Shrine of Bahá'u'lláh") in [Acre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acre,_Israel "Acre, Israel").[[662]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-670)[[663]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-671)[[664]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-672) The [Mahmood Mosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmood_Mosque,_Haifa "Mahmood Mosque, Haifa") is affiliated with the reformist [Ahmadiyya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmadiyya_in_Israel "Ahmadiyya in Israel") movement. [Kababir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kababir "Kababir"), Haifa's mixed neighbourhood of Jews and Ahmadi Arabs, is one of a few of its kind in the country.[[665]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-673)[[666]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-674)

### Education

[![Image 51](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg/250px-Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brain_research_labs-Bar_Ilan_university.jpg)

[Multidisciplinary Brain Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar-Ilan_University#Leslie_and_Susan_Gonda_Multidisciplinary_Brain_Research_Center "Bar-Ilan University") at [Bar-Ilan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar-Ilan_University "Bar-Ilan University")

In 2015, Israel [ranked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_tertiary_education_attainment "List of countries by tertiary education attainment") third among OECD members for the percentage of 25–64-year-olds that have attained tertiary education with 49% compared with the OECD average of 35%.[[667]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-OECD_education-675) In 2012, the country ranked third in the number of academic degrees per capita (20 per cent of the population).[[668]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-676)

Israel has a [school life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_life_expectancy "School life expectancy") of 16 years and a [literacy rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_literacy_rate "List of countries by literacy rate") of 97.8%.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-cia-19) The State Education Law (1953) established five types of schools: state secular, state religious, ultra orthodox, communal settlement schools, and Arab schools. The public secular is the largest school group and is attended by the majority of Jewish and non-Arab pupils. Most Arabs send their children to Arabic-language schools.[[644]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-arabic_lang-652) Education is compulsory between the ages of three and eighteen.[[669]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-677) Schooling is divided into three tiers—primary school (grades 1–6), middle school (grades 7–9), and high school (grades 10–12)—culminating with _[Bagrut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagrut "Bagrut")_ matriculation exams. Proficiency in core subjects such as mathematics, the Hebrew language, Hebrew and general literature, the English language, history, Biblical scripture and civics is necessary to receive a Bagrut certificate.[[670]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-moia-678)

The Jewish population maintains a relatively high level of educational attainment where just under half of all Israeli Jews (46%) hold post-secondary degrees.[[671]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-679)[[672]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-680) Israeli Jews 25 and older have an average 11.6 years of schooling, making them one of the most highly educated of all major religious groups in the world.[[673]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-681)[[674]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-682) In Arab, Christian and Druze schools, the exam on Biblical studies is replaced by an exam on Muslim, Christian or Druze heritage, respectively.[[675]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-683) In 2020, 68.7% of 12th graders earned a matriculation certificate.[[676]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-684)

### Health

[![Image 53](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/PTBeilinson.jpg/250px-PTBeilinson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PTBeilinson.jpg)

[Rabin Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabin_Medical_Center "Rabin Medical Center") in [Petah Tikva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petah_Tikva "Petah Tikva"), Israel

[Health in Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_in_Israel "Health in Israel") is advanced and efficient compared to other developed countries; Israel spends 7.3% of their gross domestic product on health compared to 9.3% in the OECD and 18% in the US. With the passing of the 1995 National Healthcare Law, there is mandated universal healthcare for 100% of the population funded by a health tax which is a fixed percentage of income.[[681]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-wi-689)[[682]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-690) This health care 'basket' includes a list of services mandated by the Ministry of health. Individuals can purchase coverage for additional services for an extra charge.[[683]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-691) Despite the cost savings in healthcare, the health status in Israel is satisfactory compared to other countries.[[681]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-wi-689)[[684]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-692)

The life expectancy in Israel is 83.8 years, above the [OECD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECD "OECD") average by 2.7 years. Preventable mortality is 78 per 100,000, which is less than the OECD average of 145, whereas treatable mortality is 56 per 100,000, also less than the OECD average of 77. The suicide rate is 4 per 100,000, which is lower than the OECD average of 11. However, 9.1% of Israelis consider their health status bad or very bad, which is higher than the OECD average of 8.0%.[[685]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-z261-693) Major risk factors include, smoking by 17.0 percent of the population, above the OECD average of 14.8 percent. Alcohol use is less at 2.7 liters per person compared to 8.5 liters. Twenty-eight percent of adults do not get exercise, a little below the 30 percent average. Obesity in Israel is 18 percent, near the OECDs 19 percent.[[685]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-z261-693)

## Culture

Cultural diversity stems from its diverse population: Jews from various diaspora communities brought their cultural and religious traditions with them.[[686]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-694)[Arab influences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_citizens_of_Israel#Culture "Arab citizens of Israel") are found in [architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Architecture_of_Israel "Architecture of Israel"),[[687]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-695)[music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Israel "Music of Israel"),[[688]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-696) and [cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_cuisine "Israeli cuisine"),[[689]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-697) among others.[[690]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-MendelRanta2016p137-698) Israel is the only country where life revolves around the [Hebrew calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_calendar "Hebrew calendar"), which is aligned to the seasons in the Levant. [Public holidays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_holidays_in_Israel "Public holidays in Israel") are determined by the [Jewish holidays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_holidays "Jewish holidays"), and except for [Yom HaAtzma'ut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_HaAtzma'ut "Yom HaAtzma'ut") (Independence Day) there are no annual civil holidays. The official day of rest is Saturday, the [Jewish Sabbath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat").[[691]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-699)

### Literature

[Israeli literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_literature "Israeli literature") is primarily [poetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Hebrew_poetry "Modern Hebrew poetry") and prose written in Hebrew, as part of the [renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_of_the_Hebrew_language "Revival of the Hebrew language") of Hebrew as a spoken language since the mid-19th century, although a small body of literature is published in other languages. By law, two copies of all works published in Israel must be deposited in the [National Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Library_of_Israel "National Library of Israel").[[692]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-700) In 2016, 89 per cent of the 7,300 books transferred to the library were in Hebrew.[[693]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-701)

In 1966, [Shmuel Yosef Agnon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shmuel_Yosef_Agnon "Shmuel Yosef Agnon") shared the [Nobel Prize in Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature") with German Jewish author [Nelly Sachs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelly_Sachs "Nelly Sachs").[[694]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-702) Leading poets include [Yehuda Amichai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yehuda_Amichai "Yehuda Amichai"), [Nathan Alterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Alterman "Nathan Alterman"), [Leah Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leah_Goldberg "Leah Goldberg"), and [Rachel Bluwstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Bluwstein "Rachel Bluwstein").[[695]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-703) Internationally famous contemporary novelists include [Amos Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amos_Oz "Amos Oz"), [Etgar Keret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etgar_Keret "Etgar Keret") and [David Grossman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Grossman "David Grossman").[[696]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-704)[[697]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-705)

### Music and dance

[![Image 54: Several dozen musicians in formal dress, holding their instruments, behind a conductor](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Israel_Philharmonic_Orchestra.jpg/330px-Israel_Philharmonic_Orchestra.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Israel_Philharmonic_Orchestra.jpg)

[Israel Philharmonic Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Philharmonic_Orchestra "Israel Philharmonic Orchestra") conducted by [Zubin Mehta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zubin_Mehta "Zubin Mehta")

[Israeli music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Israel "Music of Israel") includes [Mizrahi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mizrahi_music "Mizrahi music") and [Sephardic music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephardic_music "Sephardic music"), [Hasidic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasidic_Judaism "Hasidic Judaism") melodies, [Greek music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_music_in_Israel "Greek music in Israel"), [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz"), and [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock").[[698]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBroughtonEllinghamTrillo1999365%E2%80%93369-706)[[699]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-707) The [Israel Philharmonic Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Philharmonic_Orchestra "Israel Philharmonic Orchestra")[[700]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBen-Sasson19851095-708)[[701]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-709) has been in operation for over seventy years and performs more than two hundred concerts each year.[[702]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-710)[Itzhak Perlman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itzhak_Perlman "Itzhak Perlman"), [Pinchas Zukerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinchas_Zukerman "Pinchas Zukerman") and [Ofra Haza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ofra_Haza "Ofra Haza") are among the internationally acclaimed musicians born in Israel. The country [has participated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest "Israel in the Eurovision Song Contest") in the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest "Eurovision Song Contest") nearly every year since 1973, winning it four times and hosting three times.[[703]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-history-711)[Eilat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eilat "Eilat") has hosted its own international music festival, the [Red Sea Jazz Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea_Jazz_Festival "Red Sea Jazz Festival"), every summer since 1987.[[704]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-712) The nation's canonical [folk songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") are known as "Songs of the Land of Israel".[[705]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-713)

### Cinema and theatre

Ten Israeli films [have been final nominees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Israeli_submissions_for_the_Academy_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "List of Israeli submissions for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film") for [Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film") at the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). Palestinian Israeli filmmakers have made films dealing with the Arab-Israeli conflict and status of Palestinians within Israel, such as [Mohammad Bakri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_Bakri "Mohammad Bakri")'s 2002 film _[Jenin, Jenin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenin,\_Jenin "Jenin, Jenin")_ and _[The Syrian Bride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Syrian\_Bride "The Syrian Bride")_.

Continuing the strong theatrical traditions of the [Yiddish theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yiddish_theatre "Yiddish theatre") in Eastern Europe, Israel maintains a vibrant theatre scene. Founded in 1918, [Habima Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habima_Theatre "Habima Theatre") in Tel Aviv is Israel's oldest [repertory theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repertory_theatre "Repertory theatre") company and national theatre.[[706]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-714) Other theatres include [Ohel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohel_Theater "Ohel Theater"), [the Cameri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameri_Theatre "Cameri Theatre") and [Gesher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gesher_Theater "Gesher Theater").[[707]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-715)[[708]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-716)

### Visual arts

[![Image 55](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/%D7%A9%D7%90%D7%92%D7%AA_%D7%94%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%94.jpg/250px-%D7%A9%D7%90%D7%92%D7%AA_%D7%94%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%94.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%D7%A9%D7%90%D7%92%D7%AA_%D7%94%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%94.jpg)

_[The Roaring Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Roaring\_Lion\_(sculpture) "The Roaring Lion (sculpture)")_ sculpture by [Avraham Melnikov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avraham_Melnikov "Avraham Melnikov")

Israeli Jewish art has been particularly influenced by the [Kabbalah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabbalah "Kabbalah"), the [Talmud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talmud "Talmud") and the [Zohar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zohar "Zohar"). Another art movement that held a prominent role in the 20th century was the [School of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_of_Paris "School of Paris"). In the late 19th and early 20th century, the Yishuv's art was dominated by art trends emanating [Bezalel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezalel_Academy_of_Arts_and_Design "Bezalel Academy of Arts and Design"). Beginning in the 1920s, the local art scene was heavily influenced by modern French art, first introduced by [Isaac Frenkel Frenel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Frenkel "Yitzhak Frenkel").[[709]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-717)[[710]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-718) Jewish masters of the [school of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_of_Paris "School of Paris"), such as [Soutine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cha%C3%AFm_Soutine "Chaïm Soutine"), [Kikoine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Kikoine "Michel Kikoine"), [Frenkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Frenkel "Yitzhak Frenkel"), [Chagall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Chagall "Marc Chagall") heavily influenced the development of Israeli art.[[711]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-719)[[712]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:43-720) Israeli sculpture took inspiration from modern [European sculpture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_of_Europe "Art of Europe") as well [Mesopotamian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_of_Mesopotamia "Art of Mesopotamia"), [Assyrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assyrian_sculpture "Assyrian sculpture") and local art.[[713]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:6-721)[[714]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-722)[Avraham Melnikov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avraham_Melnikov "Avraham Melnikov")'s [The Roaring Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Roaring_Lion_(sculpture) "The Roaring Lion (sculpture)"), David Polus' Alexander Zaid and [Ze'ev Ben Zvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeev_Ben-Zvi "Zeev Ben-Zvi")'s cubist sculpture exemplify some of the different streams in sculpture.[[713]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:6-721)[[715]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-723)[[716]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-724)

Common themes in art are the mystical cities of Safed and Jerusalem, the bohemian café culture of Tel Aviv, agricultural landscapes, biblical stories and war. Today Israeli art has delved into [optical art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_art "Optical art"), [AI art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_art "Artificial intelligence art"), [digital art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_art "Digital art") and the use of salt in sculpture.[[712]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:43-720)

### Architecture

[![Image 56](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fc/%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%96%D7%99%D7%90%D7%95%D7%9F_%D7%94%D7%91%D7%90%D7%95%D7%94%D7%90%D7%95%D7%A11.jpg/250px-%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%96%D7%99%D7%90%D7%95%D7%9F_%D7%94%D7%91%D7%90%D7%95%D7%94%D7%90%D7%95%D7%A11.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%96%D7%99%D7%90%D7%95%D7%9F_%D7%94%D7%91%D7%90%D7%95%D7%94%D7%90%D7%95%D7%A11.jpg)

[Bauhaus Museum Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bauhaus_Foundation_Tel_Aviv "Bauhaus Foundation Tel Aviv")

Due to the immigration of Jewish architects, architecture has come to reflect different styles. In the early 20th century Jewish architects sought to combine Occidental and Oriental architecture producing buildings that showcase a myriad of infused styles.[[717]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-725) The [eclectic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eclecticism_in_architecture "Eclecticism in architecture") style gave way to the modernist [Bauhaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bauhaus "Bauhaus") style with the influx of German Jewish architects (among them [Erich Mendelsohn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erich_Mendelsohn "Erich Mendelsohn")) fleeing [Nazi persecution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_persecution_of_Jews "Nazi persecution of Jews").[[718]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-726)[[719]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-727) The [White City of Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_City,_Tel_Aviv "White City, Tel Aviv") is a [UNESCO heritage site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_Heritage_site "UNESCO Heritage site").[[720]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-728) Following independence, multiple government projects were commissioned, a grand part built in a brutalist style with heavy emphasis on the use of concrete and acclimatisation to the desert climate.[[721]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-729)[[722]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-730) Several novel ideas such as the [Garden City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_city_movement "Garden city movement") were implemented in Israeli cities; the [Geddes plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geddes_Plan_for_Tel_Aviv "Geddes Plan for Tel Aviv") of Tel Aviv became renowned internationally for its revolutionary design and adaptation to the local climate.[[723]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-731)

### Museums

[![Image 57](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Billy_Rose_Art_Garden_%2814755133799%29.jpg/250px-Billy_Rose_Art_Garden_%2814755133799%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Billy_Rose_Art_Garden_(14755133799).jpg)

[Shrine of the Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_of_the_Book "Shrine of the Book"), repository of the [Dead Sea Scrolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea_Scrolls "Dead Sea Scrolls") in Jerusalem

The [Israel Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Museum "Israel Museum") in Jerusalem is one of Israel's most important cultural institutions,[[724]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-imj-732) and houses the [Dead Sea Scrolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea_Scrolls "Dead Sea Scrolls"),[[725]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-733) along with an extensive collection of [Judaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaica "Judaica") and [European art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_art "European art").[[724]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-imj-732)[Yad Vashem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yad_Vashem "Yad Vashem") ([Hebrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_language "Hebrew language"): יָד וַשֵׁם, lit.'a memorial and a name') is the world's central [Holocaust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust "Holocaust") memorial institution and archive of Holocaust-related information.[[726]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-734)[ANU - Museum of the Jewish People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANU_-_Museum_of_the_Jewish_People "ANU - Museum of the Jewish People") is an interactive museum devoted to the history of Jewish communities around the world.[[727]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-735)

Israel has the highest number of museums per capita.[[728]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-736) Several museums are devoted to Islamic culture, including the [Rockefeller Archaeological Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Museum "Rockefeller Museum") and the [L. A. Mayer Institute for Islamic Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L._A._Mayer_Institute_for_Islamic_Art "L. A. Mayer Institute for Islamic Art"), both in Jerusalem. The Rockefeller specialises in archaeological remains from Middle East history. It is also the home of the first hominid fossil skull found in West Asia, called [Galilee Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galilee_Man "Galilee Man").[[729]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-737)

### Mass media

Notable newspapers include the left-wing _[Haaretz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haaretz "Haaretz")_,[[730]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-738) centrist _[Yedioth Ahronoth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yedioth\_Ahronoth "Yedioth Ahronoth")_,[[731]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-739) and center-right _[Israel Hayom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel\_Hayom "Israel Hayom")_.[[732]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-740) There are several major television channels which cater to different audiences, from Russian-language [Channel 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Plus "Israel Plus")[[733]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-741) to Arabic-language [Kan 33](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kan_33 "Kan 33").[[734]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-742) The 2024 Freedom House report found Israeli media is "vibrant and free to criticise government policy".[[735]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-743) In the 2024 [Press Freedom Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_Freedom_Index "Press Freedom Index") by [Reporters Without Borders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reporters_Without_Borders "Reporters Without Borders"), Israel was placed 112th of 180 countries, second in the Middle East and North Africa.[[736]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-744)[[737]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-RSFNAME-745)

Reporters Without Borders reported that the Israel Defence Forces had killed more than 100 Palestinian journalists in Gaza. During the 2023 Gaza war, Israel has been alleged to be "trying to suppress the reporting coming out of the besieged enclave while disinformation infiltrates its own media ecosystem".[[737]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-RSFNAME-745) In May 2024, Israel shut down the local offices of [Al Jazeera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Jazeera "Al Jazeera").[[738]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-746) In 2024, according to the [Committee to Protect Journalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_to_Protect_Journalists "Committee to Protect Journalists"), Israel was the second leading country in jailing journalists,[[739]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-747) and responsible for the majority of journalists killed in the world.[[740]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-748)

### Cuisine

[![Image 58](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Food_in_Israel.jpg/250px-Food_in_Israel.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Food_in_Israel.jpg)

A meal including [falafel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falafel "Falafel"), [hummus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hummus "Hummus"), [French fries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_fries "French fries") and [Israeli salad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_salad "Israeli salad")

Israeli cuisine includes local dishes as well as [Jewish cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_cuisine "Jewish cuisine") brought to the country by immigrants. Particularly since the late 1970s, a [fusion cuisine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fusion_cuisine "Fusion cuisine") has developed.[[741]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-raviv-749) The cuisine has adapted elements of the [Mizrahi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mizrahi_Jewish_cuisine "Mizrahi Jewish cuisine"), [Sephardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephardic_Jewish_cuisine "Sephardic Jewish cuisine"), and [Ashkenazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_cuisine "Ashkenazi cuisine") styles of cooking. It incorporates many foods traditionally eaten in the [Levantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levantine_cuisine "Levantine cuisine"), [Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_cuisine "Arab cuisine"), [Middle Eastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Eastern_cuisine "Middle Eastern cuisine") and [Mediterranean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_cuisine "Mediterranean cuisine") cuisines, such as [falafel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falafel "Falafel"), [hummus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hummus "Hummus"), [shakshouka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakshouka "Shakshouka"), [couscous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couscous "Couscous"), and [za'atar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Za'atar "Za'atar"). [Schnitzel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schnitzel "Schnitzel"), [pizza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza "Pizza"), [hamburgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburger "Hamburger"), [French fries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_fries "French fries"), [rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice "Rice") and [salad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salad "Salad") are common. [Ptitim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_couscous "Israeli couscous") (Israeli couscous) is a notable Israeli food invented in the 1950s due to rice shortages during the [austerity period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austerity_in_Israel "Austerity in Israel").[[742]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-JannaGur-750)

Roughly half of the Jewish population attests to keeping [kosher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosher "Kosher") at home.[[743]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-751)[[744]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-bernstein_227,_233%E2%80%93234-752)[Kosher restaurants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosher_restaurant "Kosher restaurant") make up around a quarter of the total as of 2015.[[741]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-raviv-749) Pork—often called "white meat" in Israel[[745]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-bernstein-231-753)—is produced and consumed despite attempts to ban it; [it is forbidden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_restrictions_on_the_consumption_of_pork "Religious restrictions on the consumption of pork") by both Judaism and Islam but is permitted by Christianity and mostly produced in traditionally Christian areas of northern Israel.[[746]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-porkprod-754)[[747]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-755) Other non-kosher foods produced and eaten in Israel include rabbits, ostriches, and non-kosher fish.[[745]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-bernstein-231-753)

### Sports

[![Image 59](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/%D7%99%D7%A8%D7%95%D7%A7_%D7%A2%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%94.jpg/250px-%D7%99%D7%A8%D7%95%D7%A7_%D7%A2%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%94.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%D7%99%D7%A8%D7%95%D7%A7_%D7%A2%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%94.jpg)

[Maccabi Haifa F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Haifa_F.C. "Maccabi Haifa F.C.") fans at [Sammy Ofer Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sammy_Ofer_Stadium "Sammy Ofer Stadium") in the city of Haifa

The most popular spectator sports in Israel are association football and basketball.[[748]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTETorstrick2004141-756) The [Israeli Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Premier_League "Israeli Premier League") is the country's premier football league, and the [Israeli Basketball Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Basketball_Premier_League "Israeli Basketball Premier League") is the premier basketball league.[[749]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-757)[Maccabi Haifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Haifa_F.C. "Maccabi Haifa F.C."), [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_F.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C."), [Hapoel Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hapoel_Tel_Aviv_F.C. "Hapoel Tel Aviv F.C.") and [Beitar Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beitar_Jerusalem_F.C. "Beitar Jerusalem F.C.") are the largest [football clubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_football_clubs_in_Israel "List of football clubs in Israel"). Maccabi Tel Aviv, Maccabi Haifa and Hapoel Tel Aviv have competed in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") and Hapoel Tel Aviv reached the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Cup "UEFA Cup") quarter-finals. Israel hosted and won the [1964 AFC Asian Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_AFC_Asian_Cup "1964 AFC Asian Cup"); in 1970 the [Israel national football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_national_football_team "Israel national football team") qualified for the [FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_FIFA_World_Cup "1970 FIFA World Cup"), the only time it participated. The [1974 Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_Asian_Games "1974 Asian Games"), held in Tehran, were the last Asian Games in which Israel [participated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_at_the_Asian_Games "Israel at the Asian Games"), plagued by Arab countries that [refused to compete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycotts_of_Israel_in_sports "Boycotts of Israel in sports") with Israel. Israel was excluded from the [1978 Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_Asian_Games "1978 Asian Games") and since then has not competed in Asian sport events.[[750]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-758) In 1994, [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") agreed to admit Israel, and its football teams now compete in Europe. [Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_B.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.") has won the [European championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_European_Champions_Cup_and_EuroLeague_records_and_statistics "FIBA European Champions Cup and EuroLeague records and statistics") in basketball six times.[[751]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-759)

Israel has won [20 Olympic medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_at_the_Olympics "Israel at the Olympics") since its first win [in 1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics"), including a gold medal in [windsurfing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sailing_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_Mistral_One_Design "Sailing at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's Mistral One Design") at the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics"),[[752]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-760) and seven medals at the 2024 Paris Olympics.[[753]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-761) Israel has won [over 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_at_the_Paralympics "Israel at the Paralympics") gold medals in the [Paralympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralympic_Games "Paralympic Games") and is ranked 20th in the [all-time medal count](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-time_Paralympic_Games_medal_table "All-time Paralympic Games medal table"). The [1968 Summer Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Paralympics "1968 Summer Paralympics") were hosted by Israel.[[754]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-762) The [Maccabiah Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabiah_Games "Maccabiah Games"), an Olympic-style event for [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Jews_in_sports "List of Jews in sports") and Israeli athletes, has been held every four years since the 1930s. [Krav Maga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krav_Maga "Krav Maga"), a martial art developed by Jewish ghetto defenders, is used by the Israeli security forces and police.[[755]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-763)

[Chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess "Chess") is a leading sport. There are many Israeli grandmasters and [Israeli chess players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Israeli_chess_players "List of Israeli chess players") have won a number of youth world championships.[[756]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-764) Israel stages an annual international [championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Chess_Championship "Israeli Chess Championship") and hosted the [World Team Chess Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Team_Chess_Championship "World Team Chess Championship") in 2005.

Scholars have long doubted the historical accuracy of Cassius Dio's account of the consequences of the Bar Kokhba War (Roman History 69.14). According to this text, considered the most reliable literary source for the Second Jewish Revolt, the war encompassed all of Judea: the Romans destroyed 985 villages and 50 fortresses, and killed 580,000 rebels. This article reassesses Cassius Dio's figures by drawing on new evidence from excavations and surveys in Judea, Transjordan, and the Galilee. Three research methods are combined: an ethno-archaeological comparison with the settlement picture in the Ottoman Period, comparison with similar settlement studies in the Galilee, and an evaluation of settled sites from the Middle Roman Period (70–136 CE). The study demonstrates the potential contribution of the archaeological record to this issue and supports the view of Cassius Dio's demographic data as a reliable account, which he based on contemporaneous documentation.

The Jewish community strove to recover from the catastrophic results of the Bar Kokhva revolt (132–135 CE). Although some of these attempts were relatively successful, the Jews never fully recovered. During the Late Roman and Byzantine periods, many Jews emigrated to thriving centres in the diaspora, especially Iraq, whereas some converted to Christianity and others continued to live in the Holy Land, especially in Galilee and the coastal plain. During the Byzantine period, the three provinces of Palestine included more than thirty cities, namely, settlements with a bishop see. After the Muslim conquest in the 630s, most of these cities declined and eventually disappeared. As a result, in many cases the local ecclesiastical administration weakened, while in others it simply ceased to exist. Consequently, many local Christians converted to Islam. Thus, almost twelve centuries later, when the army led by Napoleon Bonaparte arrived in the Holy Land, most of the local population was Muslim.

**Israel**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-29) officially the **State of Israel**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-30) is a country in the [Southern Levant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Levant "Southern Levant") region of [West Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia"). It is [bordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borders_of_Israel "Borders of Israel") by [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon "Lebanon") to the north, [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria") to the northeast, [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan "Jordan") to the east, and [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt") to the southwest. [Israel's western coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_coastal_plain "Israeli coastal plain") lies on the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea"), its southern tip reaches the [Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea"), and to the east is [Earth's lowest point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extremes_on_Earth "Extremes on Earth") near the [Dead Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea "Dead Sea"). [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem") is the government seat and [proclaimed capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_of_Jerusalem "Status of Jerusalem"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-31) while [Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv "Tel Aviv") is Israel's [largest urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gush_Dan "Gush Dan") and economic centre.

The [Land of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_of_Israel "Land of Israel"), also called [Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_(region) "Palestine (region)") or the [Holy Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Land "Holy Land"), was home to the ancient [Canaanites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canaan "Canaan") and later the kingdoms of [Israel and Judah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Israel_and_Judah "Ancient Israel and Judah") and [Hasmonean Judea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmonean_Judea "Hasmonean Judea"). Located near [continental crossroads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levantine_corridor "Levantine corridor"), its [demographics shifted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_Palestine_(region) "Demographic history of Palestine (region)") under various empires. 19th-century Jewish nationalism, alongside [European antisemitism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_antisemitism "European antisemitism"), fuelled the [Zionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionist "Zionist") movement for a [Jewish homeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_homeland "Jewish homeland") in Palestine, then an Ottoman region with an overwhelming Arab majority.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-32) The movement gained [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") support with the 1917 [Balfour Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balfour_Declaration "Balfour Declaration"). After [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), Britain occupied the region and established [Mandatory Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine "Mandatory Palestine"). British rule and [Jewish immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah "Aliyah") in the leadup to the Holocaust intensified [Arab-Jewish tensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercommunal_conflict_in_Mandatory_Palestine "Intercommunal conflict in Mandatory Palestine") with Arab opposition to Zionism driven largely by concerns of displacement and dispossession.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-33)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-34) The 1947 [UN Partition Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine "United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine") proposed separate Arab and Jewish states. The Jewish leadership accepted the plan while the Palestinian Arab leadership rejected it, arguing it violated the principle of [self-determination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-determination "Self-determination") and constituted Western colonial interference.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-35)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:0-36)[Civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947%E2%80%931948_civil_war_in_Mandatory_Palestine "1947–1948 civil war in Mandatory Palestine") followed, and Israel [declared independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence "Israeli Declaration of Independence") on 14 May 1948, shortly before the end of the [mandate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandate_for_Palestine "Mandate for Palestine"). The conflict subsequently escalated with the [intervention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War "1948 Arab–Israeli War") of [Arab states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world "Arab world").

The [1949 armistice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements "1949 Armistice Agreements") left Israel controlling more territory than had been allocated to it under the UN partition plan.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Britannica-37) No independent Palestinian Arab state was established, leaving [Gaza under Egyptian control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Gaza_Strip_by_the_United_Arab_Republic "Occupation of the Gaza Strip by the United Arab Republic") and the [West Bank ruled by Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordanian_annexation_of_the_West_Bank "Jordanian annexation of the West Bank").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Britannica-37)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-38)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFischbach200826%E2%80%9327-39) Most [Palestinian Arabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians")[fled or were expelled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Palestinian_expulsion_and_flight "1948 Palestinian expulsion and flight") during the [Nakba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakba "Nakba"),[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTESlater202081%E2%80%9392,_350-40)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-41)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-42) while Israeli independence prompted [antisemitism in the Arab world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism_in_the_Arab_world "Antisemitism in the Arab world") and [Jewish exodus therefrom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_exodus_from_the_Muslim_world "Jewish exodus from the Muslim world"), mainly to Israel.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:05-43)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:22-44) After the 1967

**Israel**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-29) officially the **State of Israel**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-30) is a country in the [Southern Levant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Levant "Southern Levant") region of [West Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia"). It is [bordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borders_of_Israel "Borders of Israel") by [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon "Lebanon") to the north, [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria") to the northeast, [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan "Jordan") to the east, and [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt") to the southwest. [Israel's western coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_coastal_plain "Israeli coastal plain") lies on the [Mediterranean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea"), its southern tip reaches the [Red Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea "Red Sea"), and to the east is [Earth's lowest point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extremes_on_Earth "Extremes on Earth") near the [Dead Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Sea "Dead Sea"). [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem") is the government seat and [proclaimed capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_of_Jerusalem "Status of Jerusalem"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-31) while [Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv "Tel Aviv") is Israel's [largest urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gush_Dan "Gush Dan") and economic centre.

The [Land of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_of_Israel "Land of Israel"), also called [Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_(region) "Palestine (region)") or the [Holy Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Land "Holy Land"), was home to the ancient [Canaanites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canaan "Canaan") and later the kingdoms of [Israel and Judah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Israel_and_Judah "Ancient Israel and Judah") and [Hasmonean Judea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmonean_Judea "Hasmonean Judea"). Located near [continental crossroads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levantine_corridor "Levantine corridor"), its [demographics shifted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographic_history_of_Palestine_(region) "Demographic history of Palestine (region)") under various empires. 19th-century Jewish nationalism, alongside [European antisemitism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_antisemitism "European antisemitism"), fuelled the [Zionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionist "Zionist") movement for a [Jewish homeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_homeland "Jewish homeland") in Palestine, then an Ottoman region with an overwhelming Arab majority.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-32) The movement gained [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire") support with the 1917 [Balfour Declaration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balfour_Declaration "Balfour Declaration"). After [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), Britain occupied the region and established [Mandatory Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine "Mandatory Palestine"). British rule and [Jewish immigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah "Aliyah") in the leadup to the Holocaust intensified [Arab-Jewish tensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercommunal_conflict_in_Mandatory_Palestine "Intercommunal conflict in Mandatory Palestine") with Arab opposition to Zionism driven largely by concerns of displacement and dispossession.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-33)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-34) The 1947 [UN Partition Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine "United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine") proposed separate Arab and Jewish states. The Jewish leadership accepted the plan while the Palestinian Arab leadership rejected it, arguing it violated the principle of [self-determination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-determination "Self-determination") and constituted Western colonial interference.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-35)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:0-36)[Civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947%E2%80%931948_civil_war_in_Mandatory_Palestine "1947–1948 civil war in Mandatory Palestine") followed, and Israel [declared independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Declaration_of_Independence "Israeli Declaration of Independence") on 14 May 1948, shortly before the end of the [mandate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandate_for_Palestine "Mandate for Palestine"). The conflict subsequently escalated with the [intervention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War "1948 Arab–Israeli War") of [Arab states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world "Arab world").

The [1949 armistice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements "1949 Armistice Agreements") left Israel controlling more territory than had been allocated to it under the UN partition plan.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Britannica-37) No independent Palestinian Arab state was established, leaving [Gaza under Egyptian control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_the_Gaza_Strip_by_the_United_Arab_Republic "Occupation of the Gaza Strip by the United Arab Republic") and the [West Bank ruled by Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordanian_annexation_of_the_West_Bank "Jordanian annexation of the West Bank").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-Britannica-37)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-38)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFischbach200826%E2%80%9327-39) Most [Palestinian Arabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians")[fled or were expelled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Palestinian_expulsion_and_flight "1948 Palestinian expulsion and flight") during the [Nakba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakba "Nakba"),[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-FOOTNOTESlater202081%E2%80%9392,_350-40)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-41)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-42) while Israeli independence prompted [antisemitism in the Arab world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism_in_the_Arab_world "Antisemitism in the Arab world") and [Jewish exodus therefrom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_exodus_from_the_Muslim_world "Jewish exodus from the Muslim world"), mainly to Israel.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:05-43)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel#cite_note-:22-44) After the 1967
