Abraham Chepkirwok

[![Image 1: Abraham Chepkirwok at ISTAF 2008](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Abraham_Chepkirwok.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Abraham_Chepkirwok.jpg "Abraham Chepkirwok at ISTAF 2008")
Personal information
Born 18 November 1988 (age 37)
Medal record Men's [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_(sport) "Athletics (sport)") Representing ![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Flag_of_Uganda.svg/40px-Flag_of_Uganda.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") [World Junior Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "IAAF World Junior Championships in Athletics") ![Image 3: Bronze medal – third place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Bronze_medal_icon_%28B_initial%29.svg/20px-Bronze_medal_icon_%28B_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2006 Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "2006 World Junior Championships in Athletics")800 m [World Athletics Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "IAAF World Athletics Final") ![Image 4: Silver medal – second place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg/20px-Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2008 Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "2008 IAAF World Athletics Final")800 m

**Abraham Chepkirwok** (born 18 November 1988) is a [Ugandan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")[middle-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle-distance_runner "Middle-distance runner") who specializes in the [800 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/800_metres "800 metres"). He is the Ugandan record holder in this distance, with 1:43.72 minutes, achieved in July 2008 in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid"). He is a [World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "IAAF World Junior Championships in Athletics") bronze medalist from 2006 and [Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics") competitor from 2008.

He was born in [Kapchorwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapchorwa "Kapchorwa"). By June 2006 he had run the 800 metres in 1:45.0 minutes, at a meet in [Kampala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala "Kampala").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) With this he was the season's world leader for juniors—athletes aged nineteen and less.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-beij-2) With electronic timing his best time was 1:45.44 minutes, achieved in a meet in Heusden.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) He competed at the [2006 World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "2006 World Junior Championships in Athletics") in Beijing, and won the bronze medal, having led the race halfway through but been outsprinted near the end by two Kenyan runners.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-beij-2)

In the 2006–07 indoor season he ran the 800 metres in 1:46.91 minutes in Stuttgart.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) This was a Ugandan indoor record.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) He opened the outdoor season by winning the IAAF Grand Prix in Dakar. He also won the Grand Prix meet in Hengelo, and finished third at the Super Grand Prix meet in Doha, the [Golden Spike Ostrava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Spike_Ostrava "Golden Spike Ostrava") and the [Bislett Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bislett_Games "Bislett Games").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) Then, in July 2007 he achieved a new personal best time of 1:44.78 minutes at the Grand Prix meet in Athens.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) A fifth place at the [All-Africa Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2007_All-Africa_Games "Athletics at the 2007 All-Africa Games")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) was followed by the entrance in the [2007 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2007 World Championships in Athletics"). Chepkirwok reached the final round, and in an unusually tight race, where all eight runners finished in the range of 1 minute 47 seconds, Chepkirwok finished fourth with 1:47.41. This was 0.02 seconds behind the bronze medalist, and 0.01 second ahead of the fifth placer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-4) Rounding off the season, Chepkirwok finished seventh at the [2007 World Athletics Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "2007 IAAF World Athletics Final").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1)

In the 2007–08 indoor season Chepkirwok competed at the [2008 World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships_-_Men's_800_metres "2008 IAAF World Indoor Championships - Men's 800 metres"). He reached the semi-final round, finished fourth there but did not progress to the final.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) During the summer he performed better. He opened with a second place in Doha, then won the [ISTAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internationales_Stadionfest "Internationales Stadionfest")[Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_IAAF_Golden_League "2008 IAAF Golden League") meet in Berlin. He then finished second at the Grand Prix meets in Madrid and Athens, and won the Super Grand Prix meet in Crystal Palace, London.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) In Madrid he had achieved a personal best time is 1:43.72 minutes,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) which is also the Ugandan record.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) Entering the [2008 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics"), then, Chepkirwok was the only middle distance runner in the Ugandan squad.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-5) In the [800 metres competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_800_metres "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 800 metres") he did not reach the final, however. He rounded off the season with a second place at the [2008 World Athletics Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "2008 IAAF World Athletics Final").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) In early 2009 it was announced that Chepkirwok was a candidate for the title Ugandan Athlete of the Year.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-6) He eventually finished second runner-up for the award, behind [Moses Kipsiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Kipsiro "Moses Kipsiro") and [Benjamin Kiplagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Kiplagat "Benjamin Kiplagat").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-7)

In February 2009 he set a national indoor record in the 1000 metres, running in 2:18.18 minutes in Stuttgart.

Chepkirwok is represented by PACE Sports Management, and is coached by Ricky Simms.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Abraham Chepkirwok

[![Image 1: Abraham Chepkirwok at ISTAF 2008](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Abraham_Chepkirwok.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Abraham_Chepkirwok.jpg "Abraham Chepkirwok at ISTAF 2008")
Personal information
Born 18 November 1988 (age 37)
Medal record Men's [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_(sport) "Athletics (sport)") Representing ![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Flag_of_Uganda.svg/40px-Flag_of_Uganda.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") [World Junior Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "IAAF World Junior Championships in Athletics") ![Image 3: Bronze medal – third place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Bronze_medal_icon_%28B_initial%29.svg/20px-Bronze_medal_icon_%28B_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2006 Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "2006 World Junior Championships in Athletics")800 m [World Athletics Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "IAAF World Athletics Final") ![Image 4: Silver medal – second place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg/20px-Silver_medal_icon_%28S_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2008 Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "2008 IAAF World Athletics Final")800 m

**Abraham Chepkirwok** (born 18 November 1988) is a [Ugandan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")[middle-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle-distance_runner "Middle-distance runner") who specializes in the [800 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/800_metres "800 metres"). He is the Ugandan record holder in this distance, with 1:43.72 minutes, achieved in July 2008 in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid"). He is a [World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "IAAF World Junior Championships in Athletics") bronze medalist from 2006 and [Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics") competitor from 2008.

He was born in [Kapchorwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapchorwa "Kapchorwa"). By June 2006 he had run the 800 metres in 1:45.0 minutes, at a meet in [Kampala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala "Kampala").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) With this he was the season's world leader for juniors—athletes aged nineteen and less.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-beij-2) With electronic timing his best time was 1:45.44 minutes, achieved in a meet in Heusden.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) He competed at the [2006 World Junior Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "2006 World Junior Championships in Athletics") in Beijing, and won the bronze medal, having led the race halfway through but been outsprinted near the end by two Kenyan runners.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-beij-2)

In the 2006–07 indoor season he ran the 800 metres in 1:46.91 minutes in Stuttgart.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) This was a Ugandan indoor record.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) He opened the outdoor season by winning the IAAF Grand Prix in Dakar. He also won the Grand Prix meet in Hengelo, and finished third at the Super Grand Prix meet in Doha, the [Golden Spike Ostrava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Spike_Ostrava "Golden Spike Ostrava") and the [Bislett Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bislett_Games "Bislett Games").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) Then, in July 2007 he achieved a new personal best time of 1:44.78 minutes at the Grand Prix meet in Athens.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) A fifth place at the [All-Africa Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2007_All-Africa_Games "Athletics at the 2007 All-Africa Games")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) was followed by the entrance in the [2007 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2007 World Championships in Athletics"). Chepkirwok reached the final round, and in an unusually tight race, where all eight runners finished in the range of 1 minute 47 seconds, Chepkirwok finished fourth with 1:47.41. This was 0.02 seconds behind the bronze medalist, and 0.01 second ahead of the fifth placer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-4) Rounding off the season, Chepkirwok finished seventh at the [2007 World Athletics Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "2007 IAAF World Athletics Final").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1)

In the 2007–08 indoor season Chepkirwok competed at the [2008 World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships_-_Men's_800_metres "2008 IAAF World Indoor Championships - Men's 800 metres"). He reached the semi-final round, finished fourth there but did not progress to the final.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) During the summer he performed better. He opened with a second place in Doha, then won the [ISTAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internationales_Stadionfest "Internationales Stadionfest")[Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_IAAF_Golden_League "2008 IAAF Golden League") meet in Berlin. He then finished second at the Grand Prix meets in Madrid and Athens, and won the Super Grand Prix meet in Crystal Palace, London.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) In Madrid he had achieved a personal best time is 1:43.72 minutes,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) which is also the Ugandan record.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3) Entering the [2008 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics"), then, Chepkirwok was the only middle distance runner in the Ugandan squad.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-5) In the [800 metres competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_800_metres "Athletics at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 800 metres") he did not reach the final, however. He rounded off the season with a second place at the [2008 World Athletics Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "2008 IAAF World Athletics Final").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-iaaf-1) In early 2009 it was announced that Chepkirwok was a candidate for the title Ugandan Athlete of the Year.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-6) He eventually finished second runner-up for the award, behind [Moses Kipsiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Kipsiro "Moses Kipsiro") and [Benjamin Kiplagat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Kiplagat "Benjamin Kiplagat").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-7)

In February 2009 he set a national indoor record in the 1000 metres, running in 2:18.18 minutes in Stuttgart.

Chepkirwok is represented by PACE Sports Management, and is coached by Ricky Simms.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Chepkirwok#cite_note-pace-3)

**Jessica Rose Epel Alupo** (born 23 May 1974) commonly known as **Jessica Alupo**, is a [Ugandan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugandan "Ugandan")[politician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politician "Politician") who has been in the ninth parliament and is the current [vice president of Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_Uganda "Vice president of Uganda") since 2021. She is an educator and a former military officer. She previously served in the [cabinet of Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Uganda "Cabinet of Uganda") as minister of education between the year 2011 and 2016. She is also an elected [member of parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Uganda "Parliament of Uganda") as [Katakwi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi_District "Katakwi District")'s women's representative in the 12th Parliament of Uganda.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-ProfR-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jessica_Alupo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Jessica Alupo was born in [Katakwi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi_District "Katakwi District") on 23 May on the year 1974. She attended Apuuton Primary School. She then attended Kangole Girls School for her O-Level studies. For her A-Level education, she studied at [Ngora High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngora_High_School "Ngora High School"). Alupo trained as a high school canteen attendant before she underwent the [officer cadet course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_Cadet "Officer Cadet") at the [Uganda Junior Staff College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Junior_Staff_College "Uganda Junior Staff College") in [Jinja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinja,_Uganda "Jinja, Uganda"). She holds a Bachelor of Arts in political science and linguistics, obtained in 1997 from [Makerere University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makerere_University "Makerere University"). Her first master's degree of Arts in international relations and diplomacy, was also obtained from Makerere University in 2008. She also holds a diploma in public administration and management, obtained in 2008 from the [Uganda Management Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Management_Institute "Uganda Management Institute") (UMI). Her second master's degree is Master's in public administration and management, obtained in 2009, also from Makerere University.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-3)

Over the years, Jessica has been employed in various capacities, including:[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-4)

*   As a headteacher at the Katakwi Primary School in the town of [Katakwi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi "Katakwi"), [Katakwi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi_District "Katakwi District"), [Eastern Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Region,_Uganda "Eastern Region, Uganda") of Uganda
*   As an instructor at the _Uganda Urban Warfare Training School_, Singo, [Nakaseke District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakaseke_District "Nakaseke District"), [Central Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Region,_Uganda "Central Region, Uganda") of [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")
*   As an intelligence officer at the Chieftaincy of Military Intelligence in [Kampala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala "Kampala"), Uganda's capital city.

In 2001, she entered politics as a candidate for the [Katakwi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi_District "Katakwi District") women's representative. She ran on the ticket of the [National Resistance Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Resistance_Movement "National Resistance Movement") (NRM) political party. She won and was re-elected in 2006. In 2009, she was appointed as the state minister for youth and children's affairs.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-5) In 2011, she was re-elected to her parliamentary constituency. In the cabinet reshuffle of 27 May 2011, she was promoted to the post of Minister of Education and Sports.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-6) She replaced [Namirembe Bitamazire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namirembe_Bitamazire "Namirembe Bitamazire"), who was dropped from the cabinet.

Alupo is married to Innocent Tukashaba.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-7) She is reported to enjoy reading, [community mobilization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activism "Activism"), and travel.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-9)

**Jessica Rose Epel Alupo** (born 23 May 1974) commonly known as **Jessica Alupo**, is a [Ugandan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugandan "Ugandan")[politician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politician "Politician") who has been in the ninth parliament and is the current [vice president of Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_Uganda "Vice president of Uganda") since 2021. She is an educator and a former military officer. She previously served in the [cabinet of Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Uganda "Cabinet of Uganda") as minister of education between the year 2011 and 2016. She is also an elected [member of parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Uganda "Parliament of Uganda") as [Katakwi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi_District "Katakwi District")'s women's representative in the 12th Parliament of Uganda.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-ProfR-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jessica_Alupo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Jessica Alupo was born in [Katakwi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi_District "Katakwi District") on 23 May on the year 1974. She attended Apuuton Primary School. She then attended Kangole Girls School for her O-Level studies. For her A-Level education, she studied at [Ngora High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngora_High_School "Ngora High School"). Alupo trained as a high school canteen attendant before she underwent the [officer cadet course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_Cadet "Officer Cadet") at the [Uganda Junior Staff College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Junior_Staff_College "Uganda Junior Staff College") in [Jinja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinja,_Uganda "Jinja, Uganda"). She holds a Bachelor of Arts in political science and linguistics, obtained in 1997 from [Makerere University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makerere_University "Makerere University"). Her first master's degree of Arts in international relations and diplomacy, was also obtained from Makerere University in 2008. She also holds a diploma in public administration and management, obtained in 2008 from the [Uganda Management Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Management_Institute "Uganda Management Institute") (UMI). Her second master's degree is Master's in public administration and management, obtained in 2009, also from Makerere University.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-3)

Over the years, Jessica has been employed in various capacities, including:[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-4)

*   As a headteacher at the Katakwi Primary School in the town of [Katakwi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi "Katakwi"), [Katakwi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi_District "Katakwi District"), [Eastern Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Region,_Uganda "Eastern Region, Uganda") of Uganda
*   As an instructor at the _Uganda Urban Warfare Training School_, Singo, [Nakaseke District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakaseke_District "Nakaseke District"), [Central Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Region,_Uganda "Central Region, Uganda") of [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")
*   As an intelligence officer at the Chieftaincy of Military Intelligence in [Kampala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala "Kampala"), Uganda's capital city.

In 2001, she entered politics as a candidate for the [Katakwi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katakwi_District "Katakwi District") women's representative. She ran on the ticket of the [National Resistance Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Resistance_Movement "National Resistance Movement") (NRM) political party. She won and was re-elected in 2006. In 2009, she was appointed as the state minister for youth and children's affairs.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-5) In 2011, she was re-elected to her parliamentary constituency. In the cabinet reshuffle of 27 May 2011, she was promoted to the post of Minister of Education and Sports.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-6) She replaced [Namirembe Bitamazire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namirembe_Bitamazire "Namirembe Bitamazire"), who was dropped from the cabinet.

Alupo is married to Innocent Tukashaba.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-7) She is reported to enjoy reading, [community mobilization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activism "Activism"), and travel.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Alupo#cite_note-9)

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Ugandan_Defence_Minister_Dr_Crispin_Kiyonga_arrives_in_Mogadishu_%286165594704%29.jpg/250px-Ugandan_Defence_Minister_Dr_Crispin_Kiyonga_arrives_in_Mogadishu_%286165594704%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ugandan_Defence_Minister_Dr_Crispin_Kiyonga_arrives_in_Mogadishu_(6165594704).jpg)

Ugandan Defence Minister Dr Crispus Kiyonga arrives in Mogadishu

**Crispus Walter Kiyonga** (born 19 September 1952) is a Ugandan medical doctor, politician and career diplomat. He is the [Second Deputy Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Prime_Minister_of_Uganda "Deputy Prime Minister of Uganda") of Uganda Since 2026. He is the current [Chancellor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancellor "Chancellor") of the [Makerere University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makerere_University "Makerere University"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-1) the largest public university of [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda"). He served as [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")'s Ambassador to [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-1R-2) He previously served as the [Minister of Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Defence "Minister of Defence") in the [Cabinet of Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Uganda "Cabinet of Uganda") from 2006 to 2016.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-2R-3)

Prior to that, he was [Minister Without Portfolio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_Without_Portfolio "Minister Without Portfolio") in the Office of the President from 2005 to 2006. During the cabinet reshuffles of 16 February 2009,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-3R-4) 27 May 2011,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-5) and 1 March 2015,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-Shuffle-6) he retained his cabinet post. In 2016, he lost the Member of Parliament (MP) seat for Bukonjo County West to Robert Katusabe in [Kasese District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasese_District "Kasese District"), in the [Ugandan Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Uganda "Parliament of Uganda").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-7) However, in the 2026 elections, he reclaimed the Bukonzo West parliamentary seat in the 12th Parliament of Uganda which led to his appointment by President Museveni as the Second Deputy Prime Minister and Deputy Leader of Government Business in Parliament.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-8)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Crispus_Kiyonga&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Kiyonga was born in [Kasese District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasese_District "Kasese District") in the [Western Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Region,_Uganda "Western Region, Uganda") of Uganda on 19 September 1952. Between 1959 and 1966, he attended Bwera Primary School, in [Bwera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mpondwe "Mpondwe"), a few kilometres from the Ugandan border with the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo"). During 1967 through 1970, he attended [Nyakasura School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyakasura_School "Nyakasura School") from S1 to S4. He studied for his S5 and S6 at [Kings College Budo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_College_Budo "Kings College Budo") from 1971 to 1972.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-BioR-9)

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Ugandan_Defence_Minister_Dr_Crispin_Kiyonga_arrives_in_Mogadishu_%286165595076%29.jpg/250px-Ugandan_Defence_Minister_Dr_Crispin_Kiyonga_arrives_in_Mogadishu_%286165595076%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ugandan_Defence_Minister_Dr_Crispin_Kiyonga_arrives_in_Mogadishu_(6165595076).jpg)

Dr. Crispus Kiyonga in Mogadishu

From 1973 through 1978, he attended [Makerere University School of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makerere_University_School_of_Medicine "Makerere University School of Medicine") where he obtained his first medical degree, the [Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Medicine_and_Bachelor_of_Surgery "Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery") (MBChB) in 1978. Later, in 2004, he obtained a [Master of Health Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Health_Science "Master of Health Science") (MHS) with specialisation in Population Dynamics from the [Johns Hopkins School of Public Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_School_of_Public_Health "Johns Hopkins School of Public Health"). His studies at Johns Hopkins were funded through a [Fogarty International Center Scholarship](https://www.fic.nih.gov/).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-Profile-11)

During the first post-[Idi Amin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idi_Amin "Idi Amin") national elections in Uganda in 1980, Kiyonga participated as a candidate on the [Uganda Patriotic Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Patriotic_Movement "Uganda Patriotic Movement") (UPM) platform. He won in his constituency, making him the only UPM candidate who won during those elections. He joined the [National Resistance Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Resistance_Movement "National Resistance Movement") (NRM) during its struggle against the second [Milton Obote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Obote "Milton Obote") regime from 1981 until 1986.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-BioR-9)

From 1986, when the NRM assumed power in Uganda, until 2006 when he was appointed as Minister of Defense, Crispus Kiyonga held several cabinet and non-cabinet posts in the [Ugandan Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Uganda "Government of Uganda"):[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-BioR-9)

*   1986 - 1986: Minister for Cooperatives & Marketing
*   1986 - 1992: [Minister of Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Finance,_Planning_and_Economic_Development_(Uganda) "Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development (Uganda)") - Credited with the establishment of [Uganda Revenue Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Revenue_Authority "Uganda Revenue Authority").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-auto-12)
*   1994 - 1996: Minister of Internal Affairs
*   1996 - 2001: Minister of Health - Credited with efficient handling of [Ebola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebola "Ebola") outbreak in [Gulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulu "Gulu") in 2000. Chairman Global Fund.
*   2001 - 2006: [Minister without Portfolio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_without_Portfolio "Minister without Portfolio") in the [Office of the President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Uganda "President of Uganda") and National Political Commissar.
*   2006 - 2016: Minister of Defense

Between 1992 and 1994, Kiyonga left the government temporarily to serve as a consultant with the [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank") and the [African Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Development_Bank "African Development Bank"). He returned to active politics in 1994 when he was elected to the [Constituent Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_Assembly "Constituent Assembly") that drew up the 1995 [Uganda Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Uganda "Constitution of Uganda").

In August 2003, he led a Ugandan government delegation to the [Ugandan North American Association (UNA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugandan_North_American_Association_(UNA)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ugandan North American Association (UNA) (page does not exist)") convention in Boston, Massachusetts.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-13)

He continuously represented Bukonjo County West, in the [Ugandan Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Uganda "Parliament of Uganda"), from 1980 until 2016.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-Profile-11) In 2016, he was appointed Uganda's Ambassador to China.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-AmbR-14)

During the cabinet reshuffles of 16 February 2009,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-3R-4) 27 May 2011,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-5) and 1 March 2015,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-Shuffle-6) he retained his cabinet post. Between 1959 and 1966, he attended Bwera Primary School, in [Bwera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mpondwe "Mpondwe"), a few kilometres from the Ugandan border with the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo"). During 1967 through 1970, he attended [Nyakasura School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyakasura_School "Nyakasura School") from S1 to S4. He studied for his S5 and S6 at [Kings College Budo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kings_College_Budo "Kings College Budo") from 1971 to 1972.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-BioR-9)

Dr. Crispus Kiyonga in Mogadishu

Later, in 2004, he obtained a [Master of Health Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Health_Science "Master of Health Science") (MHS) with specialisation in Population Dynamics from the [Johns Hopkins School of Public Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_School_of_Public_Health "Johns Hopkins School of Public Health"). His studies at Johns Hopkins were funded through a [Fogarty International Center Scholarship](https://www.fic.nih.gov/).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-Profile-11)

He won in his constituency, making him the only UPM candidate who won during those elections. *   1986 - 1986: Minister for Cooperatives & Marketing
*   1986 - 1992: [Minister of Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Finance,_Planning_and_Economic_Development_(Uganda) "Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development (Uganda)") - Credited with the establishment of [Uganda Revenue Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_Revenue_Authority "Uganda Revenue Authority").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-auto-12)
*   1994 - 1996: Minister of Internal Affairs
*   1996 - 2001: Minister of Health - Credited with efficient handling of [Ebola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebola "Ebola") outbreak in [Gulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulu "Gulu") in 2000. Chairman Global Fund.
*   2001 - 2006: [Minister without Portfolio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_without_Portfolio "Minister without Portfolio") in the [Office of the President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Uganda "President of Uganda") and National Political Commissar.
*   2006 - 2016: Minister of Defense

Between 1992 and 1994, Kiyonga left the government temporarily to serve as a consultant with the [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank") and the [African Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Development_Bank "African Development Bank"). In August 2003, he led a Ugandan government delegation to the [Ugandan North American Association (UNA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugandan_North_American_Association_(UNA)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ugandan North American Association (UNA) (page does not exist)") convention in Boston, Massachusetts.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crispus_Kiyonga#cite_note-13)

**Beatrice Chebet** (born 5 March 2000) is a Kenyan [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running") and world record holder in the [5000 meters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres"), [10,000 meters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres"), and [road 5k](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5K_run "5K run"). She won gold medals in both the 5000 and 10,000 m at the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") and repeated the double at the [2025 World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Athletics_Championships "2025 World Athletics Championships"). In the 5000 m, Chebet won the silver medal at the [2022 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships "2022 World Athletics Championships"), and the bronze in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Championships "2023 World Athletics Championships"). Chebet is a three-time [World Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "World Athletics Cross Country Championships") champion, having won the junior race in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2019 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") and the senior race in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "2023 World Athletics Cross Country Championships") and [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "2024 World Athletics Cross Country Championships").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-6) Additionally, Chebet was the 5000 m champion at the [2018 World U20 Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IAAF_World_U20_Championships "2018 IAAF World U20 Championships"), the [2022 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Commonwealth_Games "2022 Commonwealth Games"), and the [2022 African Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2022 African Championships in Athletics").

Chebet trains in [Londiani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Londiani "Londiani"), Kericho County.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-U20X-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-8)

## Early life and junior career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and junior career")]

Chebet was born on 5 March 2000, the daughter of Francis and Lilian Kirui.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-WAprofile-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-DN-10) While at primary school, she raced in 5000 m events,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-DN-10) and went on to attend Saramek Secondary School, [Londiani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Londiani "Londiani"), graduating from there in 2013.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-DN-10) She joined the Lemotit Athletics Club in November 2016.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-DN-10)

In June 2018, at the age of 18, Chebet won the Kenyan Under-20s 5000 metres. A month later at [Tampere 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IAAF_World_U20_Championships "2018 IAAF World U20 Championships"), she became the first Kenyan woman and the first non-Ethiopian since 2006 to win the 5000 m title at the [World U20 Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "IAAF World Junior Championships in Athletics").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-11)

At the [2019 World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2019 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), the top three athletes in the women's U20 race – Chebet and the Ethiopian duo of [Alemitu Tariku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alemitu_Tariku "Alemitu Tariku") and [Tsigie Gebreselama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsigie_Gebreselama "Tsigie Gebreselama") – were all awarded the time of 20:50 as they finished together. Tariku was initially announced as the winner, with Gebreselama awarded silver. However, after the photo finish footage was reviewed Chebet received the gold medal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-12) During the same year, Chebet won the Kenyan U20 National Cross Country Championships.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-U20X-7)

## Senior career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Senior career")]

### 2022–2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2022–2023")]

At the [2022 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships "2022 World Athletics Championships") in [Eugene, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugene,_Oregon "Eugene, Oregon"), Chebet claimed a silver medal in the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2022 World Athletics Championships – Women's 5000 metres"), with a time of [14:46.75](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2022 World Athletics Championships – Women's 5000 metres") behind [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay") in 14:46.29 and ahead of [Dawit Seyaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawit_Seyaum "Dawit Seyaum") (14:47.36).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-13)

On 31 December 2023, at the Cursa dels Nassos in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), Chebet set a new women's only [5 kilometre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5K_run "5K run") world record of 14:13, which was faster than both the previous women's only world record of 14:29, and the mixed world record of 14:19 set in 2021.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-14)

### 2024

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2024")]

At the [Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Prefontaine_Classic "2024 Prefontaine Classic") on 25 May, Chebet broke [Letesenbet Gidey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letesenbet_Gidey "Letesenbet Gidey")'s [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") world record of 29:01.03, running a time of 28:54.14 to become the first woman to break the 29 minute barrier.[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-15) The race was originally billed as a world record attempt by [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay"). Chebet attached herself to Gudaf throughout the twenty five lap race, but as Gudaf faded from world record pace nearing the end, Chebet surged with three laps to go to catch up with the world record [wavelights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelight "Wavelight") and went on to break the record.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-:0-16)

At the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 5000 metres"), Chebet won an Olympic gold medal in the [women's 5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 5000 metres") on 5 August, finishing with a time of 14:28.56, beating defending champion [Sifan Hassan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sifan_Hassan "Sifan Hassan"), reigning world champion [Faith Kipyegon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Kipyegon "Faith Kipyegon"), and world record holder [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay") in a highly anticipated race. Chebet stayed in the pack for much of the race, but as Kipyegon made a surge to the front, Chebet followed, out-kicking Kipyegon in the final hundred metres to become the Olympic Champion.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-18) Chebet also won Olympic gold in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's 10,000 metres") on 9 August, finishing in a time of 30:43.25.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-19)

At the [Weltklasse Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weltklasse_Z%C3%BCrich "Weltklasse Zürich") meeting on 5 September, Chebet attempted to break the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres") world record of 14:00.21 set by [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay") in 2023, perhaps to become the first woman under the 14 minute barrier. However, with pacing only to 2000 metres and the weather conditions proving to be too poor for a record attempt, Chebet was unable to break the world record or her personal best of 14:05.92, but still managed to dip below 14:10 to win the race in a world leading time and a new meeting record of 14:09.52.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-20)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-21) On 14 September, Chebet won the 5000 metres at the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Diamond_League "2024 Diamond League")[final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Memorial_Van_Damme "2024 Memorial Van Damme") in Brussels, Belgium, in a time of 14:09.82.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-22) On 31 December, at the Cursa dels Nassos, Chebet broke [Agnes Jebet's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agnes_Jebet_Ngetich "Agnes Jebet Ngetich") mixed 5 kilometre world record of 14:13, running 13:54. In setting this record, Chebet became the first woman to break the 14 minute barrier on any surface.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-:1-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-24)

### 2025

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Beatrice_Chebet&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2025")]

On 25 May, at the [Meeting International Mohammed VI d'Athletisme de Rabat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Meeting_International_Mohammed_VI_d'Athl%C3%A9tisme_de_Rabat "2025 Meeting International Mohammed VI d'Athlétisme de Rabat"), Chebet ran the second fastest 3000 metres of all time, finishing in 8:11.56. This time falls 5.45 seconds short of [Wang Junxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Junxia "Wang Junxia")'s officially recognized world record of 8:06.11 set in 1993.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-25) Given the [controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Junxia#After_retirement_&_controversy "Wang Junxia") surrounding Junxia's world record, some organizations outside of [World Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics "World Athletics") such as [Track and Field News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_&_Field_News "Track & Field News") do not recognize it, which would make Chebet's performance the fastest in history.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-26) On 6 June, at the [Golden Gala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Golden_Gala "2025 Golden Gala"), Chebet ran the second fastest 5000 metres of all time, finishing in 14:03.69.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-27) On 5 July, at the [Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Prefontaine_Classic "2025 Prefontaine Classic"), with a 61-second final lap, Chebet broke [Gudaf Tsegay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gudaf_Tsegay "Gudaf Tsegay")'s 5000 metre world record of 14:00.21, running 13:58.06 to become the first woman to break the 14 minute barrier on the track.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beatrice_Chebet#cite_note-28)

**Almaz Ayana Eba** ([Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language "Oromo language"): _Almaaz Ayyanaa Eebbaa_; [Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic_language "Amharic language"): አልማዝ አያና ኤባ, born 21 November 1991[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4)) is an Ethiopian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running"). She won the gold medal in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") and bronze in the [5,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres") at the [2016 Rio Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics"). Almaz is a four-time [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") medallist earning a bronze for the 5,000m in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2013 World Championships in Athletics"), gold at the event in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") as well as gold in the 10,000m and silver in the 5,000m in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2017 World Championships in Athletics").

She broke the 10,000 metres world record, set in 1993, while winning the gold medal at the Rio Olympics and held it until 2021. At the 2017 World Championships in London, Almaz won the title in the 10,000m, finishing 46 seconds ahead of the runner-up. She finished third in both the 5,000m and 10,000m on the respective world all-time lists. In 2016, she was voted [IAAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics "World Athletics")[Female World Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athlete_of_the_Year "World Athlete of the Year").

Almaz set the fastest ever women's marathon debut at the 2022 [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon").

## Early life and background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and background")]

Almaz Ayana was born in [Wenbera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenbera "Wenbera"), [Benishangul-Gumuz Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benishangul-Gumuz_Region "Benishangul-Gumuz Region"), Ethiopia.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5) Born the seventh youngest of nine siblings, she started running at local school around age 13–14.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-6) Like other notable athletes such as [Fatuma Roba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatuma_Roba "Fatuma Roba") and [Derartu Tulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derartu_Tulu "Derartu Tulu"), Almaz is also Oromo descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-7) In addition to her native [Oromo language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language "Oromo language"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-8) she also speaks [Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic "Amharic").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-9) The name Almaz means 'diamond' in Amharic.

Almaz is married to her childhood friend and longtime partner, Soressa Fida.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5) She is a devout Christian.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 2013–2014: World 5000 m bronze in Moscow

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2013–2014: World 5000 m bronze in Moscow")]

At age 21, Almaz won a bronze medal in the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2013 World Championships in Athletics – Women's 5000 metres") at the [2013 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2013 World Championships in Athletics") held in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), Russia.

At the [2014 African Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2014 African Championships in Athletics") in [Marrakesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marrakesh "Marrakesh"), she defeated favourite [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") to take the title in a championship record time of 15:32.72.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-10) One month later at the [Continental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_IAAF_Continental_Cup "2014 IAAF Continental Cup") also held in Marrakesh, she won the 5000 m by over 24 seconds.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-11)

### 2015: World 5000 m champion in Beijing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2015: World 5000 m champion in Beijing")]

[![Image 46](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg/250px-Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg)

At the [2015 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"), Almaz won her first world title with a 5000 m victory.

In May 2015, Almaz ran a personal best of 14:14.32 over 5000 m at the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_IAAF_Diamond_League "2015 IAAF Diamond League") meeting in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Golden_Grand_Prix "Shanghai Golden Grand Prix"), China, improving significantly upon her previous personal best of 14:25.84 set in 2013 in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-12)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4) This made her the [third fastest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres#Women "5000 metres") female athlete over that distance, behind compatriots [Tirunesh Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunesh_Dibaba "Tirunesh Dibaba"), the world record holder, and [Meseret Defar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meseret_Defar "Meseret Defar"). At the [Beijing World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") in August, she put on a stunning display of front-running to win the [5000 m final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2015 World Championships in Athletics – Women's 5000 metres") with a time of 14:26.83, setting a new championship record in the process and beating silver medalist [Senbere Teferi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senbere_Teferi "Senbere Teferi") by more than 17 seconds with [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") in third.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-13) Her win was named the Performance of the Championships by World Athletics.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-14) In her final race of the season, Almaz set a new 3000 m meeting record of 8:22.34 to beat Tirunesh Dibaba at the [Zurich Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weltklasse "Weltklasse").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-15)

### 2016: Rio Olympic 10,000 m champion with a world record, bronze at 5000 m

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016: Rio Olympic 10,000 m champion with a world record, bronze at 5000 m")]

Almaz opened her season by winning over 3000 m at the [Doha Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha_Diamond_League "Doha Diamond League") on the 6 May, running a time of 8:23.11 which narrowly missed her personal best.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-16) On 2 June 2016, Almaz set a new personal best in the 5000 m in a time of 14:12.59 at the [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Gala "Golden Gala")[Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_IAAF_Diamond_League "2016 IAAF Diamond League"). This made her the second fastest woman ever at this distance, behind only Tirunesh Dibaba's world record of 14:11.15, and established a new circuit record. Later that month, she ran the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") competitively for the first time at the Ethiopian Olympic trials in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), Netherlands.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-17) She posted the fastest ever debut time of 30:07.00, defeating Tirunesh Dibaba and moving up to eighth on the world all-time list.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-18)

[![Image 47](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Provas_de_Atletismo_nas_Olimp%C3%ADadas_Rio_2016_%2829109535365%29.jpg/250px-Provas_de_Atletismo_nas_Olimp%C3%ADadas_Rio_2016_%2829109535365%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Provas_de_Atletismo_nas_Olimp%C3%ADadas_Rio_2016_(29109535365).jpg)

Almaz (in second) on her way to 10,000 m gold at the [2016 Rio Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics").

At the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics") held in August in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Almaz set a world record of 29:17.45 in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 10,000 metres"), topping Chinese athlete [Wang Junxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Junxia "Wang Junxia")'s 23-year-old world record by 14 seconds.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Guardian_report-20) No one previously had run within 22 seconds of Wang's record.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-21) The 10,000 metres was already an extremely fast race when Ayana broke away with 12 laps to go. Second-placed [Vivian Cheruiyot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot "Vivian Cheruiyot") of Kenya finished just a second shy of Wang's record and double Olympic 10,000 metres champion Tirunesh Dibaba earned the bronze medal with a 12 seconds improvement on her personal best and the fourth fastest time in history. Multiple national records were set, and eighteen competitors set personal bests.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-22) The lax [drug testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_testing "Drug testing") regime in Ethiopia[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-23) and the doping scandals that embroiled athletics before the Rio Olympics caused some to question whether Almaz had been doping.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-538_discussion-24) British commentators [Brendan Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Foster "Brendan Foster") and [Paula Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe "Paula Radcliffe"), both former world record holders in distance events, were skeptical about Almaz's performance.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Guardian_report-20) Fellow competitors reported that before the race, the Ethiopian was coughing and did not seem well.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-AW_report-25) In her post-race press conference, Almaz said her time was purely the outcome of hard training.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-26) On 9 September, in her first race since the Olympics, Almaz attempted to break Tirunesh Dibaba's 2008 5000 m world record of 14:11.15 at the [Brussels Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_van_Damme "Memorial van Damme").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-27) Despite a strong start, she fell short of breaking the record but did set a meeting record of 14:18.99.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-28)

### 2017: 10,000 m gold and 5000 m silver at the London World Championships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2017: 10,000 m gold and 5000 m silver at the London World Championships")]

[![Image 48](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/Almaz_Ayana_London_2017.jpg/250px-Almaz_Ayana_London_2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Almaz_Ayana_London_2017.jpg)

Almaz celebrates her 10,000 m win at the [2017 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2017 World Championships in Athletics") in London.

On 5 August 2017, Almaz secured a dominant victory as she won over 10,000 metres at the [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2017 World Championships in Athletics") in London with a world-leading 30:16.32,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-30) She ran her final 5,000 m in 14:24.94, a time that would've placed her seventh on the [all-time 5,000 m lists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres#Women_(outdoor) "5000 metres") at the time.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Letsrun-31) Her win set the record for the biggest margin of victory over 10,000 m at a World Championship and was described as "one of the finest displays in women’s distance running history" by [Letsrun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letsrun.com "Letsrun.com").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Letsrun-31) She went on to add a silver for the 5,000 metres eight days later, having run a time of 14:40.35 to finish behind Kenya's [Hellen Obiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellen_Obiri "Hellen Obiri") (14:34.86).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-32) Almaz made her debut over the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") at the [New Delhi Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi_Half_Marathon "New Delhi Half Marathon") winning in a time of 1:07:12.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-33)

### 2018–present: Injuries, motherhood and comeback

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2018–present: Injuries, motherhood and comeback")]

The Ethiopian distance running star took almost three years off due to injury problems and pregnancy. Her only race during this time was at the [2019 Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Prefontaine_Classic "2019 Prefontaine Classic") where she placed 18th over 3,000 m in a time of 8:57.16.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-34) Almaz started regularly competing again from April 2022.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4)

Almaz made her return to the track at the 2022 [FBK Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Blankers-Koen_Games "Fanny Blankers-Koen Games") in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), placing seventh over the 10,000 m in 30:48.48. She also placed sixth over 5,000 m at the [Oslo Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Bislett_Games "2022 Bislett Games") in 14:32.17.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-35)

On 16 October 2022, the 30-year-old made the fastest ever women's [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") debut of 2:17:20 at the [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon") to win the race and defeat her old-time rival Genzebe Dibaba by 45 seconds. Almaz beat the course record by almost 40 seconds, setting a Dutch all-comers' record (best performance on country's soil) and putting her seventh on the [world all-time list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon#All-time_individual_top_25 "Marathon") at the time.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-37)

In 2023, Almaz opened her season by winning the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") in a course record of 1:05:30.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-38) On 17 September, Almaz competed over the [10 mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10-mile_run "10-mile run") distance for the first time by placing third at the [Dam tot Damloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam_tot_Damloop "Dam tot Damloop") in [Zaandam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaandam "Zaandam") in 52:23.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-39) She set a new personal best for the marathon of 2:16:20 in finishing second behind [Worknesh Degefa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worknesh_Degefa "Worknesh Degefa") at the [Valencia Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Valencia_Marathon "2023 Valencia Marathon").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-40)

**Berihu Aregawi Teklehaimanot** ([Tigrinya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tigrinya_language "Tigrinya language"): በሪሁ ኣረጋዊ; born 28 February 2001)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-WAprofile-1) is an Ethiopian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running") and the current world record holder in the [5000 m road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5K_run "5K run"). At the [Paris 2024 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_2024_Olympics "Paris 2024 Olympics"), Berihu won a silver medal in the [10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres"), and he placed fourth in the 10,000 m at the [2020 Tokyo Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics"). Berihu won a silver medal at the [2023 World Athletics Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships_%E2%80%93_Senior_men's_race "2023 World Athletics Cross Country Championships – Senior men's race"). He also won a silver medal in the [3,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Athletics_Indoor_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_3000_metres "2025 World Athletics Indoor Championships – Men's 3000 metres") at the [2025 World Athletics Indoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Athletics_Indoor_Championships "2025 World Athletics Indoor Championships") Championships.

At age 17, Berihu won a bronze medal in the 10,000 m at the [2018 World Under-20 Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IAAF_World_U20_Championships "2018 IAAF World U20 Championships").

Berihu Aregawi was the bronze medalist in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") at the [2018 World U20 Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IAAF_World_U20_Championships "2018 IAAF World U20 Championships") in [Tampere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampere "Tampere") behind [Rhonex Kipruto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhonex_Kipruto "Rhonex Kipruto") and [Jacob Kiplimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Kiplimo "Jacob Kiplimo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-2) He won the [3000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres") race at the [African Youth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2018_African_Youth_Games "Athletics at the 2018 African Youth Games") that year. He then went to Argentina for the [Summer Youth Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2018_Summer_Youth_Olympics "Athletics at the 2018 Summer Youth Olympics") held in [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires") and placed second in the [combined 3000 m event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2018_Summer_Youth_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Boys'_3000_metres "Athletics at the 2018 Summer Youth Olympics – Boys' 3000 metres").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-WAprofile-1)

In November 2019, Berihu won the [Great Ethiopian Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Ethiopian_Run "Great Ethiopian Run") ([10 kilometres road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10K_run "10K run")).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-WAprofile-1)

On 8 June 2021, he finished third in the Ethiopian trial behind [Selemon Barega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selemon_Barega "Selemon Barega") and [Yomif Kejelcha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yomif_Kejelcha "Yomif Kejelcha") in the 10,000 m to effectively seal his place at the delayed [2020 Tokyo Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Tokyo_Olympics "2020 Tokyo Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-3) Berihu finished fourth on his Olympic debut in the [10,000 metres race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's 10,000 metres") behind Barega who won gold.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-4)

On 31 December 2021, Berihu set a world record in the [5 km run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5K_run "5K run") at the Cursa dels Nassos 5K in Barcelona in a time of 12 minutes 49 seconds, improving previous mark of [Joshua Cheptegei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Cheptegei "Joshua Cheptegei") by 2 seconds. He had 38 second margin of victory.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-5)

At the [2022 World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Indoor_Championships "2022 World Athletics Indoor Championships") in [Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade"), he was eliminated in the heats of the [3000 m event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Indoor_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_3000_metres "2022 World Athletics Indoor Championships – Men's 3000 metres").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-WAprofile-1) Berihu finished seventh in the [10,000 m race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_10,000_metres "2022 World Athletics Championships – Men's 10,000 metres") at the [outdoor World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Athletics_Championships "2022 World Athletics Championships") held in [Eugene, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugene,_Oregon "Eugene, Oregon") that year.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-WAprofile-1)

In February 2023, he won the silver medal on a 10 km course at the [World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "2023 World Athletics Cross Country Championships") in [Bathurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathurst,_New_South_Wales "Bathurst, New South Wales"), Australia with a time of 29:26. The winner was Jacob Kiplimo in 29:17.

On 11 March, Berihu narrowly missed by nine seconds Rhonex Kipruto's 10 km world record in [Laredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laredo,_Spain "Laredo, Spain"), Spain, clocking an Ethiopian record and the second-fastest time in history of 26:33.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-7)

He ran the fifth-fastest track 5000m time in history when running 12:40.45 to win the Diamond League event in [Lausanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne "Lausanne") in June 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-8)

In the 10,000m race at the [2023 World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Athletics_Championships "2023 World Athletics Championships") in [Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest "Budapest"), he placed fourth.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-9)

In 2024, he won the [Cross Internacional Juan Muguerza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_Internacional_Juan_Muguerza "Cross Internacional Juan Muguerza"), a World Athletics Cross Country Tour Gold meeting.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-10) He won silver at the [2024 World Athletics Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "2024 World Athletics Cross Country Championships") in Serbia.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-11) He met the 2024 Paris Olympics standard for the 5000 metres finishing second at the LA Grand Prix in May 2024.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-12)

At the [2024 Paris Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"), Berihu secured a silver medal in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's 10,000 metres"), running 26:43.44 behind [Joshua Cheptegei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Cheptegei "Joshua Cheptegei")'s new [Olympic record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics "List of Olympic records in athletics") of 26:43.14.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-14)

At the 2024 Silesia Diamond League, Berihu competed in the 3000 metres, running 7:21.28 behind [Jakob Ingebrigtsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakob_Ingebrigtsen "Jakob Ingebrigtsen")'s new world record of 7:17.55. This time places Berihu as the third fastest 3000 metre runner in history, behind [Daniel Komen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Komen "Daniel Komen"), who held the previous world record of 7:20.67, and Ingebrigtsen.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-15)

In January 2025, he retained his title at the Cross Internacional Juan Muguerza in [Elgoibar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgoibar "Elgoibar").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-16) Berihu was selected for the 3000 metres at the [2025 World Athletics Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Athletics_Indoor_Championships "2025 World Athletics Indoor Championships") in [Nanjing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanjing "Nanjing") in March 2025, where he secured a silver medal with a time of 7:46.25 behind Jakob Ingebrigtsen, who ran 7:46.09.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-18)

Be ran a meeting record of 12:50.45 to win the 5000 metres at the [2025 Shanghai Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Shanghai_Diamond_League "2025 Shanghai Diamond League") ahead of compatriot [Kuma Girma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuma_Girma "Kuma Girma").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-19) He finished second in the 10,000 metres at the [2025 Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Prefontaine_Classic "2025 Prefontaine Classic") on 5 July, in a race that doubled up as the Ethiopian trials for the 2025 World Championships.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-20) In September 2025, he competed over 10,000 metres at the [2025 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Athletics_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_10,000_metres "2025 World Athletics Championships – Men's 10,000 metres") in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Japan, finishing in twelfth place.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-21)

In January 2026, he was selected for the Ethiopian team to compete at the [2026 World Athletics Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_World_Athletics_Cross_Country_Championships "2026 World Athletics Cross Country Championships") in [Tallahassee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallahassee "Tallahassee"), winning the silver medal in the individual race and gold with Ethiopia in the team competition.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berihu_Aregawi#cite_note-23)
