In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)") in New York. Running against the world's strongest competition, she won. As a consequence she was [idolised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolatry "Idolatry") by many young people in Africa: at last, a woman champion to complement the many successful male runners. She won the New York City Marathon again in 1995 and finished 3rd in 1998.
Between 1997 and 1999, she won three world titles a row over the half marathon distance. She won [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon") three times between 1997 and 1999. She won [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") in 1999 and finished second in 2001. She finished second at the 1999 [Osaka International Ladies Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_International_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka International Ladies Marathon").

Loroupe won the [Zevenheuvelenloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zevenheuvelenloop "Zevenheuvelenloop") 15K race in the Netherland three times (1992, 1993 and 1998). She is a seven-time [Egmond Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egmond_Half_Marathon "Egmond Half Marathon") winner (1993–1998, 2000). She has won the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") a record six times: 1994–1997, 1999 and 2000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-4) She has won the [Tilburg road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tilburg_Ten_Miles "Tilburg Ten Miles"), a five times (1993, 1994, 1996, 1998, 1999), also a record number. She won the [Paris Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Half_Marathon "Paris Half Marathon") in 1994 and 1998,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-5)[City-Pier-City Loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-Pier-City_Loop "City-Pier-City Loop") half marathon in [the Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague") in 1998,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-6) and the [Parelloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parelloop "Parelloop") 10K in race in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 1999.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-7)

During the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, favoured to win both the marathon and the 10,000 meters, she suffered from violent food poisoning the night before the race. Nevertheless, she fought through the marathon race, finishing 13th, then, the next day, ran the 10,000 metres, finishing 5th,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-sr-1) running barefoot in both races, a feat she later stated she achieved out of a sense of duty to all the people taking her as a bearer of hope in her home country. Until the end of 2001, she continued to suffer from various health problems.
In 2000, she won [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") and [Rome City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_City_Marathon "Rome City Marathon"). She also won [Lausanne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne_Marathon "Lausanne Marathon") in 2002, [Cologne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Marathon "Cologne Marathon") in 2003 and [Leipzig Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leipzig_Marathon "Leipzig Marathon") in 2004.
Loroupe competed at the [2005 World Championships marathon race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics_-_Women's_Marathon "2005 World Championships in Athletics - Women's Marathon") in Helsinki, [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"), but finished only 40th. In February 2006 she won the Hong Kong Half-Marathon. The same year she finished 5th in the Rotterdam Marathon and 2nd in the [Venice Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Marathon "Venice Marathon"). In 2007, she participated again the New York City Marathon, finishing 8th.

Loroupe's biggest successes include world records over 20, 25 and 30 kilometers as well as the past record over the marathon distance. She used to hold the [One Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour_run "Hour run") running [World record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_records_in_athletics "World records in athletics") of 18,340 m set in [Borgholzhausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borgholzhausen "Borgholzhausen"), Germany, but the record was broken by Dire Tune of Ethiopia ten years later, in 2008 (new record 18,517 m).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-8)
In 2006, she was named a United Nations Ambassador of Sport by Secretary General [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan"), together with [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer"), tennis champion from Switzerland, [Elias Figueroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Figueroa "Elias Figueroa"), Latin American soccer legend from Chile, and [Katrina Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Webb "Katrina Webb") paralympics gold medalist from Australia. She is an International Sports Ambassador for the IAAF, the [International Association of Athletics Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Athletics_Federations "International Association of Athletics Federations"), and for [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF").
In 2003, Loroupe created an annual series of Peace Marathons sponsored by the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation "Peace Through Sports". Presidents, Prime Ministers, Ambassadors and government officials run with warriors and nomadic groups in her native Kenya, in Uganda and in Sudan, to bring peace to an area plagued by raiding warriors from battling tribes. In 2010 the Kenyan Government lauded her achievements as hundreds of warriors had laid down their weapons.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-9)

She has established a school ([Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe_Peace_Academy "Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy")) and orphanage for children from the region in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), a high-mountain town in north-west [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").
The 2006 Peace Marathon was held on 18 November 2006, in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), Kenya. Two thousand warriors from six tribes competed. The next Peace Marathon was 15 November 2008 in Kapenguria, Kenya. National ambassadors to Kenya participated, together with the Prime Minister, and several Kenyan, Tanzanian, and Ugandan Ministers. The Peace Marathon has been held each year since then, with the exception of the past two Covid years. Winners of the races often begin professional training in long-distance running, or join the training team of ex-warriors.
In February 2007, she was named the [Oxfam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfam "Oxfam") Ambassador of Sport and Peace to Darfur. In December 2006, she travelled with [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney"), [Joey Cheek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Cheek "Joey Cheek"), and [Don Cheadle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle "Don Cheadle") to Beijing, Cairo, and New York on a diplomatic mission to bring an end to violence in Darfur. She won the "Community Hero" category at the 2007 [Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year") awards.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-10)

In November 2009, Tegla represented the [Shoe4Africa team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoe4Africa_team?action=edit&redlink=1 "Shoe4Africa team (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-11) running the New York Marathon alongside founder Toby Tanser and actress [Sarah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Jones_(stage_actress) "Sarah Jones (stage actress)")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-12) finishing in 3:54:02.
Loroupe is a member of the 'Champions for Peace' club, a group of 54 famous elite athletes committed to serving peace in the world through sport, created by [Peace and Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_and_Sport "Peace and Sport"), a [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco")-based international organisation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-13)
As reported by Olympic news outlet [Around the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Around_the_Rings "Around the Rings"), the IOC recognised six women, five from each continent and one to represent the world, for their achievements and their work to promote women's sport. Loroupe was awarded the world trophy.
In 2015 Loroupe became an Ambassador for the [Homeless World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeless_World_Cup "Homeless World Cup").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-14)

In 2016, she was the Chef de Mission organizing the [Refugee Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics") for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) At those games Loroupe was inducted into the [Olympians for life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Olympians_Association#Olympians_for_Life "World Olympians Association") project for her work in promoting peace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-15) In October 2016 Loroupe was awarded United Nations Person of the Year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-16)

In 1994 and 1998, Loroupe won the [Goodwill Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodwill_Games "Goodwill Games") over 10,000 metres, [barefoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barefoot_running "Barefoot running"). Over the same distance she won [bronze medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") at the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1995 World Championships in Athletics") and [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1999 World Championships in Athletics").
In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)") in New York. Running against the world's strongest competition, she won. As a consequence she was [idolised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolatry "Idolatry") by many young people in Africa: at last, a woman champion to complement the many successful male runners. She won the New York City Marathon again in 1995 and finished 3rd in 1998.
Between 1997 and 1999, she won three world titles a row over the half marathon distance. She won [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon") three times between 1997 and 1999. She won [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") in 1999 and finished second in 2001. She finished second at the 1999 [Osaka International Ladies Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_International_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka International Ladies Marathon").

Loroupe won the [Zevenheuvelenloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zevenheuvelenloop "Zevenheuvelenloop") 15K race in the Netherland three times (1992, 1993 and 1998). She is a seven-time [Egmond Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egmond_Half_Marathon "Egmond Half Marathon") winner (1993–1998, 2000). She has won the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") a record six times: 1994–1997, 1999 and 2000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-4) She has won the [Tilburg road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tilburg_Ten_Miles "Tilburg Ten Miles"), a five times (1993, 1994, 1996, 1998, 1999), also a record number. She won the [Paris Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Half_Marathon "Paris Half Marathon") in 1994 and 1998,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-5)[City-Pier-City Loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-Pier-City_Loop "City-Pier-City Loop") half marathon in [the Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague") in 1998,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-6) and the [Parelloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parelloop "Parelloop") 10K in race in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 1999.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-7)

During the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, favoured to win both the marathon and the 10,000 meters, she suffered from violent food poisoning the night before the race. Nevertheless, she fought through the marathon race, finishing 13th, then, the next day, ran the 10,000 metres, finishing 5th,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-sr-1) running barefoot in both races, a feat she later stated she achieved out of a sense of duty to all the people taking her as a bearer of hope in her home country. Until the end of 2001, she continued to suffer from various health problems.
In 2000, she won [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") and [Rome City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_City_Marathon "Rome City Marathon"). She also won [Lausanne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne_Marathon "Lausanne Marathon") in 2002, [Cologne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Marathon "Cologne Marathon") in 2003 and [Leipzig Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leipzig_Marathon "Leipzig Marathon") in 2004.
Loroupe competed at the [2005 World Championships marathon race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics_-_Women's_Marathon "2005 World Championships in Athletics - Women's Marathon") in Helsinki, [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"), but finished only 40th. In February 2006 she won the Hong Kong Half-Marathon. The same year she finished 5th in the Rotterdam Marathon and 2nd in the [Venice Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Marathon "Venice Marathon"). In 2007, she participated again the New York City Marathon, finishing 8th.

Loroupe's biggest successes include world records over 20, 25 and 30 kilometers as well as the past record over the marathon distance. She used to hold the [One Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour_run "Hour run") running [World record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_records_in_athletics "World records in athletics") of 18,340 m set in [Borgholzhausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borgholzhausen "Borgholzhausen"), Germany, but the record was broken by Dire Tune of Ethiopia ten years later, in 2008 (new record 18,517 m).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-8)
In 2006, she was named a United Nations Ambassador of Sport by Secretary General [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan"), together with [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer"), tennis champion from Switzerland, [Elias Figueroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Figueroa "Elias Figueroa"), Latin American soccer legend from Chile, and [Katrina Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Webb "Katrina Webb") paralympics gold medalist from Australia. She is an International Sports Ambassador for the IAAF, the [International Association of Athletics Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Athletics_Federations "International Association of Athletics Federations"), and for [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF").
In 2003, Loroupe created an annual series of Peace Marathons sponsored by the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation "Peace Through Sports". Presidents, Prime Ministers, Ambassadors and government officials run with warriors and nomadic groups in her native Kenya, in Uganda and in Sudan, to bring peace to an area plagued by raiding warriors from battling tribes. In 2010 the Kenyan Government lauded her achievements as hundreds of warriors had laid down their weapons.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-9)

She has established a school ([Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe_Peace_Academy "Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy")) and orphanage for children from the region in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), a high-mountain town in north-west [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").
The 2006 Peace Marathon was held on 18 November 2006, in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), Kenya. Two thousand warriors from six tribes competed. The next Peace Marathon was 15 November 2008 in Kapenguria, Kenya. National ambassadors to Kenya participated, together with the Prime Minister, and several Kenyan, Tanzanian, and Ugandan Ministers. The Peace Marathon has been held each year since then, with the exception of the past two Covid years. Winners of the races often begin professional training in long-distance running, or join the training team of ex-warriors.
In February 2007, she was named the [Oxfam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfam "Oxfam") Ambassador of Sport and Peace to Darfur. In December 2006, she travelled with [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney"), [Joey Cheek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Cheek "Joey Cheek"), and [Don Cheadle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle "Don Cheadle") to Beijing, Cairo, and New York on a diplomatic mission to bring an end to violence in Darfur. She won the "Community Hero" category at the 2007 [Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year") awards.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-10)

In November 2009, Tegla represented the [Shoe4Africa team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoe4Africa_team?action=edit&redlink=1 "Shoe4Africa team (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-11) running the New York Marathon alongside founder Toby Tanser and actress [Sarah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Jones_(stage_actress) "Sarah Jones (stage actress)")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-12) finishing in 3:54:02.
Loroupe is a member of the 'Champions for Peace' club, a group of 54 famous elite athletes committed to serving peace in the world through sport, created by [Peace and Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_and_Sport "Peace and Sport"), a [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco")-based international organisation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-13)
As reported by Olympic news outlet [Around the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Around_the_Rings "Around the Rings"), the IOC recognised six women, five from each continent and one to represent the world, for their achievements and their work to promote women's sport. Loroupe was awarded the world trophy.
In 2015 Loroupe became an Ambassador for the [Homeless World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeless_World_Cup "Homeless World Cup").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-14)

In 2016, she was the Chef de Mission organizing the [Refugee Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics") for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) At those games Loroupe was inducted into the [Olympians for life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Olympians_Association#Olympians_for_Life "World Olympians Association") project for her work in promoting peace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-15) In October 2016 Loroupe was awarded United Nations Person of the Year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-16)

# Almaz Ayana
**Almaz Ayana Eba** ([Oromo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language "Oromo language"): _Almaaz Ayyanaa Eebbaa_; [Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic_language "Amharic language"): አልማዝ አያና ኤባ, born 21 November 1991[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4)) is an Ethiopian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running"). She won the gold medal in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") and bronze in the [5,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres") at the [2016 Rio Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics"). Almaz is a four-time [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") medallist earning a bronze for the 5,000m in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2013 World Championships in Athletics"), gold at the event in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") as well as gold in the 10,000m and silver in the 5,000m in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2017 World Championships in Athletics").

# Almaz Ayana
She broke the 10,000 metres world record, set in 1993, while winning the gold medal at the Rio Olympics and held it until 2021. At the 2017 World Championships in London, Almaz won the title in the 10,000m, finishing 46 seconds ahead of the runner-up. She finished third in both the 5,000m and 10,000m on the respective world all-time lists. In 2016, she was voted [IAAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics "World Athletics")[Female World Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athlete_of_the_Year "World Athlete of the Year").
Almaz set the fastest ever women's marathon debut at the 2022 [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon").

# Almaz Ayana
## Early life and background
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and background")]
Almaz Ayana was born in [Wenbera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenbera "Wenbera"), [Benishangul-Gumuz Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benishangul-Gumuz_Region "Benishangul-Gumuz Region"), Ethiopia.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5) Born the seventh youngest of nine siblings, she started running at local school around age 13–14.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-6) Like other notable athletes such as [Fatuma Roba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatuma_Roba "Fatuma Roba") and [Derartu Tulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derartu_Tulu "Derartu Tulu"), Almaz is also Oromo descent.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-7) In addition to her native [Oromo language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language "Oromo language"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-8) she also speaks [Amharic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic "Amharic").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-9) The name Almaz means 'diamond' in Amharic.
Almaz is married to her childhood friend and longtime partner, Soressa Fida.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5) She is a devout Christian.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-aips_media-5)

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2013–2014: World 5000 m bronze in Moscow
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2013–2014: World 5000 m bronze in Moscow")]
At age 21, Almaz won a bronze medal in the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2013 World Championships in Athletics – Women's 5000 metres") at the [2013 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2013 World Championships in Athletics") held in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), Russia.
At the [2014 African Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2014 African Championships in Athletics") in [Marrakesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marrakesh "Marrakesh"), she defeated favourite [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") to take the title in a championship record time of 15:32.72.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-10) One month later at the [Continental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_IAAF_Continental_Cup "2014 IAAF Continental Cup") also held in Marrakesh, she won the 5000 m by over 24 seconds.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-11)

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2015: World 5000 m champion in Beijing
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2015: World 5000 m champion in Beijing")]
[![Image 46](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg/250px-Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Almaz_Ayana_at_Beijing_2015.jpg)
At the [2015 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") in [Beijing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing "Beijing"), Almaz won her first world title with a 5000 m victory.

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2015: World 5000 m champion in Beijing
In May 2015, Almaz ran a personal best of 14:14.32 over 5000 m at the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_IAAF_Diamond_League "2015 IAAF Diamond League") meeting in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Golden_Grand_Prix "Shanghai Golden Grand Prix"), China, improving significantly upon her previous personal best of 14:25.84 set in 2013 in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-12)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4) This made her the [third fastest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres#Women "5000 metres") female athlete over that distance, behind compatriots [Tirunesh Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunesh_Dibaba "Tirunesh Dibaba"), the world record holder, and [Meseret Defar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meseret_Defar "Meseret Defar").

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2015: World 5000 m champion in Beijing
At the [Beijing World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") in August, she put on a stunning display of front-running to win the [5000 m final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "2015 World Championships in Athletics – Women's 5000 metres") with a time of 14:26.83, setting a new championship record in the process and beating silver medalist [Senbere Teferi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senbere_Teferi "Senbere Teferi") by more than 17 seconds with [Genzebe Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genzebe_Dibaba "Genzebe Dibaba") in third.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-13) Her win was named the Performance of the Championships by World Athletics.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-14) In her final race of the season, Almaz set a new 3000 m meeting record of 8:22.34 to beat Tirunesh Dibaba at the [Zurich Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weltklasse "Weltklasse").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-15)

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2016: Rio Olympic 10,000 m champion with a world record, bronze at 5000 m
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016: Rio Olympic 10,000 m champion with a world record, bronze at 5000 m")]
Almaz opened her season by winning over 3000 m at the [Doha Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doha_Diamond_League "Doha Diamond League") on the 6 May, running a time of 8:23.11 which narrowly missed her personal best.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-16) On 2 June 2016, Almaz set a new personal best in the 5000 m in a time of 14:12.59 at the [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Gala "Golden Gala")[Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_IAAF_Diamond_League "2016 IAAF Diamond League"). This made her the second fastest woman ever at this distance, behind only Tirunesh Dibaba's world record of 14:11.15, and established a new circuit record. Later that month, she ran the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") competitively for the first time at the Ethiopian Olympic trials in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), Netherlands.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-17) She posted the fastest ever debut time of 30:07.00, defeating Tirunesh Dibaba and moving up to eighth on the world all-time list.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-18)

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2016: Rio Olympic 10,000 m champion with a world record, bronze at 5000 m
At the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics") held in August in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Almaz set a world record of 29:17.45 in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 10,000 metres"), topping Chinese athlete [Wang Junxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Junxia "Wang Junxia")'s 23-year-old world record by 14 seconds.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Guardian_report-20) No one previously had run within 22 seconds of Wang's record.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-21) The 10,000 metres was already an extremely fast race when Ayana broke away with 12 laps to go. Second-placed [Vivian Cheruiyot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot "Vivian Cheruiyot") of Kenya finished just a second shy of Wang's record and double Olympic 10,000 metres champion Tirunesh Dibaba earned the bronze medal with a 12 seconds improvement on her personal best and the fourth fastest time in history.

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2017: 10,000 m gold and 5000 m silver at the London World Championships
On 5 August 2017, Almaz secured a dominant victory as she won over 10,000 metres at the [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2017 World Championships in Athletics") in London with a world-leading 30:16.32,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-30) She ran her final 5,000 m in 14:24.94, a time that would've placed her seventh on the [all-time 5,000 m lists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres#Women_(outdoor) "5000 metres") at the time.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Letsrun-31) Her win set the record for the biggest margin of victory over 10,000 m at a World Championship and was described as "one of the finest displays in women’s distance running history" by [Letsrun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letsrun.com "Letsrun.com").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-Letsrun-31) She went on to add a silver for the 5,000 metres eight days later,

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2018–present: Injuries, motherhood and comeback
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Almaz_Ayana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2018–present: Injuries, motherhood and comeback")]
The Ethiopian distance running star took almost three years off due to injury problems and pregnancy. Her only race during this time was at the [2019 Prefontaine Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Prefontaine_Classic "2019 Prefontaine Classic") where she placed 18th over 3,000 m in a time of 8:57.16.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-34) Almaz started regularly competing again from April 2022.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-WAprofile-4)
Almaz made her return to the track at the 2022 [FBK Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Blankers-Koen_Games "Fanny Blankers-Koen Games") in [Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hengelo "Hengelo"), placing seventh over the 10,000 m in 30:48.48. She also placed sixth over 5,000 m at the [Oslo Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Bislett_Games "2022 Bislett Games") in 14:32.17.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-35)

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2018–present: Injuries, motherhood and comeback
On 16 October 2022, the 30-year-old made the fastest ever women's [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") debut of 2:17:20 at the [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon") to win the race and defeat her old-time rival Genzebe Dibaba by 45 seconds. Almaz beat the course record by almost 40 seconds, setting a Dutch all-comers' record (best performance on country's soil) and putting her seventh on the [world all-time list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon#All-time_individual_top_25 "Marathon") at the time.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-37)

# Almaz Ayana
## Career
### 2018–present: Injuries, motherhood and comeback
In 2023, Almaz opened her season by winning the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") in a course record of 1:05:30.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-38) On 17 September, Almaz competed over the [10 mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10-mile_run "10-mile run") distance for the first time by placing third at the [Dam tot Damloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam_tot_Damloop "Dam tot Damloop") in [Zaandam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaandam "Zaandam") in 52:23.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-39) She set a new personal best for the marathon of 2:16:20 in finishing second behind [Worknesh Degefa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worknesh_Degefa "Worknesh Degefa") at the [Valencia Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Valencia_Marathon "2023 Valencia Marathon").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaz_Ayana#cite_note-40)

**Paula Jane Radcliffe** (born 17 December 1973) is a British former [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She is a three-time winner of the [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") (2002, 2003, 2005), three-time [New York Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Marathon "New York Marathon") champion (2004, 2007, 2008), the 2002 [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon") winner, and the [2005 World Champion in the marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics_%E2%80%93_Women's_marathon "2005 World Championships in Athletics – Women's marathon"). She was previously the fastest female [marathoner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathoner "Marathoner") of all time, and held the [women's marathon world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_world_record_progression "Marathon world record progression") with a time of 2:15:25 for 16 years from 2003 to 2019, when it was broken by [Brigid Kosgei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigid_Kosgei "Brigid Kosgei").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-2)

Radcliffe is a former world champion in the marathon, [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") and [cross country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_country_running "Cross country running"). She has also been European champion over [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") and in cross country. On the [track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_running "Track running"), Radcliffe won the 10,000 metres silver medal at the [1999 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1999 World Championships in Athletics")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-3) and was the [2002 Commonwealth champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2002_Commonwealth_Games "Athletics at the 2002 Commonwealth Games") at [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres"). She represented [Great Britain at the Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain_at_the_Olympics "Great Britain at the Olympics") in four consecutive games (1996 to 2008), although she never won an Olympic medal.

Her running has earned her a number of accolades including the [BBC Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "BBC Sports Personality of the Year"), [Laureus World Comeback of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureus_Awards "Laureus Awards"), [IAAF World Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Athlete_of_the_Year "IAAF World Athlete of the Year"), [AIMS World Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AIMS_World_Athlete_of_the_Year "AIMS World Athlete of the Year") (three times) and a [Member of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Member of the Order of the British Empire") (MBE). She has also been nominated for World Sportswoman of the year on several occasions. In 2010, she was inducted into the [England Athletics Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_Athletics_Hall_of_Fame "England Athletics Hall of Fame"). She was inducted into the [Loughborough University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loughborough_University "Loughborough University") Hall of Fame in 2015.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-5)
Radcliffe ended her competitive running career at the [2015 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_London_Marathon "2015 London Marathon"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-6) although she later entered the 2025 editions of the Tokyo and Boston marathons.

Radcliffe was born on 17 December 1973 in [Davenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davenham "Davenham") near [Northwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwich "Northwich"), [Cheshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheshire "Cheshire"). Her family then moved to nearby [Barnton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnton,_Cheshire "Barnton, Cheshire") where she attended Little Leigh Primary School.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-7) Despite suffering from [asthma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asthma "Asthma") and [anaemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaemia "Anaemia"), she took up running at the age of seven, influenced by her father who was a keen amateur [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") runner and joined [Frodsham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frodsham "Frodsham") Athletic Club. Her family later moved to [Kingsley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsley,_Cheshire "Kingsley, Cheshire").
When Radcliffe was aged 12, the family moved to [Oakley, Bedfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakley,_Bedfordshire "Oakley, Bedfordshire") and she became a member of Bedford & County Athletics Club. Her joining the club coincided with a talented and dedicated coach, Alex Stanton, building the women's and girls' sections into one of the strongest in the country, in spite of [Bedford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedford "Bedford")'s relatively small size.
Radcliffe's father became club vice-chairman and her mother, a fun-runner, managed the women's cross-country team.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-historic_Rad-8) Her first race at a national level came as a 12-year-old in 1986 when she placed 299th out of around 600 in the girls' race of the English Schools Cross Country Championships. She finished fourth in the same race one year later.

Radcliffe attended [Sharnbrook Upper School and Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharnbrook_Academy "Sharnbrook Academy"). She went on to study French, German and [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics "Economics") at [Loughborough University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loughborough_University "Loughborough University"), gaining a degree in Modern European Studies.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-9)

Radcliffe's father was a keen marathon runner as a young man. He took up the hobby again in an attempt to lose weight after giving up smoking.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-historic_Rad-8) He famously appears in the photo of [John Lennon playing on stage with The Quarrymen on 6th July 1957, the day John first met Paul McCartney, https://www.thetimes.com/culture/books/article/get-back-boys-who-became-beatles-hunter-davies-review-nx5qmq9gn](https://www.thetimes.com/culture/books/article/get-back-boys-who-became-beatles-hunter-davies-review-nx5qmq9gn)Despite suffering from [asthma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asthma "Asthma") Radcliffe took up running at the age of seven.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-ASKman-10) In 1992 Radcliffe discovered that she suffers from [anaemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaemia "Anaemia").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-historic_Rad-8)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-anaemia-11) Radcliffe was diagnosed with exercise induced asthma at the age of 14 after blacking out whilst training.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-12) During her father's training jogs in the woods, Radcliffe and her brother would often run with him for a mile or two.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-inspire-13) Radcliffe attended Frodsham Athletic Club until the age of nine,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-historic_Rad-8) Radcliffe became a member of [Bedford & County Athletics Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedford_&_County_Athletics_Club?action=edit&redlink=1 "Bedford & County Athletics Club (page does not exist)"), when they moved to Oakley.

There she was coached by Alex Stanton, who still fulfilled that role in her professional career.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-BBC_2002-14) Stanton started to coach Radcliffe at the age of 12 after his wife Rosemary spotted her talent.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-15) At the age of 10 Radcliffe, accompanied by her father, watched [Ingrid Kristiansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingrid_Kristiansen "Ingrid Kristiansen") run in the London Marathon, inspiring her to become an athlete.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-inspire-13) Her first race at a national level came as a 12-year-old in 1986, when she placed 299th in the English Schools Cross Country Championships.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-BBC_2002-14) In 1991 Radcliffe won the English Schools [1500 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1500_metres "1500 metres") title.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Spikes-16)
> "I'm not looking to make a living out of it. Obviously it's nice that there's a bit of money coming in but that's not my goal. I just want to do my best and still enjoy it. I want to keep on enjoying it, keep on improving, get as much out of it as I can and put as much back as I can."
—Radcliffe a week after finishing second in her first senior race.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-historic_Rad-8)

At the [1992 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1992 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), Radcliffe, took the Junior title, beating [Wang Junxia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Junxia "Wang Junxia") and [Gete Wami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gete_Wami "Gete Wami") in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), after recovering from a bad asthma attack in the weeks beforehand.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-historic_Rad-8)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Rad_Bio-18) Radcliffe then went to the [Junior track World championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_World_Junior_Championships_in_Athletics "1992 World Junior Championships in Athletics") and finished fourth in the [3,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-19) In her first senior race, in [Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Cross_Country "Great North Cross Country") at the start of 1993,

Radcliffe finished second to [Olympic Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Champion "Olympic Champion")[Derartu Tulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derartu_Tulu "Derartu Tulu").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-20) At the age of 19 Radcliffe finished in seventh place at the [1993 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1993 World Championships in Athletics").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Rad_Bio-18) Radcliffe claimed back to back [World Cross Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Cross_Challenge "IAAF World Cross Challenge") wins at Durham and Mallusk to start the 1994 season.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-anaemia-11)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-21) Radcliffe missed the [World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1994 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") with a foot injury.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-22) Radcliffe was initially misdiagnosed with the injury which forced her to miss all of 1994 and thought about quitting as the injury would not get better.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Rad_Bio-18) At the [Fanny Blankers-Koen Games in Hengelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanny_Blankers-Koen_Games "Fanny Blankers-Koen Games") in 1995 Radcliffe outkicked Tulu to run the third fastest time by a British woman for the 5,000 metres.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-23)

At the [World championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1995 World Championships in Athletics"),
Radcliffe qualified comfortably for the final of the 5,000 metres,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-24) where she finished fifth.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Spikes-16)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Rad_Bio-18) At the [1996 Securicor Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Grand_Prix "London Grand Prix") Radcliffe ran the 5,000 metres finishing second.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-25) The [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Olympic_Games "1996 Olympic Games") saw Radcliffe finish fifth in the 5,000 metres.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Spikes-16) Radcliffe rounded off 1996 by finishing third in a cross country race in [Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Cross_Country "Great North Cross Country").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-26)

1997 saw Radcliffe split Wami and Tulu, and win the silver medal at the [1997 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1997 IAAF World Cross Country Championships").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-27) Radcliffe became the first woman to defend the [Fifth Avenue Mile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Avenue_Mile "Fifth Avenue Mile") title.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-28) In the 1997 World Championships, Radcliffe finished in 4th place over the 5,000 metres.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Rad_Bio-18) Wami again outsprinted Radcliffe in her final race of 1997, in the Brussels cross country event.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-29) Radcliffe had dropped out of Durham's cross country race with flu at the start of 1998,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-30) but bounced back to finish third in Dublin.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-31) At the [1998 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1998 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") of the World Cross Country, Radcliffe again won the silver medal.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-32) Radcliffe set a new world best for 5 miles (8.0 km) on the road around Balmoral Castle.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-33) At the [European Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_European_Athletics_Championships "1998 European Athletics Championships") Radcliffe, captaining the team,

won the 5,000 metres and finished second in the 1500 metres.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-34) Radcliffe set the pace in the 10,000 metres at the European Championships, but finished fifth.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Rad_Bio-18)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-35) Radcliffe, who was suffering from a virus, took some time off,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Rad_Bio-18) before returning to the cross country discipline, where she won her first senior title by taking the [European Long course race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_European_Cross_Country_Championships "1998 European Cross Country Championships").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-36) 1998 finished with a fourth-place finish in Brussels.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-38)

Radcliffe started 1999 by finishing fourth in Durham.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-39) At the World Cross Country championships, Radcliffe finished with the bronze medal.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-40) Radcliffe then ran the seventh fastest 10,000 metres ever at the European 10,000 metres challenge.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-41) At the [London Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Grand_Prix "London Grand Prix"), Radcliffe took two seconds off her own [British record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_records_in_athletics "British records in athletics") in the 5,000 metres.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-43) Radcliffe took the silver at the World Championships behind finishing behind Wami in the 10,000 metres.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-45) Radcliffe and Loruope found themselves at the front and tried to get rid of Wami but failed as the Ethiopian took the title.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-46) At the Berlin Golden league meeting, Radcliffe finished eighth in the 5,000 metres.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-48) Radcliffe then ran the second fastest [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") by a British woman, finishing third on her debut at the distance at the [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run"),

despite getting into a tangle with a spectator.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-49)
Starting 2000, Radcliffe won the Stormont Cross Country race for a third time.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-50) Radcliffe then finished fourth in Durham.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-53) Radcliffe then sustained a knee injury.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-54) For the European Cup, Radcliffe joined a host of other British athletes by pulled out injured.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-55) However, Radcliffe soon returned to the track for the first time since March after a virus, a knee operation and a calf muscle tear had kept her out;

to race over 1,500 metres in Barcelona.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-56) In her first race since the World Cross Country, Radcliffe finished 11th.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-57) At the London Grand Prix, Radcliffe finished second, one second outside of her British record, in only her second track race of the season.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-58) At the [Weltklasse Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weltklasse_Z%C3%BCrich "Weltklasse Zürich")[IAAF Golden League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_Golden_League "IAAF Golden League") meeting Radcliffe competed in the 3,000 metres and finished in fourth place.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-59) At the UK trials won the 5,000 metres title.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-60) The [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Grand_Prix_(athletics) "British Grand Prix (athletics)") saw Radcliffe race over 3000 metres, where once again she finished third.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-61) At the [2000 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, Radcliffe finished sixth in her 10,000 metres heat to qualify for the final.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-62) In the final Radcliffe set a new British record,

but crossed the line in fourth and was highly disappointed to miss out on a medal.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-63) Radcliffe returned to action by winning the BUPA Ireland five-mile race.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-64) At the [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run"), Radcliffe ran a new European record for the half marathon, as she won the race in a time of 67 minutes and 7 seconds.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-65) Radcliffe was then selected for the [2000 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2000 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") in Mexico.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-66) Radcliffe won her first World title, despite suffering a panic attack when her nose tape, designed to help her breathe, fell off halfway round.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-67) The good run of form came to an end, when she turned her attention to the Cross Country events and finished third in Brussels.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-68) Radcliffe confirmed that her last race of the year would be the [Great North Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Cross_Country "Great North Cross Country").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-69) There Radcliffe defeated Tulu by seventy-five seconds,[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-70) in eight inches of snow.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-71)

She won back-to-back titles in the 2000 and 2001 [IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"), winning a third title in 2003.

#### Cross country champion
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Cross country champion")]
On 24 March, Radcliffe won the [Ostend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostend "Ostend"), Belgium-held [World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Cross_Country_Championships "World Cross Country Championships") 2001 title in a time of 27:49.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-72)
Held in March in [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin"), Radcliffe defended her title in the Women's Long Race when she won the [2002 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2002 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") title for a second year. She won in 26:46.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-73)

### Marathon world record
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Marathon world record")]
In 2002, Radcliffe made the move up to the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)"), a decision that immediately paid off with victory at her debut in that year's [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") on 14 April 2002 in a world's best time for a women's only race (2:18:55).[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-74) Her time was the second quickest in women's marathon history behind the world record of 2:18:47 set by [Catherine Ndereba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Ndereba "Catherine Ndereba"), of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), in Chicago.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-75)
Later that year, Radcliffe set a world record time of 2:17:18 in the [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon") on 13 October 2002,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-76) breaking the previous record by a minute and a half.

### Marathon world record
She was appointed a [Member of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Member of the Order of the British Empire") (MBE) in the [2002 Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Birthday_Honours "2002 Birthday Honours") for services to athletics.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-77) She said: "It means a great deal to me, it's a great honour and it really tops off an amazing year. To come here and receive this and to meet the Queen at the end of it just finishes it off perfectly."[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-78)
Later the same year, she became the [BBC Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "BBC Sports Personality of the Year"), making her the first woman in over a decade to be honoured with the accolade. Paula thanked her husband Gary Lough, her coach Alex Stanton and her physio, Gerard Hartmann.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-79)

### Further world records
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Further world records")]
Radcliffe set her last women's marathon world record during the 2003 [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") in April, with a time of 2:15:25. The performance is one of the highest of score's values in terms of the IAAF World ranking points.
Radcliffe is the former world record holder for the women's road 10k in a time of 30 minutes and 21 seconds, which she set on 23 February 2003 in the [World's Best 10K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_Best_10K "World's Best 10K") in [San Juan, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juan,_Puerto_Rico "San Juan, Puerto Rico").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-80)
Radcliffe won the 2004 [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon") in a time of 2:23:10, beating [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya")'s [Susan Chepkemei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Chepkemei "Susan Chepkemei").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-81)

### 2004 Athens Olympics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2004 Athens Olympics")]
Radcliffe did not compete in the London Marathon in 2004, but was the favourite to win a gold medal in the marathon at the [Olympic Games in Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Olympic_Games "2004 Olympic Games"). However, she suffered an injury to her leg just two weeks prior to the event and had to use a high dose of anti-inflammatory drugs. This had an adverse effect on her [stomach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach "Stomach"), hindering food absorption. She ended up withdrawing from the race after 36 km (22 mi). Five days later she started in the 10,000 metres but, still suffering from the effects of the marathon, retired with eight laps remaining.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-82) Radcliffe said "You go through bad stages in a marathon, but never as bad as that", "I've never before not been able to finish and I'm desperately trying to find a reason for what happened", "I just feel numb – this is something I worked so hard for."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-83)
Additionally, Radcliffe, like many other athletes, complained about the very high temperatures that prevailed in Athens at the time of the Olympic games.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-85)

### 2004 Athens Olympics
Regarded as Great Britain's best gold medal hope in athletics, her withdrawal made headlines in the UK, with editorial stances ranging from support to negativity, with some newspapers deriding Radcliffe for 'quitting', rather than going on to finish the race.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-86) Television pictures showed Radcliffe in a clearly distressed state after dropping out of the marathon, being comforted by two friends from her early running days.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-87)

### 2005: Marathon World Champion
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2005: Marathon World Champion")]
[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Paula_Radcliffe_London_marathon_2005_crop.jpg/250px-Paula_Radcliffe_London_marathon_2005_crop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paula_Radcliffe_London_marathon_2005_crop.jpg)
Paula Radcliffe leading the [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") in 2005, near to [Limehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limehouse "Limehouse") in east London.

### 2005: Marathon World Champion
At the 2005 London Marathon, Radcliffe won with a time of 2:17:42, a world's best time for a women's only race by over a minute. The race is remembered for a notorious moment towards the end when Radcliffe, hindered by [runner's diarrhoea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runner's_diarrhoea "Runner's diarrhoea") and in need for a toilet break, stopped and [defecated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defecated "Defecated") on the side of the road in view of the crowd and TV cameras which broadcast the incident live.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-88) After the race, she apologised to viewers and explained what happened, "I was losing time because I was having stomach cramps and I thought 'I just need to go and I'll be fine'. ... I didn't really want to resort to that in front of hundreds of thousands of people.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-89) Basically I needed to go. I started feeling it between 15 and 16 miles (26 km) and probably carried on too long before stopping. I must have eaten too much beforehand". In November 2006, the incident was voted _top running moment in history_ in the UK from a choice of ten "unforgettable moments".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-90)

### 2005: Marathon World Champion
On 14 August 2005 at the [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2005 World Championships in Athletics") held in [Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki "Helsinki") she won Britain's only gold medal when she took the marathon title, dominating the race and setting a championship record time of 2:20:57. [Catherine Ndereba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Ndereba "Catherine Ndereba") of Kenya finished in second place, more than a minute behind. Radcliffe said: "It pretty much went according to plan. If somebody had been with me at the end I think I could have pushed it up a bit more." She and three other British runners were also awarded third place in the team competition.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-91)

### Family and autobiography
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Family and autobiography")]
[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Paula_%26_Isla_Radcliffe_2007_NYC.jpg/250px-Paula_%26_Isla_Radcliffe_2007_NYC.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paula_&_Isla_Radcliffe_2007_NYC.jpg)
Paula Radcliffe with daughter Isla at the New York City Marathon, 2007
Radcliffe took a break through the 2006 season owing to injuries and in July announced that she was expecting her first child. Her comeback was further delayed in 2007 as a result of a stress fracture in her lower back.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-92)
Radcliffe chose not to defend her world marathon crown in 2007, in order to undertake further rehabilitation, but insisted she wanted to compete in the next two Olympics. She made her return to competitive running on 30 September 2007, taking part in the BUPA [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run") in the UK on [Tyneside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyneside "Tyneside"). This was her first race in almost two years. Radcliffe finished second behind US runner [Kara Goucher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kara_Goucher "Kara Goucher").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-93)
Radcliffe made her marathon return at the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon") on 4 November 2007 which she won with an official time of 2:23:09.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-94)

### Family and autobiography
Radcliffe released an autobiography in 2004, _Paula: My Story So Far_.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-95)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems")]
[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Paula_Radcliffe.jpg/250px-Paula_Radcliffe.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paula_Radcliffe.jpg)
Paula Radcliffe at mile 14, New York City Marathon 2007
Radcliffe withdrew from the 2008 [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") due to a foot injury.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-96) Shortly after the London Marathon, it was also revealed that Radcliffe was suffering from an injury to her hip, preventing her from running. Originally thought to be a muscular problem, scans later revealed it was a [stress fracture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_fracture "Bone fracture") to her [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur "Femur"). Radcliffe won the 2008 Great South Run in 51 minutes 11 seconds, 11 seconds off of [Sonia O'Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonia_O'Sullivan "Sonia O'Sullivan")'s course record. In May, Radcliffe broke her left leg.
Radcliffe managed to get to fitness level for the 2008 Summer Olympics, but cramped during the marathon to the point where she had to stop running and stretch. She resumed the race and finished in 23rd place overall.

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Radcliffe won the 2008 [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"), making it her third victory at the competition with a time of 2:23:56. Russian [Lyudmila Petrova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyudmila_Petrova "Lyudmila Petrova") came in second, and American [Kara Goucher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kara_Goucher "Kara Goucher") took third.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-97)
Following the New York Marathon, Radcliffe suffered more injury setbacks: she had to withdraw from the [2009 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_London_Marathon "2009 London Marathon") due to a fractured toe. In March that year, she had a [bunion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunion "Bunion") removed which doctors believed was the root cause of her other injuries at that time.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-98) She did not run competitively for almost 10 months, but made herself available for inclusion in the [2009 British team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain_at_the_2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "Great Britain at the 2009 World Championships in Athletics") for the [World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics"). She announced that the [New York City Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Half_Marathon "New York City Half Marathon") would be a testing ground for her fitness before the competition.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-99)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Radcliffe went on to win the New York City Half Marathon in 1:09:45, two seconds off the course record. However, after this she pulled out of the World Championships as she felt unfit, and she missed the [2009 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2009 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") in [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham") due to a bout of [tonsillitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonsillitis "Tonsillitis").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-100) She returned to action at the 2009 New York City Marathon but failed to notch her third consecutive victory, instead fading to fourth place with knee problems.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-101)
[![Image 42](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Paula_Radcliffe_London_Marathon_2015.jpg/250px-Paula_Radcliffe_London_Marathon_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paula_Radcliffe_London_Marathon_2015.jpg)
Radcliffe in the [2015 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_London_Marathon "2015 London Marathon")

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Following a 19-month layoff that included the birth of her second child, Radcliffe returned to action at the Bupa London 10 km (6 mi), where she finished third, 55 seconds behind the winner, [Jo Pavey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Pavey "Jo Pavey"). Radcliffe called the performance "a bit of a disaster", and indicated she was suffering from a tear in one of the discs of her back.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-103)
Radcliffe set the [2011 Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Berlin_Marathon "2011 Berlin Marathon") as her comeback venue to try for an Olympic qualifying time. She came third in the race with a time of 2:23:46 — getting the Olympic standard and the fourth fastest time by a European that year.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-104) She was dissatisfied, however, saying: "I'm not particularly happy, either with my time or my place. I came here wanting to win".[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-105) She used the 2012 [Vienna Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_City_Marathon "Vienna City Marathon") to gauge her fitness and the race was set up as a battle between her and [Haile Gebrselassie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie "Haile Gebrselassie"), with Radcliffe receiving a head start of 7:52 (the difference between the two athletes' personal bests). She did not perform well and was comfortably beaten by the Ethiopian, while she crossed the line with a time of 72:03.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-106)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Radcliffe pulled out of the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") in London because of a foot injury.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-107) In January 2015, Radcliffe announced that she had decided to end her marathon career on 26 April 2015 by competing in the [2015 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_London_Marathon "2015 London Marathon").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-108) She finished in 2:36:55.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-109)
Radcliffe has served as a BBC pundit. During the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"), she apologized for wishing volleyball player and convicted rapist [Steven van de Velde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_van_de_Velde "Steven van de Velde") good luck on the [Tonight with Andrew Marr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Marr "Andrew Marr") show.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-110)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
In 2025, Radcliffe ran her first competitive marathon in a decade, finishing the [2025 Tokyo Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Tokyo_Marathon "2025 Tokyo Marathon") in 2:57:22.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-carney-111) She also registered to run in the [2025 Boston Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Boston_Marathon "2025 Boston Marathon"). She finished with a time of 2:53:44, winning her category.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-carney-111)
Radcliffe was appointed [Officer of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Officer of the Order of the British Empire") (OBE) in the [2026 New Year Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_New_Year_Honours "2026 New Year Honours") for services to sport.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-112)
