Auf Anregung von Horst Milde (Berlin-Marathon) wurde das Sportmuseum Berlin vom 14. Kongreß der AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau am 4.–8. Dezember 1994 zum AIMS Marathon-Museum of Running berufen. Damit hatte die Geschichte des Laufens in Berlin einen adäquaten internationalen Sammlungsort gefunden, den die AIMS seitdem organisatorisch und ab 2008 auch finanziell unterstützt.
Das Sportmuseum Berlin ist das älteste und größte Sportmuseum in Deutschland (seit 1925), mit fünf professsionellen Sport-Historikern, die von der Stadt Berlin finanziert werden. Die Ausstellungsräume und das umfangreiche Archiv befinden sich im Olympiapark Berlin.

Am 21. Januar 2015 wurden die Wortmarke Marathoneum und ein Läuferlogo als Bildmarke auf das Forum für Sportgeschichte beim Deutschen Patent- und Markenamt eingetragen.

Unter der Dachmarke Marathoneum werden zukünftig alle Aktivitäten des Sportmuseum Berlin und seines Förderervereins Forum für Sportgeschichte hinsichtlich der nationalen und internationalen Geschichte des Laufens gebündelt. Das Marathoneum ist somit zugleich Sammlung, Archiv, Herausgeber, Imprint, Veranstalter und Multiplikator für alle Erscheinungsformen des Laufsports! Zusätzlich verleiht das Marathoneum alle zwei Jahre den ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ für verdiente und langjährige Wegbereiter des Laufsports.

Das Marathoneum besitzt ca. 2.500 Plakate, ca. 1.500 T-Shirts, ca. 2.200 Finisher-Medaillen sowie 1.600 Akkreditierungskarten von Läufen aus der ganzen Welt. In der Bibliothek befinden sich mehr als 95 deutsche und englischsprachige Laufzeitschriften. Der Gesamtbestand der Sammlungen wird auf ca. 250 Regalmetern in zwei großen Depoträumen im Sportmuseum Berlin nach museologischen Regeln deponiert und verzeichnet. Ein wichtiger Schatz des Museums ist die umfangreiche und großartige englischsprachige Sammlung von Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), sowie die Archive von Henryk Paskal (Polen), Wim Verhoorn (Niederland) und Werner Sonntag (Deutschland).

Im Olympiapark Berlin sind in der Ausstellung „Keep on Running“ auf 300m³ ausgewählte Objekte aus der Sammlung, darunter Startnummern, Schuhe und Sportkleidung von Olympiasiegern und Weltrekordlern ausgestellt.

* * *

**English:**At the suggestion of Horst Milde (Berlin Marathon), the Berlin Sports Museum was appointed the AIMS Marathon Museum of Running at the 14th Congress of the AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau on 4-8 December 1994. So the history of running in Berlin had found an adequate international collection location, which the AIMS has been supporting organizationally and financially since 2008.

The Berlin Sports Museum is the oldest and largest sports museum in Germany (since 1925), with five professional sports historians financed by the city of Berlin. The exhibition rooms and the extensive archive are located in the Berlin Olympic Park.

On 21 January 2015, the word mark Marathoneum and a runner logo were registered as a figurative mark in the Forum for Sports History at the German Patent and Trade Mark Office.

The Marathoneum trademark will in future bundle all the activities of the Berlin Sports Museum and its supporting association “Forum für Sportgeschichte” with regard to the national and international history of running. The Marathoneum is therefore a collection, archive, publisher, imprint as well as organizer and multiplier for all forms of running! In addition, the Marathoneum awards the ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ every two years for deserving and long-standing pioneers of running.

The Marathoneum owns approx. 2,500 posters, approx. 1,500 T-shirts, approx. 2,200 finisher medals as well as 1,600 accreditation cards for races from all over the world. In the library there are more than 95 German and English language running time fonts. The total inventory of the collections is deposited and listed on approx. 250 metres of shelves in two large depot rooms in the Berlin Sports Museum according to museological rules. An important treasure of the museum is the extensive and magnificent English collection of Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), as well as the archives of Henryk Paskal (Poland), Wim Verhoorn (Netherland) and Werner Sonntag (Gemany).

In the exhibition „Keep on Running“ at the Berlin Olympic Park, selected objects from the collection, including starting numbers, shoes and sportswear of Olympic champions and world record holders, are exhibited on 300m³.

## YouTube의 사명

평범한 사람들이 자신의 목소리를 낼 수 있게 돕고 더 큰 세상과 만나게 하는 것

YouTube는 모든 사람이 마땅히 자신의 목소리를 낼 수 있어야 하고 서로의 이야기에 귀를 기울이며 의견을 나누고 커뮤니티를 형성할 때 세상이 더 나아진다고 믿습니다.

이 사이트에서 YouTube가 이 모든 일을 어떻게 실현하는지 자세히 알아보세요.

### 빠른 링크

### 새로운 소식

2026~2027학년도의 시작을 맞아, 전설적인 다큐멘터리 영화 제작자 켄 번즈는 공식 Ken Burns YouTube 채널에서 PBS LearningMedia와의 협업을 통해 강의 콘텐츠를 제공할 예정이라고 오늘 발표했습니다.

커뮤니티에서 생성형 AI 콘텐츠에 대한 투명성을 중요하게 생각한다는 의견이 꾸준히 있었습니다. 이를 반영하여 YouTube는 2024년부터 크리에이터가 AI 도구를 사용했다고 공개한 콘텐츠에 라벨을 표시하고 있습니다.

매일 수십억 명의 사람들이 YouTube를 통해 주변 세상을 배우고 이해합니다. 수업 과제에 대한 도움을 받거나, 외국어를 공부하거나, 다른 직업에 대해 알아보는 등 사람들은 YouTube에서 무엇이든 찾아보고 새로운 것을 배울 수 있습니다. 지난 6월 미국에서 학습 및 방법 안내 콘텐츠의 조회수는 55억 회를 넘었습니다.

YouTube는 속보부터 시민 담론을 이끄는 토론에 이르기까지 자신의 삶에 영향을 미치는 사건들을 이해하기 위해 전 세계 사람들이 찾는 곳입니다. AI 생성 콘텐츠가 진화함에 따라 이러한 대화의 중심에 있는 개인은 자신의 신원을 보호하기 위한 신뢰할 수 있는 도구가 필요합니다.

오늘 더블린에서 열린 '디지털 시대의 성장 서밋'에서 YouTube는 Google.org와 함께 최초의 디지털 웰빙 허브를 만들기 위해 2천만 달러의 기금을 지원한다고 발표했습니다.

새로운 세대의 저널리스트와 팟캐스터가 YouTube에서 뉴스를 새롭게 만들어가고 있습니다. 최근 이들 중 50명 이상을 초청하여 YouTube 최초의 Independent Media Summit을 개최했습니다.

Google과 YouTube는 10년 넘게 플랫폼에서 아동과 청소년을 지원하는 제품을 출시하고, 프로그램을 지원하며, 내장된 보호 기능을 제공하는 한편, 가족을 위해 기술을 현명하게 선택할 수 있도록 부모에게 도구와 리소스를 제공해 왔습니다. 안전한 인터넷의 날(Safer Internet Day)을 맞아 디지털 세상에서 아동과 청소년을 지원하는 최신 업데이트를 공유해 드립니다.

매일 수십억 명의 사람들이 YouTube를 통해 주변 세상을 배우고 이해합니다. 수업 과제에 대한 도움을 받거나, 외국어를 공부하거나, 다른 직업에 대해 알아보는 등 사람들은 YouTube에서 무엇이든 찾아보고 새로운 것을 배울 수 있습니다. 지난 6월 미국에서 학습 및 방법 안내 콘텐츠의 조회수는 55억 회를 넘었습니다.

YouTube는 속보부터 시민 담론을 이끄는 토론에 이르기까지 자신의 삶에 영향을 미치는 사건들을 이해하기 위해 전 세계 사람들이 찾는 곳입니다. AI 생성 콘텐츠가 진화함에 따라 이러한 대화의 중심에 있는 개인은 자신의 신원을 보호하기 위한 신뢰할 수 있는 도구가 필요합니다.

오늘 더블린에서 열린 '디지털 시대의 성장 서밋'에서 YouTube는 Google.org와 함께 최초의 디지털 웰빙 허브를 만들기 위해 2천만 달러의 기금을 지원한다고 발표했습니다.

새로운 세대의 저널리스트와 팟캐스터가 YouTube에서 뉴스를 새롭게 만들어가고 있습니다. 최근 이들 중 50명 이상을 초청하여 YouTube 최초의 Independent Media Summit을 개최했습니다.

Google과 YouTube는 10년 넘게 플랫폼에서 아동과 청소년을 지원하는 제품을 출시하고, 프로그램을 지원하며, 내장된 보호 기능을 제공하는 한편, 가족을 위해 기술을 현명하게 선택할 수 있도록 부모에게 도구와 리소스를 제공해 왔습니다. 안전한 인터넷의 날(Safer Internet Day)을 맞아 디지털 세상에서 아동과 청소년을 지원하는 최신 업데이트를 공유해 드립니다.

## Die Geschichte der Leichtathletik.

## Die Athletinnen und Athleten die Leichtathletik Geschichte schrieben:

**Erfolgreiche Athleten, Athletinnen und Legenden der deutschen und internationalen Leichtathletik.**In der “Hall of Fame” von German Road Races soll der deutschen und auch der internationalen Legenden und herausragenden Persönlichkeiten der Leichtathletik ein Denkmal gesetzt werden – und auch gleichzeitig ein Archiv und “Gedächtnis” entstehen, in dem man sich ihrer grossartigen Leistungen erinnert.

 Zunächst war es eine Idee vom Berlin-Marathon – in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Sportmuseum Berlin – erfolgreiche Mittel- und Langstreckler früherer Zeiten aus Ost und West zusammenzuführen und deren Leistungen statistisch zu erfassen. Im Laufe der Zeit wurden in der Rubrik “Sportmuseum” dann auch Beiträge aus Zeitungen und Zeitschriften übernommen, die sich mit den Erfolgen und der Vita überragender Leichtathleten der Vergangenheit befassten.Im Zuge der Vorbereitung und Einstimmung auf die XII. IAAF Weltmeisterschaften der Leichtathletik Berlin 2009 befasste man sich in den Medien viel mehr mit der großen leichtathletischen Vergangenheit Deutschlands. Insofern ist ein großes und über die Mittel- und Langstreckler Gruppe hinausgehendes “Erinnerungs-Archiv” entstanden.Diese Zusammenfassung mit der bisherigen Untergliederung kann sicherlich nur ein Anfang der Gestaltung eines Archives sein, es bedarf der Fortsetzung, Ergänzung, Verbesserung – aber auch weiterer Zuarbeit.

## Die Geschichte der Leichtathletik.

## Die Athletinnen und Athleten die Leichtathletik Geschichte schrieben:

**Erfolgreiche Athleten, Athletinnen und Legenden der deutschen und internationalen Leichtathletik.**In der “Hall of Fame” von German Road Races soll der deutschen und auch der internationalen Legenden und herausragenden Persönlichkeiten der Leichtathletik ein Denkmal gesetzt werden – und auch gleichzeitig ein Archiv und “Gedächtnis” entstehen, in dem man sich ihrer grossartigen Leistungen erinnert.

 Zunächst war es eine Idee vom Berlin-Marathon – in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Sportmuseum Berlin – erfolgreiche Mittel- und Langstreckler früherer Zeiten aus Ost und West zusammenzuführen und deren Leistungen statistisch zu erfassen. Im Laufe der Zeit wurden in der Rubrik “Sportmuseum” dann auch Beiträge aus Zeitungen und Zeitschriften übernommen, die sich mit den Erfolgen und der Vita überragender Leichtathleten der Vergangenheit befassten.Im Zuge der Vorbereitung und Einstimmung auf die XII. IAAF Weltmeisterschaften der Leichtathletik Berlin 2009 befasste man sich in den Medien viel mehr mit der großen leichtathletischen Vergangenheit Deutschlands. Insofern ist ein großes und über die Mittel- und Langstreckler Gruppe hinausgehendes “Erinnerungs-Archiv” entstanden.Diese Zusammenfassung mit der bisherigen Untergliederung kann sicherlich nur ein Anfang der Gestaltung eines Archives sein, es bedarf der Fortsetzung, Ergänzung, Verbesserung – aber auch weiterer Zuarbeit.

*   Where Music Grows

Promote your music. Find your fans. Turn your passion into a career on YouTube. 
*   ## **Foundry**

Introducing the Foundry Class of 2026: Fall Drop!

In 2026 Foundry supported 40 incredible independent artists from 14 countries with grants, bespoke promotional opportunities and hands-on strategic guidance. 
*   ## **Top Fan Exclusive Videos**

Your most dedicated fans crave direct recognition.

With Top Fan videos, you can now share exclusive video messages - from a quick Short to a longer video - delivered exclusively to your top fans.

Reward your inner circle with thank-you notes, backstage clips, or early song teasers. When uploading in YouTube Studio, select the Top Fans toggle under Visibility settings.  
*   ## **Resources**

Building your Fanbase

When fans are drowning in a sea of choice across digital platforms, creating deep and lasting connections between artists and fans is more important than ever.

YouTube is where these connections form and deepen.

Promote your music. Find your fans. Turn your passion into a career on YouTube. 
*   ## **Foundry**

Introducing the Foundry Class of 2026: Fall Drop!

In 2026 Foundry supported 40 incredible independent artists from 14 countries with grants, bespoke promotional opportunities and hands-on strategic guidance. 
*   ## **Top Fan Exclusive Videos**

Your most dedicated fans crave direct recognition.

With Top Fan videos, you can now share exclusive video messages - from a quick Short to a longer video - delivered exclusively to your top fans.

Reward your inner circle with thank-you notes, backstage clips, or early song teasers. When uploading in YouTube Studio, select the Top Fans toggle under Visibility settings.

Building your Fanbase

When fans are drowning in a sea of choice across digital platforms, creating deep and lasting connections between artists and fans is more important than ever.

YouTube is where these connections form and deepen.

    *   [보도자료 편의점 김밥 12종 품질 비교 정보 제공 [편의점 김밥 품질비교 결과] 편의점 김밥 영양성분 고려해 우유·달걀 함께 섭취하면 좋아 ‘편의점 김밥’에 관한 가격·품질 비교정보는 ‘소비자24(www.consumer.go.kr)’ 내 ‘비교공감’란을 통해 소비자에게 제공될 예정임. 물가 상승으로 외식 부담이 커지면서 가성비와 접근성이 좋은 편의점 김밥의 매출이 증가하고 있다. 이에 한국소비자원(원장 윤수현)이 소비자 선호도가 높은 편의점 김밥 12개 제품의 속재료 구성과 영양성분, 안전성 등을 시험·평가했다. 시험 결과, 제품별로 내용량과 속재료의 구성·비율에 차이가 있어 이를 고려해 제품을 선택하는 것이 바람직했다. 영양성분의 경우 열량과 탄수화물은 적고 나트륨은 대체로 높게 나타나 함께 먹는 식품 선택에 주의가 필요했다. 안전성 및 표시사항은 조사대상 전 제품이 관련 기준에 적합했고, 가격은 김밥종류와 속재료에 따라 최대 800원의 차이가 있었다. ☐ 참치ㆍ불고기 등 주요 속재료, 구성ㆍ비율 차이 있어(세부내용 9쪽) 소비자원 설문조사에서 소비자들은 `김밥 속재료 비율'에 가장 높은 관심을 보였다.* 시험 결과, 제품별로 참치, 불고기 등 주료 속재료 비율은 제품별 차이가 있었다. * 편의점 김밥 관련 정보 중 가장 궁금한 사항에 대한 설문조사 결과, ‘속재료 비율’이라는 응답(중복)이 51.9%로 가장 높음(한국소비자원, 2026). 조사대상 참치김밥 4종에서 주요 속재료인 참치의 비율은 전체 내용량 대비 16.5~21.9% 수준이었으며, `All New 킹듬뿍참치김밥'(세븐일레븐) 제품의 참치 비율이 가장 높았다. 불고기김밥 4종에서 주요 속재료인 불고기의 비율은 전체 내용량 대비 13.1~23.7% 수준으로 참치김밥에 비해 제품별 차이가 컸으며, 그 중 `PBICK THE KITCHEN 불고기김밥'(CU) 제품의 불고기 비율이 가장 높았다. 일반김밥 4종에서 총 속재료*의 비율은 전체 내용량 대비 36.8~45.1% 수준이었으며, `오리지널 근본김밥'(GS25) 제품의 총 속재료 비율이 가장 높았다. ☐ 영양성분, 나트륨 함량 높아 저염식과 함께 섭취해야(세부내용 12쪽) 편의점 김밥 한 줄의 열량은 1일 기준치 대비 18~27%, 탄수화물 함량은 16~23%로 나타나 한 끼 식사를 기준으로 비교했을 때 부족한 편이었다. 지방 함량은 1일 영양성분 기준치의 9~46%로 제품 간 차이가 컸고, 나트륨 함량은 38~70%로 한 끼 식사를 기준으로 평가했을 때 비교적 높은 편으로 나타났다. ※ 1일 에너지필요추정량 및 1일 영양성분 기준치 - 열량(2,000㎉) : 19~29세 여성 기준 1일 에너지필요추정량(2025 한국인 영양소 섭취기준, 보건복지부) - 탄수화물(324g), 단백질(55g), 지방(54g), 나트륨(2,000㎎)(식품 등의 표시·광고에 관한 법률 시행규칙, 총리령 제2004호) 지방 함량은 속재료에 참치와 마요네즈를 함께 사용한 참치김밥이 16~25g 수준으로 불고기김밥(6~14g), 일반김밥(5~8g)과 비교해 높은 편으로 나타났다. 단백질은 일반김밥이 9~14g으로 참치김밥(14~19g), 불고기김밥(14~18g)과 비교했을 때 적은 편이었다. 또한, 나트륨 함량의 경우 김밥 한 줄에 760~1,393mg 수준이었으며, 그 중 `한도초과 숯불향 가득 불고기김밥'(세븐일레븐) 제품이 760mg으로 가장 낮았다. 편의점 김밥은 컵라면과 함께 섭취하는 경우가 많아* 나트륨 과잉 섭취에 주의해야한다.** 또한 균형 잡힌 영양 섭취를 위해 우유·달걀 등의 식품을 함께 섭취하는 것이 바람직하다. * 편의점 김밥과 컵라면을 주로 함께 섭취한다는 설문조사 응답률이 68.9%로 가장 높음(한국소비자원, 2026). ** 컵라면 1회 섭취참고량(100g) 기준 나트륨 1,355mg(68%)(식품안전나라-식품영양성분DB, 식품의약품안전처) ☐ 안전성 및 표시사항, 전 제품이 관련 기준에 적합해(세부내용 16쪽) 판매를 목적으로 하는 식품 또는 식품첨가물의 경우 관련 법령에 따라 성분에 관한 규격을 따라야 한다. 이에, 시험대상의 속재료(단무지, 우엉)에 사용하는 보존료와 감미료를 시험한 결과, 조사대상 전 제품이 준용기준* 이내였으며 중금속과 미생물·이물 시험결과도 전 제품이 관련 기준**에 적합했다. * 보존료(소브산) : 1.0g/kg 이하(절임식품), 감미료(사카린나트륨) : 1.0g/kg(절임류)(식품첨가물의 기준 및 규격, 식약처 고시 제2026-50호) ** 중금속(납, 카드뮴, 비소), 미생물(대장균, 황색포도상구균, 바실루스 세레우스, 클로스트리디움 퍼프린젠스, 살모넬라, 리스테리아 모노사이토제네스)(식품의 기준 및 규격, 식약처 고시 제2026-55호) 또한, 관련 법령에 따라 시험대상 12개 제품에 대한 영양정보*, 알레르기 유발물질** 및 주원료 원산지 표시를 조사한 결과, 전 제품이 관련 규정에 적합했다. * 영양성분 표시량과 실제 측정값의 허용오차 범위를 정함(식품등의 표시기준, 식약처 고시 제2026-37호) ** 표시대상 알레르기 유발물질(19종) : 돼지고기, 밀, 대두, 우유, 알류, 쇠고기, 닭고기, 게, 새우, 고등어, 오징어, 조개류(굴, 전복, 홍합 포함), 복숭아, 토마토, 메밀, 땅콩, 호두, 잣, 아황산류 (식품 등의 표시·광고에 관한 법률 시행규칙, [별표2] 소비자 안전을 위한 표시사항) ☐ 가격, 동일 유형 제품 간 최대 200~400원 차이(세부내용 17쪽) 편의점 김밥 한 줄당 가격은 일반 김밥 2,800~3,000원, 참치김밥 3,100~3,400원, 불고기김밥 3,200~3,600원 수준으로 동일 유형 제품 간 최대 200~400원의 차이가 있었다. 편의점 김밥은 ▲통신사 멤버십 할인, ▲편의점 관련 구독, ▲결제 수단 할인 및 월별 행사 등을 활용하면 더 저렴한 가격에 구매할 수 있으므로, 구매 전에 사용 가능한 할인 방법을 확인할 필요가 있다. 편의점 김밥을 구매할 때는 전체 내용량, 속재료 구성ㆍ비율, 영양성분(나트륨) 함량 등 품질을 확인하고, 편의점별 할인방법을 꼼꼼히 비교한 후 제품을 선택하는 것이 바람직하다.2026-10-15 소비자안전교육과](http://www.ftc.go.kr/selectBbsNttView.do?bordCd=3&key=12&searchCtgry=01,02&nttSn=48112)
    *   [보도자료 밀가루 부산물 가격담합 사건 심의 절차 개시 밀가루 부산물 가격담합 사건 심의 절차 개시 공정거래위원회(위원장 주병기, 이하 ‘공정위’) 사무처는 밀가루 부산물 가격담합 사건에 대해 심사관이 조사한 행위 사실, 위법성 및 조치 의견 등을 기재한 심사보고서를 위원회에 제출(’26.10.13.)하고, 같은 날 6개 밀가루 부산물 제조 및 판매사업자들*(이하 ‘피심인들’)에게 송부함으로써 심의 절차가 개시되었다. * 대한제분, 사조동아원, 사조대림, 삼양사, 씨제이제일제당, 한탑 ※ 심사보고서는 심사관이 조사 과정에서 파악한 위법성 및 그에 대한 조치의견을 기재한 것으로서 위원회 최종 판단을 구속하지 않음. 향후 독립된 위원회 심의를 거쳐 사건에 대한 최종 판단이 이루어질 예정임에 유의하여 주시기 바람 심사관은 피심인들이 2017년 4월경부터 2025년 10월경(총8년 6개월)까지 매월 밀가루 부산물* 제품의 판매가격 담합행위를 하였다고 판단하였고, 이 사건 담합행위로 영향을 받은 관련매출액이 1조 4천억 원에 이르는 것으로 산정하였다. * 식용 밀가루를 제조하는 과정에서 부수적으로 생산되는 물질로서 식용이 아닌 것을 의미하고, 대표적인 밀가루 부산물로는 소맥피, 등외분 등이 있으며 주로 동물이 먹는 배합사료의 원료로 사용됨 심사관은 위와 같은 행위가 공정거래법 제40조 제1항 제1호(가격담합)를 위반하는 매우 중대한 위법행위라고 판단하고, 시정조치, 과징금 부과 및 법인과 임직원에 대한 고발 의견을 제시하였다. 향후 위원회는 심의를 거쳐 법 위반 여부에 대한 최종 판단을 내리고, 법 위반이 확인되는 경우에는 구체적인 제재 수준도 확정할 예정이다. 피심인들은 심사보고서 수령일로부터 8주 내 서면 의견 제출, 증거자료의 열람·복사 신청 등 방어권을 충분히 보장받을 수 있다. 공정위는 방어권 보장 절차가 종료되는 대로 최대한 신속하게 위원회를 개최하여 최종 판단을 내릴 계획이다.2026-10-14 국제카르텔조사과](http://www.ftc.go.kr/selectBbsNttView.do?bordCd=3&key=12&searchCtgry=01,02&nttSn=48107)

    *   [설명자료[설명] 서울신문(10.14.) 한지붕 아래에서 조사·심판... 신뢰 흔드는 기형적 공정위 기사 관련 공정위는 조사-심판 기능을 엄격하게 분리하고 피심인에게 동등한 기회를 부여하고 있으며 주요국 경쟁당국도 이같이 운영되고 있습니다. □ 2026.10.14. 서울신문 ｢‘한 지붕’ 아래서 조사·심판…신뢰 흔드는 기형적 공정위」보도 관련입니다.ㅇ 위 보도는 “사건을 조사하는 검사와 심판하는 판사가 공정위라는 한 조직 안에 있다는 점이 공정위 제재의 공정성을 의심받게 함”, “심사관과 피심인 측의 의견을 청취하는데, 똑같은 횟수와 시간이 부여되지 아니함”이라는 취지의 내용 등을 포함하고 있습니다. □ 경쟁법 집행의 전문성 및 효율성을 도모하기 위해 다수의 경쟁당국이 조사와 심판 기능을 모두 수행하고 있는 바, 현행 공정위 조직 구조가 기형적이라고 볼 수 없습니다.ㅇ 미국 연방거래위원회(FTC), EU 집행위원회, 영국 경쟁시장청(CMA) 등 다수의 해외 경쟁당국에서 조사와 심판 기능을 함께 수행하고 있으며, 조사와 심판을 분리·운영했던 일부 경쟁당국(벨기에, 핀란드, 베트남 등)도 통합하여 운영하는 추세입니다. □ 한편, 공정위는 조사와 심판 기능을 엄격히 분리 운영하고, 다양한 절차적 통제 장치를 마련하여 심결의 독립성과 공정성을 확보하고 있습니다.ㅇ 공정위는 처분의 독립성 및 정치적 중립성 확보를 위하여 민간 전문가를 포함한 합의제 행정기관으로 운영되고 있으며, 독립적 지위가 보장된 위원들이 충분한 논의를 거쳐 중립적으로 법 위반 여부를 판단하고 있습니다. - 이를 위해 위원 11명 중 5명은 비상임위원으로 구성하여, 경제학・법학 등 다양한 배경과 경험을 가진 민간 전문가들을 위촉하고 있습니다. * 「공정거래법」 제61조(위원의 임기), 제62조(신분보장), 제63조(위원의 정치운동 금지) - 위원들은 조사부서의 심사보고서와 피심인의 반박 의견을 토대로 심의·토론 및 합의를 거쳐 독립적으로 판단·결정하며, 조사부서의 조치의견은 위원회를 구속하지 않습니다.ㅇ 또한, 위원장을 비롯한 위원에게 심결의 공정을 기대하기 어려운 경우 제척ㆍ기피ㆍ회피제도를 운영하여 해당 위원이 심의·의결에 관여하지 않도록 하고 있습니다. - 특히, 사건 조사의 전(全) 기간 중 해당 사건의 심사관으로 근무한 적이 있는 위원은 실질적인 관여 여부를 불문하고 해당 사건의 심의에서 제척되도록 함으로써 동 제도를 엄격하게 적용하고 있습니다. □ 이와 더불어, 공정위는 심판의 독립성과 공정성을 높이기 위해 심사관은 위원회의 의사결정 과정에 관여할 수 없고, 위원회는 사무처의 조사 과정에 관여할 수 없도록 기능을 엄격히 분리하고 있습니다. ㅇ ’23년 법집행 시스템 개선에 따라 조사부서에서 근무한 직원이 곧바로 심판부서로 이동하지 않도록 인사원칙을 마련하여 시행하고 있습니다.ㅇ 또한, 심의 과정에서 ‘무기대등(武器對等)의 원칙’에 입각하여 심사관과 피심인에게 동등한 위원보고 및 의견 진술 기회를 부여하고 있습니다. - ‘23.4월 사건절차규칙 개정으로 심사관도 피심인과 같이 의견청취절차를 통해서만 위원에게 사건을 보고하도록 하고, 주심위원 등은 심사관 또는 피심인에게 자료 제출을 요구하는 경우 심결보좌 담당자를 통하도록 하여 비공식적인 직접 접촉을 제한하고 있습니다. □ 이외에도 심의 개시 후 조사 제한 및 조사 단계에서 피조사인 의견제출권 명문화(`20.5월), 자료의 열람·복사 업무지침 제정(`20.5월), 복잡한 사안에 대한 2회 이상 심의 진행(`23.4월), 의견서 제출 기한 연장(`25.12월) 등 피심인의 방어권 보장을 위한 제도개선을 지속하고 있습니다. □ 따라서 조사-심판 통합의 기형적 구조로 제재의 공정성이 없다거나 심사관과 피심인에게 동등한 기회를 부여하지 않는다는 주장은 사실이 아니니 보도에 유의하여 주시기 바랍니다.2026-10-14 심판총괄담당관](http://www.ftc.go.kr/selectBbsNttView.do?bordCd=3&key=13&searchCtgry=03&nttSn=48108)
    *   [설명자료[설명] 매일경제(9.30.) ｢공정위 고무줄 과징금 … 10건 중 9건 최종부과 땐 대폭 깎였다 등 기사 관련 공정위는 적법한 절차를 거쳐 조사를 진행하고 법률과 원칙에 따라 산정된 과징금을 부과하고 있으며, 국민의 알권리를 존중하여 중대 사건 진행상황을 공개하고 있습니다. □ 2026.9.30. 매일경제 ｢공정위 고무줄 과징금 … 10건 중 9건 최종부과 땐 대폭 깎였다｣, ｢모호한 규정 탓? … 공정위, 심의 前 사건공개 올해만 17건｣, ｢과잉제재에 속타는 기업｣ 보도 관련입니다.ㅇ 위 보도는 “공정위 조사에 기업으로서는 불이익을 우려해 사실상 응할 수밖에 없는 구조”, “공정위의 과징금 부과 사건 87건 가운데 75건(86%)에서 심사보고서 단계 과징금 산정액이 최종 부과액보다 많다”, “공정위가 자의적으로 사건 공개여부를 결정한다”는 등의 내용을 포함하고 있습니다. □ 기업으로서는 불이익을 우려해 공정위 조사에 사실상 응할 수밖에 없는 구조라는 보도(｢과잉제재에 속타는 기업｣)에 대해서는,ㅇ 공정위의 조사는 피조사업체의 동의가 필수인 임의조사로, 피조사업체는 조사범위를 벗어난 조사를 거부할 수 있으며, 위와 같은 사실을 피조사업체가 잘 알 수 있도록 현장조사 개시시 공정위 조사공무원은 피조사업체에게 위와 같은 사항이 명시된 서면을 교부하고 있습니다. ㅇ 또한 피조사업체는 공정위가 수집한 자료가 사건과 무관할 경우 반환･폐기를 요청할 수 있으며, 해당 자료가 실제로 사건과 무관한 경우 공정위는 이를 반환･폐기하도록 규정되어 있는 등, 피조사업체의 방어권 및 적법절차를 담보하기 위한 여러 규정들이 마련되어 있습니다. □ 기사 내용 중, 2024년 과징금 부과사건 87건 중 75건에서 ‘심사보고서의 과징금 산정액이 최종 부과액보다 많았으며, 심사단계 과징금 산정액은 최종부과액의 1.9~2.8배에 달했다’는 보도(｢공정위 고무줄 과징금 … 10건 중 9건 최종부과 땐 대폭 깎였다｣)와 관련하여, ㅇ 심사보고서에는 관련 매출액만 기재될 뿐 구체적·확정적인 과징금 액수가 기재되지 않습니다.ㅇ 기사에서 언급한 감사보고서 상 ‘심사보고서상 과징금 산정액’은 감사원이 ‘심사보고서 기초자료를 근거로 산출한 과징금 규모’로서, 심사보고서의 관련매출액과 부과기준율을 토대로 과징금을 단순계산한 것이며, 이를 실제 부과과징금과 비교한 것입니다. ㅇ 공정위 심의는 심사관과 피심인간 대심구조를 취하고 있어 심사관 의견인 심사보고서와 피심인 및 대리인의 반박의견을 공정하게 반영하여, 위원회의 최종 합의가 도출되도록 이루어집니다. 따라서 심사보고서의 의견과 최종 의결은 다른 것이 일반적입니다. ㅇ 이와 관련하여 기사에서 인용한 감사보고서 상 이동통신 3사 담합건의 경우, 피심인들이 자료 제출을 거부해 부득이 관련매출액을 추정하여 산출할 수 밖에 없었습니다. □ 심의 개시사실 공개(｢공정위 고무줄 과징금 … 10건 중 9건 최종부과 땐 대폭 깎였다｣, ｢모호한 규정 탓? … 공정위, 심의 前 사건공개 올해만 17건｣ 관련)의 경우, 국민생활과 밀접하고 경쟁질서에 영향이 큰 사건들에 한하여, 조사가 종료되어 심의・의결 절차가 개시된다는 사실을 공개함으로써 국민들의 알 권리를 보장하고, 사건 처리절차와 정보의 투명성을 높임으로써 법 집행의 민주적･사회적 견제를 보장하며, 이를 통해 경쟁질서 회복과 사회후생 개선을 앞당기기 위한 것입니다. ㅇ 조사가 종료되어 심사보고서가 위원회에 상정된 후 공개하는 것이므로, 조사 중인 내용을 공개한다는 주장은 사실이 아닙니다. ㅇ 또한 심사보고서의 내용이 위원회의 최종적인 판단이라고 오해하는 것을 방지하기 위해, 심사보고서 및 심의 개시사실을 공개하는 보도자료에는 해당 내용은 잠정적인 것으로 위원회의 최종적인 판단이 아님을 명시하도록 하고 있습니다. □ 공정위는 위 보도가 인용한 감사원의 정기감사 지적사항을 수용하여, 의결결과에 대한 보도자료 배포 시 위원회의 심의·합의 확정 내용을 최대한 반영하고, 잠정금액을 보도자료에 기재해야 하는 경우에도 보도의 적시성을 추구하면서도 최대한의 정확성을 기할 수 있도록 할 것입니다.2026-10-01 조사총괄담당관](http://www.ftc.go.kr/selectBbsNttView.do?bordCd=3&key=13&searchCtgry=03&nttSn=48078)

## German Road Races (GRR) e.V.

## Die Stimme des Laufsports

German Road Races (GRR) e.V. ist die Interessensgemeinschaft der Lauf-Veranstalter in Deutschland. Seit vielen Jahren kümmern wir uns um alle Belange des Laufsports und können dabei vielbeachtete Erfolge vorweisen. Als Stimme des Laufsports berichten, kommentieren und dokumentieren wir das Geschehen im Laufsport, in der Leichtathletik, der Sportpolitik, der Sportmedizin und weiteren interessanten Themen und erarbeiten dabei auf unterschiedlichen Feldern eigenständige Positionen und Aktivitäten.

Wir freuen uns über Ihr Interesse am Laufsport und den vielen Veranstaltungen, die unsere Mitglieder im Laufe eines Jahres anbieten. Nutzen Sie das breite Lauf- und Walking-Angebot für Jung und Alt, für Breiten- und Leistungssportler im Wald, auf der Straße oder dem in der Natur zugänglichen Terrain, das Ihnen Spaß und Freude, zudem auch ein Höchstmaß an Erholung bietet.

Wir freuen uns auf Sie.

## [Hier geht es zu der News Seite von German Road Races](https://news.germanroadraces.de/)

### Für alle Laufveranstaltende

## Warum es sich lohnt

*   Erfahrungsaustausch und Know-How-Transfer
*   Miteinander und voneinander lernern
*   Vertrauliches und kollegiales Miteinander
*   Wir sind bereits über 50 Laufveranstaltende, die sich austauschen
*   Das Beste für alle Läuferinnen und Läufer bieten

*   Regelmäßiger Austausch und Impulse in Online-Meetings

Nimm unverbindlich Kontakt mit uns auf und erfahre in einem persönlichen Gespräch, warum es sich für alle Laufveranstaltende lohnt, dabeizusein und Mitglied unserer Communtity zu werden.

Ob Straße, Trail oder Ultra, ob Volkslauf oder internationaler Marathon, bei uns seid Ihr willkommen.

## Jetzt Mitglied werden!

## **Community und Forum - wir sehen uns**

*   Wir treffen uns einmal im Jahr für ein mehrtägiges Jahrestreffen. In 2024 wird das in Hannover sein. Projekte, die wir angehen, werden von Arbeitsgruppen umgesetzt, die sich nach Bedarf treffen und natürlich sehen wir uns regelmäßig auf unseren jeweiligen Laufveranstaltungen.

*   Seit Anfang 2024 aber haben wir unseren Austausch digitalisiert und nutzen Videokonferenzen und ein Forum, um uns öfter zu sehen und über alle Themen zu sprechen, die uns verbinden und beschäftigen.

*   Immer wieder laden wir auch externe Expertinnen und Impulsgeber ein, die uns helfen, über den Tellerrand hinauszudenken.

![Image 2](https://germanroadraces.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nw_230408_12_36-69-1024x512.png)

## Unsere Kooperationspartner

## Die nächsten Laufevents unserer Mitglieder

Marathon, DuoMarathon, Halbmarathon, 10 km

*    31.10.2026 

*    06.12.2026 

Halbmarathon

## Partner, auf die wir setzen

## German Road Races (GRR) e.V.

## Die Stimme des Laufsports

German Road Races (GRR) e.V. ist die Interessensgemeinschaft der Lauf-Veranstalter in Deutschland. Seit vielen Jahren kümmern wir uns um alle Belange des Laufsports und können dabei vielbeachtete Erfolge vorweisen. Als Stimme des Laufsports berichten, kommentieren und dokumentieren wir das Geschehen im Laufsport, in der Leichtathletik, der Sportpolitik, der Sportmedizin und weiteren interessanten Themen und erarbeiten dabei auf unterschiedlichen Feldern eigenständige Positionen und Aktivitäten.

![Image 1](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1999TeglaLoroupe.jpg)

Source: Victor Sailer (link under References)

**26-Sep-1999 – Berlin Marathon – 2:20:43 – Nike Air Streak Vengeance

 Date of birth: 9-May-1973

 Nationality: Kenyan

 World Record duration: 2 years, 4 days**

**The athlete:**After setting the women’s marathon world record in 1998, Tegla Loroupe hardly rested on her laurels. She won the Rotterdam Marathon again in 1999 as well as another half-marathon championship crown. This was alongside multiple half-marathon wins across Europe. What still drove her was the chance to break the 2:20 barrier for women.

Her training had gone well. Loroupe and the organisers of the Berlin Marathon were so confident that she would break through that barrier that they gave her the number 219. With pacemakers calling her splits, Loroupe was 90 seconds ahead of her previous best in the early stages. Fatigue would begin to set in, and by halfway she was falling behind her world record pace.

At the 28 kilometre mark Loroupe found new reserves of energy and powered up the only significant incline of the course. By kilometre 32 she was back on track to break the world record. She would continue sprinting towards the finish and after 24.2 of 26.2 miles she was three seconds behind her previous best. She was disappointed not to get below 2:20, but she still set a new world record.

Loroupe would go on to win the 2000 London Marathon along with another half-marathon world championship among her other later victories. It was only Olympic gold that would elude her, the 2000 Olympics didn’t go according to plan, with Loroupe suffering severe food poisoning the night before the marathon event.

Despite some sources claiming otherwise, including initially Guinness World Records, Loroupe did not run the marathon at the 2000 Olympics barefoot. Although it would have made for an important and fascinating benchmark, Loroupe having trained in her earlier days without shoes, there is a clear picture from the event showing her wearing the Nike Air Streaks that had brought her so much success. I reached out to Guinness World Records, and they have since corrected their entry to reflect that [Phạm Thị Bình](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/2013-pham-thi-binh/) holds this distinction.

Her achievements helped inspire the rise of African women in distance running, with future world record holder Catherine Ndereba citing her as the inspiration to start running herself. Loroupe further used her position to promote peace, founding the [Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation](https://teglapeace.org/) in 2003. She later worked with both the United Nations and Oxfam to promote these ideals. She would also serve as the Chef de Mission for the refugee team at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics.

**The shoes:**

[![Image 2: 1998NikeAirStreak](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1998NikeAirStreak-400x285.jpg)](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1998NikeAirStreak.jpg "1998NikeAirStreak")

[![Image 3: 1997NikeRacingFlats](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/1997NikeRacingFlats-400x285.jpeg)](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/1997NikeRacingFlats.jpeg "1997NikeRacingFlats")

[![Image 4: 1996NikeAirStreakLight](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1996NikeAirStreakLight-400x285.jpg)](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1996NikeAirStreakLight.jpg "1996NikeAirStreakLight")

[![Image 5: 1996NikeAirStreakCatalogue](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1996NikeAirStreakCatalogue-1.jpg)](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1996NikeAirStreakCatalogue-1.jpg "1996NikeAirStreakCatalogue")

The shoes on her feet during that day in Berlin were the same model of Nike Air Streaks she had used the year before, the Vengeance. We have a clear picture of her in the runners, the overlays on the upper unmistakable in neon yellow. The picture helped with the previous entry, as oddly there were no clear photos of Loroupe from the 1998 Rotterdam Marathon. You can read more about that [here](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/1998-tegla-loroupe/).

**References:**[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe)

[https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303843104579169881599887664](https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052702303843104579169881599887664)

![Image 1](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1999TeglaLoroupe.jpg)
Source: Victor Sailer (link under References)
**26-Sep-1999 – Berlin Marathon – 2:20:43 – Nike Air Streak Vengeance
Date of birth: 9-May-1973
Nationality: Kenyan
World Record duration: 2 years, 4 days**
**The athlete:**After setting the women’s marathon world record in 1998, Tegla Loroupe hardly rested on her laurels. She won the Rotterdam Marathon again in 1999 as well as another half-marathon championship crown. This was alongside multiple half-marathon wins across Europe. What still drove her was the chance to break the 2:20 barrier for women.
Her training had gone well. Loroupe and the organisers of the Berlin Marathon were so confident that she would break through that barrier that they gave her the number 219. With pacemakers calling her splits, Loroupe was 90 seconds ahead of her previous best in the early stages. Fatigue would begin to set in, and by halfway she was falling behind her world record pace.
At the 28 kilometre mark Loroupe found new reserves of energy and powered up the only significant incline of the course. By kilometre 32 she was back on track to break the world record. She would continue sprinting towards the finish and after 24.2 of 26.2 miles she was three seconds behind her previous best. She was disappointed not to get below 2:20, but she still set a new world record.
Loroupe would go on to win the 2000 London Marathon along with another half-marathon world championship among her other later victories. It was only Olympic gold that would elude her, the 2000 Olympics didn’t go according to plan, with Loroupe suffering severe food poisoning the night before the marathon event.

Despite some sources claiming otherwise, including initially Guinness World Records, Loroupe did not run the marathon at the 2000 Olympics barefoot. Although it would have made for an important and fascinating benchmark, Loroupe having trained in her earlier days without shoes, there is a clear picture from the event showing her wearing the Nike Air Streaks that had brought her so much success. I reached out to Guinness World Records, and they have since corrected their entry to reflect that [Phạm Thị Bình](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/2013-pham-thi-binh/) holds this distinction.
Her achievements helped inspire the rise of African women in distance running, with future world record holder Catherine Ndereba citing her as the inspiration to start running herself. Loroupe further used her position to promote peace, founding the [Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation](https://teglapeace.org/) in 2003. She later worked with both the United Nations and Oxfam to promote these ideals. She would also serve as the Chef de Mission for the refugee team at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics.
**The shoes:**
[![Image 2: 1998NikeAirStreak](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1998NikeAirStreak-400x285.jpg)](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1998NikeAirStreak.jpg "1998NikeAirStreak")
[![Image 3: 1997NikeRacingFlats](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/1997NikeRacingFlats-400x285.jpeg)](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/1997NikeRacingFlats.jpeg "1997NikeRacingFlats")

[![Image 4: 1996NikeAirStreakLight](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1996NikeAirStreakLight-400x285.jpg)](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1996NikeAirStreakLight.jpg "1996NikeAirStreakLight")
[![Image 5: 1996NikeAirStreakCatalogue](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1996NikeAirStreakCatalogue-1.jpg)](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1996NikeAirStreakCatalogue-1.jpg "1996NikeAirStreakCatalogue")
The shoes on her feet during that day in Berlin were the same model of Nike Air Streaks she had used the year before, the Vengeance. We have a clear picture of her in the runners, the overlays on the upper unmistakable in neon yellow. The picture helped with the previous entry, as oddly there were no clear photos of Loroupe from the 1998 Rotterdam Marathon. You can read more about that [here](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/1998-tegla-loroupe/).

# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin

[![Image 49: Facebook](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/facebook-white.png)](https://www.facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again&title=Loroupe%20breaks%20marathon%20world%20best%20in%20Berlin "Share on Facebook")[![Image 50: Twitter](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/twitter-white.png)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again&text=loroupe-breaks-marathon-world-best-in-berlin "Share on X")[![Image 51: Email](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/email-white.png)](mailto:?subject=Loroupe%20breaks%20marathon%20world%20best%20in%20Berlin&body=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again "Share via email")

Kenyan distance runner Tegla Loroupe (© Getty Images)

Kenya's Tegla Loroupe improved her own world women's best time by four seconds to win the Berlin marathon in 2:20:43 before more than a million cheering spectators on Sunday.

Kenyan Josephat Kiprono won the men's race in 2:06:45, the third best time ever, leading a record field of 28,000 participants through the German capital city under near-ideal weather conditions - 15 degrees, cloudy and little wind.

The flat and fast course that wends its way through nine of the Berlin's 23 districts now holds the world's best marks for men and women: Brazilian Ronaldo da Costa won last year's race in 2:06.05.

The diminutive Loroupe, who is based in Germany, beat the previous best time of 2:20:47 for the 42.195 km race, which she set when she won the Rotterdam marathon in April 1998.

"This was my best race ever," said Loroupe, who did not realise she had set the new best mark until several minutes after crossing the finish line. "It makes it all the nicer that I did it in Germany."

Loroupe, who came in third in the 10,000 metre event at the World Championships in Seville last month, collected 180,000 marks ($96,000) for setting the world best time on top of her first-place prize of 50,000 marks ($27,000).

Loroupe had been aiming to become the first women to run faster than 2:20, but the 26-year-old slipped behind the world-best pace midway through the race as it moved through the districts of Kreuzberg and Neukoelln.

She found a new burst of energy at the 28-km (17-mile) mark in the leafy district of Steglitz and raced up the course's only significant incline, a climb of about 30 metres between the 30 and 32-km marks, to put herself back on track for the world best time.

"I hadn't expected it for a while because I had felt very tired," said Loroupe, who has lived and trained in the German town of Detmold for the last seven years. "I tried for the 2:19 mark but I didn't manage it.

"Thanks to the support of the crowd I was able to pick up the pace again," added the Kenyan, who stands 1.53 metres tall and weighs 40 kg.

"Tegla really broke the record in the last 100 metres," said her coach Volker Wagner. "I don’t think even Carl Lewis could have beaten her over the last couple of kilometres. She really sprinted right at the end."

Marleen Renders of Belgium was second in the women's race finishing in 2:23.58, followed by Russia's Svetlana Zakharova in 2:27.07.

Kiprono completed a fine day for Kenya and came close to setting a men's best time with a strong kick on the final mile of the race down the fashionable Kudamm shopping boulevard.

Only da Costa's world best mark in Berlin last year and South Africa's Gerd Thys, who set the year's best time in 2:06:32 in February in Tokyo, have been faster.

Kiprono, who came in second in the 1997 race, was followed to the line by Takayuki Inubushi of Japan in 2:06.57 and compatriot Samson Kandie in 2:08.34.

The 28,000 participants in 26th annual Berlin marathon included 4,000 rollerbladers, wheelchair racers and power walkers.

Only the New York and London marathons, with about 30,000 participants, are larger, organisers said.

# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin
[![Image 49: Facebook](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/facebook-white.png)](https://www.facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again&title=Loroupe%20breaks%20marathon%20world%20best%20in%20Berlin "Share on Facebook")[![Image 50: Twitter](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/twitter-white.png)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again&text=loroupe-breaks-marathon-world-best-in-berlin "Share on X")[![Image 51: Email](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/email-white.png)](mailto:?subject=Loroupe%20breaks%20marathon%20world%20best%20in%20Berlin&body=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again "Share via email")
Kenyan distance runner Tegla Loroupe (© Getty Images)
Kenya's Tegla Loroupe improved her own world women's best time by four seconds to win the Berlin marathon in 2:20:43 before more than a million cheering spectators on Sunday.
Kenyan Josephat Kiprono won the men's race in 2:06:45, the third best time ever, leading a record field of 28,000 participants through the German capital city under near-ideal weather conditions - 15 degrees, cloudy and little wind.
The flat and fast course that wends its way through nine of the Berlin's 23 districts now holds the world's best marks for men and women: Brazilian Ronaldo da Costa won last year's race in 2:06.05.
The diminutive Loroupe, who is based in Germany, beat the previous best time of 2:20:47 for the 42.195 km race, which she set when she won the Rotterdam marathon in April 1998.
headings: # Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin

chunks.text:
# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin
"This was my best race ever," said Loroupe, who did not realise she had set the new best mark until several minutes after crossing the finish line. "It makes it all the nicer that I did it in Germany."
Loroupe, who came in third in the 10,000 metre event at the World Championships in Seville last month, collected 180,000 marks ($96,000) for setting the world best time on top of her first-place prize of 50,000 marks ($27,000).
Loroupe had been aiming to become the first women to run faster than 2:20, but the 26-year-old slipped behind the world-best pace midway through the race as it moved through the districts of Kreuzberg and Neukoelln.
She found a new burst of energy at the 28-km (17-mile) mark in the leafy district of Steglitz and raced up the course's only significant incline, a climb of about 30 metres between the 30 and 32-km marks, to put herself back on track for the world best time.
"I hadn't expected it for a while because I had felt very tired," said Loroupe, who has lived and trained in the German town of Detmold for the last seven years. "I tried for the 2:19 mark but I didn't manage it.
"Thanks to the support of the crowd I was able to pick up the pace again," added the Kenyan, who stands 1.53 metres tall and weighs 40 kg.
"Tegla really broke the record in the last 100 metres," said her coach Volker Wagner. "I don’t think even Carl Lewis could have beaten her over the last couple of kilometres. She really sprinted right at the end."
Marleen Renders of Belgium was second in the women's race finishing in 2:23.58, followed by Russia's Svetlana Zakharova in 2:27.07.
Kiprono completed a fine day for Kenya and came close to setting a men's best time with a strong kick on the final mile of the race down the fashionable Kudamm shopping boulevard.
headings: # Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin

chunks.text:
# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin
Only da Costa's world best mark in Berlin last year and South Africa's Gerd Thys, who set the year's best time in 2:06:32 in February in Tokyo, have been faster.
Kiprono, who came in second in the 1997 race, was followed to the line by Takayuki Inubushi of Japan in 2:06.57 and compatriot Samson Kandie in 2:08.34.
The 28,000 participants in 26th annual Berlin marathon included 4,000 rollerbladers, wheelchair racers and power walkers.
Only the New York and London marathons, with about 30,000 participants, are larger, organisers said.

# Die Geschichte der Leichtathletik.

# Die Athletinnen und Athleten die Leichtathletik Geschichte schrieben:

**Erfolgreiche Athleten, Athletinnen und Legenden der deutschen und internationalen Leichtathletik.**In der “Hall of Fame” von German Road Races soll der deutschen und auch der internationalen Legenden und herausragenden Persönlichkeiten der Leichtathletik ein Denkmal gesetzt werden – und auch gleichzeitig ein Archiv und “Gedächtnis” entstehen, in dem man sich ihrer grossartigen Leistungen erinnert.

 Zunächst war es eine Idee vom Berlin-Marathon – in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Sportmuseum Berlin – erfolgreiche Mittel- und Langstreckler früherer Zeiten aus Ost und West zusammenzuführen und deren Leistungen statistisch zu erfassen. Im Laufe der Zeit wurden in der Rubrik “Sportmuseum” dann auch Beiträge aus Zeitungen und Zeitschriften übernommen, die sich mit den Erfolgen und der Vita überragender Leichtathleten der Vergangenheit befassten.Im Zuge der Vorbereitung und Einstimmung auf die XII. IAAF Weltmeisterschaften der Leichtathletik Berlin 2009 befasste man sich in den Medien viel mehr mit der großen leichtathletischen Vergangenheit Deutschlands. Insofern ist ein großes und über die Mittel- und Langstreckler Gruppe hinausgehendes “Erinnerungs-Archiv” entstanden.Diese Zusammenfassung mit der bisherigen Untergliederung kann sicherlich nur ein Anfang der Gestaltung eines Archives sein, es bedarf der Fortsetzung, Ergänzung, Verbesserung – aber auch weiterer Zuarbeit.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –

AIMS Marathon Museum of Running

Auf Anregung von Horst Milde (Berlin-Marathon) wurde das Sportmuseum Berlin vom 14. Kongreß der AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau am 4.–8. Dezember 1994 zum AIMS Marathon-Museum of Running berufen. Damit hatte die Geschichte des Laufens in Berlin einen adäquaten internationalen Sammlungsort gefunden, den die AIMS seitdem organisatorisch und ab 2008 auch finanziell unterstützt.

Das Sportmuseum Berlin ist das älteste und größte Sportmuseum in Deutschland (seit 1925), mit fünf professsionellen Sport-Historikern, die von der Stadt Berlin finanziert werden. Die Ausstellungsräume und das umfangreiche Archiv befinden sich im Olympiapark Berlin.

Am 21. Januar 2015 wurden die Wortmarke Marathoneum und ein Läuferlogo als Bildmarke auf das Forum für Sportgeschichte beim Deutschen Patent- und Markenamt eingetragen.

Unter der Dachmarke Marathoneum werden zukünftig alle Aktivitäten des Sportmuseum Berlin und seines Förderervereins Forum für Sportgeschichte hinsichtlich der nationalen und internationalen Geschichte des Laufens gebündelt. Das Marathoneum ist somit zugleich Sammlung, Archiv, Herausgeber, Imprint, Veranstalter und Multiplikator für alle Erscheinungsformen des Laufsports! Zusätzlich verleiht das Marathoneum alle zwei Jahre den ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ für verdiente und langjährige Wegbereiter des Laufsports.

Das Marathoneum besitzt ca. 2.500 Plakate, ca. 1.500 T-Shirts, ca. 2.200 Finisher-Medaillen sowie 1.600 Akkreditierungskarten von Läufen aus der ganzen Welt. In der Bibliothek befinden sich mehr als 95 deutsche und englischsprachige Laufzeitschriften. Der Gesamtbestand der Sammlungen wird auf ca. 250 Regalmetern in zwei großen Depoträumen im Sportmuseum Berlin nach museologischen Regeln deponiert und verzeichnet. Ein wichtiger Schatz des Museums ist die umfangreiche und großartige englischsprachige Sammlung von Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), sowie die Archive von Henryk Paskal (Polen), Wim Verhoorn (Niederland) und Werner Sonntag (Deutschland).

Im Olympiapark Berlin sind in der Ausstellung „Keep on Running“ auf 300m³ ausgewählte Objekte aus der Sammlung, darunter Startnummern, Schuhe und Sportkleidung von Olympiasiegern und Weltrekordlern ausgestellt.

* * *

**English:**At the suggestion of Horst Milde (Berlin Marathon), the Berlin Sports Museum was appointed the AIMS Marathon Museum of Running at the 14th Congress of the AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau on 4-8 December 1994. So the history of running in Berlin had found an adequate international collection location, which the AIMS has been supporting organizationally and financially since 2008.

The Berlin Sports Museum is the oldest and largest sports museum in Germany (since 1925), with five professional sports historians financed by the city of Berlin. The exhibition rooms and the extensive archive are located in the Berlin Olympic Park.

On 21 January 2015, the word mark Marathoneum and a runner logo were registered as a figurative mark in the Forum for Sports History at the German Patent and Trade Mark Office.

The Marathoneum trademark will in future bundle all the activities of the Berlin Sports Museum and its supporting association “Forum für Sportgeschichte” with regard to the national and international history of running. The Marathoneum is therefore a collection, archive, publisher, imprint as well as organizer and multiplier for all forms of running! In addition, the Marathoneum awards the ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ every two years for deserving and long-standing pioneers of running.

The Marathoneum owns approx. 2,500 posters, approx. 1,500 T-shirts, approx. 2,200 finisher medals as well as 1,600 accreditation cards for races from all over the world. In the library there are more than 95 German and English language running time fonts. The total inventory of the collections is deposited and listed on approx. 250 metres of shelves in two large depot rooms in the Berlin Sports Museum according to museological rules. An important treasure of the museum is the extensive and magnificent English collection of Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), as well as the archives of Henryk Paskal (Poland), Wim Verhoorn (Netherland) and Werner Sonntag (Gemany).

In the exhibition „Keep on Running“ at the Berlin Olympic Park, selected objects from the collection, including starting numbers, shoes and sportswear of Olympic champions and world record holders, are exhibited on 300m³.

# Die Athletinnen und Athleten die Leichtathletik Geschichte schrieben:
**Erfolgreiche Athleten, Athletinnen und Legenden der deutschen und internationalen Leichtathletik.**In der “Hall of Fame” von German Road Races soll der deutschen und auch der internationalen Legenden und herausragenden Persönlichkeiten der Leichtathletik ein Denkmal gesetzt werden – und auch gleichzeitig ein Archiv und “Gedächtnis” entstehen, in dem man sich ihrer grossartigen Leistungen erinnert.
Zunächst war es eine Idee vom Berlin-Marathon – in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Sportmuseum Berlin – erfolgreiche Mittel- und Langstreckler früherer Zeiten aus Ost und West zusammenzuführen und deren Leistungen statistisch zu erfassen. Im Laufe der Zeit wurden in der Rubrik “Sportmuseum” dann auch Beiträge aus Zeitungen und Zeitschriften übernommen, die sich mit den Erfolgen und der Vita überragender Leichtathleten der Vergangenheit befassten.Im Zuge der Vorbereitung und Einstimmung auf die XII. IAAF Weltmeisterschaften der Leichtathletik Berlin 2009 befasste man sich in den Medien viel mehr mit der großen leichtathletischen Vergangenheit Deutschlands. Insofern ist ein großes und über die Mittel- und Langstreckler Gruppe hinausgehendes “Erinnerungs-Archiv” entstanden.Diese Zusammenfassung mit der bisherigen Untergliederung kann sicherlich nur ein Anfang der Gestaltung eines Archives sein, es bedarf der Fortsetzung, Ergänzung, Verbesserung – aber auch weiterer Zuarbeit.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
AIMS Marathon Museum of Running
Auf Anregung von Horst Milde (Berlin-Marathon) wurde das Sportmuseum Berlin vom 14. Kongreß der AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau am 4.–8. Dezember 1994 zum AIMS Marathon-Museum of Running berufen. Damit hatte die Geschichte des Laufens in Berlin einen adäquaten internationalen Sammlungsort gefunden, den die AIMS seitdem organisatorisch und ab 2008 auch finanziell unterstützt.
Das Sportmuseum Berlin ist das älteste und größte Sportmuseum in Deutschland (seit 1925), mit fünf professsionellen Sport-Historikern, die von der Stadt Berlin finanziert werden. Die Ausstellungsräume und das umfangreiche Archiv befinden sich im Olympiapark Berlin.
Am 21. Januar 2015 wurden die Wortmarke Marathoneum und ein Läuferlogo als Bildmarke auf das Forum für Sportgeschichte beim Deutschen Patent- und Markenamt eingetragen.
Unter der Dachmarke Marathoneum werden zukünftig alle Aktivitäten des Sportmuseum Berlin und seines Förderervereins Forum für Sportgeschichte hinsichtlich der nationalen und internationalen Geschichte des Laufens gebündelt. Das Marathoneum ist somit zugleich Sammlung, Archiv, Herausgeber, Imprint, Veranstalter und Multiplikator für alle Erscheinungsformen des Laufsports! Zusätzlich verleiht das Marathoneum alle zwei Jahre den ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ für verdiente und langjährige Wegbereiter des Laufsports.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
Das Marathoneum besitzt ca. 2.500 Plakate, ca. 1.500 T-Shirts, ca. 2.200 Finisher-Medaillen sowie 1.600 Akkreditierungskarten von Läufen aus der ganzen Welt. In der Bibliothek befinden sich mehr als 95 deutsche und englischsprachige Laufzeitschriften. Der Gesamtbestand der Sammlungen wird auf ca. 250 Regalmetern in zwei großen Depoträumen im Sportmuseum Berlin nach museologischen Regeln deponiert und verzeichnet. Ein wichtiger Schatz des Museums ist die umfangreiche und großartige englischsprachige Sammlung von Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), sowie die Archive von Henryk Paskal (Polen), Wim Verhoorn (Niederland) und Werner Sonntag (Deutschland).
Im Olympiapark Berlin sind in der Ausstellung „Keep on Running“ auf 300m³ ausgewählte Objekte aus der Sammlung, darunter Startnummern, Schuhe und Sportkleidung von Olympiasiegern und Weltrekordlern ausgestellt.
* * *
**English:**At the suggestion of Horst Milde (Berlin Marathon), the Berlin Sports Museum was appointed the AIMS Marathon Museum of Running at the 14th Congress of the AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau on 4-8 December 1994. So the history of running in Berlin had found an adequate international collection location, which the AIMS has been supporting organizationally and financially since 2008.
The Berlin Sports Museum is the oldest and largest sports museum in Germany (since 1925), with five professional sports historians financed by the city of Berlin. The exhibition rooms and the extensive archive are located in the Berlin Olympic Park.
On 21 January 2015, the word mark Marathoneum and a runner logo were registered as a figurative mark in the Forum for Sports History at the German Patent and Trade Mark Office.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
The Marathoneum trademark will in future bundle all the activities of the Berlin Sports Museum and its supporting association “Forum für Sportgeschichte” with regard to the national and international history of running. The Marathoneum is therefore a collection, archive, publisher, imprint as well as organizer and multiplier for all forms of running! In addition, the Marathoneum awards the ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ every two years for deserving and long-standing pioneers of running.
The Marathoneum owns approx. 2,500 posters, approx. 1,500 T-shirts, approx. 2,200 finisher medals as well as 1,600 accreditation cards for races from all over the world. In the library there are more than 95 German and English language running time fonts. The total inventory of the collections is deposited and listed on approx. 250 metres of shelves in two large depot rooms in the Berlin Sports Museum according to museological rules. An important treasure of the museum is the extensive and magnificent English collection of Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), as well as the archives of Henryk Paskal (Poland), Wim Verhoorn (Netherland) and Werner Sonntag (Gemany).
In the exhibition „Keep on Running“ at the Berlin Olympic Park, selected objects from the collection, including starting numbers, shoes and sportswear of Olympic champions and world record holders, are exhibited on 300m³.

# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin
[![Image 49: Facebook](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/facebook-white.png)](https://www.facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again&title=Loroupe%20breaks%20marathon%20world%20best%20in%20Berlin "Share on Facebook")[![Image 50: Twitter](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/twitter-white.png)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again&text=loroupe-breaks-marathon-world-best-in-berlin "Share on X")[![Image 51: Email](https://www.worldathletics.org/static/email-white.png)](mailto:?subject=Loroupe%20breaks%20marathon%20world%20best%20in%20Berlin&body=https://www.worldathletics.org/news/report/loroupe-does-it-again "Share via email")
Kenyan distance runner Tegla Loroupe (© Getty Images)
Kenya's Tegla Loroupe improved her own world women's best time by four seconds to win the Berlin marathon in 2:20:43 before more than a million cheering spectators on Sunday.
Kenyan Josephat Kiprono won the men's race in 2:06:45, the third best time ever, leading a record field of 28,000 participants through the German capital city under near-ideal weather conditions - 15 degrees, cloudy and little wind.
The flat and fast course that wends its way through nine of the Berlin's 23 districts now holds the world's best marks for men and women: Brazilian Ronaldo da Costa won last year's race in 2:06.05.
The diminutive Loroupe, who is based in Germany, beat the previous best time of 2:20:47 for the 42.195 km race, which she set when she won the Rotterdam marathon in April 1998.

# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin
"This was my best race ever," said Loroupe, who did not realise she had set the new best mark until several minutes after crossing the finish line. "It makes it all the nicer that I did it in Germany."
Loroupe, who came in third in the 10,000 metre event at the World Championships in Seville last month, collected 180,000 marks ($96,000) for setting the world best time on top of her first-place prize of 50,000 marks ($27,000).
Loroupe had been aiming to become the first women to run faster than 2:20, but the 26-year-old slipped behind the world-best pace midway through the race as it moved through the districts of Kreuzberg and Neukoelln.
She found a new burst of energy at the 28-km (17-mile) mark in the leafy district of Steglitz and raced up the course's only significant incline, a climb of about 30 metres between the 30 and 32-km marks, to put herself back on track for the world best time.
"I hadn't expected it for a while because I had felt very tired," said Loroupe, who has lived and trained in the German town of Detmold for the last seven years. "I tried for the 2:19 mark but I didn't manage it.
"Thanks to the support of the crowd I was able to pick up the pace again," added the Kenyan, who stands 1.53 metres tall and weighs 40 kg.
"Tegla really broke the record in the last 100 metres," said her coach Volker Wagner. "I don’t think even Carl Lewis could have beaten her over the last couple of kilometres. She really sprinted right at the end."
Marleen Renders of Belgium was second in the women's race finishing in 2:23.58, followed by Russia's Svetlana Zakharova in 2:27.07.
Kiprono completed a fine day for Kenya and came close to setting a men's best time with a strong kick on the final mile of the race down the fashionable Kudamm shopping boulevard.

# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin
Only da Costa's world best mark in Berlin last year and South Africa's Gerd Thys, who set the year's best time in 2:06:32 in February in Tokyo, have been faster.
Kiprono, who came in second in the 1997 race, was followed to the line by Takayuki Inubushi of Japan in 2:06.57 and compatriot Samson Kandie in 2:08.34.
The 28,000 participants in 26th annual Berlin marathon included 4,000 rollerbladers, wheelchair racers and power walkers.
Only the New York and London marathons, with about 30,000 participants, are larger, organisers said.

# Die Athletinnen und Athleten die Leichtathletik Geschichte schrieben:
**Erfolgreiche Athleten, Athletinnen und Legenden der deutschen und internationalen Leichtathletik.**In der “Hall of Fame” von German Road Races soll der deutschen und auch der internationalen Legenden und herausragenden Persönlichkeiten der Leichtathletik ein Denkmal gesetzt werden – und auch gleichzeitig ein Archiv und “Gedächtnis” entstehen, in dem man sich ihrer grossartigen Leistungen erinnert.
Zunächst war es eine Idee vom Berlin-Marathon – in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Sportmuseum Berlin – erfolgreiche Mittel- und Langstreckler früherer Zeiten aus Ost und West zusammenzuführen und deren Leistungen statistisch zu erfassen. Im Laufe der Zeit wurden in der Rubrik “Sportmuseum” dann auch Beiträge aus Zeitungen und Zeitschriften übernommen, die sich mit den Erfolgen und der Vita überragender Leichtathleten der Vergangenheit befassten.Im Zuge der Vorbereitung und Einstimmung auf die XII. IAAF Weltmeisterschaften der Leichtathletik Berlin 2009 befasste man sich in den Medien viel mehr mit der großen leichtathletischen Vergangenheit Deutschlands. Insofern ist ein großes und über die Mittel- und Langstreckler Gruppe hinausgehendes “Erinnerungs-Archiv” entstanden.Diese Zusammenfassung mit der bisherigen Untergliederung kann sicherlich nur ein Anfang der Gestaltung eines Archives sein, es bedarf der Fortsetzung, Ergänzung, Verbesserung – aber auch weiterer Zuarbeit.
[office@germanroadraces.de](mailto:office@germanroadraces.de)

# Die Athletinnen und Athleten die Leichtathletik Geschichte schrieben:
**Erfolgreiche Athleten, Athletinnen und Legenden der deutschen und internationalen Leichtathletik.**In der “Hall of Fame” von German Road Races soll der deutschen und auch der internationalen Legenden und herausragenden Persönlichkeiten der Leichtathletik ein Denkmal gesetzt werden – und auch gleichzeitig ein Archiv und “Gedächtnis” entstehen, in dem man sich ihrer grossartigen Leistungen erinnert.
Zunächst war es eine Idee vom Berlin-Marathon – in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Sportmuseum Berlin – erfolgreiche Mittel- und Langstreckler früherer Zeiten aus Ost und West zusammenzuführen und deren Leistungen statistisch zu erfassen. Im Laufe der Zeit wurden in der Rubrik “Sportmuseum” dann auch Beiträge aus Zeitungen und Zeitschriften übernommen, die sich mit den Erfolgen und der Vita überragender Leichtathleten der Vergangenheit befassten.Im Zuge der Vorbereitung und Einstimmung auf die XII. IAAF Weltmeisterschaften der Leichtathletik Berlin 2009 befasste man sich in den Medien viel mehr mit der großen leichtathletischen Vergangenheit Deutschlands. Insofern ist ein großes und über die Mittel- und Langstreckler Gruppe hinausgehendes “Erinnerungs-Archiv” entstanden.Diese Zusammenfassung mit der bisherigen Untergliederung kann sicherlich nur ein Anfang der Gestaltung eines Archives sein, es bedarf der Fortsetzung, Ergänzung, Verbesserung – aber auch weiterer Zuarbeit.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
AIMS Marathon Museum of Running
Auf Anregung von Horst Milde (Berlin-Marathon) wurde das Sportmuseum Berlin vom 14. Kongreß der AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau am 4.–8. Dezember 1994 zum AIMS Marathon-Museum of Running berufen. Damit hatte die Geschichte des Laufens in Berlin einen adäquaten internationalen Sammlungsort gefunden, den die AIMS seitdem organisatorisch und ab 2008 auch finanziell unterstützt.
Das Sportmuseum Berlin ist das älteste und größte Sportmuseum in Deutschland (seit 1925), mit fünf professsionellen Sport-Historikern, die von der Stadt Berlin finanziert werden. Die Ausstellungsräume und das umfangreiche Archiv befinden sich im Olympiapark Berlin.
Am 21. Januar 2015 wurden die Wortmarke Marathoneum und ein Läuferlogo als Bildmarke auf das Forum für Sportgeschichte beim Deutschen Patent- und Markenamt eingetragen.
Unter der Dachmarke Marathoneum werden zukünftig alle Aktivitäten des Sportmuseum Berlin und seines Förderervereins Forum für Sportgeschichte hinsichtlich der nationalen und internationalen Geschichte des Laufens gebündelt. Das Marathoneum ist somit zugleich Sammlung, Archiv, Herausgeber, Imprint, Veranstalter und Multiplikator für alle Erscheinungsformen des Laufsports! Zusätzlich verleiht das Marathoneum alle zwei Jahre den ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ für verdiente und langjährige Wegbereiter des Laufsports.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
Das Marathoneum besitzt ca. 2.500 Plakate, ca. 1.500 T-Shirts, ca. 2.200 Finisher-Medaillen sowie 1.600 Akkreditierungskarten von Läufen aus der ganzen Welt. In der Bibliothek befinden sich mehr als 95 deutsche und englischsprachige Laufzeitschriften. Der Gesamtbestand der Sammlungen wird auf ca. 250 Regalmetern in zwei großen Depoträumen im Sportmuseum Berlin nach museologischen Regeln deponiert und verzeichnet. Ein wichtiger Schatz des Museums ist die umfangreiche und großartige englischsprachige Sammlung von Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), sowie die Archive von Henryk Paskal (Polen), Wim Verhoorn (Niederland) und Werner Sonntag (Deutschland).
Im Olympiapark Berlin sind in der Ausstellung „Keep on Running“ auf 300m³ ausgewählte Objekte aus der Sammlung, darunter Startnummern, Schuhe und Sportkleidung von Olympiasiegern und Weltrekordlern ausgestellt.
* * *
**English:**At the suggestion of Horst Milde (Berlin Marathon), the Berlin Sports Museum was appointed the AIMS Marathon Museum of Running at the 14th Congress of the AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau on 4-8 December 1994. So the history of running in Berlin had found an adequate international collection location, which the AIMS has been supporting organizationally and financially since 2008.
The Berlin Sports Museum is the oldest and largest sports museum in Germany (since 1925), with five professional sports historians financed by the city of Berlin. The exhibition rooms and the extensive archive are located in the Berlin Olympic Park.
On 21 January 2015, the word mark Marathoneum and a runner logo were registered as a figurative mark in the Forum for Sports History at the German Patent and Trade Mark Office.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
The Marathoneum trademark will in future bundle all the activities of the Berlin Sports Museum and its supporting association “Forum für Sportgeschichte” with regard to the national and international history of running. The Marathoneum is therefore a collection, archive, publisher, imprint as well as organizer and multiplier for all forms of running! In addition, the Marathoneum awards the ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ every two years for deserving and long-standing pioneers of running.
The Marathoneum owns approx. 2,500 posters, approx. 1,500 T-shirts, approx. 2,200 finisher medals as well as 1,600 accreditation cards for races from all over the world. In the library there are more than 95 German and English language running time fonts. The total inventory of the collections is deposited and listed on approx. 250 metres of shelves in two large depot rooms in the Berlin Sports Museum according to museological rules. An important treasure of the museum is the extensive and magnificent English collection of Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), as well as the archives of Henryk Paskal (Poland), Wim Verhoorn (Netherland) and Werner Sonntag (Gemany).
In the exhibition „Keep on Running“ at the Berlin Olympic Park, selected objects from the collection, including starting numbers, shoes and sportswear of Olympic champions and world record holders, are exhibited on 300m³.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
AIMS Marathon Museum of Running
Auf Anregung von Horst Milde (Berlin-Marathon) wurde das Sportmuseum Berlin vom 14. Kongreß der AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau am 4.–8. Dezember 1994 zum AIMS Marathon-Museum of Running berufen. Damit hatte die Geschichte des Laufens in Berlin einen adäquaten internationalen Sammlungsort gefunden, den die AIMS seitdem organisatorisch und ab 2008 auch finanziell unterstützt.
Das Sportmuseum Berlin ist das älteste und größte Sportmuseum in Deutschland (seit 1925), mit fünf professsionellen Sport-Historikern, die von der Stadt Berlin finanziert werden. Die Ausstellungsräume und das umfangreiche Archiv befinden sich im Olympiapark Berlin.
Am 21. Januar 2015 wurden die Wortmarke Marathoneum und ein Läuferlogo als Bildmarke auf das Forum für Sportgeschichte beim Deutschen Patent- und Markenamt eingetragen.
Unter der Dachmarke Marathoneum werden zukünftig alle Aktivitäten des Sportmuseum Berlin und seines Förderervereins Forum für Sportgeschichte hinsichtlich der nationalen und internationalen Geschichte des Laufens gebündelt. Das Marathoneum ist somit zugleich Sammlung, Archiv, Herausgeber, Imprint, Veranstalter und Multiplikator für alle Erscheinungsformen des Laufsports! Zusätzlich verleiht das Marathoneum alle zwei Jahre den ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ für verdiente und langjährige Wegbereiter des Laufsports.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
Das Marathoneum besitzt ca. 2.500 Plakate, ca. 1.500 T-Shirts, ca. 2.200 Finisher-Medaillen sowie 1.600 Akkreditierungskarten von Läufen aus der ganzen Welt. In der Bibliothek befinden sich mehr als 95 deutsche und englischsprachige Laufzeitschriften. Der Gesamtbestand der Sammlungen wird auf ca. 250 Regalmetern in zwei großen Depoträumen im Sportmuseum Berlin nach museologischen Regeln deponiert und verzeichnet. Ein wichtiger Schatz des Museums ist die umfangreiche und großartige englischsprachige Sammlung von Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), sowie die Archive von Henryk Paskal (Polen), Wim Verhoorn (Niederland) und Werner Sonntag (Deutschland).
Im Olympiapark Berlin sind in der Ausstellung „Keep on Running“ auf 300m³ ausgewählte Objekte aus der Sammlung, darunter Startnummern, Schuhe und Sportkleidung von Olympiasiegern und Weltrekordlern ausgestellt.
* * *
**English:**At the suggestion of Horst Milde (Berlin Marathon), the Berlin Sports Museum was appointed the AIMS Marathon Museum of Running at the 14th Congress of the AIMS (Association of International Marathons and Road Races) in Macau on 4-8 December 1994. So the history of running in Berlin had found an adequate international collection location, which the AIMS has been supporting organizationally and financially since 2008.
The Berlin Sports Museum is the oldest and largest sports museum in Germany (since 1925), with five professional sports historians financed by the city of Berlin. The exhibition rooms and the extensive archive are located in the Berlin Olympic Park.
On 21 January 2015, the word mark Marathoneum and a runner logo were registered as a figurative mark in the Forum for Sports History at the German Patent and Trade Mark Office.

# Sportmuseum Berlin –
The Marathoneum trademark will in future bundle all the activities of the Berlin Sports Museum and its supporting association “Forum für Sportgeschichte” with regard to the national and international history of running. The Marathoneum is therefore a collection, archive, publisher, imprint as well as organizer and multiplier for all forms of running! In addition, the Marathoneum awards the ‚Horst-Milde-Award‘ every two years for deserving and long-standing pioneers of running.
The Marathoneum owns approx. 2,500 posters, approx. 1,500 T-shirts, approx. 2,200 finisher medals as well as 1,600 accreditation cards for races from all over the world. In the library there are more than 95 German and English language running time fonts. The total inventory of the collections is deposited and listed on approx. 250 metres of shelves in two large depot rooms in the Berlin Sports Museum according to museological rules. An important treasure of the museum is the extensive and magnificent English collection of Dr. David Martin (Atlanta/USA), as well as the archives of Henryk Paskal (Poland), Wim Verhoorn (Netherland) and Werner Sonntag (Gemany).
In the exhibition „Keep on Running“ at the Berlin Olympic Park, selected objects from the collection, including starting numbers, shoes and sportswear of Olympic champions and world record holders, are exhibited on 300m³.

## German Road Races (GRR) e.V.

## Die Stimme des Laufsports

German Road Races (GRR) e.V. ist die Interessensgemeinschaft der Lauf-Veranstalter in Deutschland. Seit vielen Jahren kümmern wir uns um alle Belange des Laufsports und können dabei vielbeachtete Erfolge vorweisen. Als Stimme des Laufsports berichten, kommentieren und dokumentieren wir das Geschehen im Laufsport, in der Leichtathletik, der Sportpolitik, der Sportmedizin und weiteren interessanten Themen und erarbeiten dabei auf unterschiedlichen Feldern eigenständige Positionen und Aktivitäten.

Wir freuen uns über Ihr Interesse am Laufsport und den vielen Veranstaltungen, die unsere Mitglieder im Laufe eines Jahres anbieten. Nutzen Sie das breite Lauf- und Walking-Angebot für Jung und Alt, für Breiten- und Leistungssportler im Wald, auf der Straße oder dem in der Natur zugänglichen Terrain, das Ihnen Spaß und Freude, zudem auch ein Höchstmaß an Erholung bietet.

Wir freuen uns auf Sie.

## [Hier geht es zu der News Seite von German Road Races](https://news.germanroadraces.de/)

### Für alle Laufveranstaltende

## Warum es sich lohnt

*   Erfahrungsaustausch und Know-How-Transfer
*   Miteinander und voneinander lernern
*   Vertrauliches und kollegiales Miteinander
*   Wir sind bereits über 50 Laufveranstaltende, die sich austauschen
*   Das Beste für alle Läuferinnen und Läufer bieten

*   Regelmäßiger Austausch und Impulse in Online-Meetings

Nimm unverbindlich Kontakt mit uns auf und erfahre in einem persönlichen Gespräch, warum es sich für alle Laufveranstaltende lohnt, dabeizusein und Mitglied unserer Communtity zu werden.

Ob Straße, Trail oder Ultra, ob Volkslauf oder internationaler Marathon, bei uns seid Ihr willkommen.

## Jetzt Mitglied werden!

## **Community und Forum - wir sehen uns**

*   Wir treffen uns einmal im Jahr für ein mehrtägiges Jahrestreffen. In 2024 wird das in Hannover sein. Projekte, die wir angehen, werden von Arbeitsgruppen umgesetzt, die sich nach Bedarf treffen und natürlich sehen wir uns regelmäßig auf unseren jeweiligen Laufveranstaltungen.

*   Seit Anfang 2024 aber haben wir unseren Austausch digitalisiert und nutzen Videokonferenzen und ein Forum, um uns öfter zu sehen und über alle Themen zu sprechen, die uns verbinden und beschäftigen.

*   Immer wieder laden wir auch externe Expertinnen und Impulsgeber ein, die uns helfen, über den Tellerrand hinauszudenken.

![Image 1](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/1999TeglaLoroupe.jpg)
Source: Victor Sailer (link under References)
**26-Sep-1999 – Berlin Marathon – 2:20:43 – Nike Air Streak Vengeance
Date of birth: 9-May-1973
Nationality: Kenyan
World Record duration: 2 years, 4 days**
**The athlete:**After setting the women’s marathon world record in 1998, Tegla Loroupe hardly rested on her laurels. She won the Rotterdam Marathon again in 1999 as well as another half-marathon championship crown. This was alongside multiple half-marathon wins across Europe. What still drove her was the chance to break the 2:20 barrier for women.
Her training had gone well. Loroupe and the organisers of the Berlin Marathon were so confident that she would break through that barrier that they gave her the number 219. With pacemakers calling her splits, Loroupe was 90 seconds ahead of her previous best in the early stages. Fatigue would begin to set in, and by halfway she was falling behind her world record pace.
At the 28 kilometre mark Loroupe found new reserves of energy and powered up the only significant incline of the course. By kilometre 32 she was back on track to break the world record. She would continue sprinting towards the finish and after 24.2 of 26.2 miles she was three seconds behind her previous best. She was disappointed not to get below 2:20, but she still set a new world record.
Loroupe would go on to win the 2000 London Marathon along with another half-marathon world championship among her other later victories. It was only Olympic gold that would elude her, the 2000 Olympics didn’t go according to plan, with Loroupe suffering severe food poisoning the night before the marathon event.
state.next_chunk:
Despite some sources claiming otherwise, including initially Guinness World Records, Loroupe did not run the marathon at the 2000 Olympics barefoot. Although it would have made for an important and fascinating benchmark, Loroupe having trained in her earlier days without shoes, there is a clear picture from the event showing her wearing the Nike Air Streaks that had brought her so much success. I reached out to Guinness World Records, and they have since corrected their entry to reflect that [Phạm Thị Bình](https://www.marathonshoehistory.com/2013-pham-thi-binh/) holds this distinction.
Her achievements helped inspire the rise of African women in distance running, with future world record holder Catherine Ndereba citing her as the inspiration to start running herself. Loroupe further used her position to promote peace, founding the [Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation](https://teglapeace.org/) in 2003. She later worked with both the United Nations and Oxfam to promote these ideals. She would also serve as the Chef de Mission for the refugee team at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics.

**26-Sep-1999 – Berlin Marathon – 2:20:43 – Nike Air Streak Vengeance
Date of birth: 9-May-1973
Nationality: Kenyan
World Record duration: 2 years, 4 days**
**The athlete:**After setting the women’s marathon world record in 1998, Tegla Loroupe hardly rested on her laurels. She won the Rotterdam Marathon again in 1999 as well as another half-marathon championship crown. This was alongside multiple half-marathon wins across Europe. What still drove her was the chance to break the 2:20 barrier for women.
Her training had gone well. Loroupe and the organisers of the Berlin Marathon were so confident that she would break through that barrier that they gave her the number 219. With pacemakers calling her splits, Loroupe was 90 seconds ahead of her previous best in the early stages. Fatigue would begin to set in, and by halfway she was falling behind her world record pace.
At the 28 kilometre mark Loroupe found new reserves of energy and powered up the only significant incline of the course. By kilometre 32 she was back on track to break the world record. She would continue sprinting towards the finish and after 24.2 of 26.2 miles she was three seconds behind her previous best. She was disappointed not to get below 2:20, but she still set a new world record.
Loroupe would go on to win the 2000 London Marathon along with another half-marathon world championship among her other later victories. It was only Olympic gold that would elude her, the 2000 Olympics didn’t go according to plan, with Loroupe suffering severe food poisoning the night before the marathon event.

Kenyan distance runner Tegla Loroupe (© Getty Images)
Kenya's Tegla Loroupe improved her own world women's best time by four seconds to win the Berlin marathon in 2:20:43 before more than a million cheering spectators on Sunday.
Kenyan Josephat Kiprono won the men's race in 2:06:45, the third best time ever, leading a record field of 28,000 participants through the German capital city under near-ideal weather conditions - 15 degrees, cloudy and little wind.
The flat and fast course that wends its way through nine of the Berlin's 23 districts now holds the world's best marks for men and women: Brazilian Ronaldo da Costa won last year's race in 2:06.05.
The diminutive Loroupe, who is based in Germany, beat the previous best time of 2:20:47 for the 42.195 km race, which she set when she won the Rotterdam marathon in April 1998.

# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin
"This was my best race ever," said Loroupe, who did not realise she had set the new best mark until several minutes after crossing the finish line. "It makes it all the nicer that I did it in Germany."
Loroupe, who came in third in the 10,000 metre event at the World Championships in Seville last month, collected 180,000 marks ($96,000) for setting the world best time on top of her first-place prize of 50,000 marks ($27,000).
Loroupe had been aiming to become the first women to run faster than 2:20, but the 26-year-old slipped behind the world-best pace midway through the race as it moved through the districts of Kreuzberg and Neukoelln.
She found a new burst of energy at the 28-km (17-mile) mark in the leafy district of Steglitz and raced up the course's only significant incline, a climb of about 30 metres between the 30 and 32-km marks, to put herself back on track for the world best time.
"I hadn't expected it for a while because I had felt very tired," said Loroupe, who has lived and trained in the German town of Detmold for the last seven years. "I tried for the 2:19 mark but I didn't manage it.
"Thanks to the support of the crowd I was able to pick up the pace again," added the Kenyan, who stands 1.53 metres tall and weighs 40 kg.
"Tegla really broke the record in the last 100 metres," said her coach Volker Wagner. "I don’t think even Carl Lewis could have beaten her over the last couple of kilometres. She really sprinted right at the end."
Marleen Renders of Belgium was second in the women's race finishing in 2:23.58, followed by Russia's Svetlana Zakharova in 2:27.07.
Kiprono completed a fine day for Kenya and came close to setting a men's best time with a strong kick on the final mile of the race down the fashionable Kudamm shopping boulevard.

# Loroupe breaks marathon world best in Berlin
"This was my best race ever," said Loroupe, who did not realise she had set the new best mark until several minutes after crossing the finish line. "It makes it all the nicer that I did it in Germany."
Loroupe, who came in third in the 10,000 metre event at the World Championships in Seville last month, collected 180,000 marks ($96,000) for setting the world best time on top of her first-place prize of 50,000 marks ($27,000).
Loroupe had been aiming to become the first women to run faster than 2:20, but the 26-year-old slipped behind the world-best pace midway through the race as it moved through the districts of Kreuzberg and Neukoelln.
She found a new burst of energy at the 28-km (17-mile) mark in the leafy district of Steglitz and raced up the course's only significant incline, a climb of about 30 metres between the 30 and 32-km marks, to put herself back on track for the world best time.
"I hadn't expected it for a while because I had felt very tired," said Loroupe, who has lived and trained in the German town of Detmold for the last seven years. "I tried for the 2:19 mark but I didn't manage it.
"Thanks to the support of the crowd I was able to pick up the pace again," added the Kenyan, who stands 1.53 metres tall and weighs 40 kg.
"Tegla really broke the record in the last 100 metres," said her coach Volker Wagner. "I don’t think even Carl Lewis could have beaten her over the last couple of kilometres. She really sprinted right at the end."
Marleen Renders of Belgium was second in the women's race finishing in 2:23.58, followed by Russia's Svetlana Zakharova in 2:27.07.
Kiprono completed a fine day for Kenya and came close to setting a men's best time with a strong kick on the final mile of the race down the fashionable Kudamm shopping boulevard.
